courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Algorithms
courses.description: Algorithms, covering basic analysis techniques, basic design techniques (divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming, greedy), basic and advanced graph algorithms, and NP-completeness theory.
courses.course_objectives: By the end of this course, students will be able to analyze time complexity for algorithms using asymptotic notation. By the end of this course, students will be able to apply various sorting and selection algorithms and determine which algorithm to apply for different types of data. By the end of this course, students will be able to apply advanced design and analysis techniques, including greedy and dynamic programming techniques. By the end of this course, students will be able to analyze and prove properties for various graph algorithms. By the end of this course, students will be able to choose (and/or apply) the appropriate algorithm to solve real-world problems and defend the selection (integrated into the above outcomes). By the end of this course, students will be able to describe decision problems and prove problems are in P. By the end of this course, students will be able to prove a problem is in NP, co-NP, or NP-complete.
courses.topical_outline:
Analyze complexity of algorithms.
a. Analysis of recursive algorithms using recursion trees.
b. Analysis of recursive algorithms using substitution method.
c. Analysis of recursive algorithms using Master theorem. Apply various sorting and selection algorithms and determine which algorithm to apply for different types of data.
a. Provide runtime analysis of various sorting algorithm including heapsort, quicksort, counting sort, and radix sort.
b. For a given type of input data, determine the best choice of sorting algorithm.
c. Prove the O (n lg n) lower bound for comparison-based sorting algorithms. Advanced design and analysis techniques, including greedy algorithms and dynamic programming.
a. Design and prove the optimality of greedy algorithms.
b. Design dynamic programming algorithms, including solution recurrence formulation, iterative, bottom-up design, and development of trace-back subroutines. Analyze and prove properties for various graph algorithms.
a. Depth-first search and breadth-first search.
b. Minimum spanning tree.
c. Single-source shortest path and all-pairs shortest path.
d. Network flow – max flow / min cut. Choose (and/or apply) the appropriate algorithm to solve real-world problems and defend the selection.
a. Select between various sorting algorithm for different data scenarios and justify selection.
b. Select between using a greedy strategy or dynamic programming for optimization problems.
c. Select appropriate graph algorithm for a given graph-related question.
d. Derive a graphical representation for a real-world problem and solve the problem using graph properties. Describe decision problems and prove problems are in P.
a. Describe decision problems.
b. Prove a problem is in P by providing a deterministic decider. Prove a problem is in NP, co-NP, or NP-complete.
a. Prove a problem is in NP by providing a verifier or a nondeterministic decider.
b. Prove a problem is NP-Complete by providing a polynomial time reduction from a known NP-Complete problem.
c. Describe the Cook-Levin Theorem proving SAT is NP-Complete.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Algorithms for Computational Biology
courses.description: Application of discrete algorithms to computational problems in molecular biology.  Topics are drawn from such areas as classical sequence comparison, multiple sequence alignment, DNA sequence assembly, DNA physical mapping, genome rearrangement, evolutionary tree construction, and protein folding.  Background in molecular biology is not required.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Programming Languages
courses.description: Several modern programming languages and the paradigm -- procedural programming, object-oriented programming, functional programming, and logic programming -- that each strives to accommodate.  Projects involve at least three languages.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Functional Programming
courses.description: The functional programming paradigm:  functions and types, type inference and polymorphism, higher order functions and recursion, evaluation strategies, abstract data types and modules, lists, trees, and lazy data structures, reasoning about functional programs.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Evolutionary Computation and Its Applications
courses.description: An in-depth introduction to evolutionary computation methods and an exploration of research problems in evolutionary computation and its applications which may lead to work on a project or a dissertation.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Compilers
courses.description: Design and implementation of compilers for high-level programming languages.  Topics include all phases of a typical compiler, including scanning, parsing, semantic analysis, intermediate code generation, code optimization, and code generation. Students design and develop a compiler for a small programming language. Emphasis is placed on using compiler development tools.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Foundations of Deep Learning and Generative AI
courses.description: An introduction to advanced deep learning for AI applications, covering modern neural network architectures such as MLPs, CNNs, and Transformers. Students will learn to use, build, and train deep networks for vision and language tasks, such as classification, detection, and generation.
courses.course_objectives: Students will understand the architecture and training algorithms of feedforward neural networks. Students will understand the structure and applications of deep convolutional neural networks (e.g., VGG, ResNet, MobileNet, Yolo). Students will understand the principles and applications of transformer-based neural networks (e.g., BERT, ViT, GPT). Students will understand autoencoders, representation learning, and transfer learning techniques. Students will understand the structure and applications of generative adversarial networks (GANs). Students will understand the basic concepts of recurrent neural networks and reinforcement learning. Students will understand and apply deep learning models to computer vision and natural language processing tasks. Students will implement deep learning systems using GPU-based frameworks. Students will understand the bottlenecks and limitations of modern deep learning techniques (e.g., memory and computation costs, security and ethical limitations). Students will work effectively in a team to design and implement a project that applies deep learning techniques to solve a real-world problem.
courses.topical_outline: Introductions Classification problem, basic machine learning models Neural networks, deep convolutional neural networks (DCNN) Training and inference techniques Using GPU to accelerate learning and inference Autoencoder, representation and transfer learning Self-attention and transformer-based neural networks Neural networks for computer vision and natural language processing Foundation models (LLMs, VLMs) Generative adversarial networks (GAN) Hardware acceleration of deep learning systems
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Computer Architecture and Organization
courses.description: Design and analysis of the structure and function of modern computing systems. Topics studied include combinational and sequential logic, number systems and computer arithmetic, hardware design and organization of CPU, I/O systems and memory systems, instruction set and assembly language design, performance characterization and measurement, and current trends and developments in computer architecture and organization.
courses.prerequisiteText: (CSCI 2670 or CSCI 2670E or CSEE 2220 or CSEE 2220E) and CSCI 1730

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Computer Architecture and Organization
courses.description: Design and analysis of the structure and function of modern computing systems. Topics studied include combinational and sequential logic, number systems and computer arithmetic, hardware design and organization of CPU, I/O systems and memory systems, instruction set and assembly language design, performance characterization and measurement, and current trends and developments in computer architecture and organization.
courses.prerequisiteText: (CSCI 2670 or CSCI 2670E or CSEE 2220 or CSEE 2220E) and CSCI 1730
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Operating Systems
courses.description: Coverage of the key concepts in modern operating systems. Specific topics include process management, synchronization mechanisms, scheduling strategies, deadlock detection/avoidance, memory management, file systems, protection and security, and distributed systems. Concepts will be reinforced through programming projects using a realistic operating system.
courses.prerequisiteText: (CSCI 4720 or CSCI 4720E or CSEE 4280) and CSCI 2720

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Real-Time Scheduling for the Internet of Things
courses.description: Basic concepts of real-time systems, with an emphasis onscheduling issues. Consideration of both offline and onlinescheduling. Online schedules will include static and dynamicpriority systems, with and without allowing preemption. Also,consideration of resource sharing and multiprocessor scheduling.Course will include programming projects on a microprocessor.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Computer Networks
courses.description: In-depth coverage of computer networks, including digital data transmission and encoding, layered protocol models, Internet protocol, Internet client-server models, and network design methodology.
courses.prerequisiteText: (CSCI 1730 or CSCI 1730E) and (CSCI 2720 or CSCI 2720E) and (CSCI 2670 or CSCI 2670E or CSEE 2220 or CSEE 2220E or CSEE 2220H))

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Computer Networks
courses.description: In-depth coverage of computer networks, including digital data transmission and encoding, layered protocol models, Internet protocol, Internet client-server models, and network design methodology.
courses.prerequisiteText: (CSCI 1730 or CSCI 1730E) and (CSCI 2720 or CSCI 2720E) and (CSCI 2670 or CSCI 2670E or CSEE 2220 or CSEE 2220E or CSEE 2220H)

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Ubiquitous Computing
courses.description: Introduces the technologies required to develop mobile and ubiquitous computing applications, including communication protocols, naming and location management, replication and consistency management, security and privacy, content adaptation, and battery power management.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Distributed Computing Systems
courses.description: The fundamental concepts in distributed computing and the practical techniques for building distributed systems. Topics include distributed computing models, naming, synchronization, replication and consistency, fault tolerance, and security. Widely deployed distributed systems are used as case studies. Students design, implement, and analyze prototype systems.
courses.prerequisiteText: CSCI 2720 and CSCI 1730 | Graduate Prerequisite | CSCI 7010

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Cloud Computing
courses.description: Introduction to cloud computing for undergraduate and graduate students. Topics include virtualization, data centers, virtual machines, cloud service models, public vs. private vs. hybrid clouds, open stack, container and orchestration infrastructure, cloud storage, mobile cloud, IoT, and big data. Students also learn how to design, implement, and test cloud applications.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Human-Computer Interaction
courses.description: Issues in the design, development, and evaluation of user interfaces for computer systems.  Concepts in human factors, usability, and interface design, and the effects of human capabilities and limitations on interaction with computer systems.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Computer Graphics
courses.description: Principles of two-dimensional and three-dimensional interactive raster graphics.  Principles of scan conversion algorithms for two-dimensional and three-dimensional graphics primitives; data structures and modeling techniques for raster graphics; interaction, visual realism, animation and user interface design; ray tracing, illumination, shading, data storage/retrieval, software engineering and parallel computing for graphics.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Signal Processing
courses.description: Introduction to signal processing. Students will learn basic concepts, algorithms, and software tools for multidimensional signal representation, processing and analysis. 1-D, 2-D, 3-D, and 4-D signal processing techniques and applications will be discussed.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Biomedical Image Analysis
courses.description: Introduction to the standard approaches to biomedical image analysis, including basic concepts of biomedical imaging, basic algorithms, principles of software systems, and their applications.  Biomedical image analysis software tools will be used in hands-on projects.
courses.prerequisiteText: CSCI 2720 or CSCI 2725 or permission of department
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Computational Neuroscience
courses.description: Introduction to computational neuroscience. Students will learn basic concepts, algorithms, and software tools for computational neuroscience models. Neural signal processing and neural network models will be discussed.
courses.prerequisiteText: CSCI 2720 or CSCI 2725 or permission of department
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Special Topics in Computer Science
courses.description: Various advanced topics in Computer Science.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Capstone Design I
courses.description: Computer Science design project experience under the supervision of a project director.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Capstone Design II
courses.description: Computer Science design experience, including completion of a design project under the supervision of a project director.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Directed Study in Computer Science
courses.description: Content will vary in response to the interests, needs, and capability of the students and faculty involved.  Individual, guided study in computer science.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Faculty Mentored Research in Computer Science
courses.description: Content will vary in response to the interests, needs, and capability of the students and faculty involved. Individual,guided study in computer science.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research I
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research II
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research III
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Undergraduate Research Thesis (or Final Project)
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data. Students will write or produce a thesis or other professional capstone product, such as a report or portfolio that describes their systematic and in-depth inquiry.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Internship in Computer Science Business/Industry
courses.description: Internship in a professional setting allowing the student to integrate his/her educational experience with real-world situations in software development, database technology, hardware design, networks, etc.
courses.prerequisiteText: Permission of department | Graduate Prerequisite | Permission of department

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Web Composing and Scripting
courses.description: Web site design from a technical viewpoint. Covers applicable network protocols; HTML, CSS, XML, and JavaScript; Web standards and cross-browser compatibility issues; code development and debugging techniques; server-side scripting; database-driven Web applications; navigation and usability concerns; search engine optimization; and security concerns.
courses.prerequisiteText: CSCI 1100-1100L or CSCI 1301-1301L | Graduate Prerequisite | CSCI 7010
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Approximation Algorithms
courses.description: This is a graduate-level course on algorithms for finding approximate solutions to NP-complete problems.  It introduces the class NP and explores the importance of the NP-complete problems. Approaches for finding approximate solutions to many combinatorial and LP-based problems will be discussed.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Automata and Formal Languages
courses.description: The fundamental limitations on mechanized computation.  In the first part of the course, the emphasis is on possible versus impossible computations.  Three classes of languages are considered:  regular, context-free, and recursively enumerable.  In the second part of the course the emphasis shifts  to possible versus feasible computations.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Computer Systems Architecture
courses.description: Functional components and structure of computing systems.  Topics include principles of combinational and sequential logic, number systems and computer arithmetic, hardware subsystem design and test, I/O and memory subsystem principles and techniques, instruction set architecture and implementation, pipelining andsystem-level parallelism, interconnection networks, trends.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Master's Research
courses.description: Research while enrolled for a master's degree under the direction of faculty members.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Graduate Student Seminar
courses.description: Advanced supervised experience in an applied setting.  Thiscourse may not be used to satisfy a student's approved program ofstudy.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Computer Programming
courses.description: Algorithms, programs, and computing systems. Topics studied include: fundamental techniques of program development and supportive software tools; and programming projects and applications in a structured computer language.  Hands-on experience using microcomputers.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Technical Report
courses.description: Preparation of a technical report to satisfy requirements for the MAMS degree.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Master's Project
courses.description: Applied research project under the direction of the major professor for the Computer Science Non-thesis MS degree.  As part of the requirements, a comprehensive report must beprepared detailing the student's procedures and findingsregarding the completed project work.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Master's Thesis
courses.description: Thesis writing under the direction of the major professor.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Advanced Special Topics in Computer Science
courses.description: Various advanced and current topics in Computer Science.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Knowledge-Based Systems
courses.description: Theory and practice of knowledge-based system construction.  Topics will include knowledge-based construction, inference engines, reasoning from incomplete or uncertain information, and user interfaces.
courses.prerequisiteText: [CSCI(ARTI) 4540/6540 and CSCI(PHIL) 4550/6550] or permission of department
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Advanced Software Engineering
courses.description: Analysis of advanced methods in software engineering. Emphasis is placed on formal specification methods, advanced software testing, software reuse, distributed software design, and communication protocol specification. Studies include advanced software development tools and systems.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Parallel Processing and Computational Science
courses.description: Topics include computer architectures, interconnection networks, basic concepts in parallel computing, parallel algorithms,  matrix multiplications, solving systems of equations, parallel direct and iterative methods, programming on different parallel architectures, and applications.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Advanced Numerical Methods and Scientific Computing
courses.description: Advanced numerical methods for solving problems in science andengineering. Computationally-oriented course guiding students bymodeling, choosing appropriate numerical methods, implementingthe methods and analyzing the numerical results by visualizationtools.  Topics include computer architectures, interconnectionnetworks, basic concepts in parallel computing, parallelalgorithms, matrix multiplications, solving systems of equations,parallel direct and iterative methods, programming on differentparallel architectures, and applications.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Parallel and Distributed Simulation Systems
courses.description: The mechanisms used in parallel and distributed simulationsystems.  Topics will include synchronization algorithms, datadistribution techniques, parallel and distributed applicationsrunning on top of simulation executives, high-performanceanalytic simulation, and distributed virtual environments.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Software Security and Cyber Forensics
courses.description: Exploration of both the foundation and recent advances in software security and cyber forensics. Topics will include software vulnerability analysis, advanced attack and defense techniques, cybercrime investigation and forensics, and security and forensics in different platforms (e.g., mobile, cloud computing, web application).
courses.prerequisiteText: CSCI 4730/6730 or CSCI 4250/6250 or permission of department
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Secure Programming
courses.description: Our core software stacks are built upon unsafe language (e.g. C/C++). However, with the progress of safe languages, such as Rust and Go, industries are rewriting legacy codes to make our systems safer. In this course, students will learn about security concerns related to unsafe language and then teach about secure programming with one of the fastest-growing safe languages. For example, Rust and Go are ranked top in the 2020 developer survey by Stack Overflow.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Advanced Cyber Security
courses.description: Recent advances in computer networks and system security.  Fastand secure network systems, secure storage systems, highperformance intrusion detection systems, and efficient anti-abusesystems.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Computer Network Attacks and Defenses
courses.description: This is an advanced course on computer and network security. Thecourse will mainly focus on reading and analyzing recent top-tier research publications in the field of computer security andprivacy and on the research and development of systems that canenforce security and privacy in the real world.
courses.prerequisiteText: CSCI 4760/6760 or CSCI 4250/6250 or permission of department
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Trustworthy Machine Learning
courses.description: An introduction to technologies that support building trustworthy machine learning systems. Topics include, but are not limited to, adversarial machine learning, privacy-preserving machine learning, transparency in machine learning, and fairness of machine learning.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Enterprise Integration
courses.description: Technical information management aspects of enterprise integration using recent advances in workflow management, database management, distributed systems, and information systems areas of computer science. Topics include federated/multidatabase architectures and systems for integration of distributed, heterogeneous, and autonomous databases, business process modeling and workflow automation.  Large group project.
courses.prerequisiteText: (CSCI 4370/6370 or CSCI 4570/6570) and permission of department
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Data Science Practicum
courses.description: Advanced data science techniques for analyzing large-scale data in distributed environments. Students will develop scalable algorithms in frameworks such as Spark and Flink. This course is team-based, involving several mini-projects over the course of the semester with a competition as the final project.
courses.prerequisiteText: CSCI 4360/6360 or CSCI 4380/6380 or permission of department
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Advanced Database Systems
courses.description: Advanced study of database systems.  The course focuses on concepts, algorithms and technologies for relational, object-oriented and distributed database systems.  Related technologies such as data warehouses and repositories will also be covered.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Information Systems
courses.description: Advanced topics in information systems and databases.  The two major issues dealt with are: (1) information integration and interoperability, and (2) novel database technologies.  The first addresses the integration of autonomous and heterogeneous resources managing structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data.  The second deals with the query formulation, and processing on heterogeneous content.  Special attention will be given to emerging research areas fueled by the Web and related technologies.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Efficient Deep Learning
courses.description: Students will explore cutting-edge techniques in efficient deep learning, such as model compression, neural architecture search, and data efficient learning. Course covers advanced strategies for optimizing deep learning models for speed, memory, and scalability, enabling deployment on resource-limited devices and platforms while maintaining high performance.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be competitive in the growing job markets and be able to research activities of artificial intelligence and big data areas. Students will understand cutting-edge techniques in efficient deep learning, such as model compression, neural architecture search, and data efficient learning. Students will understand advanced strategies for optimizing deep learning models for speed, memory, and scalability, enabling deployment on resource-limited devices and platforms while maintaining high performance.
courses.topical_outline: Basics of deep learning Model pruning Sparse training Quantization Efficient network design and Neural Architecture Search (NAS) Data-efficient learning

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Advanced Algorithms
courses.description: Further study of fundamental algorithms.  Topics covered include advanced data structures, graph algorithms, string algorithms, geometric algorithms, parallel algorithms, and approximation algorithms for NP-complete problems.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Robotics
courses.description: This is primarily a research-oriented and seminar-style course  covering topics of robotics in field and service industries, urban search and rescue, and applications in nuclear environments and logistics. It enables students to understand, devise, and solve problems in advanced robotics applications.
courses.prerequisiteText: CSCI(ARTI) 4530/6530 and (CSCI 4500/6500 or CSCI 1730) or permission of department
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Multi-Robot Systems
courses.description: This is primarily a research oriented, seminar-style course covering the topics of control, communication, cooperation, and coordination aspects in multi-robot systems. It enables students to understand, devise, and solve problems in multi-robot systems and will include project-based assignments.
courses.prerequisiteText: CSCI(ARTI) 4530/6530 and (CSCI 4500/6500 or CSCI 1730 or permission of department)
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Topics in Theoretical Computer Science
courses.description: Advanced topics in theoretical computer science.  The selection of topics varies from year to year.  Areas may include, but are not limited to, denotational semantics, complexity theory, recursion theory, and discrete algorithms.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Topics in Human-Centered Computing
courses.description: Introduction to issues in human-centered computing (HCC) including design and research methodologies; cognitive, social, and cultural theories; assessment and evaluation; ethical issues; and socially responsible computing practices. HCC is interdisciplinary; course bridges concepts from Human-Computer Interaction (HCI); Science and Technology studies (STS), AI, Sociology, Anthropology, and Design.
courses.course_objectives: By the end of this course, students will be able to recognize, describe, and evaluate core HCC theories and research methods. By the end of this course, students will be able to summarize and analyze issues in HCC. By the end of this course, students will be able to assess their own research and/or development practices based on socially responsible computing principles.
courses.topical_outline: What is Human-Centered Computing? Research Paradigms and Methods Cognitive, Social, and Cultural Theories Sociotechnical Systems Topics in Human-Centered Computing (varied) Ethical Issues in Computing: Equity, Bias, Fairness, etc. Socially Responsible Computing

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Advanced Computer Architecture
courses.description: Advanced and high-performance computer architecture. Topics covered include hierarchical memory design, cache memory design, pipelining, vector processing and parallel processing.  Case studies of vector processors and multi-processor architectures:  shared memory, distributed memory, data parallel (SIMD) and control parallel (MIMD) architectures, and heterogeneous parallel computing on a network of workstations.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Operating Systems
courses.description: Software systems geared at supporting parallel and distributed computing.  Programming language support will focus on simple and efficient ways to express parallel programs.  Compiler and operating system support will focus on new optimizations to make parallel programs execute more efficiently.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Real-Time Scheduling
courses.description: Advanced topics in real-time systems with an emphasis on scheduling issues.  Topics will be different each semester.  Possible topics include: multiprocessor scheduling, power-aware scheduling, application-specific scheduling (e.g., multimedia scheduling issues).
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Distributed Systems
courses.description: The design and implementation of a wide class of distributed systems. The selection of topics will vary from year to year.  Topics may include, but are not limited to, distributed file systems, peer-to-peer systems, distributed spam processing, content delivery networks, and security and privacy.
courses.prerequisiteText: At least one of the following: CSCI 4730/6730 or CSCI 4760/6760 or CSCI 4370/6370
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Data Intensive Computing
courses.description: Modern computing applications require storage, management, andprocessing of petabytes of data. The data is not only extremelydiverse, ranging from unstructured text and relational tables to complex graphs, but it is also dynamic. This course focuses on developing scalable architectures, algorithms, and techniques for supporting various data intensive applications.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Cloud Computing
courses.description: This advanced course in cloud computing investigates the research that leads to the creation of “clouds” and includes in-depth discussion for new research that will soon be reflected in real-world clouds. Topics include cloud infrastructure, microservices, cloud functions, cloud-based large-scale machine learning and AI, and cloud IoT.
courses.prerequisiteText: CSCI 4730/6730 or CSCI 4780/6780 or permission of department
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Image Processing and Computer Graphics
courses.description: Image processing and computer graphics.  Topics include:  image representation, restoration, transformation, classification, compression, enhancement, segmentation, image filter, design, histogram techniques, sampling and quantization, Fast Fourier Transform, image data structures, parallel/distributed processing, illumination models and surface-rendering methods.  A number of applications will be presented as case studies.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
courses.description: Low-level and high-level vision including edge detection, connected component labeling, boundary detection, segmentation, stereopsis, motion analysis, and object recognition.  Knowledge representation, knowledge retrieval and reasoning techniques in computer vision.  Parallel computing, parallel architectures and neural computing for computer vision.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Advanced Opt Methods in AI
courses.description: Course will equip graduate students in quantitative fields with foundational and advanced optimization techniques for AI and machine learning. It covers core strategies, state-of-the-art algorithms, and theoretical principles essential for addressing machine learning challenges, emphasizing their application in the era of big data.
courses.course_objectives: Students will learn optimization algorithms to address fundamental machine learning challenges encountered in data analysis and broader data science contexts. Students will deepen their understanding of basic optimization techniques, enabling them to implement these strategies in their research. This includes gaining a solid grasp of both the theoretical underpinnings and practical applications of solving typical optimization problems in machine learning and data science.
courses.topical_outline: Introduction and Convexity Gradient Descent Project Gradient Descent Proximal Method Project GD Nonconvex optimization Accelerated Gradient Newton’s Methods Quasi-newton Methods Derivative-free Optimization Federated Learning Distributed Learning Sharpness-Aware Minimization Bi-level Optimization
courses.prerequisiteText: CSCI 4380/6380 or CSCI(ARTI) 8950 or permission of department
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Advanced Biomedical Image Analysis
courses.description: Introduction to advanced approaches to, and applications of, biomedical image analysis, including imaging biomarker discovery, computer-aided diagnosis, computer-aided follow-up, image-guided therapy, molecular imaging, functional imaging, and translational imaging.  Advanced applications of state-of-the-art biomedical image analysis software systems will be emphasized.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Biomedical Informatics
courses.description: This course introduces advanced topics and applications ofbiomedical informatics, including health informatics systems,imaging informatics systems, computer-aided diagnosis,computer-aided follow-up, and translational biomedicalinformatics systems. Advanced applications of state-of-the-artbiomedical informatics software systems will be emphasized.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Decision Making Under Uncertainty
courses.description: Choosing optimally among different lines of actions is a key aspect of autonomy in artificial agents. This course will focuson how to make optimal and approximately optimal decisions insingle and multiagent settings. It will be self-contained,introducing  background literature such as aspects of probability and game theories.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Advanced Representation Learning
courses.description: Advanced representation learning algorithms in machine learning, from the traditional subspace learning models to the recent deep representation learning models. Applications in the fields of computer vision, data mining, and natural language processing will be covered.
courses.prerequisiteText: (CSCI 4380/6380 and CSCI(PHIL) 4550/6550) or permission of department
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Large-Scale Optimization for Machine Learning
courses.description: Introduction of optimization algorithms suitable for solving large-scale problems, with a focus on exploring recent advances in the context of machine learning. Students will learn several algorithms for solving smooth and non-smooth problems, compare the efficacy of those methods, and discuss the trade-offs in terms of statistical accuracy, scalability, and algorithmic complexity.
courses.prerequisiteText: CSCI 4380/6380 or CSCI 4360/6360 or permission of department
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Advanced Data Analytics: Statistical Learning and Optimization
courses.description: Advanced topics in data analysis, with an emphasis on statistical learning and related optimization problems. The applications include regression, classification, and other tasks in image analysis. The lectures will be based on books and articles in the field of computer vision and medical image analysis.
courses.prerequisiteText: CSCI 4150/6150 or CSCI 4380/6380 or permission of department.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Privacy-Preserving Data Analysis
courses.description: An introduction to the privacy preservation problems, as well asalgorithmic and statistical techniques for data privacy, in modern data analysis, such as machine learning and data mining. Approaches include randomized algorithms, synthetic data generation, stability analysis, and so on.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Machine Intelligence for Ubiquitous IoT Systems
courses.description: Exploration of advanced machine learning techniques for IoT ecosystems, covering sensor data management, resource-aware algorithms, and real-world scenarios driving smart connectivity. Students gain hands-on experience designing intelligent systems, leveraging data analytics for ubiquitous environments, and building next-generation intelligent systems.
courses.course_objectives: Students will learn basic context of modern machine learning techniques. Students will learn major Internet of Things applications. Students will learn how to do paper review and paper presentation. Students will learn how to implement machine learning algorithms and solve real-world IoT problems.
courses.topical_outline: 1. Machine Learning in Smart Home 2. Machine Learning in Smart Healthcare 3. Machine Learning in Intelligent Agriculture 4. Machine Learning in Smart Transportation 5. Machine Learning in Smart Industrial and Manufacturing 6. Machine Learning in Smart Environmental Systems
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Internet of Things Security
courses.description: Introduction to security problems associated with the emerging Internet of Things (IoT) technologies, including privacy disclosure and data manipulation. Topics studied include architectural differences leading to such issues, how adversaries launch attacks by either exploiting software vulnerabilities or physically hacking into the hardware, and mitigation techniques, such as trusted booting.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Machine Learning System
courses.description: Introduction to system design for supporting large-scale ML applications, and how to use ML to optimize resource usage in computer systems, and how to efficiently deploy ML models on different platforms. Course is suitable for graduate students from all disciplines who have an interest in machine learning and systems.
courses.course_objectives: Students will understand how to use ML to optimize resource usage in computer systems. Students will learn that how to efficiently deploy ML models on different platforms. Students will gain the experience with how to evaluate performance (i.e., memory, latency) the deep neural networks. Students will recognize the potential optimizations for broad scientific applications.
courses.topical_outline: I. Introduction to Machine Learning System II. ML Frameworks and Graph-level Optimizations III. Operator-level and Code-level Optimizations IV. Memory-level and Hardware-level Optimizations V. Parallelism and Machine Learning Compilation VI. Automatic Optimizations VII. Efficient on-device Learning
courses.prerequisiteText: Some experience in machine learning and system programming
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Research Seminar
courses.description: Weekly research seminar.  Students must attend and give at least one presentation at the seminar.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Doctoral Research
courses.description: Research while enrolled for a doctoral degree under the direction of faculty members.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Doctoral Graduate Student Seminar
courses.description: Advanced supervised experience in an applied setting.  Thiscourse may not be used to satisfy a student's approved program ofstudy.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Doctoral Dissertation
courses.description: Dissertation writing under the direction of the major professor.

courses.subject: CSEE(BIOE)
courses.title: Applied Biomedical Instrumentation
courses.description: Lab-based design and realization of electronic devices with a biomedical emphasis. Multidisciplinary teams select a biomedical application as a semester project and plan, design, and build a prototype that typically combines elements of sensors, controls, and mechatronics with embedded software. A lecture component complements this problem-based learning course.
courses.prerequisiteText: ENGR 2170-2170L or ENGR 2170E or ECSE 2170-2170L or ECSE 2170H

courses.subject: CSEE(CSCI)
courses.title: Computer Systems Engineering Design Project
courses.description: Fundamentals of engineering design with emphasis toward integrating engineering science and computer science knowledge in team projects.  Problem selection and application of design principles will be stressed.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSEE(CSCI)
courses.title: Advanced Image Analysis
courses.description: Gain in-depth understanding, knowledge, and the ability to apply cutting-edge methods to process and quantitatively analyze images. This class presents modern image analysis tools,including wavelets, adaptive filters, active contours, and fractals. An important aspect is the design of unsupervised image analysis chains.
courses.prerequisiteText: CSEE 4630 or ENGR 4540/6540 or ELEE 4540/6540 or CSCI 8810 or CSCI 8820 or permission of department
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Introduction to Computer Systems Engineering I
courses.description: An introduction to computer engineering with an integrated hardware and software focus through hands-on activities.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Introduction to Computer Systems Engineering II
courses.description: Designed to foster independent learning, innovation, relativity, critical thinking, communication, teamwork, and design skills.  Students are provided with an overview of the major, design methodology, a major group design experience, and relevant professional development experience.  The goal is to strengthen the cohort and prepare students to succeed in the major.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Fundamentals of Logic Design
courses.description: Course introduces the principles and practices of digital logic design. Student will learn about number systems, Boolean algebra, sum-of-product equations, minterms, Karnaugh maps, optimization, combinational circuit design, sequential circuit design, datapath components, and physical implementation. Students will have the opportunity to design and implement digital circuits using software.
courses.course_objectives: By the end of this course, students should have obtained knowledge on logic functions and Boolean algebra. By the end of this course, students should have learned how to apply formal design methods (minimization methods), the Karnaugh Table, and the Quine-McCluskey method. By the end of this course, students should have gained the ability to formalize a problem and convert it into a logic expression and then into a circuit on the gate level. By the end of this course, students should have obtained an overview how a gate-level circuit can be realized using integrated circuits and programmable logic.
courses.topical_outline: Introduction: Digital systems and number systems Components of digital systems, basic logic functions Boolean algebra: Terminology and properties, DeMorgan’s law Boolean functions: Different representation of Boolean functions including sentence, truth tables, equations, and circuits; Conversion between different representation Canonical representations and Standard form of Boolean functions; Minterms, sum-of-minterms, and compact sum-of-minterms representation Combinational logic design process Universal logic gates Multiplexers and decoders Combinational logic optimization and tradeoffs Simplification of Boolean expressions; The Karnaugh map method; Algebraic 2-level simplification; Don’t care input combinations Sequential logic; SR Latch, D Latch, D-Flip Flop, and registers Timing diagram; State diagrams/finite state machine; Formal design of sequential circuits Datapath components; Multi-function registers, adders, comparators, multiplier Number systems (binary, decimal, hexadecimal); Addition and subtraction; Unsigned and signed numbers; 2's complement Arithmetic-logic unit Physical implementation; Tradeoffs and comparisons between different approaches Realization using gates; AND/OR networks, NAND networks, NOR networks Memory elements; ROM and RAM Gate delays and number of transistors; Simulation of combinatorial circuits; Propagation delay Programmable logic: Gate arrays; Logic design and programming tools
courses.prerequisiteText: CSEE 2210 or ECSE 1100 or ECSE 1100E or ESCE 1100H or ELEE 1030

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Computer Systems Engineering Design Methodology
courses.description: Engages students in Computer Systems Engineering (CSE) project-based design experience and instruction in CSE design methodology.  Students will leverage and build on design experience gained in freshman year to critically and holistically evaluate problems involving computational hardware and software requirements towards producing solutions that address societal, economical, and technical demands and constraints.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Network System Engineering
courses.description: Introduction to the network systems and engineering. Covers  network system programming, communication protocols and security, software and hardware tools, and platforms.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Digital Signal Processing
courses.description: Introduction to Digital Signal Processing.  Students will develop an understanding of discrete-time signals and systems, perform signal analyses in the time and frequency domains using Z and Fourier transforms, and apply them in the design of filters in application areas such as sound, images, and video.
courses.course_objectives: Students will develop an understanding of continuous- and discrete-time signals and systems. Students will be able to perform signal analyses in the time and frequency domains using Z- and Fourier transforms. Students will learn computer-aided design techniques and apply them in the design of filters in application areas such as sound, images and video.
courses.topical_outline:
1. Signals in continuous-time and discrete-time systems - Concept of frequency in continuous and discrete signals / A/D 
and D/A conversions. 2. Discrete Signals - Operations on Discrete Signals / Decimation and Interpolation / Discrete-Time Harmonics and 
Sampling Theorem / Random Signals. 3. Time-Domain Analysis - Difference Equations / Zero-Input Response and Zero-State Response / Impulse Response / Discrete Convolution / Stability and Causality / System Response to Periodic Inputs / Periodic or Circular Convolution / 
Deconvolution. 4. z-Transform Analysis - Poles, Zeros, and the z-Plane / Transfer Function / Inverse z-Transform / z-Transform and System Analysis. 5. Frequency Domain Analysis – Discrete-time Fourier Transform from z-Transform / Properties / DTFT of Discrete-Time Periodic Signals / Inverse DTFT / Frequency Response / System Analysis Using DTFT. 6. Digital Processing of Analog Signals - Sampling, Interpolation, and Signal Recovery / Sampling Rate Conversion / Quantization / Dynamic Range Processors. 7. Design of Finite Impulse Response Filters. 8. Design of Infinite Impulse Response Filters. 9. Discrete Fourier Transform and Its Applications.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Wireless Sensor Networks
courses.description: The design and deployment of wireless sensor networks.  Students will learn the fundamental issues in sensing, data acquisition, power, synchronization, and informatics as related to the unique requirements and constraints of distributed wireless sensor systems.
courses.prerequisiteText: CSCI 1730 or ELEE 2045 or permission of department

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Microcontroller Interfacing
courses.description: From digital cameras to smart speakers, the microcontroller enables internet-connected electronics that keep us connected with our data and the world. This course focuses on developing higher level hardware/software expertise for developing microcontroller-based systems that interface with sensors, displays, and other technologies that are ubiquitous in modern electronics.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Design of Digital Systems
courses.description: Students will learn the building blocks of digital systems and design methods to construct combinatorial and sequential circuits through the use of hardware description language (HDL) and field-programmable gate array (FPGA). Designing digital systems based on application specifications.
courses.prerequisiteText: CSEE 2220 and (ECSE 2170-2170L or ECSE 2170H or ENGR 2170-2170L)

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Advanced Digital Design
courses.description: Introduction to a basic understanding of how microprocessorswork. Students will learn the tools and techniques necessary tosimulate and construct arithmetic-logic unit (ALU), data path andcontroller, memory, and eventually assemble everything into a toyprocessor and implement on a field programmable gate array (FPGA)board.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Computer Architecture
courses.description: Provides a strong foundation to understand computer system architecture from a quantitative perspective and apply it to modern computer designs. Students will utilize hardware and software modeling to implement concepts presented in the class. The class will include both individual and group components.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Embedded Robotics
courses.description: This is an advanced practicum wherein students learn about embedded controller programming, sensors, servo motors, serial communications, autonomous, and remotely controlled systems.  These concepts and methodologies are demonstrated in class and further expanded in a series of student robotic projects of increasing complexity from carbots to humanoids.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Mechatronics Systems Engineering
courses.description: Integration/design techniques for mechatronics systems which are a mixture of mechanical, electrical, electronic, and digital components.  Students will develop an integrative understanding of selected sensors, actuators, interfaces, simulations and controls.  These objectives will be achieved through case studies, exercises, models, and laboratory exercises.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Introduction to Optical Engineering
courses.description: An overview of the major topics in optical engineering, covering both optical instruments as computer systems and the use of optical subsystems in computer systems. Emphasis will be on geometrical optics; major topics will be optical instruments and sensors, multilayer thin films, waveguides, and fiber optics.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Biomedical Imaging
courses.description: Presentation of modern imaging modalities: X-rays, computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, and ultrasound imaging.  Physical principles and instrumentation will be covered, but also the necessary computer algorithms for image formation, including image enhancement, segmentation, quantification, and visualization.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Instrumentation for Monitoring Biological Signals
courses.description: From the cellular to the systemic level, computers can help us understand biological systems or assist in performing specific tasks.  This class covers interfacing techniques and instruments from the cellular level (e.g., patchclamp method) to the systemic level (e.g., ECG and EEG) and includes discussion of topical applications.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Programming for Computational and Systems Biology
courses.description: Introduction to programming skills in computational and systemsbiology. Topics include real-world examples, processing genome orproteome data, and analyzing large-scale data. The idea of “bigdata” will be emphasized to help students with their codingskills to discovering new knowledge in biomedical sciences andsolving biomedical problems.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Special Topics in Computer Systems Engineering
courses.description: Special topics in computer systems engineering design, analysis, or synthesis.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Capstone Design I
courses.description: Engineering design project experience under the supervision of aproject director.
courses.course_objectives: After successfully completing Capstone Senior Design I, students will have advanced in the development of critical thinking skills. After successfully completing Capstone Senior Design I, students will be able to follow the design process. After successfully completing Capstone Senior Design I, students will know how to use project management tools. After successfully completing Capstone Senior Design I, students will be able to synthesize and apply engineering and scientific knowledge towards the solution of a specific problem. After successfully completing Capstone Senior Design I, students will have improved their written and verbal communication skills. After successfully completing Capstone Senior Design I, students will have learned to work in teams effectively.
courses.topical_outline: The topical content depends on the specific project assigned to each team. All projects follow a standardized design process that consists of the following steps: problem definition, scope of work, customer discovery, ideation, conceptual design, and detailed engineering design.
courses.prerequisiteText: (ECSE 2920 or ECSE 2920H) and (ECSE 4230 or ELEE 3270 or ELEE 3270E) | Pre or

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Capstone Design II
courses.description: Engineering design experience, including completion of a design project under the supervision of a project director.
courses.course_objectives: By the end of this course, students will have had a meaningful computer systems engineering design experience. Students will gain enhanced critical thinking skills. Students will gain reinforcement in the logical steps of design. Students will enhance their understanding of engineering philosophies and procedures. Students will synthesize knowledge gained in math, physics, computer science, chemistry, engineering, humanities, and social sciences. Students will reinforce their communication skills through group project activities, mid-term and final presentations, including oral and written reports, and a poster presentation to classmates, faculty, and stakeholders. Students will develop their teamwork capabilities through the computer systems engineering design experience.
courses.topical_outline: This course is designed to provide students with a true engineering design experience. The activities in this course will include problem definition, concept development, detail design, and fabrication.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Undergraduate Research in Computer Systems Engineering
courses.description: Independent laboratory research and design for computer systems engineering students in CURO engineering program. Research is done under the direction of an engineering faculty member.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research I
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, and synthesize and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Directed Reading and/or Projects in Computer Systems Engineering
courses.description: Individual study, reading, and/or research projects under the direction of a faculty director.

courses.title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research II
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, and synthesize and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Special Topics: CURO Computer Systems Engineering
courses.description: Independent laboratory research and design for computer systems engineering students in CURO engineering program. Research is done under the direction of an engineering faculty member.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research III
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, and synthesize and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Undergraduate Research Thesis (or Final Project)
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, and synthesize and interpret data. Students will write or produce a thesis or other professional capstone product, such as a report or portfolio that describes their systematic and in-depth inquiry.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Principles of Cyber-Physical Systems
courses.description: Design principles, algorithms, protocols, and tools incyber-physical systems. The students will be introduced to theprinciples of cyber-physical systems, including sensing, computing, communication, and security, and case studies in realapplications. Specific topics covered will change from year to year.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Security in Cyber-Physical Systems
courses.description: An introduction to fundamental security and resilience issues in cyber-physical systems. Cyber-attacks may impact physical systems and physical attacks may bypass the traditional cyber defense. Theory and principles, attack detection and defense mechanisms, and selected case studies of cyber-physical security will be discussed in this course.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CSEE
courses.title: Virtual Reality and Augmented Reality User Interface Design
courses.description: Advanced topics in virtual reality and augmented reality, such as calibration and sensor fusion in motion-tracking system design, locomotion techniques for fixed physical spaces, haptics, robotic teleoperation, and collaborative experiences. Students will also study research methods to evaluate virtual and augmented reality systems and experiences.

courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.
