courses.title: Undergraduate Research Thesis (or Final Project)
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data. Students will write or produce a thesis or other professional capstone product, such as a report or portfolio that describes their systematic and in-depth inquiry.

courses.subject: CVLE(MCHE)(LAND)
courses.title: Sustainable Building Design
courses.description: Design features and technologies contained in sustainable (green) building design and the process to create a green building to include commercial and residential construction. Topics include energy and water, construction materials, site work, indoor environmental quality, and how design practices fit into the overall picture of developing a more sustainable society.
courses.prerequisiteText: Third-year student standing or higher for CVLE and MCHE and LAND majors | Graduate Prerequisite | Permission of department

courses.subject: CVLE(MCHE)(LAND)
courses.title: Sustainable Building Design
courses.description: Design features and technologies contained in sustainable (green) building design and the process to create a green building, including commercial and residential construction. Topics include energy and water, construction materials, site work, indoor environmental quality, and how design practices fit into the overall picture of developing a more sustainable society.
courses.prerequisiteText: Third-year student standing or higher for CVLE and MCHE and LAND majors | Graduate Prerequisite | Permission of department

courses.subject: CVLE(MCHE)
courses.title: Engineering Design of Residential Structures
courses.description: Design of foundations, structural members; heating and cooling systems; water supply and distribution; waste removal; electrical systems; and lighting.  Selection of thermal insulation, vapor barriers, windows and doors, and HVAC equipment determined by engineering principles.
courses.prerequisiteText: (ENGR 2140 or ENGR 2140E) and (ENGR 3160 or ENGR 3160E) | Pre or

courses.subject: CVLE(MCHE)
courses.title: Advanced Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: A mathematical treatment of fluid mechanics using tensors with emphasis on viscosity, momentum balance in laminar flow, equations of change, velocity distribution in laminar and turbulent flow, interphase transport, macroscopic balance, and polymeric liquids.  Analytical and numeric methods for solving fluid mechanic problems will be used.

courses.subject: CVLE(MCHE)
courses.title: Nonlinear Finite Element Analysis
courses.description: The formulations and numerical solution of nonlinear problems in structural, mechanical, and biological/biomedical engineering by finite element methods. Both geometric and material nonlinearities will be studied. Students are expected to learn how to use a finite element analysis tool and complete a practical engineering project.
courses.course_objectives: In this course students will learn non-linear finite element techniques via computer implementation. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to perform nonlinear FEA of real engineering problems. In this course students will learn non-linear finite element techniques via computer implementation. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to understand material and geometric nonlinearities. In this course students will learn non-linear finite element techniques via computer implementation. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to have knowledge of different solution methods for nonlinear equations. In this course students will learn non-linear finite element techniques via computer implementation. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to suggest appropriate analysis methods for different types of nonlinear problems. In this course students will learn non-linear finite element techniques via computer implementation. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to solve nonlinear problems using an engineering analysis tool. In this course students will learn non-linear finite element techniques via computer implementation. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to interpret the analysis results from Nonlinear FEA. In this course students will learn non-linear finite element techniques via computer implementation. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to understand errors and convergence problems.
courses.topical_outline: Overview of Nonlinear Problems Formulation of Nonlinear Equations and Methods Numerical Solution of Nonlinear Equations (e.g., Incremental, Newton, Secant, and Line Search Methods) Computer Implementation of Nonlinear Problems (Geometric Nonlinearities) Error Analysis and Convergence Computer Implementation of Nonlinear Problems (Material Nonlinearities such as Plasticity and Hyperplasticity) Transient Problems (e.g., Implicit and Explicit Methods, Newmark’s and Runga-Kutta’s Methods) Nonlinearities in Contact Mechanics Special Topics in Nonlinear FEA

courses.subject: CVLE(MCHE)
courses.title: Advanced Strength of Materials
courses.description: Provides students with the essential knowledge necessary to analyze structural/mechanical systems and components as well as the ability to interpret analysis results. Basic concepts and tools for analyzing engineering problems (elasticity equations, equilibrium, compatibility, etc.) will be emphasized as well as the mathematical formulations.
courses.course_objectives: This course extends the understanding that students acquired from their undergraduate Strength of Materials course and builds the capability to use fundamental skills and advanced knowledge that are the traits of a successful structural, mechanical, or geotechnical engineer. It is intended that the students will learn to extend and apply this basic knowledge to real-life two dimensional and three-dimensional structural/mechanical systems and components. Upon the completion of the course, students will be able to create conceptual models of structural/mechanical systems and design new solutions to meet technical challenges. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to understand the fundamentals of 2-d and 3-d stress-strain analyses with linear materials. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to understand the classical theory of elasticity (e.g., elasticity equations, equilibrium, and compatibility) and transition to advanced computational mechanics courses (e.g., continuum mechanics and nonlinear analysis). At the completion of this course, the student should be able to develop a fundamental background to pursue further study in structural, mechanical, and geotechnical engineering. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to develop an ability to apply classical and contemporary analysis methods to discrete and continuous structural systems and mechanical components. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to understand how to apply fundamental theories and engineering solutions to particular situations. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to create conceptual models of systems and design new solutions to meet technical challenges. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to understand professional and ethical responsibilities. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to effectively communicate solutions to problems through technical writing and oral presentations.
courses.topical_outline:
Fundamental Components of Analyzing Continuous Systems Basic Operations Required to Build the Continuum Mechanics Framework Vectors, Tensors, Differential Geometry, Coordinate Transformations, Transformation of Stress and Strain, Index
Notation, Divergence, PDEs Equilibrium and Stress Displacement, Strain, and Compatibility Linear Constitutive Relations From 1-D spring systems to 2-D Elasticity (torsion, beams, truss and frame elements, solutions, and applications in plane stress and plane strain elements) Classical Theories (Bernoulli-Euler beam theory and Kirchoff plate theory) Variational Methods (equilibrium, virtual work, and other energy formulations) Case study in failure analysis emphasizing implications Special Topics (e.g., Finite Element Method, Fourier Analysis)

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Surveying and Geomatics
courses.description: Survey errors and error propagation, survey computations and adjustments, distance measurements, leveling, directions and angles, traverse computations, earthwork analysis, mass diagrams, map projection and coordinate systems, and theories of circular and parabolic curves for geometric design of highways; advanced geospatial technologies, including GPS, GIS, and remote sensing.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Numerical Methods for Engineers
courses.description: Numerical solution of simple mathematical models frequently encountered by engineers. Roots of nonlinear equations, solutions of system of linear equations, regression and interpolation, numerical differentiation and integration, and solution of ordinary differential equations.
courses.course_objectives: Students will identify sources of error in numerical algorithms and solutions. Students will determine roots of nonlinear equations. Students will solve a system of linear equations. Students will apply numerical equivalents of differentiation and integration. Students will solve ordinary differential equations numerically. Students will develop computer programs to implement basic numerical algorithms using user-defined and built-in functions.
courses.topical_outline: - Basics of numerical analysis-mathematical models, accuracy and error analysis - Roots of nonlinear equations - System of linear equations - Curve fitting (regression and interpolation) - Numerical differentiation and integration - Numerical solutions to ordinary differential equations - Computer programs to implement basic numerical algorithms
courses.prerequisiteText: (ENGR 1140 or ENGR 1140H) and MATH 2500 | Pre or

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Numerical Methods for Engineers
courses.description: Numerical solution of simple mathematical models frequently encountered by engineers. Roots of nonlinear equations, solutions of system of linear equations, regression and interpolation, numerical differentiation and integration, and solution of ordinary differential equations.
courses.course_objectives: The typical sources and manufacturing procedures. Students will determine roots of nonlinear equations. Students will solve a system of linear equations. Students will apply numerical equivalents of differentiation and integration. Students will solve ordinary differential equations numerically. Students will develop computer programs to implement basic numerical algorithms using user-defined and built-in functions.
courses.topical_outline: Basics of numerical analysis-mathematical models, accuracy and error analysis Roots of nonlinear equations System of linear equations Curve fitting (regression and interpolation) Numerical differentiation and integration Numerical solutions to ordinary differential equations Computer programs to implement basic numerical algorithms
courses.prerequisiteText: (ENGR 1140 or ENGR 1140H) and MATH 2500 | Pre or

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Civil Engineering Materials
courses.description: Physical and mechanical properties of materials used in construction: aggregates, masonry, cementitious materials, bituminous materials, soils, metals, wood and composites. Testing for properties of cement concrete and metals; includes specimen preparation, standardized testing procedures, equipment handling and safety. Procedures and tools for data collection, analysis, interpretation, and presentation.
courses.course_objectives: Students will understand the typical sources and manufacturing procedures. Students will understand the physical and mechanical properties of manufacturing procedures. Students will understand standardized laboratory testing procedures for tensile, compressive, and shear strengths. Students will understand how to operate equipment involved in standardized tests while being aware of its capabilities and limitations. Students will understand how to prepare suitable specimens for testing. Students will understand how to write technical laboratory reports.
courses.topical_outline: • Construction Materials – history and economics • Desirable properties – mechanical and non-mechanical • Aggregates • Masonry • Cement and cement concrete • Asphalt and asphalt concrete • Soils • Metals – iron, steel, aluminum • Wood • Composites • Emerging materials • Laboratory procedures, rules and safety • Technical report writing and relevant tools of statistical analysis • Specimen preparation, temperature and aging • Equipment handling, capabilities and limitations • Tension, compression and shear tests

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Introduction to Soil Mechanics
courses.description: Topics including soil shear strength, shallow foundations, slope stability, lateral earth pressure and soil compaction, design of shallow foundations for agricultural structure, retaining walls, and engineered slopes will be discussed.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Hydraulics of Closed Conduit Flow
courses.description: Science and design methods associated with managing water with closed conduits on a field scale. Topics will include the management of stormwater, sewerage collection, and potable water distribution systems.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Civil Engineering Laboratory – Soils
courses.description: Soil properties of interest to engineers. Grain size analysis, determining Atterberg limits, measuring specific gravity, permeability, compaction, consolidation, and shear using standardized tests. Procedures and tools for data collection, analysis, interpretation, and presentation.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to experimentally determine specific gravity, Atterberg limits, permeability, compaction, consolidation, and shear properties of soils using standardized testing procedures. Students will be able to classify soils visually and perform grain size Analysis. Students will be able to present results in a technical format is expected.
courses.topical_outline: Laboratory procedures, rules and safety Technical report writing and relevant tools of statistical analysis Standards Specific gravity, unit weight, relative density Grain size analysis Atterberg limits Compaction Permeability Consolidation Shear

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Civil Engineering Laboratory – Hydraulics
courses.description: Measurement of velocity distributions, flow rates, Reynolds number, drag, and friction factors. Studies on flow in pipes, open channel flow, flow over weirs, Bernoulli's theorem, and momentum transfer. Procedures and tools for data collection, analysis, interpretation, and presentation.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Civil Engineering Laboratory – Structural
courses.description: Behavior of simple structural elements and systems. Focus on comparison with theoretical results, acceptable discrepancies between experimental and theoretical results, and viable explanations of these discrepancies. Procedures and tools for data collection, analysis, interpretation, and presentation.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Structural Design
courses.description: Deals with the relationships between loads and deflections which occur in structures as well as designing with wood and concrete.
courses.course_objectives: Students will determine the vertical and horizontal deflections in beams and rigid frames using governing equations and energy techniques. Students will draw shear and moment diagrams for continuous beams and rigid frames. Students will determine the internal forces and moments for indeterminate beams and rigid frames using equilibrium methods. Students will calculate normal and shear stresses caused by various types of external forces. Students will design wood beams, columns, beam columns, wood nailed and bolted joints according to NDS Design Criteria. Students will design plywood members according to APA Design Criteria. Students will design concrete beams, spread footings, wall footings and columns according to ACI Design Criteria. Students will design masonry block walls using ACI Design Criteria.
courses.topical_outline: 1. Determinate Structural Systems 2. Structural Design Fundamentals 3. Computation of Deflections 4. Indeterminate Structural Systems 5. Light Timber Design 6. Plywood Design 7. Reinforced Concrete Design 8. Other Topics

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Civil Engineering Project Management
courses.description: Construction contracts, project planning and scheduling, resource management, cost estimation, budgeting, project organization, project control, use of specialized software, labor, health, and safety.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Civil Engineering Project Management
courses.description: Construction contracts, project planning and scheduling, resource management, cost estimation, budgeting, project organization, project control, use of specialized software, labor, health, and safety.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Civil Engineering Cooperative Work Experience
courses.description: The UGA Engineering Cooperative Education Program (co-op program) will provide a structured means for engineering students to gain valuable and relevant experiential learning through a work experience while growing as professionals in their chosen fields.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Design of Water Distribution and Sewer Systems
courses.description: Science and design methods associated with the managing water with the closed conduits on a field scale. Topics will include the design of storm water, sewerage collection, and potable water distribution systems.
courses.course_objectives: Students will have the ability to identify, formulate, and solve complex engineering problems by applying principles of effective design. Students will have the ability to apply engineering design to produce solutions that meet specified needs. Students will have the ability to communicate effectively with a range of audiences. Students will have the ability to recognize ethical and professional responsibilities in engineering situations. Students will have the ability to function effectively on a team whose members together provide leadership. Students will have the ability to develop and conduct appropriate experimentation, analyze and interpret results. Students will have the ability to acquire and apply new knowledge as needed, using appropriate learning techniques.
courses.topical_outline: Review of fluid mechanics principles in close conduit flow Design of Potable Water Distribution Systems Pumps and Tanks Fillings Design of Sewer Water Systems Trench design and load on buried pipes Design of Stormwater Water Systems Roadway Drainage System Design
courses.prerequisiteText: (ENGR 3160 or ENGR 3160E) and ENVE 4435/6435 | Graduate Prerequisite | (ENGR 3160 or ENGR 3160E) and ENVE 4435/6435

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Transportation Engineering
courses.description: This course introduces fundamentals and principles of transportation engineering, emphasizing traffic analysis. Principal topics covered in this course include significance of transportation to the social and economic underpinnings of society, road vehicle performance, geometric design of highways, traffic flow theory, capacity and level of service analysis, and travel demand modeling.
courses.course_objectives: Students will gain a broad understanding of the transportation engineering field. Students will understand the performance of road vehicles and its implications in design and operations. Students will evaluate vertical and horizontal curves. Students will apply queuing theory for traffic analysis. Students will evaluate the capacity and level of services of signalized intersections. Students will understand the concept and principles of travel-demand modeling.
courses.topical_outline: • Context and background • Vehicle performance and sight distance • Geometric design of highways • Traffic stream parameters • Traffic flow models • Queuing theory and applications • Highway capacity and levels of service • Traffic control and analysis • Introduction to travel demand modeling

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Highway Design and Traffic Safety
courses.description: The many challenges facing engineers for designing safe and cost-effective highways. Focus is on highway design principles and practices, particularly as they relate to safety.  Additionally, statistical and analytical methods commonly used in highway safety analysis will be introduced, including analysis of accident statistics, identification and diagnosis of hazardous locations, development and evaluation of alternative improvements.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Introduction to Intelligent Transportation Systems
courses.description: Course presents the fundamental concepts of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) to students with interest in engineering, transportation systems, communication systems, and vehicle technologies. ITS refers to information and communication technologies, as applied to transportation infrastructure and vehicles, that improve transportation safety, mobility, environment, and travel reliability.
courses.course_objectives: At the completion of this course, the student should be able to understand fundamentals of Intelligent Transportation Systems. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to understand industry applications of Intelligent Transportation Systems. At the completion of this course, the student should gain experience in conducting a comprehensive independent project related to Intelligent Transportation Systems.
courses.topical_outline: 1. Fundamentals of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) 2. Data in ITS 3. Vehicle Control and Safety Systems 4. Traffic Signal Control Systems 5. Traveler Information Systems 6. Freeway Management Systems 7. Incident Management Systems 8. Traffic Management Centers

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Transportation and Infrastructure Networks
courses.description: Course will briefly review basic topics in network formulation and then will proceed to commonly used network models with applications to planning and operations of passenger and freight transportation and other related infrastructure systems.
courses.course_objectives: At the completion of this course, the student should be able to formulate relevant engineering problems into basic networks and use certain techniques to solve the problem. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to practice models and algorithms with state-of-art computer programs and commercial solvers. At the completion of this course, the student should have a balanced view on theoretical modeling and engineering applications.
courses.topical_outline: 1. Basic networks 2. Passenger traffic models 3. Freight traffic models 4. Infrastructure coverage models 5. Selected solution algorithms

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Advanced Structural Analysis
courses.description: Provides students with an in-depth understanding of matrix and computer-oriented analysis methods for civil engineering structures. Matrix methods are at the core of structural analysis software extensively used in the industry. Explores matrix formulation of flexibility and stiffness methods. Three-dimensional truss, beam, and frame members will be studied using a commercially available structural analysis program.
courses.prerequisiteText: CVLE 3610 | Graduate Prerequisite | Permission of department

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Design of Bridges
courses.description: Types of bridges, superstructure and substructure components, design considerations, loads, reinforced concrete and steel bridges, seismic design.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Structural Dynamics
courses.description: Fundamentals of dynamic response, single and multi degrees-of-freedom systems, free and forced vibration, response spectra, numerical solution techniques.
courses.prerequisiteText: (ENGR 2130 or ENGR 2130E) and (CVLE 2710 or CVLE 2710E) and CVLE 3610

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Advanced Soil Mechanics
courses.description: Elasticity theory applied to soil as a continuum, plastic behavior, failure criteria, steady and transient flow of water, critical state concepts, computational geomechanics.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Groundwater Engineering
courses.description: Physical properties, governing equations and their solutions, flow nets, groundwater hydrology, groundwater contamination, well hydraulics.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Design with Geosynthetics
courses.description: Geotextiles, geogrids, geonets and geomembranes; physical and mechanical properties; applications involving reinforcement, filtration, drainage and containment; analysis and design.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Geotechnical Structures – Foundations and Retaining Walls
courses.description: Loads, soil strength, bearing capacity, settlement, design of shallow foundations and design of deep foundations; spread footings, slab-on-grade, mat foundation and piles; earth retaining structures – lateral pressures, stability and design; methods of construction; introduction to ground modification.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Geotechnical Earthquake Engineering
courses.description: Earthquake hazard analysis, wave propagation and ground motion, vibrations, dynamic properties of soils, liquefaction, site effects, seismic design; buried structures.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Pavement Design
courses.description: A study of the methods used to determine thickness and composition of the components of both flexible and rigid highwaypavements. Classwork will also include paving materials,Mechanistic-Empirical (ME) pavement design concept, trafficstress and strain, and pavement management system. Standardtechniques and computer software will be utilized in this class.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Design of Masonry Structures
courses.description: Properties of masonry materials; design requirements, philosophies and applicable standards; design for axial, flexural and shear forces; design of simple beams, columns and walls; connectors and construction considerations.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Design of Reinforced Concrete Structures
courses.description: Concrete and reinforced concrete; strength and design of reinforced concrete components; design requirements, philosophies and applicable standards; design for axial, flexural and shear forces; design of simple beams, columns, slabs, retaining walls and footings.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Advanced Design of Reinforced Concrete Structures
courses.description: Design of slender columns, two-way slabs, slab-on-grade and walls; biaxial bending, torsion and instabilities; building systems; seismic design requirements; introduction to prestressing.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Design of Steel Structures
courses.description: Course covers the behavior and applications of structural steel members and simple connections under various loads and introduces design techniques of structural steel framing systems.
courses.course_objectives: Upon successful completion of this course, the students will be able to apply LRFD design method, including the calculation of load effects and design resistance terms. Upon successful completion of this course, the students will be able to perform structural analysis, and interpret and communicate its results effectively for optimal structural steel design. Upon successful completion of this course, the students will be able to explain the mechanical characteristics of steel material, including yield strength, ultimate strength, and both elastic and inelastic deformation. Upon successful completion of this course, the students will be able to calculate the strength of a tension member based on its limit states, including gross yielding, fracture of an effective net section, and block shear. Upon successful completion of this course, the students will be able to develop and evaluate the design of a tension member according to AISC Specification for Structural Steel Buildings. Upon successful completion of this course, the students will be able to explain the relevant factors influencing the AISC column curve, such as its correlation with Euler Buckling, incorporation of end restraint through effective length, initial imperfections, and partial yielding. Upon successful completion of this course, the students will be able to calculate the strength of a compression member based on its limit states, including gross yielding, elastic and inelastic flexural buckling, torsional buckling, flexural-torsional buckling, and local buckling. Upon successful completion of this course, the students will be able to develop and evaluate the design of a compression member according to AISC Specification for Structural Steel Buildings. Upon successful completion of this course, the students will be able to explain the relevant factors influencing the AISC beam curve, including its relationship to lateral-torsional buckling, incorporation of brace points, moment gradient, and partial yielding. Upon successful completion of this course, the students will be able to calculate the strength of a flexural member based on its limit states, including yielding, elastic and inelastic lateral-torsional buckling, local buckling, and shear yielding. Upon successful completion of this course, the students will be able to develop and evaluate the design of a flexural member according to AISC Specification for Structural Steel Buildings. Upon successful completion of this course, the students will be able to explain the relevant factors influencing the AISC interaction equations including its relationship to structural stability and second-order effects. Upon successful completion of this course, the students will be able to develop and evaluate the design of a member subjected to the combined axial and bending effects according to AISC Specification for Structural Steel Buildings. Upon successful completion of this course, the students will be able to describe various steel connection types and the transfer of loads from the members to the connections. Upon successful completion of this course, the students will be able to develop and evaluate the design of a simple bolted and welded connections according to AISC Specification for Structural Steel Buildings. Upon successful completion of this course, the students will be able to collaborate effectively in a team to design a steel framing system by integrating effective communication and problem-solving skills.
courses.topical_outline: 1. Design of steel tension members 2. Design of steel beams 3. Design of steel columns 4. Design of steel beam-columns 5. Design of simple bolted and welded connections

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Advanced Design of Steel Structures
courses.description: Design of beam-columns, continuous beams, plate girders, composite steel-concrete members; design of braced, unbraced and rigid frames; eccentric connections, plastic behavior and torsional effects (lateral-torsional buckling); design requirements for steel hollow structural sections (HSS).

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Design of Cold-Formed Steel Structures
courses.description: Materials and methods of cold-forming; behavior of open thin-walled members, closed tubular members and sheets; ANSI/AISI design standards; design of compression and flexural elements; connections; composite design.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Infrastructure Condition Assessment
courses.description: The deterioration, monitoring, assessment, and management of infrastructure systems. Course presents different types of deterioration mechanisms, applications of nondestructive and sensing technologies, and use of innovative technologies to optimize infrastructure condition assessment and management.
courses.course_objectives: Upon successful completion of this course, the student will be able to identify the elements of civil infrastructure systems. Upon successful completion of this course, the student will be able to understand methods to manage infrastructure assets (roads, bridges). Upon successful completion of this course, the student will be able to identify the different deterioration aspects of civil infrastructure. Upon successful completion of this course, the student will be able to identify information needed and techniques used for forensic engineering. Upon successful completion of this course, the student will be able to identify and use the most appropriate nondestructive techniques to evaluate constructed facilities. Upon successful completion of this course, the student will be able to define prioritization and optimization techniques used in infrastructure management.
courses.topical_outline: An Introduction to Civil Infrastructure Current State of the U.S. Infrastructure Civil Infrastructure Groups Terminologies of Constructed Facilities Civil Engineering Materials: Concrete, Hot-Mix Asphalt, Wood, Plastics, Composites, and Steel Deterioration of Civil Constructed Facilities (Concrete) Deterioration of Civil Constructed Facilities (Asphalt) Field Inspection and Forensic Engineering Destructive vs. Nondestructive Testing; Simple NDE Methods Stress Wave Propagation: Methods and Applications Acoustic Emission Ultrasonic Pulse Velocity Impact Echo Ground Penetrating Radar Ground Penetrating Radar Applications Infrared Thermography and Other Technologies Infrastructure Monitoring: Instrumentation, Fiber Optics Global Monitoring of Civil Structures Field Studies Preventive Measures and New Civil Engineering Materials Infrastructure Management Systems Improving Infrastructure: What Needs to Be Done Class Presentation
courses.prerequisiteText: CVLE 3310 | Graduate Prerequisite | Permission of department

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Project Estimating and Planning
courses.description: This course builds upon the concepts learned in Civil Engineering Project Management. This course provides a detailed study of the processes and procedures used in the cost estimation as well as in the planning process for typical civil engineering projects, including, for example, transportation, site preparation, and structures projects.
courses.prerequisiteText: CVLE 3730 or CVLE 3730E or permission of department

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Life Cycle Analysis
courses.description: An in-depth look at life cycle analysis (LCA), the existing models and analytical methodologies, and their applications.   This course provides an introduction on how to conduct an LCA for civil engineering projects, including, for example, transportation, site preparation, and structures projects.
courses.prerequisiteText: [(ENVE 3410 or ENVE 4435/6435) and (BIOL 1104 or BIOL 1104H or FANR(MARS) 1100 or ECOL 1000 or ECOL 1000E or ECOL 1000H)] or permission of deparment

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Building Information Modeling (BIM)
courses.description: The adoption of Building Information Modeling (BIM) during the design of a commercial building project.  This course will also cover how BIM is used to help prepare or feed into key project items, such as cost estimates, architectural renderings, interference checking, and modeling of energy consumption and daylighting.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Commercial Building Systems
courses.description: An overview of the complete design of a commercial (as opposed to a residential) building project. In addition to the structural design, this includes the various systems that are required for commercial buildings, such as HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems.
courses.prerequisiteText: CVLE 3610 or permission of department | Pre or

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Urban Infrastructure Systems
courses.description: An overview of the various systems that comprise the infrastructure of urban areas.  Topics covered include transportation systems (public and private), water supply and sanitary disposal, stormwater management, buildings, communications, and urban planning.
courses.prerequisiteText: ENGR 3410 or ENVE 3410 or ENVE 4435/6435 or permission of department

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Advanced Computer-Aided Design Civil 3D
courses.description: An advanced civil engineering graphics course using computer-aided design Civil 3D software that explores techniques to enable designers in organizing project data and survey points, creating and analyzing surfaces, modeling road corridors, performing grading and volume calculations, and laying out pipe networks.
courses.prerequisiteText: CVLE 2210 or ENVE 2920 or AENG(BIOE) 2920 | Graduate Prerequisite | Permission of department

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Integrated Engineering Design and Innovation
courses.description: The objective of this course is to equip students with the knowledge and skills to effectively engage in the multidiscipline engineering design of construction projects. Students will utilize systems thinking to conceptualize engineering design and explore the principles of engineering design planning, management, delivery, and risk.
courses.course_objectives: At the completion of this course, the student should be able to analyze the engineering design process from project identification to schematic design. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to explore projects as complex socio-technical systems. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to create innovative solutions to design challenges by applying creative thinking, interdisciplinary collaboration, emerging technologies, and systems thinking methodologies. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to develop budgets, schedules and delivery plans for engineering design work. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to understand stakeholder identification and effective relationship management. At the completion of this course, the student should develop skills in managing and administering engineering design contracts.
courses.topical_outline: 1. Systems thinking and complexity 2. Stakeholder management 3. Teamwork and communication 4. Project engineering design develop from project selection through schematic design 5. Interdisciplinary collaboration and innovation 6. Work planning and the integration of breakdown structures (work, resource and cost) 7. Design delivery: deliverables, budget and schedule management 8. Risk management 9. Engineering quality management 10. Engineering contract administration and management 11. Ethics and the implications of technology
courses.prerequisiteText: Third year standing in AENG and CVLE and ENVE and MCHE

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Design of Wood Structures
courses.description: Properties of structural lumber and glued laminated timber; design requirements, philosophies and applicable standards; design for axial, flexural and shear forces; design of simple beams, columns, panels; connection requirements and design.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Special Topics in Civil Engineering
courses.description: Special topics in civil engineering design, analysis, or synthesis.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Capstone Design I
courses.description: Supervised engineering design experience, FE review, career counseling.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Capstone Design II
courses.description: Supervised engineering design experience. Lecture component will focus on professional and ethical responsibilities, awareness of contemporary engineering issues, importance of lifelong learning, and various career paths.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Undergraduate Research in Civil Engineering
courses.description: Independent laboratory research and design for civil engineering students in CURO engineering program. Research is done under the direction of an engineering faculty member.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research I
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, and synthesize and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Directed Reading and/or Projects in Civil Engineering
courses.description: Independent laboratory research and design for civil engineering students in CURO engineering program. Research is done under the direction of an engineering faculty member.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research II
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, and synthesize and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Project Management Principles
courses.description: The objective of this course is to prepare students to successfully plan, develop, lead, manage, and deliver projects. Course emphasizes leadership and management principles and practices to successfully complete a project. Course covers project planning, stakeholder mapping and engagement, work breakdown structure, cost management, time management, and risk.
courses.course_objectives: Students at the completion of this course will be able to define project management terms and fundamental concepts. Students at the completion of this course will be able to define the project and create a project charter. Students at the completion of this course will be able to develop a project management plan (PMP). Students at the completion of this course will be able to select a project development approach. Students at the completion of this course will be able to identify the necessary project stakeholders with the appropriate communication and engagement strategies based on stakeholder's needs. Students at the completion of this course will be able to define detailed scope using a work breakdown structure (WBS). Students at the completion of this course will be able to manage project scope. Students at the completion of this course will be able to establish a reasonable project schedule and employ time management processes to keep your project on track. Students at the completion of this course will be able to manage costs throughout the project’s duration. Students at the completion of this course will be able to plan for and assess project risk. Students at the completion of this course will be able to prepare for project change. Students at the completion of this course will be able to manage and communicate project performance results.
courses.topical_outline: Overview of project management (terms, concepts, and definitions) Project charter, project management plan (PMP) and approaches Stakeholder mapping and engagement Work breakdown structure and scope management Project scheduling and time management Project costs Project risk Performance and lessons learned

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Construction Management and Technologies
courses.description: Provides an advanced understanding of projects as complex systems and their evolution from bidding to commissioning and closeout. The content will focus on project delivery methods, leadership, financial management, and the implementation of assurance systems (e.g., project control, quality, and risk management). Additional topics include AI and robotics in construction.
courses.course_objectives: Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to formulate the construction process as a complex system and understand the implications of the drivers of complexity (feedback, emergent behavior, etc.) on business delivery. Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to develop a risk management framework for both tangible and intangible risks and assess risk from the enterprise to the project level. Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to compare contract delivery methods and determine appropriate contracting strategies. Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to integrate the concepts of statistical control, design structure matrices, and meta-network analysis into the decision-making process. Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to apply and adapt principles of the leadership models and tools presented in class to various construction sector settings. Understand the principles of construction financial management and identify the differences between financial management in the construction sector and standard financial management. Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to understand the legal complexities and nuances of construction contracts and their administration. Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to understand the implications of AI and Robotics in construction.
courses.topical_outline: Introduction, Industry Context, and Overview of Projects and Construction Management Projects as Complex Socio-Technical Systems The Project Development Cycle Overview Progressive Elaboration (stage by stage development) Project Delivery Models (aka contracting strategies) Construction Contract Management Risk Management Tools (qualitative, quantitative) Project Control and Reporting Project Performance Project Commissioning and Closeout AI opportunities in construction Technology (3D Printing, Robotics and autonomous equipment) Program Management and the PMO Strategy and Project Portfolio Management Leadership Skills in an AI Enabled Construction Industry Ethics in an AI Enabled Construction Industry

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: GIS in Civil Engineering Applications
courses.description: Course provides a comprehensive understanding of applied Geographic Information Systems (GIS). Students will develop skills in data acquisition, spatial analysis, and effective representation. This will include a theoretical grasp on basic data types and structures, and analysis and digital workflows. Furthermore, students will solve real-world problems through GIS.
courses.course_objectives: At the end of this course, students will understand the fundamental principles of GIS. At the end of this course, students will acquire, create, and synthesize spatial and tabular data for display and analysis. At the end of this course, students will conduct environmental assessments and suitability analysis for civil engineering projects. At the end of this course, students will integrate social data and community-based input in both feasibility and design phases. At the end of this course, students will develop a scenario-based planning approach for infrastructure projects. At the end of this course, students will deploy interoperability and digital workflows between GIS and other design software. At the end of this course, students will craft communication and user-facing applications and reports that effectively communicate analysis and design efforts.
courses.topical_outline: Introduction to data and spatial data Introduction to GIS applications: commonalities and differences Data acquisition and preparation Environmental assessment Transportation and land use assessment Basic remote sensing Small-scale design Systemic regional scale Social data and community engagement GIS for project management

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: A.I. and Informatics in Civil Engineering
courses.description: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and informatics have revolutionized the field of civil engineering. This course is designed to equip students with a comprehensive understanding of how AI, data science, and informatics are transforming the civil engineering landscape. The course explores the cutting-edge applications of AI in the context of civil engineering.
courses.course_objectives: Upon completion of this course, students will gain a solid foundation in AI principles, including machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing, with a specific focus on their applications within civil engineering. Upon completion of this course, students will learn to analyze large datasets to extract meaningful insights that inform decision-making in civil engineering projects. Upon completion of this course, students will explore how AI and informatics can be used to optimize the design, maintenance, and management of civil infrastructure, such as roads, bridges, and tunnels. Upon completion of this course, students will analyze real-world case studies and projects where AI and informatics have played a pivotal role in revolutionizing civil engineering practices.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Solid Mechanics
courses.description: A foundational course in engineering and applied science that focuses on the behavior of solid materials under various loading conditions. This course provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the principles governing the deformation and stress distribution in materials and structures, preparing them for solving real-world civil engineering problems.
courses.course_objectives:
By the end of this course, students will develop a strong conceptual understanding of stress, strain, and the mechanical properties of materials under various loading conditions. By the end of this course, students will build a solid background of the basic principles of solid mechanics including:
- Linear and angular momentum principles
- Deformation
- Stress-strain relations
- Work and energy By the end of this course, students will analyze the behavior of materials subjected to tension, compression, torsion, bending, and combined loads using solid mechanics principles. By the end of this course, students will apply mathematical methods and scientific principles to solve problems related to the mechanical behavior of engineering materials and systems. By the end of this course, students will design basic structural elements ensuring they meet required specifications and understand the factors influencing design decisions. By the end of this course, students will employ modern engineering tools and software for the analysis of stress, strain, and deformation in solid materials and structures, especially for the analysis and design for pavement engineering and structure engineering.
courses.topical_outline:
Introduction to solid mechanics: 
- History 
- Basic concepts and definitions 
- Types of loads and support conditions 
- Concepts of stress, strain and elasticity 
- Beams, columns, plates, shells 
- Elasticity, general theory 
- Continuum plasticity theory 
- Stress concentrations and fracture 
- Viscoelasticity 
- Computational mechanics Basic principles: 
- Stress and equations of motion: stress tensor, Hooke's law and material properties, stress transformations, principal stresses, stress transformation in a plane, Mohr's circle
- Strain, strain-displacement relations, compatibility: small strain tensor, strain tensor transformation, principle strains, Mohr's circle for strain transformation, strain compatibility, small strain analysis
- Work and energy: principle of virtual work, first law of thermodynamics, strain energy and potential energy, Castigliano's theorem
- Stress-strain relations: linear elastic isotropic solid, relation of material properties, anisotropy
- Thermodynamic considerations: second law, isothermal versus isentropic response, finite elastic deformations
- Nonlinear response: plasticity and creep, elastic-plastic model, co-rotational stress rate, linear viscoelasticity Advanced topics: 
- Composite materials
- Nonlinear structural analysis
- Basics of Finite Element Analysis (FEA)
- Application of FEA in structural analysis
- Advanced structural design

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Forensics of Civil Engineering Materials
courses.description: Provide the scientific principles and methodologies used in the forensic analysis of materials commonly employed in civil engineering including concrete, asphalt, and soils. By understanding how these materials fail or exhibit anomalies, students will gain the expertise needed to assess structural issues, ensure public safety, and make decisions regarding rehabilitation.
courses.course_objectives: Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to classify and characterize construction materials, such as concrete, asphalt, and soils. Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to apply the principles and techniques for investigating material failures, such as cracks, corrosion, fatigue, and deterioration, to determine the causes and propose remedial actions. Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to assess the condition of civil engineering structures and materials. Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to utilize nondestructive testing methods to assess the integrity and condition of structures without causing damage.
courses.topical_outline: Material Properties and Testing Failure Mechanisms and Modes Field Investigations and Data Collection Laboratory Techniques and Analysis Non-Destructive Testing in Civil Engineering Case Studies in Civil Engineering Material Forensics

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Computational Modeling Studio
courses.description: Fundamental finite element theory for the solution of engineering problems. Geometrical modeling techniques, element selection, and test accuracy. Emphasis on problems in structural mechanics and elasticity.
courses.course_objectives: Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to understand the basic theory of the finite element analysis. Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to develop a simple finite element computer code, interpret results, and perform verification. Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to use professional finite element analysis program to create suitable finite element models of simple structures; apply appropriate loads and constraints; and perform finite element analysis and interpret the results. Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to use professional finite element analysis programs to perform advanced analysis techniques for simulating complex structures and real-world scenarios.

courses.title: Structural Engineering Design Studio
courses.description: Structural engineering through hands-on design projects. This studio course explores advanced concepts in structural design, material selection, and innovative design solutions. courses.course_objectives: Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to apply advanced structural design techniques to solve complex engineering problems. Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to collaborate in multidisciplinary teams to address real-world structural engineering challenges and integrate diverse perspectives into design solutions.

Real-world bridge engineering projects will be used to develop the skills to succeed in the modern workplace.
courses.course_objectives: At the end of this course, students will understand the various steps involved in designing a reinforced concrete, prestressed concrete, or steel bridge, including choice of bridge type, kinds and effects of loads, specialized design requirements for superstructure and substructure, and seismic design considerations. At the end of this course, students will be able to solve real-world problems and develop the skills they need to succeed in the modern bridge engineering workplace.

courses.description: The objective of this course is to equipt students with the knowledge and skills to analyze, design, and implement effective transportation systems. Students will explore the principles of transportation planning, including land use, environmental impact, multimodal systems, and policy frameworks, with a focus on creating sustainable and equitable transportation solutions.
