courses.title: Transportation Safety
courses.description: Exploration of transportation safety through data-driven analysis, human factors, and emerging vehicle technologies. Students will apply statistical models, surrogate safety measures, and traffic simulation to assess crash risks. The course also examines ADAS, V2X communication, and proactive strategies to enhance safety in a multimodal environment for all road users.
courses.course_objectives: Students will analyze and model transportation safety data to assess crash risks using statistical, machine learning, and simulation techniques. Students will evaluate human factors and emerging vehicle technologies (ADAS, V2X, surrogate safety measures) in improving roadway safety. Students will develop proactive safety strategies to mitigate risks for drivers, vulnerable road users, and connected vehicle environments.
courses.topical_outline: 1.	Safety Data & Emerging Trends 2.	Human Factors in Transportation Safety 3.	Crash frequency and severity modeling 4.	Surrogate Safety Measures & Proactive Risk Mitigation 5.	Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) & Safety 6.	Connected Vehicle Safety (V2V & V2X) 7.	Vulnerable Road User Safety 8.	Traffic simulation for safety analysis

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Mechanics of Jets and Plumes
courses.description: Advanced fluid dynamic principles applied to engineered flows.Topics covered include mixing, design of jets and plumes, effectsof ambient flows, stratification, and turbulence on jets andplumes. Advanced treatment of instability and turbulence theoryas they pertain to engineered flows. Extensive numerical projectfocused on applying theory to real-world implementation.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Transport and Mixing in Natural Flows
courses.description: Advanced fluid dynamic principles applied to natural flows.Topics covered include Fickian diffusion, scalar and momentumtransport equations, Reynolds-averaging, turbulent stresses,turbulent mixing of passive scalars, mixing in environmentalflows, including rivers, lakes, estuaries, and open coasts.Introduction of both conservative and non-conservative mixingwith application to real-world problems. Extensive treatment oftheory and implementation through a numerical design project.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Traffic Flow Theory
courses.description: A comprehensive understanding of highway traffic flow, encompassing definitions, taxonomy, and various models. It will delve into both microscopic (vehicular) and macroscopic (traffic stream) perspectives, presenting a range of traffic flow models that enable the prediction of future traffic states based on current conditions.
courses.course_objectives: At the completion of this course, the student should be able to gain a solid grasp of the fundamental concepts and methodologies underlying traffic flow dynamics. At the completion of this course, the student should possess the capability to employ basic programming languages, such as MATLAB, for modeling traffic dynamics. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to integrate their acquired knowledge into traffic operations and management practices.
courses.topical_outline: 1. Traffic flow characteristics 2. Capacity and level of service 3. Queueing theory 4. Intersection control 5. Shockwave theory 6. Cellular automata 7. Car-following model 8. Lane-changing model 9. Introduction to traffic simulation 10. Traffic sensing technologies 11. Single vehicle dynamics 12. Connected and automated vehicles

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Transportation Simulation
courses.description: Course provides graduate students with a foundation to implement simulations in traffic analysis for various roadway facilities and help students prepare for their professional and academic careers. Introduces traffic analysis packages that are widely used in industry and academia. It is assumed that students enrolling in this course have a background in transportation engineering and/or civil engineering.
courses.course_objectives: At the completion of this course, the student should be able to implement Traffic Simulations: Set up and run simulations for various traffic scenarios. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to interpret Simulation Data: Learn to critically analyze and interpret data from traffic simulations. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to optimize Traffic Operations: Apply simulation techniques to optimize traffic flow and signal timings. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to run Car Learning to Act (CARLA) for autonomous driving simulation.
courses.topical_outline:
Transportation Simulation Introduction Potential software to be covered in class: 
Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) VISSIM Waymax FHWA: Interactive Highway Safety Design Model (IHSDM) Synchro Studio Highway Capacity Software (HCS) CARLA

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Nonlinear Finite Element Analysis
courses.description: The formulations and numerical solution of nonlinear problems in structural, mechanical, and biological/biomedical engineering by finite element methods. Both geometric and material nonlinearities will be studied. Students are expected to learn how to use a finite element analysis tool and complete a practical engineering project.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Earthquake Engineering and Dynamics of Structures
courses.description: The fundamental concepts, principles, and application of earthquake engineering in seismic analysis and design of structures using simulation of ground motion models. The concept of response spectrum to determine structural response and design forces is introduced. Additional topics include an inelastic analysis and interpretation of the results.
courses.course_objectives: Course introduces students to principles of seismic hazards analysis, advanced structural dynamics, and inelastic behavior. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to understand how the effects of ground shaking are amplified by structural vibration. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to understand how a response spectrum is used to characterize ground shaking. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to understand the procedures used to estimate the intensity of ground shaking at a given site. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to perform a seismic analysis using ground motion models. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to learn how excessive torsional response, configuration irregularities, and lack of redundancy can have catastrophic consequences on the seismic performance of building structures. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to interpret dynamic analysis results. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to learn how building codes and standards control the inelastic behavior by imposing detailing requirements and deformation limits. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to learn the limitations, requirements, advantages, and disadvantages of the various analysis methods.
courses.topical_outline: Overview of Past Earthquakes and Associated Damage Quantification of Ground Motion Effects Formulation of SDOF Equations of Motion MDOF Systems and Modal Properties Computation of Effective Earthquake Forces Development of Elastic Response Spectrum Seismic Load Analysis using Equivalent Lateral Force Method and Modal Response Spectrum Method Concepts of Risk and Hazard Sources of Inelastic Behavior Importance of Ductility Structural Systems and Design Requirements Special Topics in Modeling (e.g., Diaphragm Rigidity)

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Earthquake Engineering and Dynamics of Structures
courses.description: The fundamental concepts, principles, and application of earthquake engineering in seismic analysis and design of structures using simulation of ground motion models. The concept of response spectrum to determine structural response and design forces is introduced. Additional topics include an inelastic analysis and interpretation of the results.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Inelastic Behavior of Construction Materials
courses.description: Provides graduate students with the essential knowledge necessary to understand inelastic behavior of construction materials. Topics will include linear and nonlinear viscoelasticity and basic fracture mechanics.
courses.course_objectives: At the completion of this course, the student should be able to understand inelastic behavior of construction materials. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to understand theory of viscoelasticity. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to understand mechanical analogs and linear viscoelastic constitutive equation. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to analyze experimental data generated from laboratory testing of construction materials.
courses.topical_outline:
I. Representative Volume Element and Constitutive Behavior of Materials II. Theory of Viscoelasticity
1. Time-dependent material responses (mechanical analogs)
2. Linear black box theory using hereditary integral
3. Creep compliance, relaxation modulus, and complex modulus
4. Time-temperature superposition with growing damage
5. Linear viscoelastic constitutive equations
6. Linear elastic-viscoelastic correspondence principle
7. Elastic-viscoelastic correspondence principle based on pseudo variables III. Continuum Damage Mechanics (Internal State Variable Formulation) IV. Viscoelastoplastic Continuum Damage Model for Construction Materials

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Inelastic Behavior of Construction Materials
courses.description: Provides graduate students with the essential knowledge necessary to understand inelastic behavior of construction materials. Topics will include linear and nonlinear viscoelasticity and basic fracture mechanics.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Geomechanics
courses.description: An introduction to the theory and application of fundamental mechanics, such as elasticity, plasticity, and viscoelasticity, to soil mechanics problems.
courses.course_objectives: Course is designed to introduce theory and application of fundamental mechanics, such as elasticity, plasticity, and viscoelasticity, to soil mechanics problems. On completion of this course, the student should be able to solve stress problem of geo materials using elastic, plastic, and viscoelastic theory. On completion of this course, the student should be able to apply constitutive modeling to the behavior of geo materials.
courses.topical_outline: Representative Volume Element and Constitutive Behavior of Geomaterials Theory of Elasticity Theory of Plasticity Theory of Viscoelasticity

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Geomechanics
courses.description: An introduction to the theory and application of fundamental mechanics, such as elasticity, plasticity, and viscoelasticity, to soil mechanics problems.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Soil Improvement
courses.description: A study of various soil improvement techniques for civil and construction engineering projects. Subjects include stone columns, soil stabilization, grouting, deep soil mixing, reinforced slopes, soil nailing, and geogrids in highways.
courses.course_objectives: Designed to introduce the advantages and limitations to properly selecting ground modification techniques and design considerations for infrastructure projects. On completion of this course, the student should be able to investigate and discuss alternative soil improvement methods satisfying the project requirements.
courses.topical_outline: Compaction Deep Dynamic Compacting Surcharging Stone Columns Soil Stabilization Grouting/Jet Grouting Deep Soil Mixing MSE Walls Reinforced Slopes Soil Nailing Geogrids in Highways

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Soil Improvement
courses.description: A study of various soil improvement techniques for civil and construction engineering projects. Subjects include stone columns, soil stabilization, grouting, deep soil mixing, reinforced slopes, soil nailing, and geogrids in highways.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Advanced Pavement System Design
courses.description: Essential knowledge necessary to understand Mechanistic Empirical (ME) pavement system design approaches is covered. Pavement distress/performance simulation models and errors associated with simplifying assumptions and subsequent impacts on the design process are explored. Current literature is an integral part of the course as students complete the listed topics.
courses.course_objectives: At the completion of this course, the student should be able to understand global distress/performance simulation models for pavement distress types. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to understand derivation of the local calibration coefficients for pavement Mechanistic Empirical (ME) design. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to determine appropriate default values for input parameters to the pavement system design.
courses.topical_outline: Introduction Sampling Matrices and Factorials (Long-Term Pavement Performance Test Sections) Field and Laboratory Test Methods for Pavement Input Parameter Site Conditions and Design Features (Climate, Traffic, Layer Properties, Distress Data) Calibration Coefficients for Rigid Pavement Calibration Coefficients for Flexible Pavement Applicability of Calibration Coefficients

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Advanced Pavement System Design
courses.description: Essential knowledge necessary to understand Mechanistic Empirical (ME) pavement system design approaches is covered. Pavement distress/performance simulation models and errors associated with simplifying assumptions and subsequent impacts on the design process are explored. Current literature is an integral part of the course as students complete the listed topics.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Advanced Concrete Materials
courses.description: Provides an advanced understanding of the design and production of concrete mixtures for strength and durability as well as testing methods for strength, permeability, freeze-thaw, sulfate attack, and non-destructive methods of evaluation of concrete structures. Additional topics will include critical properties of concrete and trouble shooting and prevention.
courses.course_objectives: The objective of this course is to provide the student with advanced coverage of concrete materials, production, and behavior. Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to explain in detail the types and effects of the constituents that make up concrete mixtures. Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to evaluate the performance of concrete mixtures based on fresh and hardened concrete properties. Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to describe the appropriate methods for placement and curing of concrete to ensure quality concrete performance is met. Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to design High Performance concrete mixtures utilizing blended and optimized aggregate gradations as well as other mixture modifications. Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to understand concrete’s response to stress and the effect of time-dependent deformation. Upon completion of this course, the student should be able to explain the forensics of concrete through evaluation and testing and recommend suitable repair/rehabilitation.
courses.topical_outline: Concrete as a Material Cement Type, Blended Cements, and Cement Production Cement Hydration Mineral Admixtures Chemical Admixtures Fresh Concrete Properties Mixture Proportioning Mixture Reproportioning Preparation for Concrete Placement and Construction Practices and Curing Aggregate Optimization for Concrete Mixtures High-Strength Concrete Concrete Response to Stress, Hardened Concrete Properties Time-Dependent Deformation Durability of Concrete Testing Methods for Concrete Evaluation Types of Repair Material/Construction Troubleshooting and Prevention

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Advanced Concrete Materials
courses.description: Provides an advanced understanding of the design and production of concrete mixtures for strength and durability as well as testing methods for strength, permeability, freeze-thaw, sulfate attack, and non-destructive methods of evaluation of concrete structures. Additional topics will include critical properties of concrete and trouble shooting and prevention.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Design of Prestressed Concrete Structures
courses.description: Provides the engineering student with the knowledge required to design and construct prestressed concrete structures. Emphasis will be placed on the behavior of prestressed concrete under load along with potential failure mechanisms.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Design of Prestressed Concrete Structures
courses.description: Provides the engineering student with the knowledge required to design and construct prestressed concrete structures. Emphasis will be placed on the behavior of prestressed concrete under load along with potential failure mechanisms.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Advanced Strength of Materials
courses.description: Provides students with the essential knowledge necessary to analyze structural/mechanical systems and components, as well as the ability to interpret analysis results. Basic concepts and tools for analyzing engineering problems (elasticity equations, equilibrium, compatibility, etc.) will be emphasized, as well as the mathematical formulations.

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Smart and Sustainable Infrastructure
courses.description: Course provides graduate students with essential knowledge on sustainability, infrastructure, sensing, sensor network, digital twin, multiscale modeling and simulation, and data analytics for decision-making to enable sustainable and smart infrastructure.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to understand the concept and the evolution history of sustainability. Students will be able to understand the concept of infrastructure and its implications to the human society. Students will be able to understand the concept of smartness and how to achieve it. Students will be able to understand the functionality of sensing materials. Students will be able to understand typical sensing algorithms. Students will understand how to design a sensor network and establish digital twin models. Students will understand how to apply AI-based data analytics for decision-making.
courses.topical_outline: Concept and Evolution of Sustainability Types of Infrastructure Concept of Smartness Design of Functional Materials Preserving Infrastructures Infrastructure Inspection and Monitoring Making Timely Repairs for Durable Infrastructures Sensing and Sensors Sensor Network CPS and IoT Smart City Technologies Data Analytics Machine Learning and Deep Learning for Vibration Sensing Risk Analysis and Decision-Making

courses.subject: CVLE
courses.title: Sensing and Perception for Convergent Safety
courses.description: Students will develop a fundamental knowledge about intelligent sensing and perception and its role in convergent safety, including transportation, infrastructure, environmental, and other safety. Course covers sensing materials, sensing technologies, deep learning methods, and AI-based techniques for improving human recognition, perception, and safety in civil and environmental engineering.
courses.course_objectives: At the completion of this course, the student should be able to understand different types of sensing mechanisms, sensing materials, sensor design and networks, and their application in civil engineering infrastructure and systems. At the completion of this course, the student should be able to develop different types of data analytics of the sensed data to form perception and recognition of human centered safety in mobility, infrastructure, and environment.
courses.topical_outline: Human Senses Human Mind Decision Process Advanced Sensing Materials Advanced Sensing Technologies IoT Technologies AI Approaches Big Data Analytics Deep Learning Infrastructure Health Monitoring Safety of Autonomous and Connected Mobility Environmental Safety Safety Cause and Solution Convergence Safety Perception and Recognition

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Performance Company I
courses.description: Participation as a dancer in a faculty-choreographed dance piece.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Tap Dance Foundations I
courses.description: Foundation training necessary for the development of skill proficiency in tap dance.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Tap Dance Foundations II
courses.description: Second level of foundation training necessary for the development of skill proficiency in tap dance for students with some previous experience.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Folk Dance Foundations
courses.description: Foundation training necessary for the development of skillproficiency in folk dance.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Jazz Dance Foundations
courses.description: Foundation training necessary for the development of skillproficiency in the jazz dance idiom.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Contemporary Modern Dance Foundations I
courses.description: Introductory level foundation training necessary for the development of skill proficiency in contemporary dance for students with no previous experience.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Ballet Foundations I
courses.description: Introductory level foundation training necessary for the development of skill proficiency in ballet for students with no previous experience.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Ballroom Foundations I - Lead/Male
courses.description: Foundational training necessary for the development of skilled proficiency in beginning ballroom dance. Ballroom dance requires a partnership, two persons forming a couple, made up of leads and follows.  This course is open to those in the role of “leads,” who are traditionally males.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Ballroom Foundations I - Follow/Female
courses.description: Foundational training necessary for the development of skilled proficiency in beginning ballroom dance. Ballroom dance requires a partnership, two persons forming a couple, made up of leads and follows. This course is open to those in the role of “follows,” who are traditionally females.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Contemporary Modern Dance Foundations II
courses.description: Second level of foundation training necessary for the development of skill proficiency in contemporary dance for students with some previous experience.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Ballet Foundations II
courses.description: Second level of foundation training necessary for the development of skill proficiency in ballet for students with some previous experience.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Ballroom Foundations II - Lead/Male
courses.description: Continued foundational training necessary for the development of skilled proficiency in ballroom dance at the intermediate level. Ballroom dance requires a partnership, two persons forming a couple, made up of leads and follows. This course is open to those in the role of “leads,” who are traditionally males.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Ballroom Foundations II - Follow/Female
courses.description: Continued foundational training necessary for the development of skilled proficiency in ballroom dance at the intermediate level. Ballroom dance requires a partnership, two persons forming a couple, made up of leads and follows. This course is open to those in the role of “follows,” who are traditionally females.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Jazz Dance I
courses.description: Movement fundamentals for improving the technical execution and stylistic definition of jazz dance.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Contemporary Dance I
courses.description: The acquisition and development of technical skills in contemporary dance. Techniques basic to this dance form plus motional properties as they relate to dance will be emphasized.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Ballet I
courses.description: Designed to build the strength, flexibility, endurance, and control necessary for performance of low intermediate-level ballet barre exercises, adagio sequences, and allegro enchainments.  An understanding of proper body mechanics and the French vocabulary for ballet will also be emphasized.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Pointe I
courses.description: Pointe technique, which is an extension of ballet technique skills, with attention to strengthening pointe and ballet skills, placement, vocabulary, musicality, and stylistic elements. Application of pointe skills in the study of variations from classical ballet repertoire.
courses.course_objectives:
By the end of this course, students will be able to perform exercises on pointe at the barre with correct placement.
- Execute exercises on pointe in the center
- Demonstrate knowledge of ballet vocabulary applied to pointe 
- Discuss theoretical elements of pointe technique skills
- Perform class combinations and variations from the classical ballet repertoire on pointe with correct ballet and pointe technique
- Display strength and control when dancing on with musicality, and correct stylistic elements By the end of this course, students will be able to execute exercises on pointe in the center. By the end of this course, students will be able to demonstrate knowledge of ballet vocabulary applied to pointe. By the end of this course, students will be able to discuss theoretical elements of pointe technique skills. By the end of this course, students will be able to perform class combinations and variations from the classical ballet repertoire on pointe with correct ballet and pointe technique. By the end of this course, students will be able to display strength and control when dancing on with musicality, and correct stylistic elements.
courses.topical_outline: Execute barre exercises, developing strength on pointe, and continue development of ballet technique skills Perform center exercises on pointe, developing coordination and movement quality Review classical ballet vocabulary Explore theory of pointe technique skills that extend from ballet technique including placement, musicality, and stylistic elements Practice class combinations on pointe with correct ballet and pointe technique Study and practice selected variations from the classical ballet repertoire

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Pas De Deux
courses.description: Designed to develop the beginning-intermediate-level dance student's ability to transfer classical ballet and pointe skills into partnered pas de deux work. In classical ballet, women wear pointe shoes, but men do not.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Production Assignment I
courses.description: Experience in publicity, graphic design, stage lighting, stage management, and costuming through faculty-supervised and monitored participation as a member of the production crew for three dance concerts sponsored by the department of Dance.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Dance Appreciation
courses.description: Examine various aspects of the dance experience and explore the mover, dance maker/choreographer, and viewer. Historical and critical readings, video viewings, and assignments investigating the art of dance and dance as part of the human experience; develop skills in articulating personal responses to dance.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Dance Appreciation
courses.description: Examine various aspects of the dance experience and explore the mover, dance maker/choreographer, and viewer. Historical and critical readings, video viewings, and assignments investigating the art of dance and dance as part of the human experience; develop skills in articulating personal responses to dance.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Practicing Wellness
courses.description: An experiential-based course that offers an introduction to fundamental wellness principles and practices, with an aim to increase health and well-being and reduce injury through embodied practices both in the studio and the classroom.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: The Pilates Method I
courses.description: Introduces students to the Pilates Mat repertoire. The history of The Pilates Method is introduced, as well as the Pilates principles, guiding beginner Pilates students into a strong personal Pilates practice.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Yoga: Asana Practice I
courses.description: Introduces yoga as a mindful movement practice used to increase the mind-body connection. In this fundamental course, yoga postures, or asanas, will explore alignment and breath to improve balance, strength, and flexibility.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Yoga: Asana Practice I
courses.description:
Introduces yoga as a mindful movement practice used to increase the mind-body connection. In this fundamental
course, yoga postures, or asanas, will explore alignment and breath to improve balance, strength, and flexibility.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Training in Alternate Dance Forms I
courses.description: Training in a movement system complementing the development ofthe dancer.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Aerial Yoga Trapeze I
courses.description: This movement course will focus on exercises and skills utilizing the Yoga Trapeze and also prepare or supplement aerial dance training. The course will emphasize methods to improve spinal and joint strength, flexibility, and balance and promote improved centeredness, core support, and connectivity of the torso to the body limbs.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Aerial Dance I
courses.description: Introduction to aerial dance technique and creative practice utilizing vertical and bar apparatuses (i.e. aerial fabric, trapeze). Students will develop an awareness of effective technique and alignment through beginning skill vocabulary including mounts, climbs, wraps, locks, and inversions. Contextual information on rigging, anatomy, history, and aesthetics will augment practice-based learning.
courses.course_objectives: Students will demonstrate beginning aerial skill vocabulary with effective technique and alignment. Students will identify beginning aerial skill families, common bases of support, and root positions on vertical and bar apparatuses. Students will apply the elements of dance to create personally expressive aerial sequences at a beginning level. Students will describe basic rigging and risk management practices for aerial training.
courses.topical_outline: Beginning aerial skill vocabulary for vertical apparatuses. Beginning aerial skill vocabulary for bar apparatuses. Inversion progressions and conditioning. Creative application of the elements of dance to aerial sequences. Basic rigging and risk management practices for aerial training.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Performance Company II
courses.description: Participation as a dancer in a faculty-choreographed dance piece.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Dance Improvisation I
courses.description: Provides the individual an opportunity to explore movement initiated through various sources including internal motivation. Emphasis will be on individual and group interaction within structured and free improvisational situations, all for the purpose of developing the student's creative approach to composing and performing.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Dance Repertory Lab I
courses.description: In-depth explorations with guided instruction in foundational technical and performance/artistry skills involved in developing, rehearsing, and performing faculty and/or guest artist dance repertory.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Music for Dance
courses.description: This course will teach dancers to understand the language of music and build the necessary vocabulary to analyze, develop, and communicate musical ideas.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Tap Dance II
courses.description: Intermediate-level exploration and practice of tap dance skills and artistry.
courses.course_objectives: Students will learn to perform tap skills and vocabulary at an intermediate level. Students will demonstrate and refine basic coordination, motor memory, and fine and gross motor skills. Students will demonstrate intermediate-level skills in rhythmic awareness and musical knowledge.
courses.topical_outline: Time Steps Pull Backs Wing Trenches Open and Closed Thirds Maxi Fords Tap Dance Repertoire Musical Structures of Straight and Swing Time Improvisation and Composition Exercises

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: West African Dance Forms and Styles
courses.description: Traditional and contemporary dance forms and styles of the West African culture that share common aesthetic principles will be explored through movement, music, storytelling, poetry, and discussion. This course is designed to explore the West African cultural experience when taught away from its original setting.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Methods of Teaching Social Dance
courses.description: Methods of teaching ballroom, folk, line, and square dance to grades kindergarten through twelve.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Hip-Hop Dance and Culture
courses.description: Exploration into the history and movement technique styles of Hip-Hop dance. The primary focus of this course is to develop Hip-Hop related dance skills as a medium of communication beyond the entertainment aspects. Students will explore movement isolations, rhythms, and Hip-Hop origins in the context of contemporary social culture.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Jazz Dance II
courses.description: Movement applications for improving technical proficiency, performance dynamics, and stylistic clarity at the intermediate level. Dance combinations will explore various contemporary jazz styles, infused with rhythmic and syncopated musicality.
courses.course_objectives: Students will demonstrate improved motor control and execution of body isolations and alignment. Students will identify jazz specific movement and positions, both in stillness and in motion, and work toward mastering these identified stylistic elements. Students will know and recall historical and cultural content related to jazz dance. Students will demonstrate the ability to self-direct and self-correct. Students will demonstrate rhythm, syncopation, and musicality development. Students will build a sense of artistry, expression, and performance quality. Students will build awareness of personal strengths and limitations with the ability to recognize these in others.
courses.topical_outline: A) Warm-up B) Center floor exercises and combinations C) Locomotor exercises and combinations D) Featured combination synthesizing fundamental concepts

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Contemporary Modern Dance II
courses.description: Intermediate-level course designed to aid the student in continued acquisition and development of technical skills in contemporary dance. Techniques basic to this dance form plus motional properties as they relate to dance will be emphasized.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Ballet II
courses.description: Designed to build the strength, flexibility, endurance, and control necessary for performance of intermediate-level ballet barre exercises, adagio sequences, and allegro enchainments.  An understanding of proper body mechanics and the French vocabulary will also be emphasized.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Ballet II Lab
courses.description: An intensive physical laboratory course emphasizing specificity in skills, methods, and tools used for refinement in ballet training. A companion course to Ballet II. The laboratory experience focuses on mastering difficult skills in ballet training to acquire a kinesiological strong ballet technique and performance.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Pointe II
courses.description: Pointe technique, which is an extension of ballet technique, with exercises to strengthen correct placement and develop musicality, artistry, and stylistic elements. Pointe skills applied to study and practice of variations from classical repertoire.
courses.course_objectives: By the end of this course, students will be able to perform barre exercises on pointe with correct placement. By the end of this course, students will be able to execute exercises on pointe in the center. By the end of this course, students will be able to demonstrate knowledge of ballet vocabulary. By the end of this course, students will be able to discuss content, context, and style of variations from the classical ballet repertoire. By the end of this course, students will be able to perform combinations and variations on pointe with correct ballet and pointe technique. By the end of this course, students will be able to display strength and control when dancing sur les pointes. By the end of this course, students will be able to perform variations with musicality, artistry, and correct stylistic elements.
courses.topical_outline: Execute barre exercises that develop strength on pointe and reinforce ballet technique skills Perform center exercises on pointe, developing coordination and movement quality Apply classical ballet vocabulary to pointe technique Explore the theory of pointe technique skills that extend from ballet technique including placement, musicality, and stylistic elements Investigate and discuss content, context, and stylistic elements of the choreography in variations learned from the classical ballet repertoire Practice and perform variations with attention to correct placement musicality, artistry, and stylistic elements
courses.prerequisiteText: Two hours of DANC 1671 and permission of department

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Pas De Deux
courses.description: Continued development of the intermediate-level dance student's ability to transfer classical ballet and pointe skills into partnered pas de deux work. In classical ballet, women wear pointe shoes, but men do not.
courses.prerequisiteText: DANC 1680 and permission of department | Pre or

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Pre-Professional Performance Company I
courses.description: The practice and experience of performance in a dance company. Training and participation in all areas critical to the operation of a dance company, including mainstage performance, touring, and management of all production concerns.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Student Performance I
courses.description: Performance in an original student-choreographed work through a faculty supervised production.
courses.course_objectives: Students will develop knowledge and skills in performance and artistry, as well as skills in working in a dance-making process, culminating in a public performance.
courses.topical_outline: Attend audition of all genres and choreographers Attend all weekly rehearsals Participate collaboratively and cooperatively with choreographer and other performers in dance-making process Attend technical and dress rehearsals, and performances Assist in cleanup of dressing room or other (strike)

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Production Assignment II
courses.description: Continued experience in publicity, graphic design, stage lighting, stage management, and costuming through faculty-supervised and monitored participation as a member of the production crew for three dance concerts sponsored by the Department of Dance.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Laban/Bartenieff Movement Studies
courses.description: An introduction to Laban/Bartenieff Movement Studies (LBMS) and its elemental framework of body, effort, shape, and space. Students will experience, observe, describe, coach, and make meaning of human movement through the specific lens of LBMS. Students will also critically examine how historical and cultural contexts inform movement observation and analysis.
courses.course_objectives: At the successful conclusion of this course, students will be able to identify and apply Laban/Bartenieff Movement Studies terminology to movement experience and observation. At the successful conclusion of this course, students will be able to perform the Patterns of Total Body Connectivity in differentiated and integrated movement contexts. At the successful conclusion of this course, students will be able to reflect on one’s personal movement signature and enact lesser-known aspects of the elemental framework of Laban/Bartenieff Movement Studies. At the successful conclusion of this course, students will be able to synthesize knowledge of the Laban/Bartenieff Movement Studies framework with an area of personal and/or professional interest.
courses.topical_outline: The Elemental Framework of LBMS (Body, Effort, Shape, Space) Organizing Themes of LBMS (inner <--> outer, part <--> whole, function <--> expression, simple <--> complex, stability <--> mobility, exertion <--> recuperation) Patterns of Total Body Connectivity (Breath, Core-Distal, Head-Tail, Upper-Lower, Body-Half, Cross-Lateral) Special Considerations in Movement Observation (Body Knowledge/Body Prejudice, troubling the frame)
courses.prerequisiteText: DANC 2652 and DANC 2662 and permission of department

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Principles of Science and Somatics in Dance Training
courses.description: Survey of primary scientific and somatic principles that inform dance training and performance, including anatomical and kinesiological components, injury prevention, rehabilitation, safe practices, somatic neuromuscular re-education methods, and an introduction to dance movement therapy.
courses.course_objectives: By the end of this course, students will have developed a broader understanding and efficient function of the body in dance as it is viewed through both scientific and somatic perspectives. By the end of this course, students will have learned basic anatomical knowledge of the human musculoskeletal system and acquire both visual image and perceptual sense of the body's structure. By the end of this course, students will have learned to detect and correct particular muscular imbalances that may relate to physical stress. By the end of this course, students will have developed an awareness of one’s own alignment. Conduct alignment analysis and identify common alignment deviations and postural conditions. By the end of this course, students will understand and apply physical training principles, and about the prevention and care of common dance injuries. By the end of this course, students will identify major physical, environmental, and psychological stress factors relating to dance training. By the end of this course, students will have gained an understanding of the major somatic movement therapies, their purposes and their founders, through readings, discussion, and experiential applications. By the end of this course, students will have developed an understanding of dance therapy, its history, its purpose, and its primary pioneers.
courses.topical_outline:
- Introduction to fundamental knowledge and principles of dance science and somatic perspective and approaches  
- Identifying and applying neuromuscular and skeletal language, landmarks, and landscapes  
- Identifying and recalling major muscles and bones throughout the body, section by section 
- Analyzing a sample of current research from the literature  
- Applying current evidence-based safe and healthy dance practice  
- Executing and present final presentations

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: The Pilates Method II
courses.description: Advances students in the Pilates Mat repertoire from intermediate to advanced level Pilates exercises. The history of The Pilates Method is introduced, as well as the Pilates principles, guiding Pilates practitioners into a strong personal practice. Some prior Pilates experience is required, or prior experience with a mind-body connected physical practice.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Yoga: Asana Practice II
courses.description: Progresses intermediate through advanced students through the mindful movement practice of yoga.  Yoga postures, or asanas, will challenge the balance, strength, and flexibility of more experienced practitioners. Prior experience of yoga or years of training in other movement practices is required.
courses.prerequisiteText: (DANC 2040 or DANC 2040E) and permission of department

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Yoga: Asana Practice II
courses.description:
Progresses intermediate through advanced students through the mindful movement practice of yoga. Yoga postures, or
asanas, will challenge the balance, strength, and flexibility of more experienced practitioners. Prior experience of yoga
or years of training in other movement practices is required.
courses.prerequisiteText: (DANC 2040 or DANC 2040E) and permission of department

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Training in Alternate Dance Forms II
courses.description: In-depth training in a movement system complementing thedevelopment of the dancer.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Aerial Yoga Trapeze II
courses.description: This movement class will further develop fundamental exercises and skills utilizing the Yoga Trapeze and prepare or supplement aerial dance training. Through continued practice and improved spinal and joint strength, flexibility and balance, more advanced exercises and skills are obtained.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Introduction to Creative Movement
courses.description: An introduction to teaching creative movement for children, targeted for classroom teachers and general education majors.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Aerial Dance II
courses.description: Continuation of aerial dance technique and creative practice utilizing vertical and bar apparatuses (i.e. aerial fabric, trapeze). Students will continue to develop an awareness of effective technique and alignment as they learn intermediate aerial skill vocabulary. Contextual information on rigging, anatomy, history, and aesthetics will augment practice-based learning.
courses.course_objectives: Students will demonstrate intermediate aerial skill vocabulary with effective technique and alignment. Students will identify intermediate aerial skill families, common bases of support, and root positions on vertical and bar apparatuses. Students will apply the elements of dance to create personally expressive aerial sequences at an intermediate level. Students will describe and facilitate effective warm-up procedures and injury prevention related to aerial training.
courses.topical_outline: Intermediate aerial skill vocabulary for vertical apparatuses Intermediate aerial skill vocabulary for bar apparatuses Creative application of the elements of dance to aerial sequences Effective warm-up procedures and injury prevention related to aerial training

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Teaching Practicum in Dance I
courses.description: Field experience and limited teaching practicum, including observation of children and/or adolescents in a classroom context, grades pre-k through college.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Teaching Practicum in Dance II
courses.description: Field experience and teaching practicum, including observation of children and/or adolescents in a classroom context, grades pre-K-12.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Teaching Practicum in Dance III
courses.description: Field experiences and teaching practicum, pre-K classroom or community-based setting.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Performance Company III
courses.description: Participation as a dancer in a faculty-choreographed dance piece.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Dance Composition
courses.description: Introduction to dance composition emphasizing fundamental choreographic elements, structures, devices, and improvisation in developing an artistic stimulus into movement material. Students will engage in solo, duo, and collaborative small group studies and participate in class showings and peer feedback throughout the course. Students will also critically examine dance choreography through a variety of readings and video viewings to give context to their own creative work.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Digital Media for Dance
courses.description: A continuation of Dance Composition, this course focuses on artistic creation through the medium of film. Students will learn technical skills and aesthetic principles of the genre through hands-on class activities and studies in cinematography and editing. Students will consider project pre- and post-production and digital platforms for film sharing.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Seminar in Dance
courses.description: Topics for the course will be designed for each particular study abroad program. Students will explore and experience social, traditional, and theatrical dance in various world cultures. Participatory discussions on issues in world dance, as well as performative experiences, will be a focus in the course.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Dance in New York City Field Study
courses.description: First-hand dance experience in New York City, exploring the historic dance scene. Visit/work in theatres, professional schools, and Dance Collection at the New York Public Library for Performing Arts; participate in dance classes, network with professionals, learn professional practices in preparing for job auditions, and attend performances. Readings, discussions, and reflective practice activities.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Movement and Community in Ghana
courses.description: Course explores traditional/cultural, pedagogical/theoretical, well-being, and performance experiences in Ghana. Work with influential artists and learn techniques of community engagement through dance movement leading to collaborative, community-based performances in various cities in Ghana. Course also embraces a study of the history and culture of Ghana.
courses.course_objectives: At the conclusion of the course, students should be able to discuss community-based movement/dance in Ghana. At the conclusion of the course, students should be able to explain how movement and community work together and are intertwined in Ghana’s culture and history. At the conclusion of the course, students should be able to explore therapeutic topics through movement exploration. At the conclusion of the course, students should be able to demonstrate a West African movement vocabulary. At the conclusion of the course, students should be able to organize and/or participate in events and performances that bring people together as a community. At the conclusion of the course, students should be able to work with a community partner to collaboratively create a community-based performance/experience. At the conclusion of the course, students should be knowledgeable about the history and culture of Ghana.
courses.topical_outline: This is an intensive three-week immersion in movement and community in Ghana. Through dance/movement classes with influential local artists, visits to various sites and local communities, performances, discussions, and readings, this class explores the culture and community of the people of Ghana and prepares students for building community engagement through movement/dance.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Dance Repertory Lab II
courses.description: Further explorations with guided instruction in intermediate-level technical and performance/artistry skills involved in developing, rehearsing, and performing faculty and/or guest artist dance repertory.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Tap Dance III
courses.description: Advanced-level exploration and practice of tap dance skills and artistry.
courses.course_objectives: Students will learn to perform a large variety of tap skills and vocabulary at an advanced level. Students will execute complex coordination, motor memory, and fine and gross motor skills. Students will demonstrate advanced-level skills in rhythmic awareness and musical knowledge.
courses.topical_outline: Review of foundational tap vocabulary Contextual background of the genre Tap dance repertoire Musical structures of straight and swing time, meters Advanced improvisational and compositional exercises

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Intermediate/Advanced West African Dance Forms and Styles
courses.description: An intense study of movement and performance as a way of knowing, understanding, and experiencing culture, community, and diversity. This course works through dynamics of movement and music performance practice rooted in African traditional and contemporary aesthetics. The focus will be West African traditional dance and music.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Intermediate/Advanced Hip-Hop Dance and Culture
courses.description: An in-depth research exploration of the evolution and development of Hip-Hop dance. Focusing on the origins of Hip-Hop movement performance and rhythm coordination in the context of contemporary culture. This course will strongly explore how Hip-Hop culture embraces the youth through oppression, violence, identity, personal expression, culture, and power.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Jazz Dance III
courses.description: Movement applications for improving technical proficiency, performance dynamics, and stylistic clarity at the intermediate/advanced level. Dance combinations will explore various contemporary jazz styles, infused with rhythmic and syncopated musicality.
courses.prerequisiteText: Four hours of DANC 2642 and permission of department

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Contemporary Modern Dance III
courses.description: Intermediate to advanced-level course designed to aid the student in the continued acquisition and development of technical skills in contemporary dance. Technique and theory basic to this dance form plus motional properties as they relate to dance will be emphasized.
courses.course_objectives: Students will apply foundational movement concepts such as breath support, intra-bodily patterning, core support and spatial tethering, dynamic alignment, and rhythmic understanding and phrasing, to a contemporary modern context in exercises and phrases with clarity, versatility (in varied contexts) and consistency Students will demonstrate applied knowledge and understanding of intermediate/advanced level of contemporary modern vocabulary including but not limited to falls, spinal articulation in all planes, spiraling, off-verticality, weight-shifting, level changes, and apply basic improvisational tools Students will synthesize applied knowledge of anatomy, safe dance practices, and their individual first-person experience of their body with clarity, versatility (in varied contexts) and developing consistency to move both safely, and intuitively in fulfilling an intention or goal Students will demonstrate/perform artistic skills (such as risk, focused presence, emotional connection, projection, and musicality) with clarity and versatility (in varied contexts) and developing consistency to communicate ideas/emotions and/or movement forms for an audience
courses.topical_outline:
Review of basic, foundational movement contexts of the contemporary modern idiom
Applying safe warmup and cool-down princples in various contexts
Practices in  floor-based vocabulary and principles
Practices in standing and locomotor vocabulary and principles
Practices in rehearsing and performing extended phrases to develop performance and artistry
Creative problem solving in the building of phrases or exercises based on given material or structures
Analysis of performance, self-reflection, and integration of peer and instructor feedback
courses.prerequisiteText: Four hours of DANC 2652 and permisson of department

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Ballet III
courses.description: Designed to build the strength, flexibility, endurance, andcontrol necessary for performance of intermediate-advanced level ballet barre exercises, adagio sequences andallegro enchainments. Style, perfection, and performance qualitywill be emphasized.
courses.prerequisiteText: Four hours of DANC 2662 and permission of department

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Ballet III Lab
courses.description: An intensive physical laboratory course emphasizing specificity in skills, methods, and tools used for refinement in intermediate-advanced ballet training that is a companion course to Ballet III. The laboratory experience focuses on mastering difficult skills in ballet training to acquire a kinesiological strong ballet technique and performance.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Pointe III and Variations
courses.description: Continued practice of pointe technique, which is an extension of ballet technique. Focus on building strength and confidence on pointe necessary to perform variations from the classical repertoire. Develop musicality, artistry, interpretation, and stylistic elements.
courses.course_objectives: By the end of this course, students will be able to perform barre exercises on pointe with correct placement. By the end of this course, students will be able to execute exercises on pointe in the center with sustained balances. By the end of this course, students will be able to demonstrate skills in knowledge of ballet vocabulary. By the end of this course, students will be able to discuss content, context, and stylistic nuances of variations from the classical ballet repertoire learned in class. By the end of this course, students will be able to perform combinations and variations on pointe with correct technique. By the end of this course, students will be able to display strength and control when dancing on pointe. By the end of this course, students will be able to exhibit emerging skills in musicality, artistry, interpretation, and correct stylistic elements while performing variations.
courses.topical_outline: Execute barre exercises that develop strength on pointe and reinforce ballet technique skills Perform center exercises on pointe, developing coordination, and movement quality Review and practice classical ballet vocabulary applied in pointe work Embody and discuss theory of pointe technique skills that extend from ballet technique in placement, musicality, and stylistic elements Practice performance elements of musicality, artistry, interpretation, and stylistic elements Investigate and discuss content, context, and stylistic elements of the choreography in variations from the classical ballet repertoire learned in class Practice and perform variations with attention to sustained steps on pointe in correct placement with musicality, artistry, interpretation, and stylistic elements
courses.prerequisiteText: Two hours of DANC 2672 and permission of department

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Pas De Deux
courses.description: Further development of the intermediate-advanced-level dance student's ability to transfer classical ballet and pointe skills into partnered pas de deux work. In classical ballet, women wear pointe shoes, and men do not.
courses.prerequisiteText: DANC 2680 and permission of department | Pre or

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Teaching Dance for Children
courses.description: Principles, materials, and methods for teaching brain-compatible dance education (based in creative movement) to the pre-adolescent child in and beyond the K-12 environment. Includes 4-8 hours of community and or K-12 field experience.
courses.course_objectives: By the end of the course, each student will identify, compare, and apply a range of learning and instructional theories as they apply to the young dancer. By the end of the course, each student will discern the difference between teaching technique and a conceptual creative movement approach. By the end of the course, each student will identify and apply of development principles (motor learning, cognition) and application to the dance learning environment. By the end of the course, each student will identify the dance concepts and apply them in creative movement games and activities. By the end of the course, each student will develop skills in planning, formulating, executing, and reflecting upon lesson plans for children’s dance based on Ann Green Gilbert’s conceptual approach. By the end of the course, each student will gain knowledge and understanding of a diversity of learners in the dance learning environment and how to apply pedagogical and content knowledge in an instructional context. By the end of the course, each student will practice teaching young children in the field through observation and minimal teaching in a K-5 PE classroom or a P-3 environment. Students will identify their relationship to teaching and reflect upon their own identity as teacher
courses.topical_outline: Identify the four main areas of teaching to the whole child and their relation to creative movement Identify and apply tools for differentiating instruction by learner, content, process, and product Identify and apply instructional/learning theories applied to the young dance learner Critically analyze current selected research in children's dance Identify and apply motor development and motor learning issues for young children Identify and apply factors in the creative movement learning environment Plan and teach a creative movement lesson segment Identify and correspond the categories of the National Standards in dance education (pK-5) Identify, apply, and create assessments and assessment strategies

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Choreographic Lab
courses.description: Students will create, rehearse, and produce an original work to be presented in the fall student concert each year.
courses.course_objectives: Students will practice concepts and skills related to dance composition as well as skills in working in a dance-making process, culminating in a public performance.
courses.topical_outline: Audition performers and work with peer choreographers to cast works Write a descriptive proposal of project Conduct/lead weekly rehearsals with dancers Manage communication and scheduling with dancers and technical director, in technical and dress rehearsals and performances Participate collaboratively and cooperatively with choreographer and other performers in dance-making process Attend technical and dress rehearsals and performances Assist in cleanup of dressing room or other (strike) Reflection and analysis of project
courses.prerequisiteText: Second or third-year student standing and permission of department

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Writing in Dance
courses.description: Introduction to writing about dance in different contexts through informal and formal written assignments (including a research paper), as well as readings and discussions.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Pre-Professional Performance Company II
courses.description: The continued practice and experience of performance in a dance company. Training and participation in all areas critical to the operation of a dance company, including mainstage performance, touring, and management of all production concerns.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Young Choreographer's Lab II - Performer
courses.description: Upper-level performance in an original student choreographic work to be presented in the fall student concert each year.
courses.course_objectives: Students will develop knowledge and skills in performance and artistry, as well as skills in working in a dance-making process, culminating in a public performance.
courses.topical_outline: Attend audition of all genres and choreographers Attend all weekly rehearsals Participate collaboratively and cooperatively with choreographer and other performers in dance-making process Attend technical and Dress rehearsals, and performances Assist in cleanup of dressing room or other (strike)

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Independent Study in Dance
courses.description: Independent study in a selected dance topic.
courses.course_objectives: The student must be able to demonstrate that an independent research project would be more beneficial than a more traditional course and/or address a topic beyond course offerings. The student would be expected to develop a plan and schedule for their research and to submit progress reports as well as to meet regularly with their faculty advisor. The student would be expected to conduct individual research. The student would be expected to discuss the topic/area of research knowledgeably. The student would be expected to explain the research process and methodology. The student would be expected to produce a rigorously researched and correctly referenced (citations) scholarly paper or appropriately documented research for a creative project.
courses.topical_outline: As an independent study, the topic will be proposed by the student and approved by the faculty advisor and will follow the parameters of research (scholarly or creative) appropriate to the topic: •  Define a research topic/idea •  Develop a research/creative project from its inception through completion •  Synthesize and analyze materials on the selected topic in dance and dance-related subjects •  Create an annotated bibliography •  Submit an original project with drafts and revisions from feedback •  Present final project

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description:
A special topics course in a variety of dance subjects, 
depending upon faculty instructor proposals; intensive study in
selected topics in dance.
courses.course_objectives: Students will prepare a research presentation of their work in a seminar-like format to their colleagues and professors. Students will conduct research on an advanced level. Students will produce a comprehensive review of current and essential literature on the topic. Students will investigate, analyze, and organize materials. Students will deliver a research presentation (to colleagues and peers). Students will use the research in preparation of a proposal/abstract for a conference presentation.
courses.topical_outline: The format for this course may be nontraditional and will address the above learning objectives under the guidance of the sponsoring faculty member for each special topics course that is taught. •  Topic or Topics will be assigned •  Preliminary review of literature on topic •  Design research argument •  Conduct research •  Present Research •  Discuss Research Findings •  Evaluate Research
courses.prerequisiteText: Permission of department | Graduate Prerequisite | Permission of department

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Dance and Community
courses.description: Explore dance and community through cultural/traditional, pedagogical/theoretical, well-being, and performance experiences. Study of influential artists and techniques of community engagement through dance will lead to collaborative, community-based dance performances.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Contemporizing Ballet: Histories, Choreographies, and Pedagogies
courses.description: Classical ballet examined through historical, social, political, and pedagogical contexts. Theory and practice of major ballet styles including historical figures, choreography, and foundations of training; also, current issues in reframing ballet training and performance, applied practice in vocabulary, stylistic nuances, and ballet pedagogy. Classroom and studio work.
courses.course_objectives:
Unit 1 - Ballet Histories: Creating the 'Canon'
•  Defining the classical ballet 'canon' – histories of ballets and historical figures
•  Investigating specific ballets in historical, social, political, and pedagogical contexts as well as in content and style  
•  Personal history in ballet Unit 2 - Contemporizing Ballet: Questions, Issues, and Contexts
•  Ballet then and now: 'dismantling the canon'
•  What works and what doesn’t
•  Identifying and understanding context then and now
•  Appropriation, acculturation, (mis)representation, gender binaries, and cultural identities in choreography, performance, and training
•  What changes are being made? What changes can we make? Unit 3 - Ballet Styles: Histories and Pedagogies
•  Philosophical and stylistic differences and vocabulary in the foundational teaching technique methods in major training schools/styles: French foundation, Italian-Cecchetti, Danish-Bournonville, Russian-Vaganova, British-Royal Ballet/Royal Academy of Dance, American-Balanchine 
•  Ballet vocabulary/terminology
•  Framework for structuring a ballet class
•  Reframing the narrative of ballet in training and performance
•  Personal teaching philosophy; how does it advance ballet training?
courses.topical_outline:
Unit 1 - Ballet Histories: Creating the 'Canon'
•  Defining the classical ballet 'canon' – histories of ballets and historical figures
•  Investigating specific ballets in historical, social, political, and pedagogical contexts as well as in content and style

•  Ballet vocabulary/terminology

•  Reframing the narrative of ballet in training and performance

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Aerial Dance III
courses.description: Continuation of aerial dance technique and creative practice utilizing vertical and bar apparatuses (i.e., aerial fabric, trapeze). Students will continue to develop an awareness of effective technique and alignment as they learn advanced intermediate aerial skill vocabulary. Contextual information on rigging, anatomy, history, and aesthetics will augment practice-based learning.
courses.course_objectives: At the successful conclusion of this course, students will be able to demonstrate advanced intermediate aerial skill vocabulary with effective technique and alignment. At the successful conclusion of this course, students will be able to identify advanced intermediate aerial skill families, common bases of support, and root positions on vertical and bar apparatuses. At the successful conclusion of this course, students will be able to apply the elements of dance to create personally expressive aerial sequences at an advanced intermediate level. At the successful conclusion of this course, students will be able to synthesize personal aerial arts aesthetic informed by various aerial performance contexts.
courses.topical_outline: Concepts covered in this course include advanced intermediate aerial skill vocabulary for vertical apparatuses Advanced intermediate aerial skill vocabulary for bar apparatuses Creative application of the elements of dance to aerial sequences Aerial arts aesthetics across various aerial performance contexts

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Performance Company IV
courses.description: Participation as a dancer in a faculty-choreographed piece.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Dance Improvisation II
courses.description: Continued exploration of movement initiated through various sources including internal motivation.  Students will gain experience in the leading of improvisational structures.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Dance Composition and Technology Interface
courses.description: Dance composition specifically applied to the development ofgroup choreography. Students will explore the role technologyplays in dance art of the twenty first century and learn tocreate a screen dance.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Studies in Dance History
courses.description: Dance as a reflection of culture and as an art form from the times of earliest lineage-based societies up to the 21st century. Socio-cultural influence and the contributions of individual artists will be investigated.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Dance History II
courses.description: Prevalent twentieth-century dance forms.  Socio-cultural influences and the contributions of individual artists will be investigated.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Dance Repertory Lab III
courses.description: Advanced technical and performance/artistry skills involved in developing, rehearsing, and performing faculty and/or guest artist dance repertory with guided leadership role opportunities.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Jazz Dance III
courses.description: Continued movement applications for improving technical proficiency, performance dynamics, and stylistic clarity at the intermediate/advanced level. Dance combinations will explore various contemporary jazz styles, infused with rhythmic and syncopated musicality. Undergraduate students may be asked to lead/demonstrate instructor-guided combinations in class.
courses.prerequisiteText: Four hours of DANC 3643 and permission of department

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Contemporary Modern Dance IV
courses.description: Advanced-level course designed to aid the student in further continued acquisition and development of technical skills in contemporary dance. Technique and theory basic to this dance form plus motional properties as they relate to dance will be emphasized.
courses.course_objectives: Students will harness the foundational movement concepts (breath support, intra-bodily patterning, core support and spatial tethering, dynamic alignment, and rhythmic understanding and phrasing) to a contemporary modern context in exercises and phrases with clarity, versatility (in varied contexts) and consistency to further their skills in advanced level contexts such as guided, advanced-level movement problems and structures for both duet and solo contexts Students will demonstrate applied knowledge and understanding of advanced level of contemporary modern vocabulary including but not limited to combined, complex contexts of falls, spinal articulation in all planes, spiraling, off-verticality, weight-shifting, level changes, and apply advanced improvisational tools Students will synthesize applied knowledge of anatomy, safe dance practices, and their individual first-person experience of their body with clarity, versatility (in varied contexts) and consistency to move both safely, and intuitively in fulfilling an intention or goal, and have opportunities to develop warmups or other activities to lead the class to demonstrate their understanding Students will demonstrate/perform artistic skills (such as risk, focused presence, emotional connection, projection, and musicality) with clarity and versatility (in varied contexts) and consistency  in varied contexts, including solo performance,  to communicate ideas/emotions and/or movement forms for an audience
courses.topical_outline:
Applying safe warmup and cool-down principles in various contexts
Practices in advanced-level floor-based vocabulary and principles
Practices in advanced-level standing and locomotor vocabulary and principles
Practices in rehearsing and performing extended phrases, including solo performance, to develop performance and artistry
Creative problem solving in the building of phrases or exercises based on given material or structures
Leading peers in movement activities to demonstrate understanding
Reflection and peer-review of performances
courses.prerequisiteText: Four hours of DANC 3653 and permission of department

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Ballet IV
courses.description: Designed to further build the strength, flexibility, endurance,and control necessary for performance of advanced level balletbarre exercises, adagio sequences and allegro enchainments.Style, perfection, and performance quality will be emphasized.
courses.prerequisiteText: Four hours of DANC 3663 and permission of department

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Ballet IV Lab
courses.description: An intensive physical laboratory course emphasizing specificity in skills, methods, and tools used for refinement in advanced ballet training is a companion course to Ballet IV. The laboratory experience focuses on mastering difficult skills in ballet training to acquire a kinesiological strong ballet technique and performance.

courses.subject: DANC
courses.title: Pointe IV and Variations
courses.description: Further practice of pointe technique, which is an extensions of ballet technique. Maintain strength and refine skills in performance of class exercises and variations from classical and contemporary ballet repertoire. Focus on performance qualities of artistry, interpretation, theatricality, stylistic elements, and musicality.
courses.course_objectives: By the end of this course, students will be able to perform ballet technique barre exercises on pointe with correct placement. By the end of this course, students will be able to execute exercises on pointe in the center with sustained balances. By the end of this course, students will be able to demonstrate confidence in knowledge of ballet vocabulary. By the end of this course, students will be able to knowledgeably discuss content, context, aesthetics and stylistic nuances of variations from the classical and contemporary ballet repertoire learned in class. By the end of this course, students will be able to perform combinations and variations on pointe with correct technique. By the end of this course, students will be able to display refined strength and control on pointe when dancing on pointe. By the end of this course, students will be able to perform variations with refined artistry, personal interpretation, theatricality, stylistic elements and musicality.
courses.topical_outline: Execute barre exercises that maintain strength on pointe and skills in ballet technique Perform complex center exercises on pointe, developing coordination, movement quality, and sustained steps on pointe Demonstrate proficiency in classical ballet vocabulary Embody and discuss theory of pointe technique skills (that extend from ballet technique) in classical and contemporary ballet movement, musicality and stylistic elements Practice performance elements of artistry, interpretation, theatricality, stylistic elements, and musicality Investigate and discuss content, context and stylistic elements of the choreography in variations from the classical ballet repertoire learned in class Practice and perform variations with refined skills, focusing on sustained steps on pointe with artistry, personal interpretation, theatricality stylistic elements, and musicality
courses.prerequisiteText: Two hours of DANC 3672 and permission of department
