courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Emerging Topics in Healthcare and Leadership
courses.description: Course leverages topics in current media, such as innovations in administration and care delivery, technology, regulations, and payer behavior, to identify emerging factors impacting healthcare organizations. Course is intended to support aspiring leaders identify credible information sources and recognize implications of forthcoming innovations on healthcare organizations.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to recognize and describe recent innovations in healthcare administration and care delivery. Students will be able to identify the benefits and challenges associated with new healthcare technologies. Students will be able to analyze the effects of recent regulatory changes on healthcare operations. Students will be able to describe how changes in healthcare financing and payer behavior impact strategic planning. Students will be able to apply critical thinking skills to determine the reliability and relevance of information.
courses.topical_outline: 1.	Recent innovations in healthcare administration and care delivery 2.	Finding and leveraging credible sources of healthcare information 3.	Critical thinking and information analysis 4.	Emerging trends in patient care delivery 5.	Integrating new healthcare practices and technologies 6.	Landscape of recent regulatory changes 7.	Trends in healthcare finance 8.	Strategies for continuous learning and professional development in healthcare

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Practice Management Consulting in Healthcare
courses.description: Practice management consulting skills and principles. Focuses on skills necessary to successfully complete a short-term consulting engagement with a physician practice. The students will gather data, research the problem, prepare a report, and present their report to the principals of the practice.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Economic Evaluation Methods in Health I
courses.description: Introduction to economic evaluation methods of healthcare and public health programs: cost analysis, cost-effectiveness analysis, and benefit-cost analysis. An emphasis on defining outcomes, policy implications, and appropriate use of the methods.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Economic Evaluation Methods in Health I
courses.description:
Introduction to economic evaluation methods of healthcare and public health programs: cost analysis, cost-effectiveness
analysis, and benefit-cost analysis. An emphasis on defining outcomes, policy implications, and appropriate use of the methods.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Economic Evaluation Methods in Health I Laboratory
courses.description: This lab complements the lecture portion, which includes an introduction to several methods for conducting economic evaluation of public health programs. A focus on the practical application of these methods in Excel and other programs.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Strategic Management and Marketing in Health Care Organizations
courses.description: Advanced concepts, principles, and practices involved in strategic management and marketing in healthcare. A case-based approach focused on the complex, real-world challenges encountered in both public and private healthcare settings will be employed. The course will address principles and methods of strategic assessment, strategy formulation, evaluation, implementation, and control.
courses.prerequisiteText: (HPAM 7250 or HPAM 7250E) and (HPAM 7550 or HPAM 7550E) and (HPAM 7650 or HPAM 7650E)

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Internship in Health Administration
courses.description: Practical experience in health administration through placement in appropriate field experiences. The internship is intended to provide students with opportunities to apply theories and techniques learned in the classroom to actual situations within the health care community and administrative work experience in a health care facility.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Professional Development Seminar in Health Administration I
courses.description: Seminar I focuses on resume building and development of interpersonal skills related to health administration, including interaction with faculty and community leaders for skill-building in resume writing, interviewing, and professional presentations.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Professional Development Seminar in Health Administration II
courses.description: Seminar II will build upon skills learned in Seminar I, with focus on development of professional ethics and leadership through interaction with faculty and community leaders and practice of these skills.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Professional Development Seminar in Health Administration III
courses.description: Seminar III will build upon skills learned in Seminars I and II, and will focus on career planning through portfolio design and development and job and administrative fellowship search skills.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Professional Development Seminar in Health Administration IV
courses.description: Seminar IV will build upon skills learned in Seminars I, II, and III. This seminar is focused on preparing students to transition into careers in healthcare. Topics covered include job applications, strategic networking, and executive presence.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to identify and apply to positions in healthcare. Students will be able to develop and refine industry-appropriate resumes and cover letters. Students will be able to demonstrate written and oral communication skills appropriate for professional settings. Students will be able to utilize networking strategies to build relationships with healthcare professionals.
courses.topical_outline: 1.	Mastering job applications 2.	Strategic networking in healthcare 3.	Developing and demonstrating executive presence 4.	Continuous professional development

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Capstone Project in Health Administration
courses.description: Course covers advanced strategic management in healthcare using a case-based approach. It addresses strategic assessment, formulation, evaluation, implementation, and control. The course culminates in a capstone project where students apply MHA competencies to analyze and develop recommendations to address a complex healthcare challenge.
courses.course_objectives: Students will evaluate concepts acquired from previous courses and apply them to a project. Students will integrate and apply prior knowledge of management techniques to develop appropriate strategies or solutions. Students will formulate and deliver results of organizational analyses in a professional manner.
courses.topical_outline: Proposal Development Project Management Research and Analysis Professionalism and Ethics

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Directed Research in Health Policy and Management
courses.description: Individual research under the direction of a department facultymember.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Advanced Service-Learning in Health Policy and Management
courses.description: Students will apply health policy and management methods andapplications in one or more public health related settingsthrough participation in a collaborative health policy andmanagement project within the public health community.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: HSR PhD Doctoral Seminar I
courses.description: This seminar is organized as a series of public health relevant research presentations by faculty members and other researchers. Each week, one researcher presents a research topic of interest. Each presentation provides an introductory overview of the research with specific aims, conceptual model, and research strategy.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to identify the types of public health research relevant for health services research areas. Students will be able to describe and explain the approaches followed to develop a research project in health services research area. Students will be able to explain the basic components of research proposals, from background to interpretation of results. Students will be able to discuss empirical research for policy analysis.
courses.topical_outline: 1.	Examples of health services research relevant for improving access and quality of healthcare services locally, nationally and internationally 2.	How to write the rationale for a research study 3.	Developing the specific aims for different types of studies and how the specific aims are linked with the research strategy 4.	Translating the research strategy into empirically variable approaches 5.	Empirical results of each of the studies and interpretation of results 6.	Derivation of policy implications and conclusions

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: HSR PhD Doctoral Seminar II
courses.description: This seminar is the second of four seminar courses required for the PhD in Health Services Research. In the course, students will review specific aims from faculty that have presented in seminar I and develop their own specific aims towards developing a research proposal across the three seminars.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to conduct literature reviews in the field of health services research. Students will be able to discuss approaches to develop literature reviews into systematic reviews. Students will be able to identify gaps in scientific literature. Students will be able to develop research questions, study aims, and hypotheses.
courses.topical_outline: 1. Introduction to the seminar and seminar sequence in the series 2. Approaches to literature review and types of literature 3. Synthesize literature 4. Identify confirmatory vs exploratory research 5. Develop research questions and hypothesis 6. Draft conceptual framework and develop research strategy 7. Identify analytic strategies and available datasets 8. Develop research aims (realistic, achievable)

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: HSR PhD Doctoral Seminar III
courses.description: This seminar is the third of four seminars required for the PhD in Health Services Research. The seminar will focus on how to write the background of the research question and create the conceptual framework. A few frameworks will be reviewed throughout the seminar.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to identify gaps in the research area chosen. Students will be able to describe conceptual frameworks. Students will be able to develop a conceptual framework for their dissertation.
courses.topical_outline: 1. Recap of Seminar I and Seminar II 2. Review of specific aims and hypothesis 3. What is a conceptual framework? 4. What are the commonly used conceptual frameworks? 5. Conceptual frameworks for the topics identified in previous semesters 6. Reading literature with and without a conceptual framework

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: HSR PH.D. Doctoral Seminar IV
courses.description: Students will focus on how to write the approach for the research question they have identified in Seminar I, developed in Seminar II, and finalized with conceptual framework in Seminar III. The final product of Seminar IV will be a National Institute of Health type R03 proposal.
courses.course_objectives: Students will apply a research design that is best suited for the research question. Students will identify strengths limitations and relevance of the study. Students will develop a grant proposal and defend their proposal in a peer review process.
courses.topical_outline: Identify research designs Draft research proposals Critically peer review proposals Present and received feedback on proposals

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Research Methods in Health Policy
courses.description: Focuses on the practice of research with an emphasis on topics relevant in the field of health policy. Topics include a review of empirical techniques, the tools for understanding and critically assessing the literature, and the tools for conducting original research.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Research Methods in Health Policy
courses.description: Focuses on the practice of research with an emphasis on topics relevant in the field of health policy. Topics include a review of empirical techniques, the tools for understanding and critically assessing the literature, and the tools for conducting original research.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Survey Research Methods in Health Policy and Management
courses.description: An introduction to principles of survey design that are the basis of standard practices in the field.  There is a strong emphasis on surveys and design principles used when collecting health related data.  The rheoretical, empirical, and applied literature related to survey methodology will be examined.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Programming for Health Services Research
courses.description: Course focuses on analyzing commonly used health services research data sources to derive policy-relevant results. The programming language may differ based on specific type of health services research questions being addressed. It is designed to enhance students’ ability to manipulate, analyze, and interpret complex health data for policy evaluations.
courses.course_objectives: Students will describe the general structure and common characteristics of secondary data sources, including survey, census, and administrative data. Students will identify datasets that align with specific research topics and study objectives. Students will clean, organize, and manage data using statistical software. Students will construct outcome variables, exposure variables, and covariates, transforming variables as appropriate for analysis. Students will develop an analytic file that is well-organized and optimized for empirical analysis. Students will conduct diagnostics to assess data quality. Students will generate visualizations to explore data patterns and illustrate study hypotheses. Students will perform descriptive and multivariate regression analyses. Students will interpret outputs and effectively communicate statistical results in both written and oral formats.
courses.topical_outline:
Understanding secondary data sources Structure and key variables in:
•	Survey data •	Area-level data •	Provider-level data •	Claims data •	Firm-/plan-level data Statistical software programming and data management
•	Data cleaning, variable creation, and constructing analytic files •	Pooling data across multiple years •	Merging datasets using common identifiers •	Aggregating data at various levels •	Running diagnostics to identify data quality issues •	Data visualization techniques •	Handling missing data •	Generating summary statistics with survey weights •	Conducting multivariate regression analyses •	Exporting regression outputs

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Social Determinants of Health and Health Disparities
courses.description: Analysis of the social determinants of health and health disparities, focusing on economic, social, and policy factors related to the population health and health disparities in the United States. Provides a strong foundation in the methodology to measure and quantify the impact of social determinants of health and health disparities.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Social Determinants of Health and Health Disparities
courses.description: Analysis of the social determinants of health and health disparities, focusing on economic, social, and policy factors related to the population health and health disparities in the United States. Provides a strong foundation in the methodology to measure and quantify the impact of social determinants of health and health disparities.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Research Methods II
courses.description: Introduction to empirical methods used in health services research. Topics include models for skewed positive outcomes and binary or categorical outcomes, models to identify causal effects including difference-in-differences, matching, instrumental variables, regression discontinuity, and hands-on programming exercises to implement the methods learned using data and statistical software.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to describe various quantitative methods commonly used in health services research. Students will be able to implement methods using statistical software. Students will be able to compare analytic approaches used in peer-reviewed articles. Students will be able to develop a proposal based on research interests. Students will be able to identify relevant datasets and assess the structure and quality of the data. Students will be able to apply appropriate quantitative methods in the final research project. Students will be able to interpret results for diverse audiences in both written and oral formats.
courses.topical_outline:
1.	Introduction to quantitative analysis and statistical software 2.	Review of regression analysis 3.	Extension of linear regression models:
a.	Generalized linear models
b.	Heterogenous effects and quantile regression models 4.	Models for limited dependent variables:
a.	Logit, probit for binary outcomes
b.	Multinomial probit, ordered logit for categorical outcomes
c.	Poisson, negative binomial regression models for count data
d.	Log transformation, two-part models for cost data 5.	Methods for causal inference:
a.	Difference-in-differences
b.	Matching
c.	Instrumental variables
d.	Regression discontinuity

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Advanced Policy Analysis in Public Health
courses.description: In-depth analysis of major health politics and policy issues confronted by a broad spectrum of public and private sectors. Provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the theoretical and practical basis for the development and analysis of policies for the improvement of health in a variety of health care settings.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Advanced Health Informatics
courses.description: Examination of informatics in the U.S. healthcare environment, data security and privacy, informatics terminology and technology, data standards, and health data sets. In this doctoral-level course, students receive hands-on experience with primary data. Students will analyze de-identified data sets, utilizing data visualization software. Students will also create unique management operations plans from their results, and present their comprehensive plans to their peers.
courses.prerequisiteText: [(HPAM 7010 or HPAM 7010E) and (BIOS 7010 or BIOS 7010E) and HPAM 7700] or permission of department

courses.title: Advanced Policy Evaluation in Public Health
courses.description: The field of policy evaluation from a public health perspective. Provides a survey of standard quantitative and qualitative techniques for prospectively analyzing health policy issues, including multi-criteria decision making, benefit-cost and cost-effectiveness analyses, and political analysis.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Advanced Policy Evaluation in Public Health
courses.description: The field of policy evaluation from a public health perspective. Provides a survey of standard quantitative and qualitative techniques for prospectively analyzing health policy issues, including multi-criteria decision making, benefit-cost and cost- effectiveness analyses, and political analysis.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Advanced Health Economics
courses.description: Applies economics theory in health, health care, and health policy with an emphasis on core themes applicable to health economics. Lectures will include economic evaluation, demand for health care, insurance markets, asymmetric information, managed care, hospital and pharmaceutical industry, and governmental role.

courses.subject: HPAM

courses.description: Applies economics theory in health, health care, and health policy with an emphasis on core themes applicable to health economics. courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Politics of Disease Control
courses.description: Students develop tools for identifying and explaining the rolesthat political institutions and actors play in controllingdisease. Through a detailed exploration of contemporary andhistorical examples, students will be able to articulate thesystematic impact of politics on attempts to control diseasearound the globe.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Healthcare Finance
courses.description: Introduction to financial management, financial analysis,and financial decision-making within the healthcare environment.Basic financial management concepts will be explored to answerquestions such as which projects to finance, how to financeshort-term operations, and how to finance long-term projectswithin the healthcare setting.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Advanced Management of Public Health Organizations
courses.description: Public health professionals assume leadership roles in organizations where they are responsible for planning, organizing, staffing, coordinating, reporting, and budgeting of activities. This course is designed to stimulate critical thinking about modern public health administrative issues, address DrPH core competencies, and develop selected management techniques and perspectives.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Public Health Law and Ethics for Public Health Practitioners
courses.description: Strengthens students' and practitioners’ knowledge on current and foundational issues in law and ethics that impact the policies and practice of public health. Allows students to identify and appropriately assess legal, ethical, and human rights issues that underlie the field of public health.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Public Health Law and Ethics for Public Health Practitioners
courses.description: Strengthens students' and practitioners’ knowledge on current and foundational issues in law and ethics that impact the policies and practice of public health. Allows students to identify and appropriately assess legal, ethical, and human rights issues that underlie the field of public health.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Leadership in Public Health
courses.description: Designed to develop leadership competencies relevant for work in healthcare institutions by introducing major theories and concepts of leadership, ways of applying these to public health issues, and providing opportunities for students to develop skills and resources to further develop their own and others’ leadership.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Leadership in Public Health
courses.description: Designed to develop leadership competencies relevant for work in healthcare institutions by introducing major theories and concepts of leadership, ways of applying these to public health issues, and providing opportunities for students to develop skills and resources to further develop their own and others' leadership.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Health Policy Planning and Evaluation
courses.description: Introduces the skills and techniques required to research and develop health policy and programmatic initiatives in national and state systems and at the community level. Students will be presented with concepts, processes, and techniques used in health policy planning and will engage in various planning exercises.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Health Policy Planning and Evaluation
courses.description: Introduces the skills and techniques required to research and develop health policy and programmatic initiatives in national and state systems and at the community level. Students will be presented with concepts, processes, and techniques used in health policy planning and will engage in various planning exercises.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Managerial Epidemiology for Public Health Practitioners
courses.description: Designed to apply epidemiological principles and tools to decision-making in a healthcare environment. Builds upon fundamental epidemiologic principles and theory and enables students to develop advanced knowledge in statistics, population health management, and assessment of medical care processes and outcomes in public health services.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Managerial Epidemiology for Public Health Practitioners
courses.description: Designed to apply epidemiological principles and tools to decision-making in a healthcare environment. Builds upon fundamental epidemiologic principles and theory and enables students to develop advanced knowledge in statistics, population health management, and assessment of medical care processes and outcomes in public health services.

courses.description: Introduction to economic evaluation methods of health care and public health programs: cost analysis, cost-effectiveness analysis, and benefit-cost analysis. Includes an emphasis on defining outcomes, policy implications, and appropriate use of the methods.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Economic Evaluation Methods in Health
courses.description: Introduction to economic evaluation methods of health care and public health programs: cost analysis, cost-effectiveness analysis, and benefit-cost analysis. Includes an emphasis on defining outcomes, policy implications, and appropriate use of the methods.

courses.title: Economic Evaluation Methods in Health Lab
courses.description: This lab complements the lecture portion, which includes an introduction to several methods for conducting economic evaluation of public health programs. A focus on the practical application of these methods in Excel and other programs.

courses.subject: HPAM
courses.title: Decision Analysis and Economic Evaluation in Health
courses.description: This course presents the analytic tools of decision analysis foruse in economic evaluations in health care and public health.Development of different modeling strategies will be introduced,including decision trees, state-transition models, and discreteevent simulation. Application of the methods in Excel and otherprograms will also be included.

Development of different modeling strategies will be introduced, including decision trees, state-transition models, and discrete event simulation. Application of the methods in Excel and other programs will also be included.

courses.subject: HPRB(BIOS)
courses.title: Multivariate Statistics in the Behavioral Health Sciences
courses.description: In-depth coverage of multivariate analysis of variance; multivariate analysis of covariance; binary and multinomial logistic regression; factor analysis; discriminant function analysis; path analysis; and structural equation modeling. Using SPSS and “real-world” datasets, students in the public health, behavioral, and social sciences will apply techniques to “real-world” datasets.

courses.subject: HPRB
courses.title: Health and Wellness
courses.description: Factors affecting the level of wellness of the individual are considered.  Topics include mental health, nutrition, diet and weight control, physical fitness, smoking, human sexuality, consumer health, alcohol and other drugs, disease, environmental health, and injury prevention.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to define health and wellness, social determinants of health, sustainability, and public health. Students will be able to identify aspects of the environment that affect health. Students will be able to discuss basic information on current health issues. Students will be able to identify behaviors that are detrimental to health and discuss their short-term and long-term effects. Students will be able to explore attitudes, values, and beliefs about health and lifestyle. Students will be able to identify and use reliable sources of health information. Students will be able to identify local, state, national, and global health promotion organizations. Students will be able to present current and accurate information to facilitate health decision-making.

courses.subject: HPRB
courses.title: Health Promotion in Public Health
courses.description: Examination of health promotion in the field of public health.  History, role in society, resources, theoretical underpinnings,ethical principles, and planning.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to describe the role of health promotion and behavior in public health and in the health of our society. Students will be able to discuss the history of health promotion and public health. Students will be able to explain the theoretical bases for health promotion programming and discuss application for health promotion. Students will be able to identify sources of health disparity and possible methods to reduce disparity. Students will be able to explain ethical principles as applied to health promotion. Students will be able to explain the importance of research, needs assessment, planning and evaluation in health promotion. Students will be able to examine the influence of media, communication, and marketing on health promotion issues.
courses.topical_outline: Historical perspective on health promotion. Current societal needs and health problems. The concept of health in our society. Behavioral science, social science, and public health. Ethics in public health practice. Health determinants and the ecology of health and disease. Theoretical perspectives: the health and behavior interface.

courses.subject: HPRB
courses.title: Women's Health
courses.description: Explores health concerns of individuals identifying as women across the lifespan, with focus on social and environmental factors impacting well-being. Ideal for future professionals in fields such as public health, healthcare, psychology, social work, education, and law. This course provides insights for those seeking to promote health for women.
courses.course_objectives: Students will compare and contrast gender, race, and class differences in morbidity, mortality, and the prevalence of chronic conditions. Students will investigate specific health concerns of the birth experience, discuss issues surrounding high-risk pregnancies, and examine the health effects and outcomes of reproductive technologies associated with infertility. Students will discuss issues surrounding the health concerns of women across the lifespan (adolescence - elderly). Students will identify symptoms and discuss treatment options for reproductive system disorders, disorders of the breasts, nutritional disorders, and illnesses common to women (diabetes, systemic lupus, erythematosus, multiple sclerosis, rheumatoid arthritis).
courses.topical_outline: Introduction and Overview Taking Care of Ourselves Sexuality, Sexual Health, and Controlling our Fertility Women's Health Issues in Perspective Synthesis and Reflection

courses.subject: HPRB
courses.title: Rural and Frontier Health
courses.description: Course introduces students to the unique dynamics of health within rural communities. Topics include rural and frontier culture, rural health needs, rural-specific determinants of health, and the rural healthcare system. Students will learn the contextual and social/structural attributes of rural communities and the effects on individual and population health.
courses.course_objectives: Students will compare and contrast the terms rural, frontier, and urban. Students will explain the process of classifying rural, frontier, and urban designations. Students will identify risk factors and health issues related specifically to rural populations. Students will examine the predominant health issues faced in rural settings. Students will describe the historical and current conditions that affect health in rural communities. Students will discuss the unique challenges of rural populations related to workforce, ethics, economics, environment, behavior, and access to care. Students will summarize the unique aspects of rural culture that affect the ways in which rural residents seek, achieve, and maintain health and wellbeing. Students will examine and explain evidence-based solutions to challenges related to rural health. Students will relate health issues to the ways in which the healthcare and preventive health system operate within rural areas. Students will discuss future directions related to rural/frontier health.
courses.topical_outline: What is rural/frontier health? History of health in rural/frontier communities Barriers and access to care in rural areas Public health workforce issues in rural areas Ethical issues in rural communities Rural health research & data Mental health in rural areas Integrated care in rural areas Substance use and abuse in rural areas HIV in rural areas Heart disease, diabetes, and obesity in rural areas Maternal and child health in rural areas Environmental and occupational health in rural areas Farmers and migrant farmworker health in rural areas Aging in rural areas

courses.subject: HPRB
courses.title: Health and Technology
courses.description: This course delves into the human technology interaction, exploring the range of its implications on the individual, community, and society. This course covers essential topics such as: Person and technology, Technology adoption frameworks, Emerging and existing technologies (e.g., robotics, AI), focusing on both practical application and ethical considerations.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to describe health technology and application of various types of information communication technologies (e.g., telepresence, socially assistive robots) to support individual, community, and societal health. Students will be able to identify ways that technology supports access to community resources. Students will be able to identify the impact of local, state, and national policy on the use and implementation of health technologies. Students will be able to recommend the application of health technologies to develop and support interventions and programs. Students will be able to identify the implications of technology adoption to facilitate equitable access to resources and services. Students will be able identify the role of existing and emerging technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence, social media) in advancing health behaviors and monitoring. Students will be able to describe the safety and security implications of health technologies.
courses.topical_outline: Person and technology Technology adoption frameworks Health technologies Telepresence Robotics Artificial Intelligence Social Media Extended reality Smart home technologies Community and technology Policy and technology Technology based interventions and programs Diversity and disparity in health technology Infodemiology and infoveillance Safety and security

courses.subject: HPRB
courses.title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research I
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, and synthesize and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to identify and test questions, hypotheses, or problems drawn from concepts in their discipline. Students will be able to plan and execute a research project of their choice. Students will be able to apply basic research techniques and methods to a topic of their choice. Students will be able to manage research according to the highest ethical standards. Students will be able to demonstrate how a research program is organized and carried out. Students will be able to demonstrate professional communication through written and verbal participation in laboratory, academic, or professional meetings or conferences.
courses.topical_outline: Students must apply through a sponsoring faculty member to conduct research. courses.title: Program Evaluation in Health Promotion and Health Education
courses.description: Introduction to strategies for evaluating health promotion and health education programs in community, worksite, school and health care settings.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to describe the purpose of evaluation for health promotion, health behavior, and public health interventions. Students will be able to describe the major characteristic of health promotion and public health policy, and select appropriate evaluation objectives. Students will be able to define the role of stakeholders, decision-makers, and target populations in the needs assessment process. Students will be able to describe methods for monitoring program coverage, reach, and fidelity of implementation. Students will be able to identify appropriate strategies for health-related interventions as they related to primary, secondary, and tertiary prevention. Students will be able to identify various evaluation designs, their characteristics, strengths, and limitations. Students will be able to choose appropriate data collection methods (qualitative and quantitative) for health-related outcomes. Students will be able to identify strengths and offer constructive criticism on a health promotion program evaluation proposal. Students will be able to choose appropriate statistical methods to assess behavioral health and other health outcomes. Students will be able to identify key issues related to the evaluation of health behavior programs targeting high risk and underserved populations. Students will be able to identify human subject issues, budget requirements, and write a complete proposal for an evaluation of health promotion program.

Specific topics will include theoretical frameworks for innovation and problem-solving, process models for understanding and addressing business or organizational challenges, and strategies/tactics for implementing innovative solutions. The course places a heavy emphasis on consultative approaches and experiential learning through site visits, case studies, or invited speakers.

Current persistent, epidemic, and emerging diseases and how they are identified, studied, and combatted will be discussed.  Topics will also include the sociological, psychological, historical, legal, environmental, and economic implications of disease.

courses.description: Delivers an in-depth comprehension of specially selected areas of vector ecology and emerging vector-borne diseases. Emphasis will be placed on arthropod vectors such as mosquitoes and pathogens of medical and veterinary importance.
courses.course_objectives: Students will read and present primary scientific research articles on vector-borne diseases and vector ecology. Students will name important arthropod vectors, their ecologies, and pathogen associations. Students will contrast differences in pathogen transmission cycles and implications for combatting vector-borne diseases. Students will evaluate and critique emerging topics and recent publications in vector borne disease. Students will evaluate and critique responses to current outbreaks. Students will develop ideas that build on current work to address emerging vector-borne disease issues.
courses.topical_outline: TOP 1) Vector biology TOP 2) Vector ecology TOP 3) Vector-pathogen associations TOP 4) Pathogen transmissions cycles TOP 5) Pathogen transmission cycle disruption TOP 6) How to read and evaluate primary research articles on vector-borne diseases TOP 7) Review/discuss articles on vector-borne diseases TOP 8) Review/discuss articles on vector-borne disease outbreaks

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Infectious Disease Treatment and Prevention
courses.description: This course will equip students with a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental principles regarding the treatment and prevention of infectious diseases. Students will explore essential concepts related to vaccines and various treatment modalities, including antibiotics, antifungals, antiparasitic, and antivirals. Students will acquire the necessary knowledge to approach infectious diseases with informed and effective strategies.
courses.course_objectives: Students will identify major classes of antibiotics, antivirals, antifungals, and antiparasitics and their mechanisms of action. Students will interpret antimicrobial susceptibility data (e.g., MIC, disk diffusion assays). Students will explain the molecular and evolutionary basis of antimicrobial resistance. Students will explain the principles behind vaccination, including types of vaccines and immune responses elicited. Students will evaluate infection control measures (e.g., isolation, hand hygiene, sterilization, PPE use). Students will analyze real-world public health interventions (e.g., outbreak containment, contact tracing, prophylaxis). Students will assess the impact of social determinants, globalization, and climate change on infectious disease dynamics. Students will critically evaluate emerging infectious threats and pandemic preparedness strategies. Students will propose evidence-based interventions for managing an outbreak or controlling disease spread. Students will discuss ethical issues in infectious disease management (e.g., vaccine equity, antimicrobial stewardship).
courses.topical_outline: 1.	Viral Vaccines 2.	Bacterial, Parasitic, and Fungal Vaccines 3.	Antibiotics and antifungals 4.	Antivirals and Antiparasitics
courses.prerequisiteText: [(BIOL 1103 or BIOL 1103E or BIOL 2103H or BIOL 2103S) and (BIOL 1103L or BIOL 1113E)] or [(BIOL 1107 or BIOL 1107E or BIOL 2107H) and (BIOL 1107L or BIOL 2107L)]

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Exploration of Infectious Diseases
courses.description: Current research by Infectious Disease Faculty on the physiology of bacterial, viral, fungal, and parasitic pathogens, host-pathogen interactions, and the management of infectious diseases. Students will learn about current infectious disease research occurring on UGA campus.
courses.course_objectives: Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to describe experimental approaches to understand elements of infectious disease, ranging from how a microbial pathogen spreads through tissues of an infected host to modeling the global spread of pathogens in a pandemic. Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to describe and appraise the ways in which infectious disease research and information are translated for the general public. Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to defend and support their own conclusions on the importance of infectious disease research by analyzing all learned viewpoints with sound reasoning and judgment.
courses.topical_outline: 1.	Bacterial Infectious Disease Research 2.	Viral Infectious Disease Research 3.	Parasite Infectious Disease Research 4.	Infectious Disease Immunology Research 5.	Research on Infectious Disease Vectors 6.	Fungal Infectious Disease Research

courses.description: Analysis and presentation of primary research articles on infectious diseases, including microbial pathogen biology, pathogen-host interactions, disease transmission, and medical interventions.
courses.course_objectives: Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to think about and arrive at their own conclusions regarding how basic infectious disease research is conducted, the pros and cons related to animal models of disease versus in vitro experiments, the requirements needed to complete studies safely, and how basic research can be translated into treatments and vaccines in the clinic. Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to interpret and explain basic infectious disease data and literature. Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to critically evaluate conclusions and predictions by researchers based on published approaches and data.
courses.topical_outline: 1.	Critical reading of primary research articles 2.	Effective communication and presentation of scientific concepts, methods, data, and interpretations. 3.	Active participation in scientific discussions 4.	Bacterial Infectious Disease Research 5.	Viral Infectious Disease Research 6.	Parasite Infectious Disease Research 7.	Immunity to Infectious Disease Studies 8.	Vectors of Infectious Disease Research 9.	Fungal Infectious Disease Research

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Bugs and Drugs: Biomedical Applications of Beneficial Microorganisms
courses.description: While microorganisms (bacteria, fungi, viruses) are often associated with disease, microbes can also promote good health in humans and animals. The purpose of this course is to develop an understanding as to how microorganisms, both naturally occurring and genetically modified, can be used to detect, treat, and prevent diseases.
courses.course_objectives: At the completion of this course, students should be able to distinguish between genetic, physiological, and structural features of microorganisms to differentiate between their roles in providing health benefits vs. contributing to disease processes. At the completion of this course, students should be able to demonstrate how different disease processes (e.g., infectious vs. non-infectious) respond to therapeutic approaches afforded by live biotherapeutic products in the development of new intervention strategies. At the completion of this course, students should be able to compare the advantages and disadvantages, including ethical considerations, of using live biotherapeutic products vs. more traditional drug treatment regimens for treatment of specific diseases. At the completion of this course, students should be able to design a microbial system (e.g., bacteria, yeast, or virus) that could be engineered or modified with new or refined features (e.g., genes encoding new therapeutic products, genetic elements that control their expression) to detect, diagnose, or treat a specific disease.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: An individualized research project under the guidance of afaculty mentor within a research laboratory on campus thatconducts infectious disease research. How to conduct and documentscientific experiments.  The risks and appropriate precautions towork safely within that particular laboratory environment.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research I
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, and synthesize and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research II
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, and synthesize and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research III
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, and synthesize and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Undergraduate Research Thesis (or Final Project)
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, and synthesize and interpret data. Students will write or produce a thesis or other professional capstone product, such as a report or portfolio that describes their systematic and in-depth inquiry.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Veterinary Bacteriology and Mycology
courses.description: Basic properties of microorganisms. The pathogenic mechanisms and the diseases caused by bacteria.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Veterinary Virology
courses.description: The important, clinically-relevant concepts about the basic nature of viruses, such as their biological processes, the diseases they cause in animals, and the methods of diagnosis and control of viral disease.  An attempt is made to cover the more important veterinary viral diseases, and those that represent instructive examples of basic concepts in viral disease.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Veterinary Immunology
courses.description: Provides veterinary students with a basic knowledge of the mechanisms of immunity in animals. Components of the immune system are described, including the different types of immune responses and the mechanisms by which the immune system provides protection against foreign invaders. The consequences of exaggerated immunity, the failure of immunoregulation, and the factors affecting immune responses to vaccines will also be covered.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Veterinary Parasitology
courses.description: Parasitic helminths, protozoa, and arthropods are studied on the basis of taxonomy, morphology, life cycle, and pathological manifestations.  A brief comprehensive overview of parasite diagnosis, treatment, and control is also provided.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Large Animal Parasitology
courses.description: Biology, epidemiology, and control of clinically important parasites of ruminants, horses, and swine.  Emphasis is placed on clinical and diagnostic issues relating to host-parasite interactions and the development of parasite control programs.  Laboratory portion will emphasize diagnostic methods, interpretation of laboratory results, and problem solving.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Special Topics in Public Health, Community Engagement, and Service-Learning in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: Introduction to concepts of service-learning and community engagement to develop positive professional attitudes that encompass cultural competencies, utilize professional skills and knowledge in addressing community needs, with emphasis on local under-serviced societal segments. Emphasis on “One Health” concepts and initiatives that pertain to service-learning objectives.
courses.prerequisiteText: Enrollment in the third year of the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine curriculum

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Veterinary Emergency Response and Preparedness
courses.description: Introduces students to veterinary emergency preparedness and response principles that may be applied at personal, community, State, and Federal levels. It will also provide students with the knowledge, skills, and abilities to help respond to various types of emergencies, including natural and man-made disasters.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Clinical Parasitology for Companion Animals
courses.description: This course will expand on foundational knowledge. Biology, diagnostics, treatment, and management of clinically important parasites of nonproduction, companion animals seen in mixed animal practice (dogs, cats, small ruminants, swine, horses). Client communication and parasiticide management will be covered, including a Spectrum of Care approach to parasite control.
courses.course_objectives: By the end of the course, students will be able to prevent, diagnose, and treat parasitic infections of companion animals (dog, cat, small ruminant, pet swine, horses). By the end of the course, students will be able to apply appropriate strategic control programs tailored to the needs of individual animals and companion animals in group settings (kennels, shelters, barns).
courses.topical_outline: Course introduction Host-parasite interactions Diagnostic parasitology, including novel testing modalities Antiparasitic drugs and combatting anthelmintic resistance Principles of parasite control to prevent infection and disease, including best practices for animal relocations and travel Spectrum of Care and risk-based recommendations for the management of parasitic diseases
courses.prerequisiteText: Enrollment in the third year of the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine curriculum

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Studies in Advanced Clinical Parasitology
courses.description: A clinical rotation for veterinary students who wish to honetheir clinical parasitology skills.  The topical focus of eachrotation is tailored to the enrolled student's career objectivesand may focus on issues important in the understanding ofparasites of small animals, exotics, and/or large animals.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Special Topics in Infectious Diseases
courses.description: Intensive and in-depth studies into specially designated areas ofinfectious diseases.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Master's Research
courses.description: Research while enrolled for a master's degree under the direction of faculty members.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Master's Thesis
courses.description: Thesis writing under the direction of the major professor.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Advanced Studies in Infectious Diseases
courses.description: Analysis of various infectious disease agents, including representative helminths, protozoa, fungi, bacteria, viruses, and prions. The epidemiology, pathogenesis, host immune response, disease transmission, treatment, and control will be presented for each highlighted infectious disease.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Vaccines: From Design to Development
courses.description: Modern approaches to design and development of vaccines for parasites, viral, and bacterial infections. Modern approaches to developing therapeutic vaccines for cancers and infectious diseases. The logistical and regulatory hurdles in taking a vaccine from concept to market.
courses.prerequisiteText: [(CBIO(MBIO)(IDIS) 4100/6100 or BCMB 4010/6010 or BCMB 4020/6020) and GENE(BIOL) 3200] or permission of department

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Parasites and Parasitic Diseases
courses.description: The pathology, cellular, and molecular biology of protozoan and metazoan parasites that cause disease in humans and animals, with current topics and controversies in animal and human parasitology. Modern advances in fundamental knowledge as well as control will be discussed. Specific topics will be examined in-depth in student-led sessions.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Problems in Parasitology
courses.description: Parasitic diseases of birds and mammals. Nature of the studies determined by the student's major field of interest.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Special Topics in Ecology and Evolution of Infectious Diseases
courses.description: This journal club will expose students to contemporary issues centered on ecological and evolutionary perspectives of infectious disease science. Students will present and discusspublished research articles relevant to ecology and evolution of infectious diseases.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Advanced Molecular Techniques
courses.description: Current techniques in molecular analysis of pathogens.  Emphasisis placed on bioinformatics and procedures for genomic analysis,rapid isolation and characterization of parasite molecules, andthe detection and identification of parasites in host vector.
courses.offeredText: Offered summer semester every even-numbered year.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Seminar in Infectious Diseases
courses.description: Semi-formal meetings for discussion of research and new developments in the field.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Research in Progress Seminar
courses.description: Semi-formal meetings for presentation and discussion of graduatestudent research.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Infectious Diseases Grant Writing
courses.description: This course introduces the fundamentals of developing, writing, and submitting research grant applications. Students will identify a study section, analyze its funding history, and draft targeted specific aims. The final product is a complete proposal. Focus areas include graduate fellowships and R21-scale grants. No prior experience required; active research engagement expected.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to describe the key elements of basic NIH and NSF grants. Students will be able to construct and support an NIH R21 style grant based on their current research project. Students will be able to critically evaluate peer grants and provide constructive critiques.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Special Topics in Parasitology
courses.description: Published research and new developments in the study of parasites, their hosts and vectors.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to confidently evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of research studies presented, identify potential biases or limitations in the study design, methods, and data interpretation. Students will be able to summarize and discuss key findings of recent research studies and relate them to the existing knowledge in the field. Students will be able to articulate their opinions and engage in thoughtful discussions about implications of research findings in the selected journal articles. Students will be able to clearly and concisely present the key aspects of a research paper and communicate its significance to audience of peers. Students will be able to engage in respectful and constructive discussions with peers and mentors.
courses.topical_outline: The topics will be current parasitic pathogenesis.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Advanced Immunology: Innate Immunity
courses.description: Provides an in-depth look at selected aspects of the innate immune response, including the cellular and molecular components critical to its development. The course will focus on fundamental discoveries and recent advances. Some selected topics will include Toll-like receptor signaling, the inflammasome, neutrophil NETosis, dendritic cells as antigen presenting cells, newly identified innate cell types, and innate immunity in disease.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Principles and Research Applications of Flow Cytometry
courses.description: Theory and research applications of flow cytometry.  Flow cytometry as it relates to immunophenotyping, cell cycle analysis, determination of cellular pathology of apoptosis as well as simultaneous four color analysis will be covered.  Students will become independent regarding instrumentation, collection of data, analysis, etc.  Additionally, students will be expected to carry out independent laboratory projects as well as participate in laboratory assignments.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Special Topics in Virology
courses.description: Discussion of current primary literature related to all topics in virology from structure, replication, pathogenesis, and more.

Students will be able to articulate their opinions and engage in thoughtful discussions about implications of research findings in the selected journal articles. Students will be able to clearly and concisely present the key aspects of a research paper and communicate its significance to audience of peers. Students will be able to engage in respectful and constructive discussions with peers and mentors.
courses.topical_outline: The topic will be current virology.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Special Topics in Structural Immunology
courses.description: Presentation and discussion of published research and new developments in structural immunology. Students will sign up to present published articles relevant in structural immunology.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to confidently evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of research studies presented, identify potential biases or limitations in the study design, methods, and data interpretation. Students will be able to summarize and discuss key findings of recent research studies and relate them to the existing knowledge in the field. Students will be able to articulate their opinions and engage in thoughtful discussions about implications of research findings in the selected journal articles. Students will be able to clearly and concisely present the key aspects of a research paper and communicate its significance to audience of peers. courses.topical_outline: The topics will be current in structural immunology, with particular focus on adaptive immunity to viral and bacterial pathogens.

courses.description: Presentation and discussion of published research and newdevelopments in bacterial pathogenesis. Students will sign up topresent a published article relevant in bacterial pathogenesis.This course is one component of the Department of InfectiousDiseases required journal club series.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Special Topics in Immunology
courses.description: Presentation and discussion of published research and new developments in immunology.  Students will sign up to present a published article relevant in immunology.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Special Topics on Diseases Intervention
courses.description: Presentation and discussion of novel research papers on disease intervention strategies.  Students will present topics of study on infectious disease immunology for discussion and interpretation.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to confidently evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of research studies presented, identify potential biases or limitations in the study design, methods, and data interpretation. courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Advanced Concepts of Virology
courses.description: Conveys the basic principles of virus biology and illustrates key concepts in the virus-host interaction, including virus replication, pathogenesis of diseases, and host response to viral infection. Much of the course will rely on the unifying principles of viruses and utilize key examples of well-studied viruses.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to summarize and explain current methods used in virus-related research articles. Students will be able to critically analyze and evaluate results in current virus-related research articles. Students will be able to discuss and apply their understanding of current virus-related research articles to their own research interests.
courses.topical_outline: Foundations of Virology Classifications, Virus Cultivation, Detection, and Genetics Virus Structure Virus Attachment and Entry Intracellular Transport of Virus RNA Virus Replication DNA Virus Replication Virus Assembly and Maturation Viral Transformation and Oncogenesis Prevention and Control I: Antivirals, Novel Therapies Prevention and Control II: Vaccinations Pathogenesis Virus-specific Presentations

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Clinical Microbiology Residency I
courses.description: Training during the first year of a residency for graduateveterinarians desiring specialization in Clinical Microbiology.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Clinical Microbiology Residency II
courses.description: Training during the second year of a residency for graduateveterinarians desiring specialization in Clinical Microbiology.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Clinical Microbiology Residency III
courses.description: Training during the third year of a residency for graduateveterinarians desiring specialization in Clinical Microbiology.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Manuscript Writing
courses.description: Scientific writing techniques, literature retrieval skills, dataanalysis, and manuscript formatting are utilized in thedevelopment of a publishable manuscript to improve students'communication skills.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Advanced Infectious Disease Modeling and Data Science with R
courses.description: This course explores statistical methods commonly used in infectious disease research, emphasizing their application in disease ecology through programming in R. It focuses on the assumptions, utility, and interpretation of these techniques, providing practical, ecology-specific context often lacking in more general biostatistics or quantitative courses.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to critically evaluate a variety of research questions and justify selection of appropriate quantitative approaches, including regressions, time-series analysis, and machine learning models, based on data structure and epidemiological context through applying statistical skills in quizzes and homework problems. By the end of the course, students will be able to construct/develop statistical models to address and interpret real-world public health problems. By the end of the course, students will be able to analyze the assumptions underlying statistical methods (e.g. independence, normality, and homoscedasticity) and identify conditions under which these assumptions may be violated. Through applied problem sets, students will evaluate the impact of such violations on results and select appropriate statistical techniques. They will also be able to solve and interpret datasets using methods that align with required assumptions. Through hands-on coding exercises and homework assignments, all students will learn to evaluate, write, develop and implement clean, reproducible R code to fit models, conduct diagnostics, and generate graphical summaries relevant to infectious disease data. By the end of the course, students will be able to create and apply R code for appropriate statistics tests. Students will develop the ability to critically analyze model results, including estimates, confidence intervals, and diagnostics, and interpret findings clearly through written and visual communication, while acknowledging uncertainty and limitations in worked homework assignments and quizzes by the end of the course.
courses.topical_outline: Introduction to basic data structures encountered in infectious disease problems in R (vectors, matrices, arrays), model matrices and effects vs means parameterizations Introduction to univariate tests and multivariate parametric tests (t-tests, correlations, ANOVA, MANOVA to Hotellings’ T) and their applications in infectious disease data Introduction to non-parametric univariate and multivariate tests (Spearman rank, Mann Whitney U, Kruskal Wallis test to Multi Response Permutation Procedure or MRPP) Classification and Ordination methods (Cluster analyses – Hierarchical clustering, K means, PCA, LDA, CCA, RDA, MDS and NMDS) and their utility in studying disease data Introduction to Regressions (linear, logistic, regularization methods, poisson, negative binomial, zero inflated models, GAMs, LOESS, ordinal regressions) Creating custom permutation and resampling tests (permutation/ bootstrapping methods applied to t-tests, regressions and other user specified metrics) Model selection and inference (performance metrics like R2 or AUC, AIC and related measures such as BIC/LOOAIC, Likelihood ratio tests, model averaging, Shapley values) Machine learning applications (what is cross-validation and types, bagging and boosting, fitting common models – random forests, gbm, XgBOOST, ridge, variable importances and marginal plots, shapley values for feature contributions) Introduction to Bayesian Hierarchical Models (Types of probability density functions and specifying hierarchical models in R, running models, posterior distributions and convergence, Gelman Rubin statistics and/or other metrics to assess model fit) Creating custom Maximum Likelihood models (specifying a model, fitting with different ML algorithms, hessian matrix and final solutions)

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Problems in Infectious Diseases
courses.description: Intensive study, under the direction of staff members, on approved problems in medical microbiology.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Doctoral Research
courses.description: Research while enrolled for a doctoral degree under the direction of faculty members.

courses.subject: IDIS
courses.title: Doctoral Dissertation
courses.description: Dissertation writing under the direction of the major professor.

courses.subject: IHDD
courses.title: Introduction to Disability
courses.description: Fifty-four million Americans have disabilities, making this one of the largest minority groups in the United States. Thoroughly understanding disability requires understanding human diversity and social justice. The course will cover a wide variety of disability topics, and prominent leaders in the disability field will serve as guest lecturers.
courses.course_objectives: Upon completion of the course, students will develop an awareness of disability as a diversity and civil rights issue. Upon completion of the course, students will understand local, national, and global social policy regarding people with disabilities. Upon completion of the course, students will think critically about contemporary and historical issues faced by people with disabilities. Upon completion of the course, students will identify the interaction between historical events and longstanding customs related to the treatment of people with disabilities and contemporary political, social, and economic issues. Upon completion of the course, students will describe how historical, economic, political, social, and spatial relationships have developed, persisted, and changed over time related to people with disabilities. Upon completion of the course, students will connect the contributions of groups and individuals to overall ideas and belief systems related to disability. Upon completion of the course, students will explain how society's perspectives on disability are influenced by the stereotypical portrayal of persons and events in a variety of media forms. Upon completion of the course, students will appreciate that a person’s perceived ability by others may affect his or her full participation in society. Upon completion of the course, students will increase comfort in interacting with people with disabilities and awareness of respectful interaction and language. Upon completion of the course, students will increase interest in understanding, supporting, and advocating for people with disabilities in the future.
courses.topical_outline: 1. Interacting with People with Disabilities/The Evolution of Language 2. National and International Understandings of Functional Difference 3. Eugenics and Institutionalization 4. Historical and Sociopolitical Aspects of Defining and Treating People with Disabilities 5. Segregation: Historical, Political, Cultural, and Economic Implications 6. Media Portrayals of Disability: Representing Disability 7. Self-Determination and the Disability Rights Movement 8. Independent Living and Full Inclusion 9. Americans with Disabilities Act: Implications for Policy and Practice 10. The Olmstead Decision 11. Employment: Historical and Social Policy Perspectives 12. Public Education: From Segregation to Inclusion 13. Disability Commonalities and Diversity 14. Intersections of Race, Ethnicity, Gender, and Disability 15. Health Disparities among Different Populations 16. Veterans with Disabilities 17. Building Strengths through Community 18. Person-Centered Approaches for Social Change

courses.subject: IHDD
courses.title: Principles of Person-Centered Practices
courses.description: Provides an in-depth understanding of the principles, design, planning, and application of person-centered practices to support people with disabilities. Students will engage in the person-centered planning process and provide supports using person-centered practices to students in the Inclusive Post-Secondary Education program at UGA.
courses.course_objectives: Students will understand the philosophical underpinning and principles of person-centered practices. Students will apply the principles of person-centered practices by participating in development of person-centered plans for students enrolled in UGA’s inclusive post-secondary education program. Students will implement and document person-centered supports as a peer mentor to assist a student in the inclusive post-secondary education program to reach his/her goals as outlined in the plan. Students will use person-centered tools for problem solving with the person being supported. Students will critically think about the role a supporter plays in the life of a person with a disability and how outcomes can be achieved or hindered.
courses.topical_outline: • Principles of person-centered practices • Person-centered planning tools • Creating a person-centered plan • Person-centered support implementation • Problem solving using person-centered methods • Recording and documentation using person-centered tools • Evaluating the outcomes of person-centered support in goal achievement

courses.subject: IHDD
courses.title: Directed Study in Disability
courses.description: This independent study course is designed to provide students with a variety of learning experiences in the field of disability through completion of prescribed activities in areas of directed readings, product development, and/or service learning under the supervision of the instructor. Students will attend designated number of IHDD seminars dependent upon the number of course credit hours (i.e., 1-3).

courses.subject: IHDD
courses.title: Critical Issues in Disability Studies
courses.description: Contemporary issues impacting people with disabilities and their families.  Self-determination, disability rights, inclusion, person-centered approaches, cultural competence, legislative/legal issues, and personal issues of people with disabilities will be addressed.  The course presents a lifespan perspective.

courses.subject: IHDD
courses.title: Disability Issues in Adulthood
courses.description: A problem-based learning and psychosocial lifespan approach to understanding disability in adulthood is taken.  Students are presented with open-ended, real-life problems for analysis. Topics explored range from transition out of high school throughadult life into old age.
courses.course_objectives: Students will demonstrate understanding of, and effectively critique, theories of adult development. Students will comprehend and apply the findings of current research and reports. Students will explain the ways in which disability may affect autonomy, work, income, and family. Students will identify social/environmental barriers to adult life for people with disabilities. Students will demonstrate knowledge of strengths-based approaches to understanding adults with disabilities. Students will interact with adults with disabilities in an age-appropriate manner. Students will challenge negative/pitying attitudes toward adults with disabilities. Students will integrate knowledge into tools for empowering individuals, families, and/or organizations in their community.
courses.topical_outline: Guardianship Transition to Adult Life Post-secondary Education Friendship and Loneliness Sexuality and Relationships Individualized Supports Housing Community Building Marriage and Parenthood Employment Retirement Aging and End-of-Life Planning

courses.subject: IHDD
courses.title: Disability Issues in Childhood and Adolescence
courses.description: A problem-based learning and psychosocial lifespan approach to understanding disability from birth through adolescence is taken. Students are presented with open-ended, real-life problems for analysis. Topics explored range from prenatal diagnosis through childhood and adolescence.
courses.course_objectives: Students will demonstrate understanding of grand theories of child development and assess the effect of these theories on social and parental expectations. Students will comprehend and apply the findings of current research and reports. Students will explain the ways in which functional difference may affect bio/psycho/social development. Students will gain an understanding of the various ways parents, grandparents, and siblings respond to having a child with a disability in the family. Students will identify and propose solutions for social/environmental barriers to the full inclusion of youth with disabilities. Students will demonstrate knowledge of strengths-based approaches to supporting youth with disabilities. Students will apply course material to the lives of children and adolescents living with disabilities in their community through service-learning. Students will interact with youth with disabilities and their families appropriately. Students will challenge negative/pitying/tragic/heroic attitudes toward youth with disabilities. Students will increase interest in working with youth with disabilities/families in their career. Students will integrate knowledge into tools for empowering individuals, families, and/or organizations in their community.

Students will interact with youth with disabilities and their families appropriately. Students will challenge negative/pitying/tragic/heroic attitudes toward youth with disabilities. Students will increase interest in working with youth with disabilities/families in their career. Students will integrate knowledge into tools for empowering individuals, families, and/or organizations in their community.

courses.description: Addresses issues considered critical in disability studies. Foundations of disability studies, including disability theories, models, definitions, ethics, laws, and culture, will be explored. Social changes in values, perception, and practice over time are examined and discussed.
courses.course_objectives: Students will have knowledge of evolving critical issues relevant to individuals with disabilities and their families. Students will understand how disabilities have been defined and how these definitions affect service delivery to individuals with disabilities and their families. Students will understand current and past state and federal policies affecting individuals with developmental disabilities and their families. Students will have knowledge of key legislation related to individuals with disabilities and their families. Students will understand the importance of social attitudes, beliefs, and behavior toward people with disabilities. Students will have an appreciation for the need and right to options and freedom of choice in the lives of individuals with disabilities and their families. Students will expand awareness of multicultural issues through understanding components of culturally competent service delivery and knowledge of the national demographic profile of individuals with disabilities from many cultural backgrounds.
