The course will cover primary and secondary sources, advanced searching skills, topical research, and cost saving strategies. Students will complete research for simulated client matters: preparing civil and criminal cases for trial, completing a business transaction, and representing a client in an administrative hearing.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Property
courses.description: The recognition, development, and regulation of rights in real property and personal property, including the nature and function of possession and title, shared ownership, private and public rights, and transfers of property.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Property
courses.description: The recognition, development, and regulation of rights in real property and personal property, including the nature and function of possession and title, shared ownership, private and public rights, and transfers of property.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Democracy and the Constitution
courses.description: An exploration of the concepts of democracy and equal citizenship through the prism of the U.S. Constitution. Students will examine the rights and responsibilities of membership in the American civic community and how those rights and responsibilities have changed over time. Examination of each of these conflicts will center on their relationship to the rights and duties embodied in the U.S. Constitution.
courses.prerequisiteText: POLS 1101 or POLS 1101E or POLS 1101S or POLS 1105H

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Democracy and the Constitution
courses.description: An exploration of the concepts of democracy and equal citizenship through the prism of the U.S. Constitution. Students will examine the rights and responsibilities of membership in the American civic community and how those rights and responsibilities have changed over time. Examination of each of these conflicts will center on their relationship to the rights and duties embodied in the U.S. Constitution.
courses.prerequisiteText: POLS 1101 or POLS 1101E or POLS 1101S or POLS 1105H

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Torts
courses.description: Covers intentional torts, which may include battery, assault, and possibly false imprisonment, trespass to land, and others. Certain defenses to intentional tort, such as consent and self defense, may also be covered. The bulk of the course is devoted to the tort of negligence, including the content of the duty of reasonable care, issues bearing on whether the defendant has breached that duty, the requirement that the plaintiff establish a causal connection between the breach and the plaintiff's harm, and proximate cause limits on liability.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Torts II
courses.description: Advanced topics in tort law, building on the coverage in the first-year Torts I course. Topics may include products liability, defamation, fraud and negligent misrepresentation, interference with contractual relations, recovery for pure economic harm, interference with intellectual property rights, nuisance, trespass to chattels, and conversion. In addition, the roles of mass tort litigation, insurance, and tort reform may be considered.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Appellate Practice
courses.description: The nuts and bolts of appellate practice, such as appellate jurisdiction, preservation of error, supersedes bonds, appellate remedies, and other appellate procedures necessary to litigate an appeal successfully from its inception to its conclusion.
courses.course_objectives: Students will understand how to determine the proper court to which the desired appeal can or must be taken. Students will understand how to explain the concept of “finality” and identify those circumstances that permit an appeal, notwithstanding a lack of finality. Students will understand how to determine the appropriate process for appeal depending upon the circumstances—i.e., direct appeal, discretionary appeal, or interlocutory appeal—and explain the mechanics of each process. Students will understand how to determine the steps of initiating an appeal in the relevant court, including filing the notice of appeal and compiling the record for appeal. Students will understand how to identify the tasks that are triggered by filing a notice of appeal and explain the mechanics of each task. Students will understand how to identify the steps associated with filing briefs and explain the mechanics of each task. Students will understand how to determine the procedural tasks of preparing for and conducting oral argument.
courses.topical_outline: Appeals and courts Concept of finality Process and mechanics of an appeal Filing a brief Oral arguments

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Appellate Advocacy
courses.description: Designed to help students to become successful appellate advocates.  Students prepare a brief and oral argument.  Grades based on evaluations of appellate brief, videotaped argument, competition argument, and writing exercises.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Appellate Advocacy
courses.description: Designed to help students to become successful appellate advocates. Students prepare a brief and oral argument. Grades based on evaluations of an appellate brief, videotaped argument, competition argument, and writing exercises.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Appellate Litigation Clinic Seminar
courses.description: Under supervision, students will represent clients in appeals before the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit and the Board of Immigration Appeals. Students will be responsible for writing briefs and for oral arguments if scheduled. This portion includes a seminar component.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Appellate Litigation Clinic I
courses.description: Under supervision, students will represent clients in appeals before the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit and the Board of Immigration Appeals. Students will be responsible for writing briefs and for oral argument if scheduled.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Appellate Litigation Clinic II
courses.description: Under supervision, students will represent clients in appeals before the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit and the Board of Immigration Appeals. Students will be responsible for writing briefs and for oral argument if scheduled.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Appellate Litigation Clinic Summer
courses.description: Under supervision, students will assist in preparing briefs and other documents submitted to the United States Circuit Courts of Appeals, the Board of Immigration Appeals, the United States Supreme Court, or the Office of the United States Pardon Attorney.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Advanced Legal Writing Seminar
courses.description: Advanced instruction in legal research and legal writing. Focuses on both training and experience in the practical skills of researching and writing as well as explicitly exploring the purposes for writing a particular document and being sure to effectively reach the intended audience. Class material will cover general writing principles, guidance on legal writing style, grammar, organization, editing, and citation form. Course consists of extensive practice, feedback, peer review, and review of excerpts from actual briefs and other documents.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Advanced Legal Writing Seminar
courses.description: Advanced instruction in legal research and legal writing. Focuses on both training and experience in the practical skills of researching and writing as well as explicitly exploring the purposes for writing a particular document and being sure to effectively reach the intended audience. Class material will cover general writing principles, guidance on legal writing style, grammar, organization, editing, and citation form. Course consists of extensive practice, feedback, peer review, and review of excerpts from actual briefs and other documents.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Fintech, Payments, and Digital Assets
courses.description: Fintech, Payments, and Digital Assets will provide a broad overview of the legal and regulatory frameworks governing modern financial technology products and services. Starting with core concepts in money movement, the course will examine both traditional rails and the newer infrastructure that powers fintech offerings.
courses.course_objectives: Students will examine both traditional rails and the newer infrastructure that powers fintech offerings, including real-time payments, open banking APIs, and digital wallets. Students will understand developments in other consumer financial services, peer-to-peer transfers, and the treatment of digital assets. Students will understand classical payment topics, including negotiable instruments.
courses.topical_outline: Key U.S. federal and state laws Network rules Compliance expectations for fintechs, especially in bank partnerships A perspective on practicing as a regulatory lawyer (especially as an in-house regulatory lawyer) Statutory and regulatory analysis and how to effectively translate that analysis into practical commercial counseling.
courses.prerequisiteText: Students must be enrolled in the School of Law to register for this course

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Consumer Law
courses.description: Legal issues concerning consumers' commercial transactions, including the following key topics: disclosure of information to consumers, consumer credit, predatory-lending prohibitions, consumer-credit reporting, privacy related to consumer transactions (both online and offline), consumer-product warranties, debt collection, and dispute-resolution methods.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Constitutional Law I
courses.description: The meaning and impact of the Constitution of the United States,particularly with regard to the subjects of federalism,separation of powers, the judicial function, and due process of law.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Constitutional Law I
courses.description: The meaning and impact of the Constitution of the United States, particularly with regard to the subjects of federalism, separation of powers, the judicial function, and due process of law.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Comparative Constitutional Rights
courses.description: Examination of how different legal systems balance the judicial protection of civil rights and liberties with the power of legislative majorities to govern. It does so by considering how different constitutional texts, governmental structures, and social and legal traditions shape juridical responses to common questions about rights.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Constitutional Law II
courses.description: An in-depth examination of the individual rights protected in the Fourteenth and First Amendments (substantive due process, equal protection, freedom of speech and association, and religious freedoms).

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Constitutional Law II
courses.description: An in-depth examination of the individual rights protected in the Fourteenth and First Amendments (substantive due process, equal protection, freedom of speech and association, and religious freedoms).

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: The Law of Constitutional Structure
courses.description: Exploration of the Constitution’s structuring of American government. Of particular importance are two key concepts, federalism (that is, the division of power between the central government and the states) and the separation of powers among the three branches of the central government.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Constitutional Identity Seminar
courses.description: Examination of how the Constitution defines national communitythrough citizenship practices.  Constitutional and other rulesrelating to acceptance, rejection, and expulsion of individualmembers as citizens; special problems of dual nationality;historical racial and gender aspects of American citizenship; andconstitutional meaning of state citizenship will also be examined.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Constitutional Theory
courses.description: Exploration of the theory that lies behind the American Constitution and its interpretation in judicial decisions.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: The Press and the Constitution
courses.description: This seminar will take an in-depth look at the constitutional rights of the “press.”   Topics of discussion will include the history of the Press Clause, the relationship between the Speech Clause and the Press Clause, the definition of the “press” under the Constitution, and the rights available to the press.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Constitutional Law Seminar
courses.description: This seminar will focus on Constitutional Law at a greater levelof depth than occurs in two basic courses.  Student efforts willcenter on researching discrete subjects within constitutionallaw.  There may, in particular, be opportunities to work on suchsubjects as religious displays, affirmative action, presidentialimmunities, etc.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Modern American Legal Theory
courses.description: This is a study in the theories that animate modern legal scholarship and practice.  The course surveys classic articles and book excerpts and reviews to provide a basic understanding of the dominant theoretical movements and their development.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Modern American Legal Theory
courses.description: This is an online class which studies the theories that animate modern legal scholarship and practice. The course surveys classic articles and book excerpts and reviews to provide a basic understanding of the dominant theoretical movements and their development.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: First Amendment Clinic Seminar
courses.description: UGA’s First Amendment Clinic defends and advances the rights of free speech, press, petition, and assembly. The Clinic provides direct client services to individuals or organizations in need of counsel with First Amendment expertise and serves as an educational resource regarding free expression, open access, and protection of newsgathering and reporting.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: First Amendment Clinic Hours
courses.description: UGA’s First Amendment Clinic defends and advances the rights of free speech, press, petition, and assembly.  The Clinic provides direct client services to individuals or organizations in need of counsel with First Amendment expertise and serves as an educational resource regarding free expression, open access, and protection of news gathering and reporting.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Corporations
courses.description: Problems in organization and functioning of corporations, including such matters as disregard of corporate entity, management and control, federal regulation of insider trading, proxy solicitation and shareholder voting, derivative actions, and special problems of the closed corporation.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Business Negotiations
courses.description: Basic negotiation skills and transactional problems commonlyconfronted in a general business law practice.  Deals with coverbilateral, multilateral, and repeated negotiations in addition toprincipal-agent problems. Timing and desirability of disclosureof information, misrepresentation, and legal ethics are alsodiscussed.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Business Negotiations
courses.description: Basic negotiation skills and transactional problems commonly confronted in general business law practice. Deals with cover bilateral, multilateral, and repeated negotiations in addition to principal-agent problems. Timing and desirability of disclosure of information, misrepresentation, and legal ethics are also discussed.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Legal Negotiation and Settlement
courses.description: Negotiation theory, practical skills training, and an examination of settlement issues combine to give students confidence that they can negotiate legal disputes effectively and with integrity. Students participate in class discussions and negotiation simulations, complete written assignments, and submit a paper.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Legal Negotiation and Settlement
courses.description: Negotiation theory, practical skills training, and an examination of settlement issues combine to give students confidence that they can negotiate legal disputes effectively and with integrity. Students participate in class discussions and negotiation simulations, complete written assignments, and submit a paper.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Fundamentals of Mergers and Acquisitions
courses.description: Designed to give the student working familiarity with how a merger or acquisition transaction is negotiated and structured, from inception to post-closing, with a heavy emphasis on how the major deal documents allocate risks between the parties through pricing structure, representations, covenants, and conditions.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Anatomy of a Mergers and Aquisition Deal
courses.description: Provides overview of typical asset sale transaction and attorney's role in it. Students will assume role of counsel for one party, as well as that of legal specialist, and will follow transaction from confidentiality agreement through closing.
courses.prerequisiteText: JURI 4210/6210 or JURI 5940/7940 | Graduate Prerequisite | JURI 4210/6210 or JURI 5940/7940

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Business Law Practicum
courses.description: Supervised students will represent entrepreneurs, small business owners, and not-for-profit organizations that cannot otherwise afford legal services. In the practicum seminar, students will learn how to interview, counsel, draft, and negotiate, and will develop problem-solving, analytical, and editorial skills.
courses.prerequisiteText: JURI 4210/6210 or JURI 4000/6000 or JURI 4212/6212 or JURI 4851 or JURI 5850/7850 or JURI 4300/6300

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Business Law Practicum Clinic Hours
courses.description: Essential lawyering skills in a professional, interactive, live-client environment. Services provided by students will relate to such matters as entity formation, corporate governance, employment, and contracts.
courses.prerequisiteText: JURI 4210/6210 or JURI 4000/6000 or JURI 4212/6212 or JURI 4851 or JURI 5850/7850 or JURI 4300/6300

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Bankruptcy Litigation
courses.description: Provide students with practical, direct, and realistic experience with the procedural rules applicable to the resolution of disputes that commonly occur in contested chapter 11 reorganization and chapter 7 bankruptcy cases. Students will individually and as part of teams draft petitions, draft and argue Contested Matter applications, motions, objections, and an Adversary Proceeding complaint and answer.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Selected Topics in Jurisprudence
courses.description: An examination of natural law theories, both those based onrevealed religion and those without religion.  Guidelines forunderstanding how law actually develops and is related tosociety, and its consequences.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Leadership and the Foundations of American Law
courses.description: Students will serve as discussants and mentors for undergraduates in a course concerning basic legal reasoning and institutions and culminating in discussion and analysis of pending and recently decided Supreme Court cases. Students will be responsible for teaching and evaluating undergraduate learners, including leading and participating in discussion sessions.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Leadership and the Foundations of American Law
courses.description: Students will serve as discussants and mentors for undergraduates in a course concerning basic legal reasoning and institutions and culminating in discussion and analysis of pending and recently decided Supreme Court cases. Students will be responsible for teaching and evaluating undergraduate learners, including leading and participating in discussion sessions.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Law and Leadership
courses.description: This course will focus on fostering engagement and leadership in the law school and community. Course will provide an overview of leadership types, factors impacting leadership style, and critical leadership skills. The course will conclude with a capstone presentation that identifies and solves a need in the law school or community.
courses.course_objectives: Students will become leaders in the law school community. Students will have an enhanced self-awareness of their own strengths and weaknesses as a leader and professional. Students will foster engagement with local leaders through the use of guest speakers.
courses.topical_outline: Personality types, emotional intelligence, and how this can affect leadership styles & strengths; Guest speaker perspectives on what makes a strong leader; Essential leadership skills, including professionalism, communication, and time management; The importance of servant leadership & community involvement in leadership development.
courses.prerequisiteText: Students must be enrolled in the School of Law to register for this course
courses.offeredText: Offered every year. Offered every even-numbered year.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Perspectives on the Legal Process
courses.description: A survey of 20th-century perspectives on the nature of law andthe legal process.  Historical and philosophical approach,focusing on key writers and "schools," including Holmes, Cardozo,legal Realism, H.L.A. Hart, Dworkin, law and economics, publicchoice, critical legal studies, feminist jurisprudence, andcritical race theory.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Jurisprudence Seminar
courses.description: Examination of modes of thinking about law.  Focus upon particular jurisprudential systems and points of view as they bear upon contemporary legal problems and lines of cases, including administrative law and environmental regulation.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Evidence
courses.description: Provides a detailed exploration of the Federal Rules of Evidence and other sources of law governing the admission of evidence in civil and criminal trials. The rules in Georgia are substantially similar to the federal rules, so this class also will give a good grounding in the Georgia rules.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Evidence
courses.description: Provides a detailed exploration of the Federal Rules of Evidence and other sources of law governing the admission of evidence in civil and criminal trials. The rules in Georgia are substantially similar to the federal rules, so this class also will give a good grounding in the Georgia rules.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Criminal Sentencing
courses.description: Examination of various aspects of the state sentencing process as it pertains to criminal charges and convictions. Includes an overview of the legal and societal objectives underlying the imposition of sentences.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Problems in Intellectual Property Seminar
courses.description: Advanced issues in the law of unfair competition, trademark, false advertising and publicity rights, with special focus on questions of pre-emption of state law, antitrust, secured transactions, and international law.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: International Intellectual Property Seminar
courses.description: Primary focus on the WTO-administered Treaty on Trade-RelatedAspects of Intellectual Property Law (TRIPS).  Secondary focus onParis Convention, Berne Convention, Madrid Protocol, bio-piracyand gray market goods.  Comparative focus on the intellectualproperty law of various nations encouraged in student presentations.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: International Criminal Law
courses.description: Examination of the development of international criminal law.  Exploration of the history of international criminal justice, the “core crimes” of international criminal law, theories of liability, and available defenses. Other topics will include the war on terrorism, United States opposition to the International Criminal Court, and transitional justice.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Transnational Criminal Law
courses.description: This course concerns crimes that, though ordinarily domestic, become “transnational” when some aspect crosses national borders. To be studied: extraterritorial jurisdiction; obligations of law enforcement officers operating overseas; substantive law of crimes like trafficking, public corruption, money laundering, and terrorism; and procedural matters like extradition, rendition, evidence gathering, and judgment enforcement.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Crime and Criminal Behavior
courses.description: Course explores documented connections between certain underlying variables and criminal behavior. These variables include the motivation of the offender, victim behavior, social variables, and situational contexts.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Landmark Cases in Criminal Procedure
courses.description: Examination of an array of notable Supreme Court criminalprocedure cases by deeply delving into the litigation andsurrounding stories that accompany each case.  Ten to fourteenlandmark cases commonly reviewed in Criminal Procedure I and II (Katz, Miranda, Terry, Batson, and Powell, to name a few) will becovered.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Criminal Justice Reform
courses.description: Exploration of contemporary criminal justice reform efforts with an emphasis on the role of race in criminal justice policy and practice. Likely areas of focus include policing, bail, and sentencing. Each student will complete a final research project evaluating or proposing a specific reform initiative.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Criminal Law Drafting
courses.description: The fundamentals of document drafting in the context of criminal law. Students will prepare documents that arise in a criminal law setting, including charging documents, notices, motions, bench briefs, and orders. Students will examine the function of these documents within the criminal justice system, including applicable statutory and case law. This course will require students to produce various graded documents of increasing complexity. Students will receive feedback from the professor on all graded assignments.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Criminal Law Drafting
courses.description: The fundamentals of document drafting in the context of criminal law. Students will prepare documents that arise in a criminal law setting, including charging documents, notices, motions, bench briefs, and orders. Students will examine the function of these documents within the criminal justice system, including applicable statutory and case law. This course will require students to produce various graded documents of increasing complexity. Students will receive feedback from the professor on all graded assignments.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Criminal Litigation
courses.description: Focuses on aspects of criminal litigation beginning in the immediate period following arrest up to trial from the perspective of both the prosecution and the defense. Coursework involves preparing for and conducting committal hearings, bond hearings, and various motions and other hearings commonly encountered in a criminal litigation practice.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Trusts and Estates I
courses.description: Substantive and procedural rules concerning disposition of wealth, including intestate succession, wills, will substitutes and inter vivos and testamentary trusts; law of express and charitable trusts; remedies for wrongs relating to disposition of wealth; fiduciary powers, duties, and liabilities; construction problems relating to future interests and powers of appointment.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Trusts and Estates II
courses.description: Continuation of study of procedural rules concerning disposition of wealth, including intestate succession, wills, will substitutes and inter vivos and testamentary trusts; express and charitable trusts; remedies for wrongs relating to disposition of wealth; fiduciary powers, duties, and liabilities; construction problems relating to future interests and powers of appointment.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Emerging Issues in Trusts, Estates, and Wealth Preservation
courses.description: This course considers emerging issues in trusts, estates, and wealth preservation. Examining both legal and social science aspects of topics such as: death technologies, digital assets, creative estate planning strategies, and rules that apply to estate plans designed to protect assets and accomplish tax-efficient intergenerational transfers of property.
courses.course_objectives: Students will synthesize competing practical, ethical, and policy issues that are raised by emerging issues in trusts and estates. Students will articulate and express well-informed opinions about potential legal impacts of innovation. Students will demonstrate skills in legal analysis, reasoning, problem solving; and written and oral communication. Students will listen actively and engage with speakers and other students to share viewpoints and identify weaknesses in other’s arguments.
courses.topical_outline: • Legal and social science aspects of innovative death technologies • Planning for digital assets • Role of trusts and retirement planning in asset protection • Creative estate planning strategies • Estate plans designed to protect assets and accomplish tax efficient intergenerational transfers of property for the extremely wealthy

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: The Law and Ethics of Lawyering
courses.description: The organization of the profession and its standards of professional conduct as set forth in the rules of professional responsibility promulgated by the American Bar Association and the State Bar of Georgia.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: The Law and Ethics of Lawyering
courses.description: The organization of the profession and its standards of professional conduct as set forth in the rules of professional responsibility promulgated by the American Bar Association and the State Bar of Georgia.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Common Law Jurisprudence
courses.description: Through a survey of the historical development of the common law, courts, and the legal profession on both sides of the Atlantic, this course will explore the goals, structure, values, and regulations of the legal profession and its members.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Administrative Law
courses.description: Focuses on law controlling federal and state administrative action.  Along with constitutional restraints, student is asked to consider statutory and judicially formulated rules for administrative process.  Control over administrative discretion and enforced accountability are major themes.  Attention is devoted to federal and state Administrative Procedure Acts.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Administrative Law
courses.description: Focuses on law controlling federal and state administrative action. Along with constitutional restraints, student is asked to consider statutory and judicially formulated rules for administrative process. Control over administrative discretion and enforced accountability are major themes. Attention is devoted to federal and state Administrative Procedure Acts.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Admiralty
courses.description: Admiralty jurisdiction and selected topics in the maritime law, including maritime liens, injuries to seamen and other maritime workers, carriage of goods, charter parties, salvage, general average, collision, limitation of liability, and the relation of maritime law to local law.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Antitrust Law
courses.description: Federal antitrust law with emphasis on leading cases decided by the United States Supreme Court under Sherman and Clayton Acts.
courses.prerequisiteText: Students must be enrolled in the School of Law to register for this course

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Antitrust Law and Policy Seminar
courses.description: Examination of the legal structures aimed at promoting a competitive market economy. Covers both public enforcement by agencies and private suits that have advanced changes in the law. While the course will pay special attention to developments in case law, it will also consider pertinent policy-making decisions by Congress and the agencies.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Bankruptcy
courses.description: This survey course is intended not only for aspiring bankruptcy lawyers, but to allow future litigators and corporate lawyers to become familiar with both consumer and corporate bankruptcy. Examines the nature of the legal relationship between debtors and creditors under the Bankruptcy Code and some non-bankruptcy law.
courses.course_objectives: Students will become familiar with bankruptcy law and practice. Students will gain experience in statutory interpretation. Students will understand strategies that use the legal structure of bankruptcy to protect a debtor/creditor’s financial and legal position. Students will be able to evaluate the role of attorneys in the United States' bankruptcy system.
courses.topical_outline: Insolvency legislation Jurisdiction of U.S. Bankruptcy Court and concurrent state jurisdiction Administrative officials, petition, and petitioners Competing elections available to consumers in bankruptcy, in both liquidation and reorganization of businesses Recovery of fraudulent transfers and preferential transfers and in the jurisdiction and venue bankruptcy courts
courses.prerequisiteText: Students must be enrolled in the School of Law to register for this course

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Bankruptcy Practice Seminar
courses.description: Current topics in bankruptcy law. For almost all class sessions, a leading practitioner, judge, trustee, journalist, academic, or other leader in the bankruptcy profession will join (typically via Zoom). Each invitee will be asked "to pick a problem currently on their desk.”
courses.course_objectives: Students will understand basic bankruptcy and learn current leading issues that arise during various parts of the bankruptcy lifecycle in both business and consumer cases. Students will understand how to develop a corporate bankruptcy practice, consumer bankruptcy practice, and/or practice commercial law in other areas.
courses.topical_outline: Mass tort bankruptcies Texas two-step Eligibility for the relatively new small business reorganization sub-chapter of bankruptcy Fiduciary duty lawsuits in bankruptcy The inner workings of the U.S. Trustee Program
courses.prerequisiteText: Students must be enrolled in the School of Law to register for this course

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Contemporary Issues in Business Law
courses.description: This seminar examines contemporary issues that are prevalent in the regulation of business organizations and activities.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Economic Analysis of Law
courses.description: Application of economic principles to analysis of legal issues and institutions.  Focus upon law's determination of fundamental market context governing economic exchange (torts, contracts, crime control) and discrimination prohibitions as definers and protectors of property rights upon effects of government intervention and performance of law enforcement agencies and judiciary.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Accounting and Finance for Lawyers
courses.description: The general foundation of accounting and finance for law students planning to manage a private law firm.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Military Law and the Role of the Judge Advocate
courses.description: Course will focus on the role of the Judge Advocate in the six service branches of the U.S. Armed Forces, with particular emphasis on the largest Judge Advocate General’s (JAG) Corps, the U.S. Army JAG Corps.
courses.course_objectives: Students will understand how to analyze and assess the role of the military in the United States in terms of its Constitutional foundation and subsequent practice. Students will understand what judge advocates and uniformed legal personnel contribute to the military and how military law has developed over time. Students will understand how to engage with current and former judge advocates and participate in challenging practical exercises that will develop their critical thinking and their understanding of the role of an advisor.
courses.topical_outline: Discuss the six core competencies of military law, which include administrative and civil law, claims, contract and fiscal law, international and operational law, legal assistance, and military justice. Review some of the most significant Supreme Court, Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces (CAAF), and federal court decisions as they relate to military law. Learn about the role of a military lawyer and the unique skills and value they bring to the mission and to a Commander’s decision-making.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Military Law and the Role of the Judge Advocate
courses.description: Course will focus on the role of the Judge Advocate in the six service branches of the U.S. Armed Forces, with particular emphasis on the largest Judge Advocate General’s (JAG) Corps, the U.S. Army JAG Corps.
courses.course_objectives: Students will understand how to analyze and assess the role of the military in the United States in terms of its Constitutional foundation and subsequent practice. Students will understand what judge advocates and uniformed legal personnel contribute to the military and how military law has developed over time. Students will understand how to engage with current and former judge advocates and participate in challenging practical exercises that will develop their critical thinking and their understanding of the role of an advisor.
courses.topical_outline: Discuss the six core competencies of military law, which include administrative and civil law, claims, contract and fiscal law, international and operational law, legal assistance, and military justice. Review some of the most significant Supreme Court, Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces (CAAF), and federal court decisions as they relate to military law. Learn about the role of a military lawyer and the unique skills and value they bring to the mission and to a Commander’s decision-making.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Civil-Military Relations: The Role of the Military in the United States
courses.description: This course is narrowly focused on the proper role of the military under the United States Constitution and other laws as well as cultural and societal norms that have been inculcated and fostered since the founding of the nation.  It is complementary to other courses that deal with broader subjects under our domestic and applicable international law, such as Constitutional Law and the Law of War.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Comparative Corporate Law
courses.description: Examination of corporate law and the corporate form from a comparative perspective, with particular emphasis placed on how large publicly traded companies are governed and regulated in some of the world’s leading commercial and financial jurisdictions.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Corporate Governance Seminar
courses.description: This seminar provides an in-depth study of corporate law and governance topics from both theoretical and practical perspectives. Focusing primarily on for-profit, publicly traded corporations, topics may include corporate social responsibility, board composition and structures, institutional investors, shareholder activism, executive compensation, corporate political spending, financial crisis, and comparative corporate governance.
courses.course_objectives: Students will classify and interpret the primary theories underlying corporate governance. Students will differentiate the roles of various corporate actors such as the board of directors, shareholders, etc. Students will explain common “failures” of corporate governance, assess regulatory responses, and appraise new solutions. Students will demonstrate familiarity with corporate law research sources and methods. Students will employ advanced research and writing skills, demonstrating critical thinking and contributing original thought to the final paper. Students will practice presentation skills in formal and informal group settings. Students will integrate critical thinking skills in weekly readings and class discussions.
courses.topical_outline: •	Theories of the corporation •	Corporate social responsibility •	The role of the board of directors •	Board composition and structures •	Institutional investors •	Shareholder activism •	Executive compensation •	Corporate political spending •	The financial crisis •	Comparative corporate governance
courses.prerequisiteText: Students must be enrolled in the School of Law to register for this course

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Conflict of Laws
courses.description: Jurisdiction over persons and things; domicile as basis of personal jurisdiction; law governing creation of personal and property rights; recognition and enforcement by one state of rights created by laws of another state, including questions arising from capacity, marriage, legitimacy, and inheritance; nature and effect of judgments and decrees, and enforcement outside rendering jurisdiction; choice of law; impact of Constitution on conflict issues.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Constitutional Litigation Seminar
courses.description: Addresses issues in damage actions under 42 U.S.C. Section 1983, authorizing cause of action against constitutional violations under color of state law.  Topics include distinction between common law and constitutional torts, scope of governmental liability, official immunity, damages, causation, state court suits, procedural defenses, attorney's fees, and meaning of "under color of."

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Foreign Affairs and National Security Law
courses.description: An examination of how United States law both constrains and isconstrained by United States foreign relations and the foreignpolicy-making process. The course covers issues relating toseparation of powers, federalism, individual rights, and theinfluence of international norms on United States constitutionaldevelopment.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Copyright Law
courses.description: Focus is upon various methods to protect literary, musical, andartistic work under law of copyright. Copyright is a statutorysubject based upon Copyright Act of 1909 and its amendments andCopyright Act of 1976. The course deals with what can becopyrighted, infringement actions, rights enjoyed by thecopyright proprietor, jurisdiction, and various remedies.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Corporate Finance
courses.description: Corporate financing, including short-term and long-term debt,preferred stock, common stock, hybrid securities, how to protectfrom value appropriation by another class of corporatecreditor/owner.  Capital structure and duties of directors tovarious claimant classes will be examined using decisions aboutdividend policy and dissidents appraisal rights.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Criminal Procedure I
courses.description: Criminal process from pre-arrest investigation to trial, including guilty pleas.  Emphasis on pre-trial rights of persons suspected of crime, including privilege against self-incrimination, right to be free from unreasonable search and seizure, and due process and other rights attaching to pre-trial confrontation between accused and witnesses.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Criminal Procedure II
courses.description: Criminal process from bringing of formal charges to adjudication of guilt or innocence.  Emphasis on prosecutorial discretion; preliminary hearing and grand jury procedures; joinder and severance; plea bargaining; criminal discovery; right to speedy trial, assistance of counsel, confrontation, and trial by jury; double jeopardy; and sentencing.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Criminal Procedure II
courses.description: The criminal process from bringing formal charges to adjudication of guilt or innocence. Emphasis on prosecutorial discretion; preliminary hearing and grand jury procedures; joinder and severance; plea bargaining; criminal discovery; right to a speedy trial, the assistance of counsel, confrontation, and trial by jury; double jeopardy; and sentencing.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Post Conviction Relief
courses.description: Analysis of judicial relief in federal and state systems for persons detained pursuant to conviction, who assert unlawful detention.  Habeas corpus, statutory motions to vacate or set aside, and other modes of relief, including coram nobis.  Consideration will be given to proposals to alter or abolish present procedures.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Federal Habeas Corpus
courses.description: Examination of the history and development of the writ of habeas corpus in the courts of the United States. Habeas corpus, known as the Great Writ, traces its history from the Magna Carta through the current term in the Supreme Court.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Crime and Punishment: Understanding the Carceral State
courses.description: The carceral state is a term used to speak about one particular mode of organizing, distributing, and justifying government power in American society. We will examine the carceral state in detail and start by looking at the history of policing and prisons.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Criminal Defense Practicum II - Service Learning
courses.description: Students will assist attorneys in Legal Aid and Defender Clinic in handling defense of criminal cases and receive intensive clinical training in trial advocacy through workshops, simulation, lecture, and actual representation of clients. Clinic also handles juvenile cases.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Criminal Defense Practicum II
courses.description: Students will assist attorneys in Legal Aid and Defender Clinic in handling defense of criminal cases and receive intensive clinical training in trial advocacy through workshops, simulation, lecture, and actual representation of clients. Clinic also handles juvenile cases.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Criminal Defense Practicum II Hours
courses.description: Intensive clinical training in trial advocacy through workshops, simulation, lecture and representation of clients by students licensed to practice under the Law School Legal Aid Agency Act.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: First Amendment Seminar
courses.description: Study of the legal aspects of First Amendment law.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Eighth Amendment Seminar
courses.description: An in-depth exploration of the Eighth Amendment’s prohibitions against excessive bail, excessive fines, and cruel and unusual punishment.
courses.course_objectives: Students will understand how the Eighth Amendment has been interpreted including its historical and doctrinal evolution. Students will have knowledge of key Supreme Court decisions on excessive bail, fines and cruel and unusual punishment. Students will evaluate how statutory frameworks and, to a lesser degree state constitutions, have shaped the application of Eighth Amendment protections in various contexts. Students will understand the disparities between formal legal protections and the real-world experiences of those affected by the criminal legal system. Students will examine the policies and practices that implicate Eighth Amendment protections from multiple perspectives. Students will explore various approaches used by system-impacted individuals and advocates to advance Eight Amendment rights. Students will engage thoughtfully and constructively in a seminar-style discussion on complex constitutional and systemic issues.
courses.topical_outline: Analyze foundational Supreme Court decisions, relevant statutory and legislative developments, and the broader historical and political contexts Examine the persistent gap between the Amendment’s formal protections and the lived experiences of individuals impacted by the criminal legal system Diverse strategies employed by system-impacted individuals and communities—including class action litigation, policy advocacy, and grassroots organizing—to advance and actualize Eighth Amendment protections
courses.prerequisiteText: Students must be enrolled in the School of Law to register for this course | Graduate Prerequisite | Students must be enrolled in the School of Law to register for this course
courses.offeredText: Offered every year. Offered every even-numbered year. Offered every odd-numbered year.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Equitable Remedies
courses.description: Study of injunction and specific performance decree. Attention given to injunction and its availability at temporary restraining order, preliminary injunction stages, and after trial upon merits.  Restitution at law studied at length. Course focuses on choice of remedies and emphasizes "election of remedies" opportunities and implications of each choice.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Estate Planning Seminar
courses.description: Typical problems involved in planning effective and economical gift distribution of property interests.  Attention given to preparation of estate plans and drafting of appropriate instruments to accomplish goals. Focus on restrictions imposed by law of trusts, wills, future interests, and federal taxation.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Federal Courts
courses.description: Nature, source, and extent of federal judicial power.  Original, removal, and appellate jurisdiction and procedure in federal courts.  Study of state law as rule of decision.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: The Federalist Papers
courses.description: Focuses on the framing and ratification of the United States Constitution and the role of The Federalist Papers in that process.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Judicial Process
courses.description: Focuses on process of judging, professionalism in court system, specialized courts, comparison of English and American judicial systems, judicial reform, and similar topics.  Designed particularly for those who will become judicial clerks upon graduation.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Select Topics in Judicature
courses.description: Selected areas of judicial administration and judging that are too narrow for a full-semester course. Topics may include judicial case management, the judicial role in criminal and civil matters, the role of judges or courts in society and literature, comparative approaches to judging in different legal systems, etc.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: The Supreme Court
courses.description: The Supreme Court of the United States is a unique institution with its own history, personalities and appellate practice. This course examines the Court, including an in-depth look at the current nine justices.  Students then argue cases from the Court's current docket and write an opinion in a case.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Federal Taxation of Estates, Gifts, and Trusts
courses.description: Focuses on federal tax law and policy affecting the transfer ofwealth, including the gift tax, the estate tax, and thegeneration-skipping transfer tax. Statutes, regulations, andinterpretative materials and their application to hypotheticalproblems are addressed to lay the groundwork for the study ofestate planning.
courses.course_objectives: Students will explore the core principles of wealth transfer taxation, including the gift tax, the estate tax, and the generation skipping transfer tax, and the policies which underlie them. Students will sharpen skills of statutory interpretation through close reading of the Internal Revenue Code and Regulations.
courses.topical_outline: 1) tax consequences of retained interests in transferred property; 2) tax consequences of retained powers over transferred property; 3) tax consequences of powers created in third parties; 4) transfer tax treatment of life insurance, retirement arrangements, and concurrent interests; 5) valuation of gifts and estates.
courses.prerequisiteText: JURI 5120/7120 or JURI 5120E/7120E | Graduate Prerequisite | JURI 5120/7120 or JURI 5120E/7120E

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Corporate Tax
courses.description: The taxation of corporations and their shareholders. Major topics include contributions of property to corporations, distributions and redemptions by corporations, and taxable and tax-free mergers and acquisitions.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Georgia Practice and Procedure
courses.description: Advanced course in Civil Procedure.  Explores Georgia Civil Practice Act and Long-Arm Statute as interpreted by Georgia appellate court decisions, along with selected constitutional and statutory provisions allocating jurisdiction among trial courts, venue, and validity of judgments.
courses.prerequisiteText: Students must be enrolled in the School of Law to register for this course | Graduate Prerequisite | Students must be enrolled in the School of Law to register for this course

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Solo and Small Firm Practice
courses.description: Provides a roadmap for the new lawyer to establish a solo law practice or to join with other lawyers in creating or expanding a small law firm.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Innovation in the Practice of Law
courses.description: Introduces students to innovations necessary to keep pace with a rapidly changing legal industry and that will ensure that those in need of representation have equal access to justice, including, among others: AI, predictive analytics, process management, alternative pricing models, and collaborative workspace platforms.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Insurance Law
courses.description: The law relating to one entity's (the insurer's) promises to payfor losses incurred by another (the insured).

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Public International Law
courses.description: Foundation for students interested in international dimensions of law.  International law concerns not only matters of intergovernmental and international organizational relations, but also many matters which the private practitioner deals with in daily work with transnational operations and transactions for national and transnational enterprises.
courses.course_objectives: Students will understand the complexities of international law, including: its nature, history, sources, and methods of enforcement. Students will understand the nature, actions, prerogatives, and responsibilities of international law's principal actors, including states and nonstate entities. Students will understand international law avenues for protecting human dignity, such as international human rights and international criminal justice. Students will understand legal regulation of armed conflict/use of force. Students will understand international law regulation of resources such as the global economy, oceans and other environs.
courses.topical_outline: Introduction:  What is International Law? The Sources of International Law Participants in the International Legal Process Relationship Between International and Domestic Law Protecting Human Dignity Interdependence and Integration The Law of Armed Conflict

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Law of War
courses.description: The laws and customs intended to regulate war – not only when and whether law permits resort to armed conflict, but also national and international legal rules and regimes governing how war is to be waged and when actors may be sanctioned for violating those rules.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: International Human Rights
courses.description: Study of international human rights law and international and regional organizations, states, and private actors in the field. Examines instruments and institutions forming sources of human rights law (UN system, including Charter and treaties, European, African and Inter-American human rights regimes), the role of NGOs, and interaction between domestic and international law.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: International Business Transactions
courses.description: Examination of the legal regime governing a variety of international business transactions. Topics include international sales, international finance, and anti-corruption legislation.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: International Business Transactions
courses.description: Examination of the legal regime governing a variety of international business transactions. Topics include international sales, international finance, and anti-corruption legislation.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: The Law of Transnational Investments
courses.description: Trade and investment in the economies of other countries are more than ever essential components of the prosperity sought in all parts of the world. This course will examine the major actors involved in investment and financing across national boundaries.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: International Taxation
courses.description: We will consider the role of an American lawyer acting as tax planner in context of transnational business transactions; U.S. income tax consequences of foreign corporations and individuals doing business and investing in the U.S.; and U.S. income tax consequences of American companies and individuals doing business and investing in foreign countries.
courses.course_objectives: By the end of this course, students will be able to identify the tax rules that are relevant to a given international tax problem. By the end of this course, students will be able to interpret those rules and analyze the tax consequences of the given problem in light of them. By the end of this course, students will be able to analyze those rules in light of the facts. By the end of this course, students will be able to provide the client with a legal conclusion and/or advice for addressing the client's goals in light of the legal analysis.
courses.topical_outline: Source rules foreign persons’ trade or business income Foreign persons’ non-business income Anti-deferral regimes The foreign tax credit
courses.prerequisiteText: JURI 5120/7120 or JURI 5120E/7120E | Graduate Prerequisite | JURI 5120/7120 or JURI 5120E/7120E

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: International Commercial Arbitration
courses.description: Examination of the legal regime governing international commercial arbitration.  Topics will include the enforcement of arbitration agreements, arbitral procedure and the enforcement of arbitral awards.  The course also will cover how to draft arbitral clauses.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Children and International Law
courses.description: Explores developments at the intersection of international, family, labor, and criminal law. The Children’s Rights Convention as well as other treaties, many of which are enforceable in United States courts, will be examined. These treaties cover issues like adoption and abduction, child labor and trafficking, and child soldiers.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Children and the Law
courses.description: Examination of the status of children in society and how the lawtreats their relationships with their parents and the state.Includes study of issues relating to child custody anddependency, neglect, abuse, medical care, abortion, foster care,adoption, illegitimacy, curfews, child pornography, pedophilia(including internet predators), and the juvenile justice system.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Lawyering for Children
courses.description: Explores the responsibilities of lawyers for children and the factors that influence their interactions with child clients and lawyering decisions.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Labor Law
courses.description: National Labor Relations Act, focusing on history and evolution of labor relations laws, union organizational activity, collective bargaining, economic weapons, the duty of fair representation, and federalism and labor relations.
courses.prerequisiteText: Students must be enrolled in the School of Law to register for this course

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: International Labor Law
courses.description: This class is about workers’ rights in the global economy. It covers the international labor rights at the International Labor Organization (ILO); the intersection of ILO governance and state governance through trade agreements; and the specific challenges confronting vulnerable workers, such as women and migrant workers, sex workers, and LGBQT+ workers.
courses.course_objectives: Students will understand the underlying themes of international law, international labor law, and global governance. Students will have practical skills of analytical and critical thinking. Student will have improved communication of ideas in speech and writing. Students will be able to engage in critical, reasoned law and policy analyses.
courses.topical_outline:
1.	Introduction to International Labor Law
2.	The International Labor Organization (ILO)
3.	The Elimination of Child Labor
4.	The Prohibition of Forced Labor
5.	Freedom of Association
6.	Collective Bargaining
7.	Non-Discrimination
8.	Occupational Safety and Health
9.	ILO Enforcement 
10.	 International Financial Institutions
11.	Vulnerable Workers
12.	State Enforcement of International Labor Law
courses.prerequisiteText: Students must be enrolled in the School of Law to register for this course

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Corporate Responsibility
courses.description: Examination of the recent increase in corporatereorganization/restructuring which created focus on decisions bymanagers which have an impact on employee jobs, such as closureor sales of plants/businesses, subcontracting or outsourcing ofwork and layoffs.  Focus on federal/state laws (NLRA; WARN Act)which impose obligations on employers in such situations.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Corporate Responsibility
courses.description:
Examination of the recent increase in corporate reorganization/restructuring which created focus on decisions by
managers which have an impact on employee jobs, such as closure or sales of plants/businesses, subcontracting or outsourcing of work, and layoffs.  Focus on federal/state laws (NLRA; WARN Act) which impose obligations on employers in such situations.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Labor Arbitration
courses.description: Simulation course in which students will take on roles of union counsel, management counsel, and arbitrators.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Real Estate Transactions
courses.description: Basic components of conveyancing with emphasis on finance, acquisition, and development of real property.  Financing techniques and default and foreclosure; review of issues raised by contemporary innovations in financing and ownership of real property.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Real Estate Transactions
courses.description: Basic components of conveyancing with emphasis on finance, acquisition, and development of real property. Financing techniques and default and foreclosure, and review of issues raised by contemporary innovations in financing and ownership of real property.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Land Use Planning
courses.description: Analysis of the legal and administrative aspects of the regulation of land use for development and the problems and techniques of urban planning.  Particular attention is given to zoning, subdivision controls, public acquisition of land, and urban redevelopment.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Land Conservation Clinic
courses.description: The legal foundations of private land conservation, as well as the policy and environmental basis for this work. Students will explore conservation easements, the role of land trusts, the ecological and public benefits of protected land, and ways to enhance the impact of private conservation.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Land Conservation Clinic Hours
courses.description: Law and graduate students from other disciplines will provide advice and drafting assistance to nonprofits, government agencies, and others on land conservation issues, with an emphasis on supporting private land conservation. Students will research, analyze, and draft transactional documents, reports, and guidebooks; counsel clients; and address policy and ecological challenges.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Sociology of Law
courses.description: Empirical patterns of legal behavior, such as initiation and winning of lawsuits, origins and content of rules, and development of legal institutions. Lectures and readings invoke social characteristics of participants (e.g., social ties, status, marginality, reputation, and organizational affiliations) to predict and explain case outcomes.  Sociological techniques by which social differentials might be minimized.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Race and Law
courses.description: Exploration of the definition of race, as well as its historical role in American society. In particular, the course will look at how the law has been used to both support and suppress racism. The course will look at historical and current illustrations of the intersection of race and law.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Sexual Orientation and Gender Law
courses.description: Examines legal regulation relating to sexual orientation andidentity and the impact of such laws on sexual minorities. Focuses on relevant constitutional, family, property, immigrationlaw and state and local laws protecting or discriminating againstsexual minorities.  Course will examine interaction between legaldevelopments and social mores.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Sexual Orientation and Gender Law
courses.description: Examines legal regulation relating to sexual orientation and identity and the impact of such laws on sexual minorities. Focuses on relevant constitutional, family, property, immigration laws, and state and local laws protecting or discriminating against sexual minorities. Course will examine the interaction between legal developments and social mores.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Law and Politics
courses.description: The role of lawyers in lawmaking and public policy, and thepolitical aspects of various policy issues.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Election Law
courses.description: Examination of the law regulating our political process, and consideration of how those regulatory choices shape substantive policy outcomes. The course covers campaign finance regulation, redistricting, voting rights, and the regulation of political party primaries.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Renewable Energy Law and Policy
courses.description: Examination of development and use of various energy sources, including traditional areas such as oil, natural gas, coal, and nuclear. Particular emphasis will be placed on development of alternative sources of energy, including solar, geothermal, wind and biomass, and the role of government in encouraging development.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Water Law
courses.description: Examination of the legal structures that govern water allocation and use in the United States beginning with an understanding of the riparian doctrine, undergirding water rights in the Eastern U.S., and the prior-appropriation doctrine, applicable in Western states.
courses.course_objectives: Students will understand the elements of water law in both the Eastern and Western United States in addition to the various regulatory frameworks, both state and federal, impacting water use in the United States. Students will understand the nuts and bolts of a water law practice in the Southeast, with focus dedicated to case studies of contemporary water disputes and regulatory conflicts within Georgia and the Southeast.
courses.topical_outline: Riparian rights Statutory frameworks governing surface water and groundwater allocation and supply The Endangered Species Act and its impact on water rights and allocation The Federal Clean Water Act Contemporary water issues facing the Southeast
courses.prerequisiteText: Students must be enrolled in the School of Law to register for this course

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Intelligence Law and National Security Policy
courses.description: Survey of intelligence and related national security law and policy issues.  The focus will be on how United States intelligence activities are affected by Constitutional separation of powers, the law of covert action, the criminal law system, the Bill of Rights, issues in counter-terrorist policy, and other federal laws.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Women and the Law
courses.description: The historical and current legal status of women and, by comparison, of men in the United States, with emphasis on recent changes in constitutional and statutory law; the role the courts have played in that change; remedies (administrative, legislative, and judicial) for challenging legal classifications based on sex stereotypes.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Critical Race Feminism
courses.description: Critical race feminism is part of an evolving tradition that originated with critical legal studies and its off-shoots of feminist critical theory and critical race theory. Critical race feminism's core mission is an anti-essentialist exploration of the historical and contemporary issues in the law that affect primarily women of color law as well as others who fall into the gaps of traditional conceptualizations in the law.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Regulation of the Human Body
courses.description: Examination of the ways in which we regulate the human body and its uses, treatment, and materials. As we study these regulations, we will also examine the underlying cultural assumptions embodied in the laws. The exact topics covered will vary by semester.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Law and Religion
courses.description: The history and judicial construction of the Establishment and Free Exercise Clauses of the First Amendment. The course will also include a section exploring how several religious traditions approach the relationship between religion and law.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Election Law Reform: Selected Issues
courses.description: In-depth look at various proposals to reform or change the way we run elections. Topics covered will include electronic and internet voting, voter registration and identification laws, and the "Democracy Index," as well as more fundamental changes, such as mandatory voting and proportional representations systems.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Law in the Gospels
courses.description: Comparative legal history, involving "law in action" in the life of one man.  This is not a class about religion or religious faith.  It is about the stance of Jesus on legal issues and the authorities' response.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Corporate Sustainability
courses.description: Examination of legal structures aimed at promoting environmental, social, and economic sustainability of corporate activities, with particular emphasis placed on how publicly traded companies are governed and regulated in some of the world's  leading commercial and financial jurisdictions. The seminar further considers the intersection of corporate law with other legal fields and disciplines that impact corporate sustainability.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Document Drafting: Survey
courses.description: An overview of drafting non-litigation documents. Develops the skills required to draft statutes, will, and contracts. The course also focuses on gathering information to provide a factual basis for the preparation of such documents and drafting such documents within the existing legal framework.
courses.course_objectives: Upon successful completion of this course, students will have the writing skills necessary to draft non-litigation documents. Upon successful completion of this course, students will understand the expectations of transactional practice.
courses.topical_outline: Drafting problems (esp. ambiguity) and appropriate language Document design Fact gathering and interviewing Presentation of legal concepts and documents to groups Drafting statutes Drafting simple wills Drafting contracts
courses.prerequisiteText: JURI 4071/6071 and JURI 4081/6081 | Graduate Prerequisite | JURI 7009 or JURI 6505 or JURI 6505E

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Document Drafting: Survey
courses.description: An overview of drafting non-litigation documents. Develops the skills required to draft statutes, wills, and contracts. The course also focuses on gathering information to provide a factual basis for the preparation of such documents and drafting such documents within the existing legal framework.
courses.course_objectives: Upon successful completion of this course, students will have the writing skills necessary to draft non-litigation documents. Upon successful completion of this course, students will understand the expectations of transactional practice.
courses.topical_outline: Drafting problems (esp. ambiguity) and appropriate language Document design Fact gathering and interviewing Presentation of legal concepts and documents to groups Drafting statutes Drafting simple wills Drafting contracts
courses.prerequisiteText: JURI 4071/6071 and JURI 4081/6081 | Graduate Prerequisite | JURI 7009 or JURI 6505 or JURI 6505E

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: English Legal History
courses.description: The evolution of English law and legal institutions, with emphasis on constitutional law, development of the court systems, and nineteenth-century legal reforms.  American legal history will also be examined when time permits.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: American Legal History
courses.description: Examination of the role that law and legal institutions have played in American history from Reconstruction until the 1980s.  We will examine the Civil War Amendments and federalism, laissez-faire formalism and economic regulation, the growth of legal liberalism, and the rights revolution.
courses.prerequisiteText: Students must be enrolled in the School of Law to register for this course

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Georgia History for Lawyers
courses.description: A survey of the people, places, and events that form the history of the State of Georgia from prehistoric times to the present, including the ways in which that history has intersected with Georgia and U.S. law. Students will be expected to produce a paper examining in depth an issue of legal importance in Georgia history.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Statutory Interpretation and the Legislative Process
courses.description: Exploration of how legislatures make statutes and how courtsinterpret them.  Rather than focusing on a single statute, theclass will familiarize students with general procedural andinterpretive principles that are relevant in a variety ofpractice settings.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Statutory Interpretation and the Legislative Process
courses.description: Exploration of how legislatures make statutes and how courts interpret them. Rather than focusing on a single statute, the class will familiarize students with general procedural and interpretive principles that are relevant in a variety of practice settings.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: How a Bill Becomes a Law: Legislative Process and Drafting
courses.description: Learn the inner workings of how a bill becomes a law, with an emphasis on the Georgia legislative process.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Legislative Interpretation Seminar
courses.description: Exploration of contemporary theories of, and debates in, statutory and constitutional interpretation.  Use of commentaries and, to a much smaller extent, Supreme Court cases from the last term or two.  Each student will complete a semester-long writing project on an interpretation question chosen in consultation with the professor.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: State and Local Governments
courses.description: Examination of the relationships among local governments, states, and the Federal government. Issues to be addressed include the role of local government, the source of local government power, and the advantages and disadvantages of decentralized decision making. These questions will be explored in both general and specific subject areas.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Natural Resources
courses.description: The law governing the acquisition and use of natural resources, with particular regard to natural resources on publicly-owned lands.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Patent Law
courses.description: Patents are federal exclusionary rights for inventions, and a few are worth billions of dollars.  Their complexity, high value, and intangibility have led to extensive litigation and judicial ingenuity at the Federal Circuit and Supreme Court.  Survey of the law and policy of validity, transactions, and enforcement for patents.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Patent Prosecution and Procedure
courses.description: Study of how to write and prosecute a United States patent application. The course both introduces students to common issues arising during patent prosecution and equips students with basic strategies to deal with those issues. The course also explores patent infringement analysis and opinion letter work in which patent lawyers routinely engage.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Patent Management
courses.description: An overview of practical patent management and correspondinglegal issues in four venues: operations, transactions (includingfinance), competition, and litigation.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Trademark Law
courses.description: Acquisition of trademark rights, registration, infringement, false advertising, dilution, remedies, and international aspects of trademark law.
courses.prerequisiteText: Students must be enrolled in the School of Law to register for this course

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Franchise Law
courses.description: Provides overview of the legal aspects of franchising as a distribution system.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Secured Transactions
courses.description: This commercial law course focuses on one of the most important devices in facilitating credit: secured financing when the collateral consists of personal property.
