courses.course_objectives: Students will understand the legal principles governing the attachment, perfection, and enforcement of security interests in personal property. Students will gain experience in statutory interpretation. Students will appreciate the economic interests and motivations of creditors and borrowers who engage in secured transactions.
courses.topical_outline: The term “personal property" includes tangible and intangible items such as motor vehicles, goods in store inventories, rights in copyrights, trademarks and patents, agricultural products and commodities, contract rights, payment intangibles, accounts receivable, and equipment. Article 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code Types of collateral defined by UCC Article 9 Perfection of security interests Priority among secured parties Priority between secured parties and other lien holders Treatment of security interests in bankruptcy
courses.prerequisiteText: Students must be enrolled in the School of Law to register for this course

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Securities Regulation
courses.description: Examination of controls relevant to the sale and distribution of securities by corporations, underwriters, and others, including such matters as scope of the securities laws, the public offering, exempt transactions, disclosure obligations, express and implied civil liability, and secondary distributions.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research I
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research II
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research III
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Disability and Education Law
courses.description: Students with disabilities are entitled to specific educational services and accommodations in public schools in the United States. This course will introduce undergraduate and graduate students to federal and state laws and regulations that apply to the provision of educational services for students with disabilities from birth through age 21.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Disability and Education Law
courses.description: Students with disabilities are entitled to specific educational services and accommodations in public schools in the United States. This course will introduce undergraduate and graduate students to federal and state laws and regulations that apply to the provision of educational services for students with disabilities from birth through age 21.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Employment Discrimination
courses.description: Law regulating distinctions in the employment relationship.  The emphasis is on federal statutory law regulating race, sex, religion, national origin, age, and disability discrimination in employment.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Undergraduate Research Thesis (or Final Project)
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data. Students will write or produce a thesis or other professional capstone product, such as a report or portfolio that describes their systematic and in-depth inquiry.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: State and Local Taxation
courses.description: A study of principles and problems of state and local taxation in our federal system. Examines ad valorem property taxes, corporate and personal income taxes, sales and use taxes, and  Federal constitutional limitations on state tax power.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Georgia Law Review
courses.description: Students participate in the management and production of a law journal through a combination of editing, writing, management, article selection, and other duties.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Georgia Law Review
courses.description: Students participate in the management and production of a law journal through a combination of editing, writing, management, article selection, and other duties.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Journal of Intellectual Property Law
courses.description: Students participate in the management and production of a law journal through a combination of editing, writing, management, article selection, and other duties.

courses.title: Journal of Intellectual Property Law
courses.description: Students participate in the management and production of a law journal through a combination of editing, writing, management, article selection, and other duties.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: The Georgia Journal of International and Comparative Law
courses.description: Students participate in the management and production of a law journal through a combination of editing, writing, management, article selection, and other duties.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: The Georgia Journal of International and Comparative Law
courses.description: Students participate in the management and production of a law journal through a combination of editing, writing, management, article selection, and other duties.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Georgia Criminal Law Review
courses.description: Students participate in the management and production of a law journal through a combination of editing, writing, management, article selection, and other duties.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Georgia Trial Court Practice
courses.description: Emphasis will be placed on Georgia trial practice through lectures, demonstrations, exercises, the performance of techniques and procedures, and mock trials. Each session includes a classroom instructional component, specific to Georgia court rules and procedure, as well as an opportunity for student performance to integrate doctrine, theory, skills, and legal ethics.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Legal Spanish I
courses.description: Spanish language skills used in legal settings. The focus will be on listening and speaking comprehension, with some reading and writing. A broad overview of the basics of the legal systems in Spanish-speaking countries will enable students to communicate legal concepts more accurately and efficiently.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Legal Spanish II
courses.description: Course will build upon the Spanish language skills used in legal settings covered in Legal Spanish I. The focus will be on advanced listening and speaking comprehension, with some reading and writing. An advanced overview of the basics of the legal systems in Spanish-speaking countries to enable students to communicate legal concepts more accurately and efficiently.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Trial Practice Seminar
courses.description: Trial methodology, including jury voir dire, opening statements in jury and bench trials, introduction of proof and pre-trial as well as trial objections to evidence, and delivery of final arguments.  Problems in civil and criminal litigation are analyzed, with emphasis on demonstration of techniques by students in the course.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Trial Practice Seminar
courses.description: Trial methodology, including jury voir dire, opening statements in jury and bench trials, introduction of proof and pre-trial as well as trial objections to evidence, and delivery of final arguments. Problems in civil and criminal litigation are analyzed, with emphasis on demonstration of techniques by students in the course.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: International Advocacy Seminar
courses.description: Preparation, handling of international law moot court case, and representation of hypothetical states before international legal tribunal. Topics covered impart knowledge of international legal reasoning, novel research, and effective oral advocacy. Enrollment extended by permission.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Moot Court Competition
courses.description: Student teams prepare appellate briefs and bench briefs and practice oral arguments under the supervision of a faculty advisor for regional, national, and international competitions. A student must be selected as a competing advocate who will attend a competition in the semester.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Negotiation Competition
courses.description: Team members prepare for oral negotiations and practice negotiation techniques under the direction of a faculty advisor for regional and national competitions. A student selected to compete is eligible for credit in the semester in which the competition is held.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Transactional Law Competition
courses.description: Team members prepare for oral negotiations, practice negotiation techniques, and draft transactional documents under the direction of a faculty advisor for regional and national competitions. A student selected to compete is eligible for credit in the semester in which the competition is held.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Hulsey-Gambrell Moot Court Competition
courses.description: A two-student team practices oral arguments under the supervision of a faculty advisor in preparation for a competition against the University of Florida before a panel of state and federal judges. A student registering for this course must be selected as a competing advocate who will attend the competition in the semester in which the student registers.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Mock Trial Competition
courses.description: Student teams prepare civil or criminal jury trials under the supervision of a faculty advisor by preparing and presenting pretrial evidentiary motions, opening statements, direct and cross examinations of witnesses, and closing arguments.  A student must be selected as a competing advocate who will attend a competition in the semester in which the student registers.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Child Welfare Mock Trial Simulation Course
courses.description: Through this simulation course, students will learn about the child welfare system, trauma-informed lawyering, and interdisciplinary collaboration through classroom instruction and participation in a mock termination of parental rights trial. Guest faculty will include attorneys, judges, and social workers.
courses.prerequisiteText: JURI 5040/7040 or JURI 5042 or JURI 5046 or JURI 5047 or JURI 4250/6250 or JURI 4250E/6250E

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Child Welfare Law and Practice
courses.description: Overview of child welfare dependency law and practice.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Intellectual Property Survey
courses.description: Federal intellectual property law and state law protection of trade secrets, unfair competition, and publicity rights, with special emphasis on trademark law, and constitutional, technological, and antitrust aspects of intellectual property protection.
courses.prerequisiteText: Students must be enrolled in the School of Law to register for this course

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Intellectual Property Survey
courses.description: Federal intellectual property law and state law protection of trade secrets, unfair competition, and publicity rights, with special emphasis on trademark law and constitutional, technological, and antitrust aspects of intellectual property protection.
courses.prerequisiteText: Students must be enrolled in the School of Law to register for this course

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Intellectual Property Research
courses.description: An introduction to researching intellectual property, including copyrights, patents, and trademarks. In addition to reviewing administrative regulation research, this course will explore a variety of free and fee-based tools. Topics include classification and search techniques and intellectual property searching in business research and competitive intelligence.
courses.prerequisiteText: JURI 5050/7050 or two of the following JURI 4430/6430 or JURI 4920/6920 or JURI 4930/6930 | Graduate Prerequisite | JURI 5050/7050 or two of the following JURI 4430/6430 or JURI 4920/6920 or JURI 4930/6930

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Workers Compensation
courses.description: The historical evolution and current operation of modern workers' compensation systems. Exploration of the extent to which the no-fault workers' compensation model could serve as an alternative to tort litigation in other areas of personal injury, such as medical malpractice.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Workers' Compensation
courses.description: The historical evolution and current operation of modern workers' compensation systems. Exploration of the extent to which the no-fault workers' compensation model could serve as an alternative to tort litigation in other areas of personal injury, such as medical malpractice.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Life Cycle of the Corporation
courses.description: A series of relatively complicated fact situations are analyzed, with special emphasis on tax, corporation law, and securities regulation aspects. Drafting exercises and legal memoranda are required to be completed.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Life Cycle of the Corporation
courses.description: A series of relatively complicated fact situations are analyzed, with special emphasis on tax, corporation law, and securities regulation aspects. Drafting exercises and legal memoranda are required to be completed.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Deals
courses.description: This course examines complex corporate transactions and contracts–that is, “deals.” The first component presents a framework for evaluating alternative transaction structures, including transaction costs, information economics, risk sharing and incentives, property rights, and finance. Students then apply these concepts to “live” deals negotiated by alumni in transactional legal practice.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Partnership Taxation
courses.description: Examination of the basic tax events in the life of an entityclassified as a partnership (including general partnerships,limited partnerships, and limited liability companies) such ascontributions of property, allocation of operating income anddeductions, allocation of entity-level indebtedness, current andliquidating distributions, and dispositions of interests in theentity.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Taxation of Business Enterprises
courses.description: The taxation of various business entities, including (1) Partnerships (2) C Corporations, and, to a lesser extent, (3) S Corporations. The course will examine the tax consequences of formations, operations, distributions, and liquidations of these entities.
courses.course_objectives: Understand the tax consequences of the choice of entity and formations of business entities. Assess the tax consequences of business enterprise operations, distributions, and liquidations. Apply their knowledge and use different sources of tax law to solve fact-pattern problems. Engage in a thoughtful discussion on the tax policy issues relating to these subjects.
courses.topical_outline: Introduction to business enterprise taxation and check-the-box rules -	Partnerships (Subchapter K): formations, accounting, operations, allocations, sales and exchanges, operating distributions, liquidating distributions, and terminations C Corporations (Subchapter C): formations, non-liquidating distributions, redemptions, partial liquidations, complete liquidations S Corporations (Subchapter S): brief overview

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Representing Investment Funds
courses.description: Review of the legal requirements concerning the structuring, formation, and regulation of pooled investment vehicles, particularly under the Investment Company Act of 1940 and the Investment Advisers Act of 1940. Attention also will be given to hedge funds, venture capital funds, private equity funds, and real estate partnerships.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to analyze a potential investment fund to determine whether that fund will be subject to the Investment Company Act of 1940 or whether it will be excepted. Students will understand the various entities involved in both a public and private investment fund and what the function of each of those entities is. Students will gain experience in the day-to-day role of a junior associate representing an investment fund in its offering. Students will gain exposure to the federal securities laws, regulations, and exemptions involved in both a public and private investment fund. Students will draft the term sheet for a private and public investment fund stating the material terms of an offering. Students will understand and be able to draft and negotiate the operative portions of an offering memorandum, including the Summary of Terms, Risk Factors and Conflicts of Interest, Investment Objectives and Strategies, and Plan of Distribution. Students will understand and be able to draft and negotiate the operative provisions of the investment advisory agreement and distribution agreement for an offering of an investment fund. Students will prepare portions of a Form ADV registering an entity under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940. Students will conduct basic research on the SEC’s Electronic Data Gathering, Analysis, and Retrieval (EDGAR) platform similar to that expected from a junior associate.
courses.topical_outline: • Introduction to the Securities Laws and the Investment Management Industry • What Is (and Is Not) an Investment Company • Registration and Disclosure under the Investment Company Act • Contents of a Prospectus • Fund Management: Advisory Function, Fees, and Contract Terms • Fund Governance: Fund Directors/Trustees, Fund Officers, and Fund Shareholders • Fund Capital Structure • Investments of an Investment Company • Fund Conflicts of Interests and Affiliated Transactions • Fund Distribution Channels • The Investment Advisers Act • Alternative Investment Funds I: Hedge Funds and Private Equity Funds • Alternative Investment Funds II: Private Investment Funds, Master-Feeder Funds, Real Estate Funds, and Business Development Companies • Scope of Representation: Ethical Issues in Investment Fund Representation
courses.prerequisiteText: Students must be enrolled in the School of Law to register for this course | Graduate Prerequisite | Students must be enrolled in the School of Law to register for this course

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Legal Aspects of Capital Utilization
courses.description: Basic concepts, institutions, instruments, and processes associated with financial markets and capital management in private and public sectors.  Special emphasis on practical illustrations of Theory of the Firm, powers of Federal Reserve Board, and consequences of diverse governmental fiscal and monetary policies.  Analysis of legal frameworks for major components of the financial services sector.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Federal Income Tax
courses.description: This course covers the fundamental and foundational principles of federal income taxation of individuals. It is the basic tax course that serves as the prerequisite for a variety of advanced tax courses.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Federal Income Tax
courses.description: This course covers the fundamental and foundational principles of federal income taxation of individuals. It is the basic tax course that serves as the prerequisite for a variety of advanced tax courses.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Business Basics for Lawyers
courses.description: Introduces non-business majors to basic business terminology and concepts to prepare students to better understand a broad array of business-related law courses. Students who have majored in business, have an MBA, have taken more than one accounting course in college, or are joint MBA/JD candidates may not take the course. Students who take this course may not take Accounting and Finance for Lawyers and vice versa.

Students who have majored in business, have an MBA, have taken more than one accounting course in college, or are joint MBA/JD candidates may not take the course. Students who take this course may not take Accounting and Finance for Lawyers and vice versa.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Tax Seminar
courses.description: This course will cover federal individual income tax issues that lawyers often deal with in practice. It will also cover tax policy issues that relate to incremental and fundamental tax reform proposals that are under consideration at the time of the course.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Tax Seminar
courses.description: This course will cover federal individual income tax issues that lawyers often deal with in practice. It will also cover tax policy issues that relate to incremental and fundamental tax reform proposals that are under consideration at the time of the course.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Family Justice Clinic - Service Learning
courses.description: Class discussion centers on readings in texts and policies of laws relating to family violence, as well as on theory and practice of lawyering in a litigation/negotiation context. Staff meetings survey existing cases, train on issues of direct relevance to the practice, and identify and discuss community problems for the client group.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Family Justice Clinic
courses.description: Class discussion centers on readings in texts and policies of laws relating to family violence, as well as on theory and practice of lawyering in a litigation/negotiation context. Staff meetings survey existing cases, train on issues of direct relevance to the practice, and identify and discuss community problems for the client group.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Family Justice Clinic Hours
courses.description: Students work as lay advocates and student practitioners to provide direct service to clients, including screening and referral, interviewing, counseling, pleading and case preparation, negotiation, and advocacy at final hearings under the Third Year Practice Act.  Class discussion centers on statutes relating to family violence, theory, and practice.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Prosecution I - Service Learning
courses.description: This course teaches how the 4th and 5th Amendments guide and limit law enforcement officers when they search or seize citizens and when they conduct pre-arrest interviews or post-arrest (custodial) interrogations. Students will also learn practical skills, including how to conduct a motion to suppress hearing and a Jackson-Denno hearing.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Prosecution I
courses.description: This course teaches how the 4th and 5th Amendments guide and limit law enforcement officers when they search or seize citizens and when they conduct pre-arrest interviews or post-arrest (custodial) interrogations. Students will also learn practical skills, including how to conduct a motion to suppress hearing and a Jackson-Denno hearing.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Prosecution II - Service Learning
courses.description: Clinical course in which students will work under the supervision of prosecutors in preparation and trial of pending misdeameanor cases, drafting of warrants, motions, orders, memoranda, and other legal documents. Students will also appear in court on behalf of prosecution.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Prosecution II
courses.description: Clinical course in which students will work under the supervision of prosecutors in preparation and trial of pending misdeameanor cases, drafting of warrants, motions, orders, memoranda, and other legal documents. Students will also appear in court on behalf of prosecution.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Prosecution II Hours
courses.description: A three-semester program. Students attend a weekly seminar andlearn how criminal cases are investigated, charged, andprosecuted in Georgia. Students extern to provide research,document drafting assistance, and make court appearances.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Prosecution III
courses.description: The procedural steps involved in the prosecution of a criminal case following a defendant’s not-guilty plea. Students will learn about jury trials and jury selection. Students will also learn about the search warrant requirement and its “well-recognized exceptions,” identification of suspects, Confrontation Clause, and Right to Counsel.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Prosecution III Hours
courses.description: Students will continue the process of learning the proper role of a prosecutor as a “minister of justice” in our criminal justice system. This portion encompasses working with professionals in this area.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Criminal Defense Practicum I - Service Learning Seminar
courses.description: The Law School owns and operates the Criminal Defense Clinic, which serves as the public defender for this judicial circuit. The full-time staff includes fourteen attorneys. Students assist the attorneys in all aspects of criminal defense representation and have significant client contact. This is the weekly seminar.
courses.course_objectives: Understand, through first-hand observation, the everyday operation of the Criminal Courts and be able to describe them Develop an understanding of the wide diversity of defendants going through the Criminal Law System Develop an understanding of client interviewing and client relations Develop an understanding of constructing a Theory of the Case Develop an appreciation for the intersections of gender, race, poverty, and the criminal law system Develop an understanding of the typical documents in a state-level criminal case, including arrest warrants, indictments, client interviews, police reports, and plea agreements Develop an understanding of pre-trial motion and hearing practice in criminal procedure This course introduces students to the indigent defense system through externship placements in public defender offices throughout Northeast Georgia. Students will gain practical experience in core legal skills including interviewing clients and witnesses, investigation, research and writing, and courtroom advocacy. The seminar is designed to facilitate your learning within your externship, to provide a safe space to discuss your work, to offer opportunities to group problem solve, to explore your professional identity as a future lawyer, and to increase your understanding of how the criminal legal system, including the indigent defense system, works in practice. There will also be required reflection journals. Reflection journals allow students to think critically about various aspects of their work, assess its impact on their professional development, and enhance their understanding of the systemic issues within our criminal legal system. The mid-semester journal must be a minimum of 3 pages and the end-of-the-semester reflection journal must be a minimum of 5 pages.
courses.topical_outline: Theory of the Case Investigation: Statutory Discovery; Pre-trial Motions - Discovery-Related Search and Seizure Elements of the Offense Pleading Guilty Interviewing Exercise Race and Representation Domestic Violence Cases Indigent Defense, Swimming Against the Current

courses.description: This is an intensive-learning class focused on the skills necessary for an animal welfare law practice. It will cover the legal regulation of animals in Georgia and the means of enforcing the various governing statutes. Students will learn to prepare the basic forms used in an animal welfare practice.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Practicum in Animal Welfare Skills I
courses.description: This is a practicum in which students will learn to identify, investigate, and prosecute animal welfare crimes and ordinance violations. In some semesters, it may include drafting ordinances and state laws, providing an analysis of laws presented for adoption by others, and other related tasks.
courses.course_objectives:
Students will learn local, state, and federal laws governing the treatment of animals in Georgia and the legal constraints on evidence collection. Students will work with professionals in the involved law enforcement communities to identify, investigate,
and prosecute breaches of these laws, as well as work with community members to come into compliance with welfare standards. Students will gain experience drafting the documents needed for each of these tasks.
courses.topical_outline: Students in this course will engage in at least 8 hours per week of practicum work and will earn variable credit depending on the number of hours they work. Students will participate in a weekly two-hour seminar addressing the law, processes, and social policy related to animal welfare laws as well as the skills required for an effective animal welfare practice. Students will engage in the following activities as part of their practicum work: participating in ride-alongs with animal control officers, including identifying violations and initial case preparation; working with investigators to compile evidence concerning animal welfare offenses; assisting government attorneys in conducting arraignments and trials; and presenting case studies. State and local animal welfare laws and ordinances Constitutional and other limitations on investigations Drafting relevant documents Understanding veterinary and other specialist reports Best practices for working with professionals across disciplines and the rules of the various courts Topics may vary depending on the nature of the cases and issues on which students will work.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Climate Change Seminar
courses.description: The law of climate change in the United States.
courses.course_objectives: Students will leave this course with a detailed understanding of how U.S. state and federal governments have responded to the evidence for climate change. Students will leave this course with a detailed understanding of the details of various legislative proposals to respond to climate change. Students will leave this course with a detailed understanding of how U.S. state and federal governments have defined, developed, compared, assessed, and chosen strategies to respond to climate change. Students will leave this course with a detailed understanding of how and why the United States has participated (and not participated) in international programs intended to respond to climate change. Students will leave this course with a detailed understanding of how U.S. environmental regulatory agencies have incorporated climate change into their agendas and requirements. Students will leave this course with a detailed understanding of how litigants have attempted to use the U.S. courts to force governmental action on climate change, and the outcomes of that litigation. Through participation in a graduate-level discussion seminar with a writing requirement, students will practice analysis of a complex, science-based regulatory topic.
courses.topical_outline: Climate change: what we know, how we know it, and what it means to trust or doubt that Climate goals: how we measure the problem and define desired future outcomes Response strategies: what they are, and how to compare them Mitigation: decarbonizing the energy, transport, agricultural, and other sectors Adaptation: planning for a world we don’t want Engineering: solar radiation management, carbon capture and storage, carbon removal, and other engineered solutions The United Nations framework: the Montreal protocol antecedent, UNFCCC, Kyoto, and Paris Domestic Litigation and the Courts: Massachusetts, AEP, Juliana, and beyond Federal Regulatory Integration: NEPA, CAA, CWA, ESA, and beyond Corporate Regulation: Securities Disclosure, #ExxonKnew, and related litigation Legislation: McCain-Lieberman, ACES, AB32, and beyond

courses.description: A look at climate change worldwide, with a focus on Georgia, looking at consequences on human health and safety, water availability, weather patterns, agriculture, infrastructure, biodiversity, environmental justice, and other issues.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Crimes Against Animals
courses.description: Examines criminal activities that harm non-human animals, including a review of applicable laws, legislative drafting considerations and practical application, special challenges inherent in working with animal victims who are also legally considered property, managing animals that are themselves dangerous, evidentiary and trial practice considerations, and Fourth Amendment search and seizure.
courses.course_objectives: Students will have a thorough understanding of animal law considerations in criminal law, including both prosecutorial and defense perspectives. Students will be able to critically evaluate laws affecting animals at multiple levels of government (primarily state law and local ordinances) and consider the practical realities of implementation and enforcement. Students will be able to persuasively and effectively communicate legal analysis and advice that also incorporates theory and policy objectives. Students will have practiced professional and ethical communication skills in the context of legal topics that are both complex and frequently emotionally fraught. Students will have a nuanced and practical understanding of the Fourth Amendment’s Search and Seizure protections, particularly as it relates to the special considerations necessary for animals as living evidence. (If 3 credit hours) Students will have drafted a sample piece of legislation and drafted documents designed for both attorneys and lay audiences in support of the proposed new law or ordinance.
courses.topical_outline: Criminal activities that harm non-human animals Criminal Law and animal protection Legislative drafting for animal laws. Fourth Amendment search and seizure

courses.description: Many controversial and fascinating issues face the modern familyand the legal system. This seminar provides the opportunity toexplore some of these issues in depth.  While the primary focuswill be on American family law, use will be made of comparativematerial.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: International Trade Laws
courses.description: National and international policies and laws relating to international trade and investment.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: International Trade and Workers Rights
courses.description: The debate surrounding workers’ rights in the global economy is increasingly heated and dogmatic, politicized, and divisive. Indeed, the recent election debates and executive orders to withdraw from trade commitments have highlighted divisions with respect to the manner and extent to which workers’ rights should be regulated in trade.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to demonstrate the ability to think about complex standards, legal systems, and trade and investment agreements. Students will be able to consider alternative approaches or fact patterns, using logical reasoning, to solve various international regulatory challenges. Students will be able to demonstrate a basic understanding of international labor standards, as well as various national approaches to incorporate those standards. They will also learn international economic legal agreements, and international doctrine applying trade principles to labor rights.
courses.topical_outline: What are international workers’ rights, how are they established, and what do they mean in theory and in practice? What tools are available to protect and promote them and how have these those tools been applied? When governments adopt policies that restrict trade to protect their workers, do they violate the principles of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) and World Trade Organization (WTO) jurisprudence? An overview of the intersection of WTO and International Labor Organization (ILO) principles Examine the evolution and implementation of labor provisions in U.S. trade agreements, from NAFTA through the present, and the labor eligibility criteria in U.S. trade preference programs and their enforcement. The course will conclude with a critical examination of the various mechanisms to promote workers’ rights and the compatibility of that system with international economic law.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Mediating Civil Cases
courses.description: Topics may include the origins of mediation, psychological obstacles to settlement, and case valuation.  The course will also explore mediation advocacy, negotiation of money and terms, and how to memorialize a settlement.  The future of mediation and possibilities for achieving an efficient and transparent marketplace will also be addressed.
courses.course_objectives: Students will understand the historical origins of mediation as an approach to civil case resolution. Students will identify barriers to successful mediation of civil cases. Students will learn how to value a client’s case based on risk assessment. Students will learn how to mediate a case on behalf of a client. Students will understand how to draft a settlement agreement. Students will explore emerging issues in mediation advocacy.
courses.topical_outline: 1.	Civil Discourse – The psychology and history of dispute resolution 2.	Heuristics – Biases at work beneath the surface 3.	Case Valuation 4.	Advocacy in Mediation – Preparing the client, communicating with the mediator, and persuading the opposing party 5.	At the Table – Negotiating money and terms 6.	Concluding – The importance and content of term sheets and final settlement agreements 7.	Future of Dispute Resolution – Moving toward a more transparent and efficient marketplace

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Banking Law
courses.description: Case and problem study of American banking system.  Focuses on federal and state regulation of financial institutions and includes analysis of bank formations, bank mergers, bank holding companies, and the FDIC.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Real Estate Development
courses.description: Selected issues in real estate development law, including financing, securities, tax, and business planning considerations. Coursework will include negotiation and drafting of documentation for real estate project and preparation of memoranda.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Independent Project
courses.description: Independent projects provide flexible opportunity to explore independently legal issues or questions sometimes not found in any course or seminar and without following format of a formal research paper.  Projects must involve significant legal, social, or empirical research or experience.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: International Law and Economic Development
courses.description: Impact on content of international law of increased concern of states with economic and social matters, both internally and at international level.  Effects of enlarged international community and emergence of important new actors (international organizations and transnational corporations) examined in light of new sources of international law.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Design and Construction Law
courses.description: Examines the legal framework of the design and construction process.  The course focuses on application of tort and contract law to contract formation and performance issues, and will examine legal remedies available to construction project participants.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Sports Law
courses.description: Basic theoretical and contractual premises of sports law, including areas of labor, antitrust, and contract law related to representation of athletic talent and sports businesses.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Sports Law
courses.description: Basic theoretical and contractual premises of sports law, including areas of labor, antitrust, and contract law related to representation of athletic talent and sports businesses.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Name, Image, and Likeness Agency
courses.description: Students will gain a comprehensive understanding of student-athletes’ Name, Image, and Likeness (NIL) needs from a high school until they graduate from higher education. Students will learn the duties and requirements of an NIL agent, state-specific sports agent rules, how to analyze NIL contracts, and athlete transfer/eligibility rules.
courses.course_objectives: Students will learn the ins and outs of the newest career in the sports industry – NIL agent. Students will learn the major NIL issues facing student-athletes as they navigate the transfer portal and enter into high-value agreements with NCAA institutions across the country. Students will learn the agent/athlete relationship and the requirements and expectations of an NIL agent.
courses.topical_outline: - State-by-state sports agent rules - The NIL agent/student-athlete relationship - Analysis of agent/athlete representation agreements - NIL rules and regulations - Transfer and eligibility rules - Analysis of NIL contracts from different conferences across the country - Updates on NIL rules in an ever-changing legal situation
courses.prerequisiteText: Students must be enrolled in the School of Law to register for this course
courses.offeredText: Offered every year. Offered every even-numbered year.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Complex Litigation
courses.description: Advanced civil procedure, including class actions, large case discovery, and judicial management of multi-party, multi-district litigation.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Entertainment Law
courses.description: Basic theoretical and contractual underpinnings of entertainment law and areas of intellectual property and contracts law related to representation of artistic talent.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Media Law
courses.description: Examination of a variety of legal issues affecting the newsmedia.  Discussion of traditional constitutional issues andexploration of how these traditional principles are balancedagainst competing interests not only in constitutional law butalso in common law and statutory regulations.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Media Law
courses.description: Examination of a variety of legal issues affecting the news media.  Discussion of traditional constitutional issues and exploration of how these traditional principles are balanced against competing interests not only in constitutional law but also in common law and statutory regulations.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Law, Science, and Technology
courses.description: Legal issues relating to science and technology, including governmental regulation of commercial application of scientific research, impact of technological developments on law, and constitutional concerns raised by modern science, technology, and medicine.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Law and Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: This course is about the developing role Artificial Intelligence plays in the practice of law.
courses.course_objectives: Students will become familiar with the technology underlying modern artificial intelligence tools Students will become familiar with their uses in the practice of law Students will become familiar with the impact this technology has on different areas of the law
courses.topical_outline: Ethical and Responsible use of Technology A History of Artificial Intelligence Analysis of the Technology Enabling Artificial Intelligence How Artificial Intelligence Impacts the Law Laws Regulating Artificial Intelligence A.I. Tools for the Practice of Law Evaluating and Implementing an A.I. Solution for your Practice

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Electronic Discovery
courses.description: Exploration of the legal issues that have arisen with the migration of business and personal transactions to the internet. Discussion of approaches to regulating internet transactions, statutes enacted to govern internet activity, and the emerging case law adapting existing statutory and case law to internet business.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Cybercrime
courses.description: Exploration of how changes in technology challenge the law's traditional approaches to combating criminal activity, enforcing criminal law, and balancing the rights of the public against the demands of justice.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Bioethics
courses.description: Examination of the legal, ethical, and social problems generatedby advances in health, medicine, and biotechnology. Some of theissues covered include human cloning and stem cell research,gene-based therapies, death and dying, reproductive technologies,experimentation with human subjects, and societal limits onscientific developments.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Bioethics
courses.description: Examination of the legal, ethical, and social problems generated by advances in health, medicine, and biotechnology. Some of the issues covered include human cloning and stem cell research, gene-based therapies, death and dying, reproductive technologies, experimentation with human subjects, and societal limits on scientific developments.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Regulating Digital Abuse
courses.description: Digital abuse is on the rise. People are increasingly using networked technologies to engage in harassment, stalking, privacy invasions, and surveillance. The law will often adapt to deal with harmful technologies, and one of the pressing challenges of our time is deciding whether and how to regulate digital abuse. This seminar will consider responses to the harms enabled by networked technologies, exploring issues related to civil rights, consumer protection, cybercrime, free speech, privacy, and private self-governance.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Special Legal Studies
courses.description: Selected areas of general law too narrow to occupy a full-semester course.  Topics may include such areas as the trial of a medical malpractice case, negotiation strategies in contract law, representation of an immigrant in deportation proceedings, etc.
courses.course_objectives: Course will provide the opportunity for upper-level Juris Doctor students to interact with resident and visiting faculty members whose teaching can draw from unique legal experiences and share knowledge about traditional and non-traditional legal topics. Juris Doctor students may be expected to complete research project(s) and Master of Laws students will be expected to meet additional requirements. Student learning will be evaluated at the discretion of the instructor but usually by way of written work.
courses.topical_outline: Course topics will vary depending upon the faculty member and course term but may include political influences on law, law practice challenges and opportunities, and other contemporary legal issues.

courses.title: Special Legal Studies

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Legal Topics Seminar
courses.description: Study of current legal topics and contemporary legal issuesusually not considered in traditional legal courses.  Facultymembers will include visitors who have unique experiences andoffer knowledge to enhance law student learning.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Legal Topics Seminar
courses.description: Study of current legal topics and contemporary legal issuesusually not considered in traditional legal courses. Facultymembers will include visitors who have unique experiences andoffer knowledge to enhance law student learning.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Political Leadership and the Law
courses.description: Examines the intersection of law and politics, with a special focus on leadership and how leadership qualities in the Executive and Legislative branches impact how federal laws ultimately affect the American public.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Criminal Tax Practice and Procedure
courses.description: Criminal tax investigations and prosecutions; constitutional defenses to the compulsory production of evidence; attorney-client privilege, confidentiality and other defenses available to taxpayers and third parties.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Public Health Law
courses.description: Public health law with historic, contemporary, and internationalcomparative law-policy perspectives, discusses the governmententities most involved in public health domestically andinternationally, and then surveys a range of applications.Coverage encompasses reproductive health, vaccination,biodefense, integration of genomics (study of gene function) andpopulation genetics into public health policy and practice, andinternational public health.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Law and Medicine
courses.description: Focuses on the relationship between health care providers and patients.  Topics include:  the treatment relationship, professional liability, licensing, access to care (including EMTALA), quality of care, privacy and confidentiality (including HIPAA), and informed consent.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Healthcare Fraud
courses.description: This course covers health care fraud and abuse laws as well as issues relating to the prosecution and defense of alleged wrongdoing within federal and state health care systems.
courses.course_objectives: Students will understand the civil and criminal laws and regulatory framework governing healthcare providers, such as hospitals, physicians and physician practices, medical device and pharmaceutical manufacturers, clinical laboratories and nursing homes. Students will understand criminal and civil prosecution and defense of actions against healthcare providers and individuals. Students will predict the remedies and civil and criminal penalties available to governmental entities and civil litigants. Students will identify and evaluate voluntary and mandatory compliance obligations and strategies faced by health care providers.
courses.topical_outline: I. Overview of Fraud and Abuse Laws II. Common Health Care Fraud Schemes III. The Prohibitions on Kickbacks IV. The Physician Self-Referral Prohibition (a.k.a. Stark Law”) V. The Civil False Claims Act VI. Criminal Enforcement VII. Administrative Enforcement VIII. Internal Investigations and Compliance Programs IX. Overpayments, Self-Disclosures and Settlements X. Pharmaceutical & Device Issues

courses.offeredText: Offered every year. Offered every even-numbered year. Offered every odd-numbered year.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Health Law Seminar
courses.description: The course will explore various topics in health law, healthpolicy, and bioethics, focusing on recurring themes of rationingscarce resources, balancing individual rights against communityneeds, and improving social welfare.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: The Law of American Health Care
courses.description: Examination of the United States health care delivery system as a regulated industry.  A survey of a variety of legal issues affecting health care providers and their interactions with commercial insurers, government health care programs, and state and federal regulators.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Mental Health Law
courses.description: The legal issues relating to mental health and illness, including competency, disability, confidentiality (HIPAA), duty to warn, civil commitment, criminal defenses, discrimination, and similar issues. Recommended for students planning careers in the helping professions, including social work, therapy, psychology, education, and criminal justice.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Community Health Law Partnership
courses.description: The Community Health Law Partnership will partner with health care professionals to tackle a variety of legal needs that impact patients, including immigration, disability rights, benefits, and family law. Students will have direct responsibility for all aspects of client representation in cases undertaken by the clinic.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Community Health Law Partnership Clinic Hours
courses.description: Course engages students in three primary learning experiences: direct exposure to the skills and methods of legal practice; focused application of legal concepts to real conflicts; and reflective appraisal of their own abilities, values, and professional goals.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Law and the Mind
courses.description: Examines how law is affected by both the traditional field of psychology and the emerging field of neuroscience. Broad topics include judge and jury decision-making, the psychological basis of criminal culpability, the psychological justifications for various legal rules and doctrines, and much more.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Food and Drug Law
courses.description: An overview of laws and regulations governing development, manufacturing, and commercial distribution of drugs, biologic, medical device products, and animal health products and how they relate to the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device industry. This includes domestic regulatory requirements and various regulatory agencies and their jurisdiction.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Whistleblower Litigation Seminar
courses.description: This seminar focuses on the major Federal whistleblower statute, the civil False Claims Act, and its role in driving Government investigations and large recoveries in recent years.  We examine liability theories and strategies for the Government, whistleblowers and defendants, as well as emerging new whistleblower programs.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Internal Investigations
courses.description: Examines how corporations and their personnel investigate their own conduct. Course will develop students’ understanding of the roles of management, the board of directors, and their respective counsel in corporate investigations and their interplay with government regulators, such as the Department of Justice and the Securities and Exchange Commission.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Employment Law
courses.description: Legal aspects of employment relationship, excluding union/management and statutory discrimination issues.  Primarily focuses on erosion of employment-at-will doctrine through various tort and contract theories.  Unemployment compensation, OSHA and wage/hour laws are also covered.
courses.course_objectives: Understand the relationship between federal employment protections, such as Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Fair Labor Standards Act, and state law protections Appreciate the dominance of common law doctrines, such as employment at will, which form the basis upon which employee protections rest Explore jurisprudence which arises when legislative employee protections are sharply restricted by judicial interpretations Compare and contrast, both orally and in writing, competing societal and economic interests which undergird parties’ arguments over employment law Recognize the breadth of employment law and its protean nature, evolving with technological and societal changes
courses.topical_outline: Law and the Workplace Hiring: Negligent and Otherwise Anti-discrimination Statues and Law The Fair Labor Standards Act and Other Wage-Hour Law, Regulation, and Litigation Health Benefits and Liberty Occupational Safety Workers’ Compensation Wrongful Discharge—The Rise and Fall of State Court Employment Actions Is there life, for employment lawyers, after employment? Retirement, including ADEA, retirement packages, lack of pension or adequate savings or safety net, complexity of ERISA, fiduciary duties, and the graying of the workforce

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: White Collar Prosecution
courses.description: An introduction to economic and political crimes (Georgia focus) under the label of “white collar crime,” including conspiracy, theft, fraud, racketeer-influenced and corrupt organizations (RICO), money laundering, computer and cyber-crimes, perjury and false statements, securities fraud, fraud upon financial institutions, and parallel non-criminal procedures associated with white collar crimes.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Commercial Law Seminar
courses.description: Advanced work on specific commercial law problems, including interrelationships between negotiability and security.  Students research, write, and defend a paper addressed to a specific problem area.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Corporate Law Appellate Litigation
courses.description: Advanced course in corporate law appellate litigation in which students learn through experiencing the roles of both oral advocate and Delaware Supreme Court Justice in connection with two currently pending Delaware Supreme Court cases and the actual briefs filed therein.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Public Interest Practicum
courses.description: How to discover peoples' needs, how to summon community's resources for meeting those needs, and how to determine what lawyers can do to insure community's services are functioning. Students are required to work with both service institutions and individuals who are clients of those institutions.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Public Interest Practicum Hours
courses.description: As part of the practicum, students are required to work with both service institutions and individuals who are clients of those institutions. This section is for the student's work.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Advanced Trial Practice
courses.description: Trials of advanced or multi-party cases, such as adverse possession, commercial litigation, conspiracy and product liability actions; some expanded problems in evidence and trial procedure.  Drafting projects include pre-trial documents, motions in limine, and post-trial motions.
courses.prerequisiteText: JURI 4250/6250 and JURI 5040/7040 | Undergraduate Pre or

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Law and Literature
courses.description: Literature and literary theory relevant to legal issues such as procedural problems in death penalty cases, criminal responsibility and plea bargaining, rape, obscenity, modern tort law and parole evidence rule.  Works covered include selections from:  Euripides, Koestler, Kierkegaard, Frisch, Eco, Fish, Nussbaum, Posner, Foucault, and Nietzche.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Elder Law
courses.description: The field of elder law is broad. This course surveys the core issues and areas of elder law practice and touches on emerging, trending issues.
courses.course_objectives: To explore ethical issues unique to elder law practice To expose the profoundly intimate and fundamental human and constitutional rights at stake in elder law advocacy To identify gaps in elder law and to think critically and creatively about needed changes to laws or approaches to elder law practice
courses.topical_outline: Elderly client population Representation of elders, including client capacity and attorney ethics Federal and state elderly programs, including Medicaid, Medicare, and Social Security Access to care and services, including housing, transportation, and medical care Advance care planning, including healthcare, surrogate decision-making, and advance directives Estate planning, including lifetime and estate disposition tools Judicial removal of rights in guardianship and conservatorship Abuse, neglect, and exploitation of elders

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Dispute Resolution and Systems Design
courses.description: In a world of settlement, this course prepares students to effectively represent clients through an understanding of the design and strategic election between ADR processes, and development of best practices as counsel in each process.  Both private processes (arbitration, negotiation, mediation) and public tribunals (domestic and international) are studied.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Advanced Dispute Resolution Systems Design
courses.description: The systemic analysis and design of dispute resolution processes, with a focus on large-scale and complex settings. Participants will survey various approaches to disputes, including facilitative, evaluative, transformative, and restorative practices. Topics will include problems of scale and methods for scaling the role of neutral parties.
courses.prerequisiteText: JURI 5975/7975 or JURI 5975E/7975E or JURI 5736/7736 or JURI 5736E/7736E or permission of department | Graduate Prerequisite | JURI 5975/7975 or JURI 5975E/7975E or JURI 5736/7736 or JURI 5736E/7736E or permission of department

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Advanced Dispute Resolution Systems Design
courses.description: The systemic analysis and design of dispute resolution processes, with a focus on large-scale and complex settings. Participants will survey various approaches to disputes, including facilitative, evaluative, transformative, and restorative practices. Topics will include problems of scale and methods for scaling the role of neutral parties.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Dispute Resolution in the 21st Century
courses.description: Students explore the modern ADR movement and its applications in law, government, business, community, and other spheres. Surveys the history of dispute resolution, various DR processes, and the work of practitioners who utilize them. Processes covered include mediation, arbitration, facilitation, case evaluation, restorative justice, mini-trials, online dispute resolution, and others.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Dispute Resolution in the 21st Century
courses.description: Students explore the modern ADR movement and its applications in law, government, business, community, and other spheres. Surveys the history of dispute resolution, various DR processes, and the work of practitioners who utilize them. Processes covered include mediation, arbitration, facilitation, case evaluation, restorative justice, mini-trials, online dispute resolution, and others.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Alternative Dispute Resolution Seminar
courses.description: Introduces the law and practices of negotiation, mediation, and arbitration through in-class discussions and role-playing exercises that simulate the work of lawyers in these contexts.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Alternative Dispute Resolution Seminar
courses.description:
Introduces the law and practices of negotiation, mediation, and arbitration through in-class discussions and role-playing 
exercises that simulate the work of lawyers in these contexts.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: ADR in the Workplace
courses.description: Skills and systems for conflict management in the workplace will prepare participants to use dispute resolution skills and design dispute resolution systems within the workplace. Participants will learn how to prevent conflict when appropriate, manage conflict when it arises, and empower stakeholders.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: ADR in the Workplace
courses.description: Skills and systems for conflict management in the workplace will prepare participants to use dispute resolution skills and design dispute resolution systems within the workplace. Participants will learn how to prevent conflict when appropriate, manage conflict when it arises, and empower stakeholders.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Comparative Labor and Employment Law
courses.description: Regulation of employment relationship by European Community and by national legal systems outside United States, as compared to United States labor and employment law.  This is a writing seminar.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: International Environmental Law
courses.description: Introduction to international environmental law and policy,focusing on how international environmental regimes emerge,develop, and influence behavior.  Selected case studies on topicssuch as acid rain, global warming, whaling, deforestation, andtrade in endangered species.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Legal Malpractice
courses.description: The law of malpractice and the context in which it arises with a view to developing a framework for analyzing problems the lawyer faces in order to avoid malpractice.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Child Endangerment and Sexual Exploitation - Service Learning
courses.description: This clinic trains students to represent victims of child sexual assault or exploitation in tort suits filed against their abusers. The clinic also meets for a two-hour seminar each week during which students will be trained on litigation skills, laws governing child sexual abuse cases, and legislation making these lawsuits possible.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Child Endangerment and Sexual Exploitation
courses.description: This clinic trains students to represent victims of child sexual assault or exploitation in tort suits filed against their abusers. The clinic also meets for a two-hour seminar each week during which students will be trained on litigation skills, laws governing child sexual abuse cases, and legislation making these lawsuits possible.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Child Endangerment and Sexual Exploitation Clinic Hours
courses.description: This clinic trains students to represent victims of child sexual assault or exploitation in tort suits filed against their abusers. The clinic also meets for a two-hour seminar each week during which students will be trained on litigation skills, laws governing child sexual abuse cases, and legislation making these lawsuits possible.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Corporate Counsel Externship Summer - Service Learning
courses.description: Exploration of the practice of law from the perspective of an in-house counsel. Covers legal and practical issues typically encountered in an in-house practice.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Corporate Counsel Externship Summer
courses.description: Exploration of the practice of law from the perspective of an in-house counsel. Covers legal and practical issues typically encountered in an in-house practice.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Corporate Counsel Externship  Summer
courses.description: Students will work in a legal department under the supervision of an in-house attorney and will gain first-hand knowledge about an in-house practice.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Advanced Copyright
courses.description: Issues of copyright created by modern communications technology; the historical and constitutional context of copyright and its relevance to the proposed National Information Infrastructure.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Education Law
courses.description: Examination of a variety of issues affecting educational institutions.  Discussion of the constitutional rights afforded students and teachers and exploration of how various federal and state statutes affect the community of learning in schools in the United States.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Education Law
courses.description: Examination of a variety of issues affecting educational institutions. Discussion of the constitutional rights afforded students and teachers and exploration of how various federal and state statutes affect the community of learning in schools in the United States.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Higher Education Law
courses.description: Examines the constitutional, statutory, administrative, and common-law principles that shape the structure, identity, and character of American public and private colleges and universities, including academic freedom, the rights and responsibilities of students and faculty, issues of identity and access, shared governance, accreditation and regulation.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Mass Torts Seminar
courses.description: Exploration of the overriding question of whether the courts can dispense individual justice in cases involving thousands of litigants. Course requirements will include writing a substantial research paper as well as actively participating in class discussion.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Western Legal Tradition
courses.description: Development of law in the western world -- continental Europe, the British Isles, North America and Latin America -- focusing on factors that cause law to change and that determine the nature and shape of the legal change.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Law and Institutions of the European Union
courses.description: History of the European Union, law-making and administrative institutions and processes, economic sectoral policies, including competition and state aids, transport and agriculture; internal market, freedoms (movement of goods, workers, capital, services); harmonization of national laws; external economic trade policy; impact of Single European Act and Treaty on European Union.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Capital Punishment
courses.description: Legal and social issues surrounding capital punishment.  Surveys legal issues in areas of criminal law and procedure, constitutional law and ethics which confront attorneys in capital cases.  Encourages students to synthesize social and legal facets to objectively evaluate complex issues involved in capital punishment.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Capital Punishment
courses.description: Legal and social issues surrounding capital punishment. Surveys legal issues in areas of criminal law, and procedure, constitutional law and ethics which confront attorneys in capital cases. Encourages students to synthesize social and legal facets to objectively evaluate complex issues involved in capital punishment.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Document Drafting: Contracts
courses.description: Provides opportunity to apply legal principles acquired in substantive courses to drafting of non-litigation documents.  Provides fundamental skills necessary to draft documents such as contracts and wills.  Also focuses on eliciting information from clients to provide factual basis for preparation of such documents.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Document Drafting: Contracts
courses.description: Provides opportunity to apply legal principles acquired in substantive courses to drafting of non-litigation documents. Provides fundamental skills necessary to draft documents such as contracts and wills. Also focuses on eliciting information from clients to provide factual basis for preparation of such documents.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: International Finance
courses.description: Analytical review of regulatory structures and procedures associated with international financial transactions.  Special emphasis is given to national and international markets that underlie these transactions.  Concept and financial instruments examined include capital adequacy, securitization, privatization, derivatives and swaps.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Mediation Clinic
courses.description: Students are required to participate in weekly two-hour classes and to be available at court for mediations for an average of five hours per week.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Mediation Clinic
courses.description: Students are required to participate in weekly two-hour classes and to be available at court for mediations for an average of five hours per week.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Global Governance
courses.description: In a globalizing world, the range of issues with cross-border implications only expands, from finance to trade, environment to human rights, food safety to sports. This course in International Law examines how and why different legal regimes have developed to govern these issues and when they succeed or fail.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Telecommunications Law and Policy
courses.description: Explores the rules and standards of U.S. telecommunications law. We examine market structures and regulatory treatment of a number of related electronic communications technologies—from wireline and wireless telephony to T.V. to the Internet backbone—whose convergence and recombination continue to challenge frameworks first established decades ago.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Global Governance Summer School: Independent Project
courses.description: During the Global Governance Summer School, students will engage with guest speakers and visit sites of historic and contemporary significance. This course will allow students to deepen their understanding of important issues in global governance and the context in which international legal institutions function. Students will critically reflect on these experiences through reflective papers and group projects.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Global Governance Summer School: Special Topics
courses.description: Examination of selected topics in global governance. Introduces actors and legal institutions that are involved in addressing issues of transnational or global significance and critically evaluates the role of various actors, legal regimes, and institutions in responding to those issues. The particular focus of the Global Governance Summer School will vary from year to year based on the Supervising Faculty Member’s area of expertise.
courses.course_objectives: By the end of this course, students will be able to identify a set of actors and legal institutions relevant to the special topic. By the end of this course, students will be able to understand how the relevant actors and institutions use legal doctrines and processes to try to set standards, encourage cooperation, facilitate compliance, or resolve disputes. By the end of this course, students will be able to understand how the actors and institutions relevant to the special topic fit within a larger set of transnational regimes and institutions.
courses.topical_outline: Each year, topics will be selected to complement the Supervising Faculty Member’s area of academic expertise and the content covered in this course’s corequisite, Global Governance Summer School: Independent Project.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: International Law Hackathon
courses.description: Introduces students to a contemporary challenge in the field of international law and prompts them to design and present a solution as part of a group. Students will learn about the historical context, institutional, legal, and theoretical frameworks, as well as the relevant law and policy frameworks, of the selected hackathon challenge through readings, lectures, recorded interviews, and more. Small groups will present their “hacks” or proposed solutions to a panel of judges at the end of the semester.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Immigration Law
courses.description: Examination of American immigration law and policy.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Crimmigration
courses.description: Crimmigration refers to the convergence of the criminal and immigration systems. Students in this course will learn to analyze the constitutional, statutory, and regulatory provisions implicated by noncitizens' interactions with the criminal justice system. They will also develop the foundation to debate the policies that animate crimmigration.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Business Immigration Law
courses.description: Examination of the intersection of immigration, labor, and employment issues from law and business perspectives. Introduces major areas of labor and employment law and explores the rights of immigrant workers under each area of law.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Refugee and Asylum Law
courses.description: The world’s refugees – persons forced to flee home countries – topped 15 million in 2014. This course will examine laws and policies governing forced migration. International and U.S. legal systems and institutions; substantive, procedural, and evidentiary aspects of an asylum claim; causes; and trafficking and other refugee experiences will be studied.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Comparative Constitutional Law
courses.description: Constitutional law of different nations, with emphasis on comparing United States constitutional theory, doctrine, and practice to the approaches of other constitutional regimes.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Supreme Court Seminar
courses.description: Consideration of selected cases pending for decision during current term of the Supreme Court of the United States.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Wage and Hour Law and Litigation
courses.description: Examines present trends in wage and hour litigation, the single dominant subject area in current labor and employment law practice.  The course examines the history of the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) and also treats wage and hour law in the states, both statutory and common law.

courses.subject: JURI
courses.title: Transferring Legal Skills
courses.description: How do law school, the bar exam, and legal practice connect? This course will review legal concepts and skills learned in law school through the lens of applying those skills to the bar exam and to legal practice.
courses.course_objectives: Students connect general components of the bar examination to concepts and skills learned in law and also to future legal or professional practice. Students, when presented with a legal problem, identify an appropriate response format and apply skills developed in law school to compose a reasoned response. Students select from a variety of learning strategies to learn and reinforce targeted content and concepts. Students implement learning strategies that are self-motivated and self-monitored.
courses.topical_outline: I. Law School, Bar Exam, and Legal Practice - a throughline II. Study Strategies III. Bar Examination Components
courses.prerequisiteText: Students must be enrolled in the School of Law to register for this course
