courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Writing for Youth
courses.description: Course engages students in writing for youth within a writing workshop setting. Students explore the processes, genres, conventions, and audiences of writing for youth. They learn from other writers and mentor texts to develop writing craft, skills, and techniques.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to compose texts following the conventions of different genres, such as picturebooks, poems, fairytales, short stories, novels, and nonfiction. Students will be able to write for youth, addressing different audiences' reading skills, needs, and interests. Students will be able to write children’s and young adult literature, incorporating knowledge from mentor texts and other writers. Students will be able to tell engaging stories, implementing writing techniques such as voice, narrative tension, and unforgettable language.
courses.topical_outline: Characteristics of literature authored for youth Children’s literature author interviews Writing picturebooks Writing poems Writing fairytales Writing fractured fairytales Writing short stories Writing nonfiction Generating story ideas Creating characters Writing the lead Using unforgettable Language Creating narrative tension Using the art of specificity Writing with voice

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Comics and Social Justice for Children and Youth
courses.description: Introduction to how comic texts can support social justice efforts in K-12 contexts. Students will analyze the socio-political importance and literacy-enhancing value of comics.
courses.course_objectives: Students will apply a critical lens to the selection, analysis, and public/scholarly discourse surrounding comic texts, especially in relationship to the inclusion of comic texts in educational spaces. Students will articulate the values inherent in and projected by comic texts, as well as those who critique and evaluate comic texts – particularly in relationship to their appropriateness for child and youth readers. Students will critically examine the contributions of authors and illustrators of comic texts using a variety of evaluation tools. Students will create written and visual responses to comic texts, incorporating a synthesis of peer-reviewed scholarly sources, research-based evidence, and applicable theory.
courses.topical_outline: * Comics and “Juvenile Delinquency” * Comics and Literacy Education * Comics and Representation * Superheroes and Villains * Comics and “America” * Comics and Belongingness * Comics and (In)Justices
courses.prerequisiteText: LLED 2110 or LLED 2110E or LLED 2110S or ENGL 1101 or ENGL 1101E or ENGL 1101S or ENGL 1102 or ENGL 1102E or ENGL 1102S | Pre or

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: International Children’s Literature
courses.description: Students explore the work of acclaimed international creators of books for children and youth. Students identify relevant theories, issues, and trends. They research the representation of different countries, languages, cultures, and communities in international children’s literature imported and published in the United States.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to analyze and present the work of acclaimed international creators of books for children and youth. Students will be able to critique the representation of different countries, languages, cultures, and communities in international children’s literature imported and published in the United States. Students will be able to discuss theories, issues, and trends in international children’s literature.
courses.topical_outline: International children’s literature theory, trends, and issues International children’s literature scholarship and social outreach Acclaimed international children’s literature creators and their work International children’s books, readers, and translators Representation of countries, languages, cultures, and communities

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Disney and Children’s Literature: Adaptations and Appropriations
courses.description: Course will engage students in critical examinations of Disney’s screen and theme-park adaptations of literary works for children. Original and Disney adaptations of texts such as Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, Pinocchio, Alice in Wonderland, and The Little Mermaid will be analyzed.
courses.course_objectives: Students will apply a critical lens to the analysis and public/scholarly discourse surrounding Disney’s book-adapted films and theme-park attractions, especially in relationship to gender, race, and class. Students will articulate values inherent in and projected by Disney films and theme-park attractions, especially in comparison to the children’s texts upon which they are based. Students will evaluate Disney texts, in comparison to the original children’s books, especially in relationship to notions of “America,” across time. Students will analyze Disney’s conceptualization of the child (and adult) audience and the impact of Disney inside and outside of the classroom. Students will create written and visual responses to Disney adaptations and their original children’s texts, incorporating a synthesis of peer-reviewed scholarly sources, research-based evidence, and applicable theory.
courses.topical_outline: * Reading popular culture and Disney - theoretical approaches * Disney’s approach to and perspective on adapting children’s texts * Differences between adaptations and appropriations of children’s texts * Gender and Disney * Race and Disney * Class and Disney * Disney and America, Across Time * Disney and the Child Audience, Inside and Outside the Classroom
courses.prerequisiteText: LLED 2110 or LLED 2110E or LLED 2110S or ENGL 1101 or ENGL 1101E or ENGL 1101S or ENGL 1102 or ENGL 1102E or ENGL 1102S | Pre or

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Planning Instruction in Secondary English Education
courses.description: In this course, students navigate two essential functions of a thriving secondary English classroom: planning and instruction. The work in this course delves deeply into assessments of and for learning; incorporate knowledge of language in historical, conventional, and structural contexts; and engage in and with multiple modes of texts.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to design goals for student learning based on Georgia performance standards and knowledge of student's needs and interest. Students will be able to differentiate instruction. Students will be able to construct rationales for instructional decision making based on sound theory and research. Students will be able to modify instructional methods, and revise plans using formative and summative assessment data and reflections on teaching.
courses.topical_outline:
1. Planning with Backwards Design
a. Learning goals
b. Learning objectives
c. Instructional frameworks 2. Assessment
a. Formative
b. Summative
c. Performance-based 3. Grading (and un-grading) 4. Reflective Praxis 5. Unit Planning Workshop (in preparation of spring student teaching)
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Adolescent and Young Adult Literature for a Changing World
courses.description: Adolescent literature and its selection and use in the middle school and high school to promote engagement with literature.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to identify a large body of literature in various genres appropriate for adolescents. Students will be able to examine in depth exceptional authors who write for adolescents. Students will be able to identify developmentally appropriate strategies through which adolescents may experience literature. Students will be able to explore themes and issues related to diversity in adolescent literature. Students will be able to develop guidelines for dealing with censorship issues in adolescent literature. Students will evaluate the historical development and cultural significance of YA literature in relation to adolescence, identity, and social change. Students will design instructional strategies that integrate YA literature into middle and high school classrooms to foster student engagement, critical thinking, and literacy growth. Students will develop assessments that measure student understanding of YA texts through multiple modalities (e.g., writing, discussion, creative projects, multimodal responses).
courses.topical_outline: The evolution of adolescent literature: An overview Literature and adolescent readers: Developmental perspectives Engagement with literature: Response processes through short fiction The adolescent novel since 1965: Major and minor authors Fantasy and science fiction for adolescents Poetry and drama for adolescents Nonfiction for adolescents Gender and culture in adolescent literature Censorship and adolescent literature

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Digital Tools and Social Media in Secondary English Education
courses.description: Teaching secondary English using the ever-increasing range of modes, media, literacies, and content available online. Critical exploration of the instructional value of specific tasks and tools, including hands-on work with participatory media. Students will integrate multiple digital tools into their own teaching and evaluate the impact of that integration.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to critically evaluate emerging technologies for instructional uses, literacies they evoke (and, potentially, supplant), and openings for content exploration. Students will be able to create multiple artifacts and exemplars for use in teaching adolescent readers and writers. Students will be able to explore digital and other methods of producing evidence of student understanding of the secondary English curriculum. Students will be able to negotiate assessment requirements within the current standards-based, 21st-century classroom. Students will be able to investigate, research, and analyze classroom practice and student learning for impact of digital technologies and social media on student learning.
courses.topical_outline: 1. Digital Youth 2. Technology in Secondary English Classrooms 3. Tools vs. Literacy Practices (as competing focuses) 4. Multimodal Composition 5. Gaming and Literacy Learning 6. Information Literacy 7. Digital Reading Practices 8. Assessment of Readers and Writers

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: AI and Language Learning
courses.description: An exploration of how artificial intelligence enhances language learning, focusing on natural language processing, its impact on linguistic analysis, and the sociocultural and ethical implications of AI-mediated language learning.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to explain the principles behind AI language models, including how these models are constructed, trained, and applied in the context of language learning. Students will critically assess existing AI-based tools and platforms for language learning, identifying strengths, limitations, and potential impacts on language acquisition and pedagogy. Students will be able to identify opportunities for enhancing language learning through AI, as well as potential challenges and ethical considerations in their implementation. Students will critique the role of artificial intelligence in language acquisition, examining its implications for linguistic diversity, cultural sensitivity, and educational equity. Students will propose innovative applications of AI language models to support language learning, grounded in theoretical knowledge and understanding of current technological capabilities and limitations.

courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to explain the principles behind AI language models, including how these models are constructed, trained, and applied in the context of language learning. Students will critically assess existing AI-based tools and platforms for language learning, identifying strengths, limitations, and potential impacts on language acquisition and pedagogy. Students will be able to identify opportunities for enhancing language learning through AI, as well as potential challenges and ethical considerations in their implementation. Students will critique the role of artificial intelligence in language acquisition, examining its implications for linguistic diversity, cultural sensitivity, and educational equity. Students will propose innovative applications of AI language models to support language learning, grounded in theoretical knowledge and understanding of current technological capabilities and limitations.
courses.topical_outline: A. Introduction to AI and Language Learning B. AI Language Models and Their Applications C. Critical Evaluation of AI in Language Learning D. Readings and course activities address critical issues at the intersection of language and globalization, spanning cross-disciplinary perspectives including linguistics, anthropology, and education.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to articulate contemporary theories and cutting-edge research on language and globalization. Students will be able to critically examine historical trends and foundational theories in the field of language and globalization. Students will be able to analyze and interpret complex issues of identity and positioning within the context of language and globalization. Students will be able to evaluate the multifaceted impact of globalization on language education, including a comprehensive analysis of language policy, technological advancements, and the integration of artificial intelligence.

courses.description: Students build on understanding of language and literacy development theory and research, learn to advocate for students and families, develop media and policy awareness to provide optimal learning environments for English learners, and conduct theory-based action research in their own classrooms in coordination with student teaching or internships.
courses.course_objectives: Students will learn to use their understanding of language and literacy development theory and research to provide optimal environments for teaching second and foreign languages, and to conduct teacher research in their language education contexts. Students will learn to provide second and foreign language students and their families with information, support, and assistance as they advocate together for best practice. Students will learn to support ESOL students and world language students and their families as they make decisions and advocate for themselves in the schools and community. Students will learn to model for their colleagues a variety of performance-based and communicative input techniques needed to work effectively with students. Students will learn to keep current with networks of language educators on social media. Students will learn to identify and utilize educational resources for best practice in secondary and foreign language learning, including technology. Students will learn to assist colleagues to appropriately select, adapt, and customize resources for student use.
courses.topical_outline: 1.  Classroom applications of current theories and research in performance-based language and literacy development. 2.  Language and education resources and advocacy for ESOL and World Language learners. 3.  The role of professional resource personnel in educational communities. 4.  Advocacy for ESOL students' access to all available academic resources. 5.  Action research to improve classroom practice.

courses.description: Examination of theories and empirical studies about immigration practices and policies in the United States. Exploration of how teachers can support immigrant students through culturally sustaining practices. The final project will explore a particular issue that immigrant communities face, based on their lived experiences in the United States.
courses.course_objectives: By the end of this course, students will have developed major research paradigms in immigration theory. By the end of this course, students will have developed their ability to integrate immigration theory into research. By the end of this course, students will become conversant in the intricacies of immigration theory, especially as it relates to K-12 education. By the end of this course, students will know how to critically read and assess a range of research in the field of immigration studies pertaining to education. By the end of this course, students will be able to apply knowledge of immigration theory constructs to inform instruction and improve communication with immigrant students and their families.
courses.topical_outline: 1. Why explore immigration theory and education? 2. Who are immigrants, and why do they come? 3. New immigration theory 4. Contemporary immigration 5. Immigration patterns 6. Segmented assimilation and selective acculturation 7. Immigrant children and adolescents 8. Immigrant schooling and education 9. Language and education 10. The 'new' 2nd generation 11. Immigrants' civic integration 12. Immigration policies post 1965 13. Social reaction to immigration policies 14. Immigration and identity

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Methods in Teaching English Education I
courses.description: Explores the underlying principles and practices of different approaches to the teaching of English in the areas of literature, reading, writing, and speaking. Provides support in constructing activities, assignments, assessments, and units that meet the differentiated needs of students given their diverse identities, lives, interests, and needs.
courses.course_objectives: Students will recognize and support the unique needs, skills, and motivation of the adolescent reader and writer. Students will study, read, problematize, and discuss writing process pedagogies and theories. Students will select, read, evaluate, and interpret literature in support of secondary classroom instruction and foster self-discovery, inclusivity, social justice, and change. Students will evaluate and experiment with multiple strategies and a range of content materials and texts, both traditional and alternative, in order to move toward the goal of reaching all students. Students will use multimodal composition and communication technologies to facilitate reflection and instruction.
courses.topical_outline: 1. Exploring different theoretical approaches to teaching English/Language Arts 2. Unique needs of secondary, adolescent readers and writers 3. Unique needs of differing instructional contexts; purposes for and approaches of teaching ELA in each 4. Text selection and approaches for reader/text matching 5. Instructional planning at the scope and sequence and unit levels 6. Curation and evaluation of strategies, teaching ideas, exemplars, mentor texts, etc. for classroom use

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: English Education Practicum Seminar I
courses.description: The first in a three-course sequence, this course examines the intersections between coursework and practice as students work across scaffolded professional experiences in both middle and high school English classrooms in a variety of contexts.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to observe and reflect on classroom learning and teaching. Students will be able to identify, recognize, and reflect on the characteristics of effective teaching (of English/Language Arts). Students will be able to compare and contrast pedagogical, structural, and contextual differences across multiple school contexts. Students will be able to co-plan activities and learning experiences with a mentor teacher, and evaluate the impact of subsequent instruction on pupil learning. Students will be able to analyze and discuss classroom/school experience in dialogue with theoretical and research-based texts from the field.
courses.topical_outline: 1. Learning and investigating secondary English classroom contexts 2. Understanding adolescent learners and their unique needs/interests as readers and writers 3. Secondary English curricular structures in placement sites 4. Methods of classroom management and responsive literacy teaching 5. Assessment tools and practices in response to student writing

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Methods in Teaching English Education II
courses.description: Explores the underlying principles and practices of different approaches to the teaching of English in the areas of literature, reading, writing, and speaking. Provides support in constructing units, lessons, and assessments that meet the differentiated needs of students given their diverse identities, literacies, and interests.
courses.course_objectives: Students will build a flexible toolkit of rigorous, meaningful teaching strategies and material for bringing composition modes, media, and tasks to life for diverse learners. Students will curate (and evaluate) strategies, teaching ideas, exemplars, mentor texts, etc. for instructional use. Students will apply research-based literacy strategies to instructional tasks, activities, and/or lessons in class and in field-based contexts. Students will develop and verbalize a philosophy in the teaching of literature in order to reflect on and defend their practice. Students will recognize ways in which our own identity and experience continue to play a role in the oppression of marginalized students to begin the work of dismantling systems of education inequity.
courses.topical_outline: 1. English/language arts curricular structures and designs for middle and high school contexts 2. Strategies for supporting readers and writers who struggle 3. Design, implement, and evaluate core practices for teaching English Language Arts 4. Assessment of and for learning 5. Methods of providing feedback on student work

courses.subject: LLED

courses.description: The second in a three-course sequence, this course examines the intersections between coursework and practice as students work across scaffolded professional experiences in both middle and high school English classrooms in a variety of contexts.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to identify, recognize, and reflect upon the characteristics of effective teaching (of English/Language Arts). Students will be able to recognize characteristics of school culture and classroom climate that affect the teaching and learning process. Students will be able to recognize examples of decision-making in the selection of content, instructional strategies, and management techniques. Students will be able to develop, implement, and evaluate the relative merits of a variety of techniques for classroom management and student motivation. Students will be able to engage in a scaffolded series of high-leverage practice tasks, evaluating the impact on both pupil learning and their understanding of what it means to teach English/Language Arts.
courses.topical_outline: 1. Teachers' professional identities 2. Analysis of texts, tools, and other resources available for teaching in practicum context 3. Methods of classroom management and responsive teaching 4. Uses of student data to inform next instruction 5. Implementation of a scaffolded series of high-leverage practice tasks; analysis of classroom video to inform next practice

courses.subject: LLED

courses.description: The third in a three-course sequence, this course examines the intersections between coursework and practice as students work across scaffolded professional experiences in both middle and high school English classrooms in a variety of contexts.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to plan structured, differentiated, original lessons with reference to appropriate English/Language Arts learning standards. Students will be able to plan sequenced unit plans with reference to the appropriate learning standards. Students will be able to use multimodal composition and communication technologies to facilitate reflection and instruction. Students will be able to build a repertoire of rigorous, meaningful teaching strategies and material for engaging with a diverse range of literacies, texts, and learners. Students will be able to teach a range of lessons, reflecting on and using feedback for continued growth, inquiry, and pedagogical skill.
courses.topical_outline: 1. Responsibilities of student teachers (and how we step into each of them) 2. Instructional planning at the lesson, unit and scope, and sequence levels 3. Working with "received curriculum" 4. Assessment of and for learning with particular attention to student self-direction and responsibility 5. Methods of responding to student work and providing connective, intentional feedback 6. Conducting teacher research and lesson study 7. Making teaching a career

courses.description: Overview of how children's and young adult literature in schools and society function as literary and societal resources to help readers critically understand themselves, the world, and themselves within the world.
courses.course_objectives: By the end of the course, students will read various genres and formats of children’s and young adult literature for today’s diverse youth populations. By the end of the course, students will describe and differentiate between key theories associated with children’s and young adult literature. By the end of the course, students will apply key theories associated with children's and young adult literature when responding to and analyzing said literature. By the end of the course, students will identify and explore primary awards for children’s and young adult literature. By the end of the course, students will use key resources to identify high quality children's and young adult literature. By the end of the course, students will make connections between school and societal policies and practices and access to children's and young adult literature.

courses.description: In this course, students navigate two essential functions of a thriving secondary English classroom - planning and instruction. The work in this course delves deeply into assessments of and for learning; incorporates knowledge of language in historical, conventional, and structural contexts; and engages in and with multiple modes of texts.

Students will be able to identify various types of artistic media and the significance of those media in the creation of and continuation of storylines. courses.description: Students build on understanding of language and literacy development theory and research, learn to advocate for studentsand families, develop media and policy awareness to provideoptimal learning environments for English learners, and conducttheory-based action research in their own classrooms incoordination with student teaching or internships.
courses.course_objectives: Students will learn to use their understanding of language and literacy development theory and research to provide optimal environments for teaching second and foreign languages, and to conduct teacher research in their language education contexts. Students will learn to provide second and foreign language students and their families with information, support, and assistance as they advocate together for best practice. Students will learn to support ESOL students and world language students and their families as they make decisions and advocate for themselves in the schools and community. Students will learn to model for their colleagues a variety of performance-based and communicative input techniques needed to work effectively with students. Students will learn to keep current with networks of language educators on social media. Students will learn to identify and utilize educational resources for best practice in secondary and foreign language learning, including technology. Students will learn to assist colleagues to appropriately select, adapt, and customize resources for student use.

Advocacy for ESOL students' access to all available academic resources. 5. Action research to improve classroom practice.

courses.description: Examination of theories and empirical studies about immigration practices and policies in the United States. Exploration of how teachers can support immigrant students through culturally sustaining practices. The final project will explore a particular issue that immigrant communities face, based on their lived experiences in the United States.
courses.course_objectives: By the end of this course, students will have developed major research paradigms in immigration theory. By the end of this course, students will become conversant in the intricacies of immigration theory, especially as it relates to K-12 education. By the end of this course, students will know how to critically read and assess a range of research in the field of immigration studies pertaining to education. By the end of this course, students will be able to apply knowledge of immigration theory constructs to inform instruction and improve communication with immigrant students and their families.

courses.title: Teaching Literature in Spanish for the K-12 Foreign Language Classroom
courses.description: A survey of Spanish children's literature from Pre-K to youngadult for K-12 Spanish foreign language educators. Works studiedcover representative texts from a range of Spanish speakingcountries that can be used with Spanish foreign language learners at various levels in United States classroom contexts.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: ESOL/EFL and World Language Teaching Practicum
courses.description: Guided teaching practice in second language or bilingualteaching, applying pedagogical knowledge and skills.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Diverse Children's Literature in a Digital Age
courses.description: Participants will engage with children’s literature that is presented in an electronic, digital, and/or alternative media format. They will learn and apply criteria for the critical evaluation and selection of children’s literature as digital media and develop instructional strategies for educational contexts to use with children’s literature in digital formats.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Supervised TESOL or World Language Internship
courses.description: Supervised TESOL or world language internship in a school for teachers employed with a provisional certificate. Students will teach full time, attend pre-planning and post-planning meetings, and present a topic of interest (personal or requested by their peers and/or instructors) in Student Teaching Seminar in World Language and TESOL Education Grades P-12 based on their teaching experience to their peers taking Full-Time Clinical Practice in TESOL or World Language Education, Grades P-12.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Non-Native Language Literacy: Elementary to Middle School Years
courses.description: Examines sociocultural and pedagogical issues concerning literacyin a non-native language in emergent and newly fluent readers andwriters in the elementary to middle school years.  Students applylinguistics to literacy theory and learn to contextualizeliteracy instruction and assessment to meet local community needs.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Non-Native Language Literacy: Elementary to Middle School Years
courses.description: Examines sociocultural and pedagogical issues concerning literacy in a non-native language in emergent and newly fluent readers and writers in the elementary to middle school years. Students apply linguistics to literacy theory and learn to contextualize literacy instruction and assessment to meet local community needs.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Non-native Language Literacy:  Secondary to Adult
courses.description: An introduction to sociocultural and pedagogical issuesconcerning writing, and reading in a non-native language inadolescents and adults.  Major theoretical perspectives andresearch traditions are reviewed.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Sociocultural Contexts of Linguistic Minority Education
courses.description: Exploration of theory and research on the social and cultural contexts of language minority education with particular reference to the United States.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Theory and Research in Second Language Writing
courses.description: Theories and current issues in the teaching and learning of second language composition and writing for academic purposes.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Applied Project in Language and Literacy Education
courses.description: Intensive study of a selected topic through library research and/or collection of original data.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Capstone Development and Lab
courses.description: In this Capstone course, students will synthesize previous course content. Students will create a portfolio and will share and interact with professionals in the field around their work.
courses.prerequisiteText: LLED 8345E and LLED 7925E and LLED 8360E and (EDAP 8113 or EDAP 8113E) and LLED 8732E and (EDAP 8025 or EDAP 8025E)

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Teacher Inquiry in English/Language Arts
courses.description: Teacher research, teacher inquiry, and publication of findings within discipline-specific communities of practice. This capstone course emphasizes translating research and theory into practice, as well as the use of teacher inquiry methods; practitioner writing; and imaginative, standards-informed literacy teaching in a diverse range of contexts and settings.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Teacher Inquiry in English/Language Arts
courses.description: Teacher research, teacher inquiry, and publication of findings within discipline-specific communities of practice. This capstone course emphasizes translating research and theory into practice as well as the use of teacher inquiry methods, practitioner writing, and imaginative, standards-informed literacy teaching in a diverse range of contexts and settings.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: International Graduate Internship I
courses.description: Provides international graduate teaching assistants with pronunciation skills and practice using spoken American English in academic settings. Students will learn about cultural expectations in U.S. undergraduate classrooms and will implement effective pedagogical practices in supervised peer teaching experiences.
courses.course_objectives: To become conversant with instructional practices and cultural norms in American higher education. To enhance student pronunciation and increase spoken English language fluency. To practice and improve classroom presentation skills.
courses.topical_outline: Diagnosis of language problems Structured opportunities to improve language proficiency Practice with English sound symbol system Work on word stress and sentence stress production Review of questions forms and intonation patterns Practice of vowels and consonants Fluency exercises

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: International Graduate Internship I
courses.description: Provides international graduate teaching assistants with pronunciation skills and practice using spoken American English in academic settings. Students will learn about cultural expectations in U.S. undergraduate classrooms and will implement effective pedagogical practices in supervised peer teaching experiences.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: International Graduate Internship II
courses.description: Provides international graduate teaching assistants with knowledge of pedagogical approaches and available support systems. The course focuses on English language for the classroom and cultural aspects of teaching, with emphasis on presentation skills and audience awareness.
courses.prerequisiteText: Level 2-4 on ITA-TEP or TOEFL speaking sub-test of at least 23 or IELTS speaking sub-bandscore of at least 7.0 or LLED 7768

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: International Graduate Internship II
courses.description: Provides international graduate teaching assistants with knowledge of pedagogical approaches and available support systems. The course focuses on English language for the classroom and cultural aspects of teaching, with emphasis on presentation skills and audience awareness.
courses.prerequisiteText: Level 2-4 on ITA-TEP or TOEFL speaking sub-test of at least 23 or IELTS speaking sub-bandscore of at least 7.0 or LLED 7768

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Graduate Teaching Seminar in Language and Literacy Education
courses.description: Provides graduate students with knowledge of pedagogical approaches and institutional support systems helpful in teaching in higher education in the department of Language and Literacy Education.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Graduate Teaching Seminar in Language and Literacy Education
courses.description: Provides graduate students with knowledge of pedagogical approaches and institutional support systems helpful in teaching in higher education in the department of Language and Literacy Education.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Teachers as Theorists in English Education
courses.description: Theoretical and philosophical approaches to education for secondary English Education teachers. Advanced professional consideration of the primary influence of theorizing and philosophy on teaching practice, both within and around the field of English Education.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Advanced English Education Methods
courses.description: Reading, writing, and assessment strategies for secondary English Education teachers. Translating research and theory into practice, teacher inquiry methods, authentic assessment, and imaginative, standards-informed literacy teaching in diverse contexts.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Teacher Action Research in English Education
courses.description: Using teacher action research in secondary English Education classrooms as a foundational component of responsive teaching which responds to the specific needs of each learner. Pedagogies of differentiation and authentic assessment, requiring participants to position themselves as both teachers and learners.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Teachers as Writers in English Education
courses.description: The practice of professional writing, focused on secondary English Education teachers and using a writing workshop approach. Feedback and response, emerging technologies for writing, and development of projects for publication.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Theories and Practices in Teaching Secondary Readers
courses.description: Integrates theory and practice in a collaborative examination of instructional approaches to teaching reading in secondary English contexts. It provides space and opportunity to interrogate the construct(s) of the "struggling reader" and to re-imagine how we design reading instruction that is effective and engaging for secondary readers who carry the weighted label of "struggling reader."

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Theories and Practices in Teaching Secondary Readers
courses.description: Integrates theory and practice in an examination of approaches to teaching reading in secondary English contexts. It interrogates the construct(s) of the "struggling reader" and reimagines how we design reading instruction that is effective and engaging for secondary readers who carry the weighted label of "struggling reader.”

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: New Literacies
courses.description: An overview of the ambiguities and tensions created by a current move from the long established autonomous model of reading to the New Literacy Studies (NLS). It also addresses the implications of NLS for teaching students to comprehend a wide range of texts.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Assessing Literacy Materials and Programs
courses.description: Assessment and evaluation of materials and programs for literacyinstruction in the classroom.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Assessment and Evaluation for Literacy Coaches
courses.description: Course is designed to develop and enrich literacy coaches’ assessment literacy. Course will show participants how to accurately and appropriately understand the accountability metrics used to gauge the status and progress of student learning at the building and district levels.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Culture and Literacy Classrooms
courses.description: Explores the ways culture transacts with teaching and learning in literacy classrooms.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Electronic Assessment in Literacy Classrooms
courses.description: Explores why and how to effectively use print-based andtechnological approaches to integrating electronic portfolioassessment into the literacy K-12 curriculum.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Advanced Seminar in Literacy Pedagogies
courses.description: Intensive seminar on issues of literacy teaching and learning inK-12 classrooms focusing on critical topical issues such astechnology, popular culture, or literacy and social class.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Doctoral Seminar in Language and Literacy Education
courses.description: Introduces doctoral students to what it means to be a scholar/researcher in academic contexts, to demystify the process involved in acquiring a doctoral degree, and to provide an introduction to the theory and practice of research in the field of language and literacy education.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Directed Study in Language and Literacy Education
courses.description: Directed readings in research related to language teaching and learning.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Theory and Research in Response to Literature, Grades P-12
courses.description: Theories of Rosenblatt, Iser, Bakhtin, and others.  Research in how readers create meaning from literature in elementary, secondary, and college classrooms.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Theoretical Stances on Literacy
courses.description: Exploration of theoretical and philosophical stances that influence literacy and literacy education.  This course is not a survey course; instead, at the discretion of the instructor, each iteration of this course will focus on the work of one theorist or school of theory (e.g., Derrida, Bakhtin, Reader Response).

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Justice as Praxis in Education
courses.description: In education, there is an urgent need to move from "justice as theory toward justice as praxis." Praxis is the ongoing relationship between dialogue, action, and reflection. Students will investigate culturally sustaining pedagogies, policies, and projects that center the teaching and learning experiences of Black, Indigenous, Latinx, and Asian/American communities.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Critical Discourse Analysis and Linguistic Ethnography
courses.description: Recent research and theories on the pedagogical role of discourse in first and second language classrooms.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Seminar on Thought and Language
courses.description: Theories of the relation between thought and language, with emphasis on the works of Vygotsky and educational theorists and researchers working from a Vygotskian frame.  Explores pedagogical implications for literacy, literature, and language learning.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Special Topics in Language and Literacy Education
courses.description: Selected topics related to the theory and research of language and literacy.
courses.course_objectives: Not applicable (will change from semester to semester based on special topic being offered)
courses.topical_outline: Not applicable (will change from semester to semester based on special topic being offered)

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Special Topics in Language and Literacy Education
courses.description: Selected topics related to the theory and research of language and literacy.
courses.course_objectives: Not applicable (will change from semester to semester based on special topic being offered)
courses.topical_outline: Not applicable (will change from semester to semester based on special topic being offered)

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Computer Assisted Language Learning
courses.description: Exploration of the theoretical and pedagogical implications of computer-assisted communication and multimedia in a wide array of language education contexts. Participants will have an opportunity to focus on specific empirical, theoretical, and/or pedagogical contexts that relate to their academic and professional specializations.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Youth Participatory Action Research
courses.description: Community-based learning to examine youth experiences in a changing urban landscape. Students will engage with theories of participatory and youth research methods in an applied setting.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Queer Theories and Education
courses.description: To queer is, fundamentally, to make strange. This course utilizes Queer Theory to make that which is normalized in and around the field of education, including the very concept of "normal," strange. As such, it engages different queer reading practices to work through various approaches to sexuality, pleasure, and identity in order to make the unthinkable in education thinkable.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Principles of Youth Community-Based Educational Research
courses.description: Examination of studies in Youth Participatory Action Research, Youth Civic Engagement, Youth Empowerment, and related realms. Drawing from Humanizing Research and Culturally Sustaining work, we approach work in education through critical engagement with the communities that surround schools and with a particular focus on ways in which youth voice can guide research practice.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: AI Applications in Qualitative Research
courses.description: Exploration of the use of artificial intelligence tools in enhancing graduate-level qualitative research and academic writing. Course covers the selection, integration, and ethical use of AI technologies to streamline data analysis, literature review, and manuscript preparation, aimed at advancing scholarly work and publication efforts.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to proficiently use specific AI tools to streamline the qualitative research process, including using these for literature review and data analysis. Students will be able to integrate AI-generated insights and analyses into their academic writing, enhancing the quality, depth, and breadth of their scholarly work. Students will critically assess the ethical implications of using AI tools in academic research, applying guidelines and best practices to ensure responsible use, data privacy, and academic integrity.
courses.topical_outline: I. Introduction to AI in qualitative research II. Enhancing qualitative research with AI III. Analyzing qualitative data with AI IV. Ethical use of AI in qualitative research V. Integrating AI into qualitative writing VI. Practical applications and hands-on learning VII. Course resources and assessment

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: AI Applications in Qualitative Research
courses.description: Exploration of the use of artificial intelligence tools in enhancing graduate-level qualitative research and academic writing. Course covers the selection, integration, and ethical use of AI technologies to streamline data analysis, literature review, and manuscript preparation, aimed at advancing scholarly work and publication efforts.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to proficiently use specific AI tools to streamline the qualitative research process, including using these for literature review and data analysis. Students will be able to integrate AI-generated insights and analyses into their academic writing, enhancing the quality, depth, and breadth of their scholarly work. Students will critically assess the ethical implications of using AI tools in academic research, applying guidelines and best practices to ensure responsible use, data privacy, and academic integrity.
courses.topical_outline: I. Introduction to AI in qualitative research II. Enhancing qualitative research with AI III. Analyzing qualitative data with AI IV. Ethical use of AI in qualitative research V. Integrating AI into qualitative writing VI. Practical applications and hands-on learning VII. Course resources and assessment

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Religion, Literacy, and Teacher Identity in Public Schools
courses.description: Historical, theoretical, and theological approaches to the ongoing presence of religion in public schooling in the United States. Emphasis on background and trends at the intersection of education, religion, sociology, and literacy education and practices.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Psychology of Reading
courses.description: Psychological foundations of reading ability, instructional methods, and materials.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Psychology of Reading
courses.description: Psychological foundations of reading ability, instructional methods, and materials.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Critical Pedagogies
courses.description: Examination of how critical teachers in elementary, secondary, and post-secondary schools, including teacher education programs, confront systems of oppression and teach for social justice. Exploration of sociopolitical contexts and sociohistorical roots of critical pedagogies. Development and critique of critical pedagogy in preK-12, university classrooms, and community organizations.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Culture, Literacy, and the Classroom
courses.description: Social and cultural factors that affect learning and teaching of literacy; application of multicultural perspectives to curriculum development and classroom literacy practice.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Race, Class, and Gender in Literature for Young People
courses.description: Historical evolution of representations of women and racial minorities in children's literature.  Theory and research exploring the relation between children's literature and changing sociocultural and political values and ideologies provide the framework for the course.  The relation between sociocultural and political values and more traditional aesthetic considerations.
courses.prerequisiteText: LLED 6310 or LLED 7310 or permission of department

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Bilingualism and Cognition
courses.description: Literature in the area of bilingualism, cognitive studies, neurolinguistics, language acquisition (first and second), and educational research to examine the dynamics of bilingual development and cognition in adults and children and the ensuing educational consequences.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Issues in Teaching Literature for Young People
courses.description: Examination of a number of often controversial issues that surround the writing, publication, and teaching of literature for young people. The issues are examined through intensive reading of research and popular literature on the subjects, as well as by reading the works that illustrate the various issues.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Popular Culture in Literacy Classrooms
courses.description: How schools should respond to popular culture especially in terms of literacy teaching and learning. Popular culture celebrates an end to elitism built on subjective notions of taste. It consists of everyday practices that connect a group of people to each other in particular times and places.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Popular Culture in Literacy Classrooms
courses.description: How schools should respond to popular culture especially in terms of literacy teaching and learning. Popular culture celebrates an end to elitism built on subjective notions of taste.  It consists of everyday practices that connect a group of people to each other in particular times and places.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: The History of Teaching Methods for Literacy Learning in the United States
courses.description: A historical examination of literacy education from colonial America to the present.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Theories and Models of Reading
courses.description: Students will explore and differentiate among theoretical lenses and models of reading instruction. They will use their understanding to critically evaluate literacy instructional practices and packaged reading programs and products.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Family and Community Literacies
courses.description: Critical assessment of research about family and community literacies and practices, including the role of class and culture in literacy; popular culture and digital and social media; and family and school involvement. Consideration of diverse methodologies and theoretical orientations in understanding families’ literate and community lives.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Literacy Frameworks and Practices with Special Populations
courses.description: Course will involve analysis of literacy programming and resources across educational contexts intended to support special populations in P-12 contexts. Students will explore approaches to support learners with exceptionalities and bi/multilingual learners through trauma-informed, evidence-based, and culturally relevant practices.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Theory and Research in English Education
courses.description: Exploration of historical and contemporary trends in theory and research about English language arts and adolescent literacies education.
courses.course_objectives: Exhibit introductory knowledge of a range of theoretical and empirical trends that are significant in research about English language arts and adolescent literacies education. Review, synthesize, and disseminate insights about emergent, contemporary trends in English language arts and adolescent literacy education. Exhibit in-depth knowledge of at least one theoretical and empirical topic that is significant in research about English language arts and adolescent literacies education. Articulate in writing a substantive synthesis of extant theoretical and/or empirical research about a scholarly topic of interest and explain the significance of these ideas for one’s own research.
courses.topical_outline: Section 1: Foundations to English Education (literacy, literacies, and adolescence/ts) Section 2: Recent Lines of Inquiry in English Education (e.g., identities, texts, classrooms, beyond schools) Section 3: Contemporary Conversations (inquiry work into recent publications and scholarship)

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Intensive Instruction in the Language Flagship Model
courses.description: Students are introduced to the theory and practice of intensive proficiency-oriented language instruction in the Language Flagship model. Course includes hands-on instructional opportunities in Language Flagship classrooms across various proficiency levels, peer and mentor feedback, and opportunities for action research.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Approaches to Curriculum in Secondary English Education
courses.description: Exploration of history and evolution of secondary English education curricula and classroom practice.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to apply knowledge of major curricular movements, publications, and seminal events within the field of secondary English/Language Arts to contextualize contemporary practices, tenets, and values. Students will be able to research and explore facets of English/Language Arts curricula: writing, reading, literary analysis, speaking, and language study. Students will be able to assess patterns and trends in assessment in secondary English/language arts including those related to standards movements. Students will be able to write (and submit for publication) original work synthesizing course concepts, histories, documents, and experiences.
courses.topical_outline: Section 1: Histories of English Education (1880's - present day) Section 2: Contextualization of Current and Emergent Practices Section 3:  Inquiry, Synthesis, and Writing

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Conducting Research in Language and Literacy Contexts
courses.description: The design and implementation of research in the field of language and literacy broadly conceived. Drawing on relevant theories, students will build and conduct theoretical and/or field-based studies that emerge from and construct new knowledge in language and literacy studies.
courses.course_objectives: Students will understand how to review theories and research in Language and Literacy, particularly as they relate to methodological approaches and innovations most relevant to contemporary and local contexts. Students will understand how to conduct a truncated literature review of Language and Literacy research across methodological and epistemological terrain in order to broaden student exposure while narrowing the focus for the purpose of conducting research. Students will understand how to construct a theoretical framework as well as methodological approach--including making decisions about relevant methods--for the implementation of a study in Language and Literacies. Students will understand how to initiate the IRB process for a study designed in the course. Students will understand how to conduct cursory analysis of data created through pilot study work in Language and Literacies.
courses.topical_outline: 1. Review of theories and research in Language and Literacies with a bent toward imminent study implementation 2. Identification of potential site for research as well as engagement with and analysis of relevant research in support of work that is of interest 3. Creation of rough study justification, with methodology and methods woven together with a literature review 4. Initiation of the IRB process 5. Data gathering and analysis 6. Research writing as well as a reflective engagement with the process of research implementation

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Temporalities and Social Change in Literacy Education
courses.description: Exploration of theory and research about temporality, time, and social change in educational research and the humanities, focusing in particular on foundational and contemporary scholarship in literacy studies.
courses.course_objectives: Exhibit introductory knowledge of a range of theories of temporality, time, and social change in educational research and the humanities. Exhibit introductory knowledge of a range of empirical trends that are significant in research about time, temporality, and social change in literacy studies. Articulate in writing a substantive synthesis of scholarship about at least one theoretical and/or empirical topic that is significant in research about time, temporality, and social change in literacy studies.
courses.topical_outline: Section 1: Introduction to foundational theories of time in literacy studies and the humanities (e.g., Bahktin's chronotope) Section 2: Temporalities, time, and social change in contemporary scholarship: past, presents, and futures (e.g., queer and trans temporalities, Afrofuturism) Section 3: Collective inquiry into recent literacy research about temporality, time, and social change

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Internship in Secondary English Education Teaching and Supervision
courses.description: Teaching and field supervision of English Education teachercandidates at the secondary level.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Ethnography of Language and Literacy
courses.description: Course immerses students in ethnography as a logic-of-inquiry guiding empirical research and theory building with respect to written and oral language practices embedded in formal and informal learning contexts. Introduces the theories and ethics undergirding this logic-of-inquiry alongside data construction methods and approaches for reflexivity and humanization.
courses.course_objectives: Articulate an understanding of ethnography as a logic-of-inquiry (i.e., a theory-method complex) for understanding language and literacy practices in formal and informal learning contexts Exhibit introductory knowledge of theories of language and literacy (i.e., oral and written language) Use an ethnographic perspective to construct data about formal and informal learning contexts through an attention to oral and written language Reflexively address questions of ethics, power, and research subjectivities when investigating language and literacy practices in formal and informal learning contexts
courses.topical_outline:
1. Locating Ethnography of Language and Literacy: Process-Product and Interpretive Traditions to Studying Formal and Informal Learning Contexts 2. Introduction to Ethnographic Approaches to Language and Literacy
o	Methodological Foundations
o	Theories of Language and Literacy
o	Humanizing Research of Learning Contexts
o	Exemplar Ethnographies of Language and Literacy 3. Constructing Ethnographic Data of Oral and Written Language to Understand Formal and Informal Learning Contexts
o	Designing Research Questions about Formal and Informal Learning Contexts through a Focus on Oral and Written Language
o	Documenting Oral and Written Language in Formal and Informal Learning Contexts through Participant Observation and Fieldnotes
o	Understanding Oral and Written Language Hierarchies in Formal and Informal Learning Contexts through Social and Spatial Mapping
o	Conducting Language and Literacy Interviews to Understand Formal and Informal Learning Contexts 4.  Interrogating the Past, Present, and Future of the Ethnography of Language and Literacy

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Arts-Based Inquiry in Diverse Learning Communities
courses.description: Examination of techniques of arts-based scholarship to increase the value, validity, and impact of qualitative research for understanding culturally and linguistically diverse learning communities. Students will practice poetic, theatrical, and artistic data collection, analysis and representation. Students will develop focused expertise, fostering a rigorous critical community for arts-based scholarship.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Arts-Based Inquiry in Diverse Learning Communities
courses.description: Examination of techniques of arts-based scholarship to increase the value, validity, and impact of qualitative research for understanding culturally and linguistically diverse learning communities.  Students will practice poetic, theatrical, and artistic data collection, analysis, and representation.  Students will develop focused expertise, fostering a rigorous critical community for arts-based scholarship.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Research on Second Language Acquisition
courses.description: Research and theories on the acquisition of other languages in classroom settings.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Translingual Memoir
courses.description: Translingual Memoir refers to autobiographical writings that revolve around an exiled or émigré writer's enforced adoption of a new language and/or the writer wrestling with one's own and another linguistic and cultural personal identity. Students will critically read published works and produce memoirs of their own.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: An Advanced Poetry Workshop for Interdisciplinary Understanding
courses.description: Students acquire poetic craft to write poetry which crossesdisciplinary, cultural, and linguistic boundaries. This“bootcamp” seminar guides students on “poetic fieldtrips” tostimulate collisions between disparate disciplinary vocabulariesand knowledges. Daily research and reading help craft poems thatdraw upon what has been experienced, witnessed, studied, and learned.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: An Advanced Poetry Workshop for Interdisciplinary Understanding
courses.description: Students acquire poetic craft to write poetry which crosses disciplinary, cultural, and linguistic boundaries. This “bootcamp” seminar guides students on “poetic fieldtrips” to stimulate collisions between disparate disciplinary vocabularies and knowledges. Daily research and reading help craft poems that draw upon what has been experienced, witnessed, studied, and learned.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Discourse Analysis for Educators
courses.description: Course supports participants in developing critical awareness of how their coaching conversations with teachers impact peer and student relationships. Participants will learn to “do” discourse analysis by engaging in collaborative and recursive roleplaying with data from classroom and coaching interactions.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Qualitative Research Writing Workshop
courses.description: Provides intensive support for graduate students who are writing up qualitative research studies for professional journals, theses, and/or dissertations. Explores a variety of models of writing within qualitative research traditions across disciplines. Supports writers through individual writing conferences, structured writing time, and group feedback.

courses.subject: LLED
courses.title: Qualitative Research Writing Workshop
courses.description:
Provides intensive support for graduate students who are writing up qualitative research studies for professional journals,
theses, and/or dissertations. Explores a variety of models of writing within qualitative research traditions across
disciplines. Supports writers through individual writing conferences, structured writing time, and group feedback.

courses.subject: LLOD
courses.title: Intercultural Workplace Leadership
courses.description: Theories, models, and practices on how to lead effectively within intercultural workplaces. As intercultural initiatives require learning, development, and change, leaders are needed to guide these efforts. Using readings, inventories, reports, and group mentoring, students will develop learning interventions to increase their individual and group level intercultural and leadership competencies.
courses.course_objectives: Upon completion of the course, students will be able to identify theories and practices employed to lead inclusively and develop those who lead in intercultural workplaces. Upon completion of the course, students will be able to identify and value differences in workplace practices that exist among intercultural members of modern organizations. Upon completion of the course, students will be able to recognize and manage intercultural conflict styles. Upon completion of the course, students will be able to explore and reflect on their personal cultural identities and experiences in the context of intercultural leadership. Upon completion of the course, students will be able to create an individual and a group level plan to increase intercultural development competencies. Upon completion of the course, students will be able to mentor classmates in peer groups on their progress in implementing their individual intercultural development plan. Upon completion of the course, students will be able to develop learning interventions to increase group level intercultural competency.
courses.topical_outline: •	Describe the theory and practice on how to lead an intercultural workplace •	Develop interculturally competence at the individual level •	Manage intercultural conflict in the workplace •	Develop intercultural competence at the group level

courses.subject: LLOD
courses.title: Complexity Leadership Practicum
courses.description: Working independently, prospective graduates of the Complexity Leadership Certificate will complete a capstone project. Students will facilitate solving a complex problem within an organizational context using analyses, synthesizing and implementing adaptive or complexity leadership principles. Alternatively, students may explore and advance the scholarly research on adaptive or complexity leadership.
courses.course_objectives: At the completion of this course, student practitioners will be able to develop an assessment of an adaptive or complexity leadership implementation plan to investigate a complex organizational problem informed by a synthesis of prior readings. At the completion of this course, student practitioners will be able to develop a plan to engage appropriate team members and stakeholders. At the completion of this course, student practitioners will be able to lead a team to solve a complex leadership issue using adaptive or complexity leadership principles. At the completion of this course, student scholars will be able to conduct a literature review. At the completion of this course, student scholars will be able to identify a research question(s)/framework and methodology. At the completion of this course, student scholars will be able to complete IRB as needed. At the completion of this course, student scholars will be able to collect data, analyze findings, present results, and discuss results and next steps.

Adaptive or Complexity Leadership Practice or Research Implementation
• Review of relevant certificate content • Develop problem statement/ proposed intervention • Conduct review of literature • Conduct analysis • Design intervention/research • Collect data • Conduct intervention/research • Summarize findings and reflect on process • Finalize project report and summary presentation project

courses.subject: LLOD
courses.title: Learning Analytics
courses.description: Course prepares students to understand and use emerging quantitative methods, drawn from statistics and data science, to improve learning and teaching in various contexts. Students will explore various data sources within educational environments, learn to use analytic tools, and apply insights to support decision-making in educational settings.
courses.course_objectives: As a result of lectures, discussions, group process activities, and independent projects, students will be able to explain the fundamental concepts and scope of learning analytics. As a result of lectures, discussions, group process activities, and independent projects, students will be able to identify and describe various data sources used in learning analytics. As a result of lectures, discussions, group process activities, and independent projects, students will be able to utilize data mining and statistical methods to analyze educational data. As a result of lectures, discussions, group process activities, and independent projects, students will be able to interpret results from learning analytics to inform instructional practices. As a result of lectures, discussions, group process activities, and independent projects, students will be able to critically assess ethical considerations related to data collection, analysis, and use in education (and organizations). As a result of lectures, discussions, group process activities, and independent projects, students will be able to develop practical skills using learning analytics tools and software.
courses.topical_outline:
This course guides you both the latest learning analytics algorithms and tools as well as how to engineer data streams to turn raw data into interpretable and valuable features. Successful use of learning analytics depends on understanding both algorithms and learning, including the social context that surrounds learning (Yoon & Han, 2023).

Module 1: Introduction to Course Module 2: Alignment and Measurement Plan Module 3: Generating Data (Data mining techniques) Module 4: Applications of Learning Analytics: Summarizing the Evidence Module 5: Beyond Return-on-Learning (ROL) to Optimization

courses.subject: MARK
courses.title: Principles of Marketing
courses.description: Examination of the ways organizations satisfy consumer and organizational needs and wants for products and services.  Emphasis is placed on how the elements of the marketing mix are used to provide customer satisfaction in the marketing of goods and services, both domestically and internationally.
courses.course_objectives: Students will define and explain the marketing concept and related terminology. Students will explain the importance of target markets and understand segmentation and positioning. Students will understand and be able to apply the elements of the marketing mix. Students will explain the importance of and the basic methodologies of marketing research. Students will know the differences between domestic and international marketing environments and understand how strategies need to be adjusted. Students will identify and appropriately respond to ethical issues faced by marketing managers.
courses.topical_outline: Marketing Environment including current demographic and economic data Marketing Ethics including AMA code of ethics Introduction to marketing research Buyer Behavior Target Marketing and Segmentation Product issues Pricing issues Promotional issues Place issues International Marketing Services Marketing Marketing Planning Online Marketing Issues

courses.subject: MARK
courses.title: Marketing Research for Business Decisions
courses.description: The value and methods of marketing research in the context of business decision making.  The course first stresses the process of obtaining information, and then emphasizes the use of this information to reduce the risks in marketing decision making.
courses.course_objectives: Students can distinguish various research methods including focus groups and surveys. courses.subject: MARK
courses.title: Professional Selling and Customer Relationship Management
courses.description: Development of professional selling skills through experiential learning emphasizing persuasive communication, adaptive selling, and professionalism. Topics include prospecting, needs discovery, presenting, objections, closing, and negotiation. Role-plays and industry-judged sales competitions reinforce sales concepts, prepare students for leadership and career success in sales.
courses.course_objectives: Students will describe career opportunities and roles in sales. Students will identify key elements of persuasive communication in selling. Students will demonstrate the steps of the sales process. Students will conduct a consultative sales meeting using effective selling techniques. Students will apply adaptive selling and persuasive communication techniques. Students will demonstrate professionalism and recognize ethical considerations in sales interactions.

courses.subject: MARK
courses.title: Services Marketing
courses.description: Examination of the nature and features of services that distinguish marketing of services from marketing of physical goods. Emphasis is placed on adapting the marketing mix to retain customers and build loyalty. Models of services marketing, including the service profit chain and the service quality gap model, are introduced.
courses.course_objectives: Students will identify the differences between marketing in the services (versus goods manufacturing) sector and the strategic implications of the defining attributed of services. Students will understand how services can add value and serve as a strategic competitive advantage in both the services and manufacturing sectors. Students will identify and analyze the various components of the services marketing mix (7Ps) as well as key issues required in managing service quality. Students will understand the human element unique to service delivery and the role of employees and customers in service delivery, customer satisfaction, and service recovery. Students will recognize other key issues for the services sector, such as the changing roles of technology and the managing service capacity and demand.

courses.prerequisiteText: MARK 3000 or MARK 3000E or MARK 3000H or MARK 3001 or MARK 3001H or MARK 3001E

courses.subject: MARK
courses.title: Multicultural Marketing
courses.description: Focuses on applying marketing principles to multicultural consumer segments in the United States. It is designed to help students develop an understanding of various multicultural consumers in the U.S. and learn how to effectively reach them through various marketing tools.
courses.course_objectives: Students will review and understand the scope and importance of multicultural marketing. Students will describe and apply concepts and strategies that companies use in targeting different racial and ethnic consumer groups. Students will identify the market potential, buying patterns, and other characteristics of selected racial and ethnic groups. Students will explain what race is, what is racial/ethnic identity, what does it mean to be "ethnic" or a "minority." Students will describe what marketers can do to enhance the valuing of diversity in the marketplace and being more culturally sensitive to customers from diverse backgrounds.
courses.topical_outline: The multicultural consumer and the marketing mix The influence of culture on marketing and advertising to multicultural consumers Reaching Hispanic consumers Reaching African American consumers Reaching Asian American consumers Advertising agencies and multicultural consumers Ethics and social responsibility in selling to multicultural consumers
courses.prerequisiteText: MARK 3000 or MARK 3000E or MARK 3000H or MARK 3001 or MARK 3001H or MARK 3001E

courses.subject: MARK
courses.title: Digital Marketing Privacy and Ethics
courses.description: Examination of the impact of data collection and privacy issues, social advertising norms, corporate and governmental policies, and the overall effects on marketing practices around the world. A comparison of European, Asian, and United States consumer attitudes, law, and ethics.
courses.course_objectives: At the end of this course, students will have gained a deep understanding of the business of digital advertising and the impact big data and AI has on consumers. At the end of this course, students will know what data the largest platforms are collecting on individual consumers and what can be done about it (EU vs U.S.). At the end of this course, students will know how to consider the ethics and unintended consequences of today’s practices and form a personal stance drawing the line between influence and manipulation. At the end of this course, students will understand the basics of the law surrounding data: GDPR vs U.S. state laws and the case for U.S. national regulation. At the end of this course, students will have gained an understanding of the current options for privacy-preserving advertising of the future and understand how to navigate a future dominated by big data and artificial intelligence.
courses.topical_outline: Evolution of Digital Marketing Big Data and AI The I in AI Foundations of Advertising Delivery The AdTech Ecosystem Out of Control: Exploitation of Consumers Harmful Effects of Profiling and Behavioral Advertising The Surveillance Economy The Platforms: Meta, Google, Amazon, TikTok, Apple Data Ethics and AI Avoiding Unintended Consequences The Law: GDPR The Law: U.S. The Future: Privacy-Preserving Advertising Future Proofing: How to Remain Relevant as a Human
courses.prerequisiteText: MARK 3000 or MARK 3000E or MARK 3000H or MARK 3001 or MARK 3001E or MARK 3001H
