courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Global-Popular Music
courses.description: Rotating subjects in popular music that circulate globally, drawing upon a wide variety of styles and genres. Course content will be drawn from such topics as media industries, fandom, global jazz, third cinema music, festivals, electronica, and digital cultures. Students will discuss the ethical and political impacts of these musical expressions, and evaluate consumer practices as American and global citizens.
courses.course_objectives: Upon completion, the successful student will be able to assess popular music from different parts of the world. Upon completion, the successful student will be able to evaluate the impact and role of popular music in identity, history, and society within localized and globalized contexts. Upon completion, the successful student will be able to adapt methods for analyzing socio-cultural issues in case studies that have ethical and political implications for individuals and communities. Upon completion, the successful student will be able to analyze the multicultural roots of popular music in America.
courses.topical_outline: Intersections of the popular and the global in expressive culture Early sound recording technology, listening, and place-making in America and global contexts Popular music in global circuits of technology, media, and industry Multicultural roots of popular music in America African-American and Latin-American jazz in global perspectives Asian-American film music and social justice

courses.subject: MUSI

courses.description: A historical survey of the development of jazz as an indigenousAmerican art form.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: History and Analysis of Rock Music
courses.description: The study of rock music from its origins to the present. Examination of the place of rock music in society, from its rootsin African American blues and European American folk to its placein current society.
courses.course_objectives: Upon completion, the successful student will be able to analyze the aesthetic qualities of rock music; students will identify patterns and draw conclusions based on this evidence. Upon completion, the successful student will be able to assess the commonality and diversity of the various cultures that have contributed to the development of rock in America; Students will gain an awareness of how their own musical choices are both effected by their environment and cause an effect on their environment. Upon completion, the successful student will be able to evaluate the impact and the role of rock music in society. Upon completion, the successful student will be able to aurally analyze various rock recordings. Upon completion, the successful student will be able to communicate understanding of these outcomes in an oral presentation.
courses.topical_outline: Pre-Rock Sources * Blues * Country & Western * Rhythm & Blues 1950s Rock 'n' Roll Styles * Northern Band * New Orleans * Memphis Country Rock * Chicago * Vocal Groups/DooWop Rock Styles * Surf * Folk Styles * Soul Styles * British Beat Groups * Psychedelic Rock * Hard Rock/Heavy Metal * Fusions * Punk * Alternative Rock

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music and Film
courses.description: Explores the history and aesthetics of film music. The course relies on three assumptions: 1) that a film's score fundamentally alters the viewer's perception of the film; 2) that the film's images affect the way the viewer hears the music; and 3) that the combination of music and images can have a much greater impact on the viewer than either medium alone.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music Theory III
courses.description: Chromatic harmony involving part-writing, composition, and analysis.
courses.course_objectives: Upon completion of this course, the successful student will be able to analyze and compose music using secondary dominant seventh functions. Upon completion, the successful student will be able to analyze and compose music using modulation. Upon completion, the successful student will be able to analyze and compose music using mode mixture. Upon completion, the successful student will be able to analyze and compose music using Neapolitan 6th and augmented sixth chords. Upon completion, the successful student will be able to identify patterns in simple musical excerpts using roman numerals and appropriate non-harmonic tone designation, drawing on all prior musical instruction including knowledge being learned in other courses such as applied music and class piano, leading to appropriate interpretation of the data.
courses.topical_outline: * Analysis and composition using secondary dominant seventh functions. * Analysis and composition using modulation. * Analysis and composition using mode mixture. * Analysis and composition using Neapolitan 6th and augmented sixth chords.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music in Athens
courses.description: Explores national and international musical and cultural trends. The course draws from Athens, Georgia’s diverse musical communities and their histories, exploring the rock, hip hop, and indie popular music scenes along with African-American traditions, folk and traditional musics, and the emergent Latin music scene.
courses.course_objectives: Students who successfully complete this course will be able to express orally and in written form basic elements of musical style with frequent assessment and feedback. Upon completion, the successful student will be able to identify and demonstrate knowledge about diverse musical communities and styles gaining knowledge of different perspectives. Upon completion, the successful student will be able to develop a critical understanding of the relationship between music and place. Upon completion, the successful student will be able to demonstrate an understanding of how local music industries function as well as how they intersect with regional, national, and global music industries. Upon completion, the successful student will be able to engage with archival resources, oral histories, and other primary source materials. Upon completion, the successful student will be able to place the contributions of the Athens music scene into a larger American and Global context. Upon completion, the successful student will be able to understand how the contributions of key individuals can impact musical communities.
courses.topical_outline: 1. Introduction of musical terminology 2. Historical introduction to Athens’ diverse musical communities 3. Music during Reconstruction 4. Religious music traditions 5. Folk and traditional music 6. The Hot Corner 7. The emergence of the art and rock scenes 8. Indie musics 9. Music industries and economies 10. Latin music in Athens 11. Festivals 12. Music and place

courses.course_objectives: Students will learn to read music notation at the keyboard. Students will learn solo and ensemble piano literature at the elementary to early intermediate levels. Students will develop fundamental keyboard technique. Students will learn fundamental concepts in keyboard theory.
courses.topical_outline: •	Beginning concepts in keyboard theory (intervals, scales, chords, key signatures) •	Beginning concepts in music reading (rhythms; treble, bass, Grand staff) •	Elementary keyboard technique and musicianship •	Elementary transposition, improvisation, and harmonization •	Study and performance of solo piano literature •	Study and performance of ensemble piano literature

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Piano Class I
courses.description: Functional keyboard skills for satisfying the piano proficiency requirement.
courses.course_objectives: Students will demonstrate the following skills, perform prepared repertoire, including several selections from Bastien and Olson. Students will demonstrate the following skills, perform prepared harmonization including several selections from tune sheet; must include: a. I - IV6/4 - V6/5 or V6 b. original key and transposed keys. c. accompanying ostinato, drones, and chord patterns.  d. two-handed accompaniments. Students will demonstrate the following skills, improvise examples from tune sheets and Bastien. Students will demonstrate the following skills, sight-read short exercises from Bastien, including transposition and harmonization at sight. Students will demonstrate the following skills, play five-tone scales in major and minor around the circle of fifths and chromatically. (Pentascales within major keys only and tetrachord scales and key signatures in all major keys). Students will demonstrate the following skills, play major scales in the keys of C, G, D, A, E, B, F, D-flat, G-flat; two octaves, hands separately with correct fingering.
courses.topical_outline: PATTERNS FOR KEYBOARD TECHNIQUE A. Single Note Patterns 1. Pentascales a. major and minor (chromatically and around circle of fifths) b. within a key (major keys only) 2. Tetrachord scales (major key signatures around circle of fifths) 3. Major Scales: hands separately, two octaves a. C major group: C, G, D, A, E (Bastien, p. 193) b. black-key pattern group: B, F, D-flat, G-flat (Bastien, p. 193-94) B. Chord Patterns 1. Root position triads within a key (major keys only) 2. Chord Progressions: I-V-I, I-V7-I, I-IV-I, I-IV-I-V(7)-I, (root position and nearest inversion), major and minor, around circle of fifths. KEYBOARD ACTIVITIES A. Sight-reading B. Harmonization using primary triads C. Easy accompaniment patterns 1. ostinato and drone 2. chord patterns (2/4: rest chord, 3/4: rest chord-chord, for example) 3. two-handed accompaniments (examples in Bastien) D. Transposition: harmonizations and easy repertoire E. Improvisation to verse, rhythm patterns, and primary chord progressions

We will be critically analyzing the underscore (and songs) for various genres to help gain an understanding of how underscore works to help tell the story.

It will examine practices and principles of music teaching and learning, historical foundations of American music education, and sociological, political, and curricular influences that have shaped its development. It will provide an opportunity for students to take a panoramic view of the profession and critically reflect upon issues of school music teaching and their role as music educators. Field experience in the schools will be required.

courses.description: Surveys music cultures of Asia, Australia, and Oceania (Pacific islands). An exploration of the structures, forms, instruments, performance practices, contexts, and roles in historical, social, cultural, and global systems.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to introduce basic skills to listen, watch, and analyze performance practices. Students will be able to identify and think critically about how music and musicians and other performance artists use aesthetic principles to express social and cultural meaning and belonging. Students will be able to discuss the relationship between performance cultures and other organizing social units such as gender, race, ritual, religion, geography, history, economics, political, and social systems. Students will be able to write effectively about music, musicians, and performance.

courses.description: Where does music come from? When, why, and how did people first start making music? What forms does creativity take in music? How do music creators turn raw inspiration into finished pieces? How do improvisers create music on the spot? How do composers create notes for many instruments playing at once? Can anyone create music, or is that something only for composers? This course will provide many and varied answers to these questions and more.

courses.description: History of western music from its beginnings through the Baroque era.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music in the Western Tradition Post-1750
courses.description: The history of western music from the Classical style period to the present day.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Instrumentation and Arranging
courses.description: Instrumentation and Arranging is the first course in orchestration. Instrument ranges and colors will be learned and discussed. After learning ranges, colors, and uses, students learn to arrange for the orchestra. Common doublings up to three- and four-part arrangements are learned and discussed. Other compositional techniques will be discussed.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Guitar Techniques
courses.description: Basic principles and methods of guitar performance and pedagogy.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Guitar Skills for Therapists
courses.description: Functional guitar skills and repertoire appropriate for use in therapeutic work.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Jazz Pedagogy
courses.description: An overview of jazz curriculum development, rehearsal techniques, and performance for secondary school teachers and prospective teachers.
courses.prerequisiteText: Junior standing in music education program or permission of department

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Percussion Techniques for Music Therapists
courses.description: Percussion methods course for music therapy majors that will cover the following topics: introduction of African percussion instruments, tone production techniques, the djembe drum, the Afro-Cuban conga and quinto. In addition, the course covers an introduction to the drumset, drumset improvisation, and performance techniques.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Vocal Pedagogy
courses.description: Presents structure and function of the singing mechanism; current research in physical development, maturation, motor learning and skill acquisition, and the application of these to vocal instruction and vocal instruction experience.
courses.course_objectives: Students will develop skills in listening to identify function and quality in singing. Students will develop skills in using voice building exercises and repertoire to improve vocal function and artistry. Students will develop skills in providing effective feedback and instruction to developing singers. Students will develop skills in differentiating between evidence-based and non-evidence-based concepts.
courses.topical_outline: •	The anatomy and physiology of the human body as it relates to respiration, phonation, registration, resonance, and articulation for singing •	The basics of motor learning and the implications for teaching singing •	Teaching special populations including child, adolescent, senescent, and transgender singers •	The acoustics of the singing voice

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Vocal Pedagogy
courses.description: Presents structure and function of the singing mechanism, current research in physical development, maturation, learning and skill acquisition and the application of these to vocal instruction for individuals and groups; research and class presentations utilizing electronic media; and service-learning vocal instruction experience with area community partners.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Vocal Pedagogy II
courses.description: A historical overview of vocal instruction from primary and secondary resources, examination of methods and materials relevant to group and individual settings; research and class presentations. Students enrolled in this course are recommended to obtain membership in professional organizations (MTNA, NATS, MENC).
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Piano Pedagogy I
courses.description: Piano teaching, surveying elementary methods and materials for teaching beginners.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Keyboard Musicianship
courses.description: Functional keyboard skills for piano performance majors and music theory majors.
courses.prerequisiteText: Permission of major: BM-Music Performance and BM-Music Theory

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Piano Technique and Repertoire
courses.description: Class piano elective for undergraduate music majors who have successfully completed Piano Class III. Students will develop their keyboard technique and reading through etudes and piano repertoire of various genres (classical, contemporary, sacred).

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Introduction to Conducting
courses.description: Basic principles, techniques, and methods of conducting and interpretation.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Choral Conducting
courses.description: Rehearsal, interpretive and conducting techniques, and methods for choral organizations.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Band Conducting
courses.description: Rehearsals, interpretive and conducting techniques, and methods for band organizations.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Orchestra Conducting
courses.description: Rehearsal, interpretive and conducting techniques, and methods for orchestra.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Piano Accompanying
courses.description: Practical experience in chamber music, piano duets, and accompanying.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Introduction to Songwriting
courses.description: The components of American popular song from the perspective of the developing songwriter. Following successful examples, techniques to improve studentsʼ expressive and artistic songwriting potential will be applied, culminating in performance of a finished song. Relevant aspects of music production and music business will also be addressed.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music Theory for Non-Majors
courses.description: The fundamentals of music and their application in composition and analysis.
courses.course_objectives: Upon completion of this course, the successful student will be able to identify visually and write scales, keys, triads, intervals, and chords, Upon completion of this course, the successful student will be able to write accompaniment to given melodies in two or four parts, Upon completion of this course, the successful student will be able to compose short works using the materials learned in a number of different musical styles. Upon completion of this course, the successful student will be able to identify patterns in simple musical excerpts using roman numerals and appropriate non-harmonic tone designation, drawing on all prior musical instruction including knowledge being learned in other courses such as applied music and class piano, leading to appropriate interpretation of the data.
courses.topical_outline: 1. Fundamentals of Music (scales, keys, triads, intervals, chords), 2. Part-writing in two and four parts in a key, 3. Comoposition of short works in a variety of musical styles.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music and Media
courses.description: An overview study of music in film, television, games, videos, and multimedia. Music for film and other media is about “helping tell the story” of the film, show, or game play. We will be critically analyzing the underscore (and songs) for various genres to help gain an understanding of how underscore works to help tell the story.
courses.prerequisiteText: MUSI 1100 or MUSI 3550 or permission of department

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Applied Music Instruction for the Non-Music Major
courses.description: Applied music instruction (instrumental or vocal) offered at all levels through enrollment in the University of Georgia Community Music School.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Applied Music Instruction for Music Minors
courses.description: Applied instruction for music minors in a musical instrument or voice.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Junior Applied Instruction
courses.description: Applied instruction for music majors in a musical instrument or voice for the junior year.
courses.course_objectives: Students will demonstrate mastery of appropriate playing or singing techniques and ability to apply principles learned in other music courses. Students will demonstrate ability to perform a broad range of literature encompassing all styles and historical periods. Students will demonstrate knowledge of style and performance practices relevant to each work studied. Students will demonstrate ability to play or sing selected scales, arpeggios, and/or other appropriate technique-building studies. Students will demonstrate ability to extemporaneously communicate one's own musical ideas, given certain parameters such as key, form, meter, harmonic progression, etc., in a variety of performance situations and musical styles. Students will demonstrate knowledge of basic pedagogical principles for teaching voice or the student's major instrument.
courses.topical_outline: * Acoustical properties of the instrument/voice and relationship to proper performance technique. * Playing/singing techniques appropriate to the literature. * Harmonic and formal analysis of performance repertoire. * Performance practices of various styles, genres, and historical periods. * Methods of improvisation. * The experience of public performance. * Pedagogical principles and teaching demonstrations.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Junior Composition Instruction
courses.description: Applied instruction for music majors in composition for the junior year.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Junior Applied Instruction and Recital
courses.description: Applied instruction and recital for music majors in a musical instrument or voice for the junior year and performance of a junior recital.
courses.course_objectives: Students will demonstrate mastery of appropriate playing or singing techniques and ability to apply principles learned in other music courses. Students will demonstrate ability to perform a broad range of literature encompassing all styles and historical periods. Students will demonstrate knowledge of style and performance practices relevant to each work studied. Students will demonstrate ability to play or sing selected scales, arpeggios, and/or other appropriate technique-building studies. Students will demonstrate ability to extemporaneously communicate one's own musical ideas through performing and verbal communication from the stage. Students will demonstrate knowledge of basic pedagogical principles for teaching voice or the student's major instrument.
courses.topical_outline: * Acoustical properties of the instrument/voice and relationship to proper performance technique. * Playing/singing techniques appropriate to the literature. * Harmonic and formal analysis of performance repertoire. * Performance practices of various styles, genres, and historical periods. * Methods of improvisation. * The experience of public performance. * Pedagogical principles and teaching demonstrations.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Applied Composition Instruction
courses.description: Applied instruction for music majors in composition for the second semester of the junior year.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: String Pedagogy
courses.description: Instruction in pedagogy for all bowed string instruments.  Class and studio teaching methods will be explored.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Instrumental Pedagogy
courses.description: Principles of teaching and learning appropriate for applied instrumental music in brass, woodwinds, strings, guitar, piano, and percussion.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Applied Instruction for the Musical Theatre Certificate Program
courses.description: Applied instruction in voice for students enrolled in the MusicalTheatre Certificate Program.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Junior Recital in Music
courses.description: Required recital for music majors in a musical instrument, voice, or composition.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Directed Independent Study in Music
courses.description: Independent research topics in any field of music directed by a faculty member.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Intro to Music Production and Audio Technology
courses.description: Course provides a foundation in audio technologies as applied in the production of music. Using the HHSOM’s 25-seat Music Technology Lab (MuTec), students will engage fundamentals of signal flow, signal processing, mixing tools and techniques, and synthesis, through a series of creative projects. Open to majors and non-majors.
courses.course_objectives: Students will understand fundamentals of digital audio and signal flow. Students will understand different microphone types and techniques, and the functions of essential hardware used in audio production. Students will become comfortable working creatively in a digital audio workstation (DAW). Students will begin to develop perception and practical skills in the application of EQ, compression, and other audio-related DSPs. Students will understand and apply fundamentals of music synthesis. Students will become conversant in underlaying sound analysis concepts being currently applied in commercial streaming and generative music algorithms.
courses.topical_outline: Fundamentals of acoustics and digital audio Microphone types and recording techniques Synthesis and MIDI Fundamentals of mixing: EQ, Compression, and other DSPs Emerging concepts in audio analysis, dissemination, and generative technologies

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Introduction to Music Technology
courses.description: Provides an overview of technologies essential to professional musicians in the 21st century. Meeting in the MuTec lab, this course offers hands-on instruction in a variety of relevant music software. Coursework is primarily creative projects, with some written examination on fundamentals.
courses.prerequisiteText: Permission of major: AB-Music, BM-Music Ed, BM-Music Therapy, BM-Music Performance, BM-Music Theory, BM-Music Composition, BM-Intended Music Education, BM-Intended Music Therapy, BM-Intended Music Performance, BM-Intended Music Theory

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Technology for Music Therapists
courses.description: An overview to develop functional skills in the basic components of technology related to music therapy practice.
courses.course_objectives: Students will demonstrate understanding and application for navigating Digital Audio Workstations (DAWs). Students will demonstrate understanding and application for recording simple audio. Students will demonstrate understanding and application for processing audio recording. Students will demonstrate understanding and application for incorporating digital instruments.
courses.topical_outline: •	Foundational Digital Audio Workstation (DAW) concepts •	Basic audio effects •	Importing and editing audio •	Introduction to mixing concepts •	Introduction to virtual instruments •	Introduction to MIDI •	Introduction to sampling and looping •	Clinical Applications of concepts to Music Therapy

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music Therapy Practicum V
courses.description: Senior level of practical experience in conducting music therapy sessions with selected clients. Includes more in-depth assessment, planning, implementation, and documentation of weekly music therapy sessions throughout the semester.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music Therapy Practicum VI
courses.description: Continuation of senior level of practical experience in conducting music therapy sessions with selected clients. Includes more in-depth assessment, planning, implementation, and documentation of weekly music therapy sessions throughout the semester.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Summer Music Therapy Practicum
courses.description: Practical experience in conducting music therapy sessions with selected clients at beginner, intermediate, and advanced student levels. Includes observation, assisting, planning, implementation, and documentation of weekly music therapy sessions throughout the semester.
courses.course_objectives: Students will select or create music therapy experiences that meet the clients' objectives. Students will formulate goals and objectives for individuals and group therapy based upon assessment findings. Students will select and adapt music consistent with the strengths and needs of the client. Students will organize and arrange the music therapy setting to facilitate the clients’ therapeutic involvement. Students will plan and sequence music therapy sessions. Students will recognize, interpret, and respond appropriately to significant events in music therapy sessions as they occur. Students will provide music therapy experiences to change nonmusical behavior. Students will conduct or facilitate group music therapy. Students will establish closure of music therapy sessions. Students will promote a sense of group cohesiveness and/or a feeling of a group membership. Students will communicate to the client's expectations of their behavior.
courses.topical_outline: AMTA Competencies to Be Addressed:  The practicum sequence is designed to facilitate the development of competency in all areas of music therapy practice, progressing from the beginning level through readiness for internship. At each level, students are to build on and further develop the competencies addressed at the previous level. While specific goals are identified at each level, in reality, the practicum sequence is a holistic process, in which each student progresses at his or her own rate.  Competency 4. Functional Music Skills • Students will provide quality musical experiences that promote continuity and group cohesiveness. • Students will demonstrate proficiency in vocal and instrumental music skills during group music therapy sessions. Competency 11. Client Assessment • Students will observe clients and identify areas of strengths and needs. • Students will record observations on an informal assessment tool. • Students will assess in greater depth clients' developmental, cognitive, and behavioral levels of functioning. • Students will assess in greater depth specific client characteristics, abilities, and behaviors. • Students will select, design, and implement effective culturally-based methods for assessing the clients’ assets, problems, musical preferences, and level of musical functioning. • Students will identify the client’s therapeutic needs through analysis and interpretation of music therapy and related assessment data. Competency 12. Treatment Planning • Students will formulate goals and objectives based on recorded observations. • Students will plan music therapy interventions that address clients’ goals and objectives. • Students will plan and sequence music therapy sessions with co-therapists. • Students will demonstrate more independence in planning in-depth music therapy experiences for special populations. • Students will formulate music therapy strategies for individuals and groups that address specific goals and objectives identified in the assessment. • Students will organize and arrange the music therapy setting to facilitate the clients’ therapeutic involvement. Competency 13. Therapy Implementation • Students will provide music therapy experiences that promote positive changes in clients’ behaviors. • Students will provide music therapy experiences that address specific social, emotional, cognitive, and behavioral needs of clients. • Students will utilize verbal skills to provide feedback on, reflect, rephrase, and translate the client’s communications. • Students will demonstrate effective verbal and nonverbal communication skills. • Students will sequence and pace music experiences within a session according to the clients’ needs and situational factors. • Students will conduct music therapy sessions that provide group cohesiveness and promote a feeling of a group membership. • Students will develop and maintain a repertoire of music for age, culture, and stylistic differences. Competency 14. Therapy Evaluation • Students will observe clients’ responses to therapy and modify treatment approaches as needed. • Students will design and implement methods for evaluating and measuring client progress and the effectiveness of therapeutic strategies. • Students will modify treatment approaches based on the client’s response to therapy. Students will continue to develop a professional writing style that is accurate, clear, and concise. • Students will recognize significant changes and patterns in the client’s response to therapy and revise the treatment plan as needed. Competency 15. Documentation • Students will write progress notes that accurately report clients’ observable behavior during group music therapy sessions. • Students will write a final treatment summary that documents clients’ progress in meeting identified goals and objectives. • Students will write professional reports describing the client throughout all phases of the music therapy process in an accurate, concise, and objective manner. • Students will develop and use data gathering techniques during all phases of the clinical process. • Students will document and present clinical data. • Students will write professional reports describing the client throughout all phases of the music therapy process in an accurate, concise, and objective manner. Competency 17. Professional Role/Ethics • Students will demonstrate professional, ethical, and dependable behavior throughout all aspects of the clinical experience. Competency 19. Supervision and Administration • Students will participate in and benefit from multiple forms of supervision.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music Therapy Internship
courses.description: In-depth experience of clinical training in a professional setting. Experience in all aspects of music therapy practice in preparation for Board Certification.
courses.course_objectives: Students will demonstrate entry-level competencies in musical foundations as written in the AMTA professional competencies. Students will demonstrate entry-level competencies in clinical foundations as written in the AMTA professional competencies. Students will demonstrate entry-level competencies in music therapy foundations as written in the AMTA professional competencies.
courses.topical_outline: Music Foundations Clinical Foundations Music Therapy Foundations
courses.prerequisiteText: Permission of department | Graduate Prerequisite | Permission of department

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Double Reed Making Seminar
courses.description: Oboe and bassoon players will learn how to create and finishreeds for their instruments. The course will cover thefundamentals of making a blank, exploring different reed scrapesand styles, and focus on detailed finishing techniques.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: A Technician's Guide for the Pianist
courses.description: Covers piano nomenclature, how pianos work, what to consider when buying a new or used piano, how to care for your piano, an in-depth look at the services that piano technicians provide, and communicating with your piano technician.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music in the City
courses.description: In New York City, students will attend jazz performances andBroadway shows, tour recording facilities used for soundtracks,attend a seminar on the American Federation of Musicians, learnabout union function, spend individual time with workingmusicians, and keep a small book on experiences to share with the class.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music Theatre in the City
courses.description: In New York City, students will attend jazz performances, Broadway shows, tour museums/factories (relevant to the industry), and have opportunities to work/Q&A with industry professionals such as casting directors, musical directors, choreographers, movement specialists, and more. Students will learn about union function, agents, audition skills, and keep a small book on experiences to share with the class.
courses.course_objectives: By the end of this course, students will develop preparation skills for auditions in various genres of musical theatre. By the end of this course, students will develop effective communication skills with musicians, agents, casting directors, and other creative professionals in musical theatre. By the end of this course, students will develop fundamentals of the acting business. By the end of this course, students will develop a broader understanding of requirements of the professional MT actor. By the end of this course, students will understand how the actors’ union functions. By the end of this course, students will to physically navigate the New York City. By the end of this course, students will to develop professional relationships within the industry.
courses.topical_outline: (1) Listening critically to performances (2) Discussions with pianists in the industry covering audition preparation and best practices of communication with audition pianists (3) Basic self-tape techniques (4) Function of AEA Union (5) Networking skills (6) Audition techniques and best practices (7) Ideas students have of their future in the industry

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Filmscoring in LA Intensive Field Study
courses.description: Field study course designed to provide first-hand exposure to Filmscore professionals in LA. Students will visit composers' studios, scoring stages with an orchestral recording session, studio music heads, music supervisors, and music editors, as well as be introduced to the professional practices of these areas through these meetings.
courses.prerequisiteText: Permission of department | Graduate Prerequisite | Permission of department

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music Theory Review
courses.description: Visual and aural skills for entering graduate students in need of remediation.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music in the Real World
courses.description: Music graduates face new challenges in today's professionallandscape, including fewer traditional jobs. Students will buildrelevant skills and tools that emphasize versatility andflexibility to better prepare them for career success in this evolving landscape.
courses.prerequisiteText: Permission of major | Graduate Prerequisite | Permission of major

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Alexander Technique
courses.description: Introduction to the practice and principles of the Alexander Technique, which enables musicians to practice and perform theirinstrument with less tension and a greater freedom of movement.
courses.prerequisiteText: Permission of major | Graduate Prerequisite | Permission of major
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music Recording Practicum
courses.description: Audio techniques, technologies, and critical listening will beapplied towards recording, mixing, editing, and mastering liveand archived recordings for the UGA HHSOM. Working in aprofessional studio environment equips students with skillsneeded to succeed in audio recording, while also empowering themin their performance, teaching, and research endeavors.
courses.prerequisiteText: MUSI 5802/7802 and permission of department | Graduate Prerequisite | MUSI 5802/7802 and permission of department

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Vocal Diction Methods
courses.description: Students will demonstrate pedagogical application of IPA anddiction principles suitable for error detection and correction in a choral or solo vocal teaching setting.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Interpreting Popular Music
courses.description: Exploration of analytical methodologies for interpreting and understanding various forms of what one might describe as “popular music.” Readings from music theory guide analyses, student-led discussions, and projects. Students are evaluated on presentations, concert reviews (with an emphasis on Athens music), and a capstone final project/presentation that entails a conference proposal suitable for submission to music theory conferences.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Modal Counterpoint
courses.description: The study of counterpoint of the Renaissance, with emphasis on model composition and analysis of the vocal music of Lassus,Josquin, Morley, and Palestrina.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Form and Analysis
courses.description: Analysis of form focusing on music from the seventeenth, eighteenth, and nineteenth centuries.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Jazz Theory
courses.description: A study of jazz music theory including chord and scale construction, jazz nomenclature, chord/scale relationships, jazz song forms (AABA, blues), harmonic progressions and chord voicing principles. Students will engage in analyses of selected transcriptions, musical excerpts, and recordings. Students will demonstrate mastery of the topics covered through written, playing, and oral assignments.
courses.course_objectives: Students will understand chord scale relationships. Students will be able to define and aurally identify melodic approaches, harmonic progressions, and techniques used in various improvisational musical styles. Students will be able to demonstrate understanding of techniques used in jazz improvisation. Students will understand advanced harmonic relationships and various jazz song forms. Students will be able to demonstrate understanding of basic chord voicing principles.
courses.topical_outline: Chord Scale Relationships Principles of Jazz Harmony Features of Bebop Jazz Composition Reharmonization

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Tonal Counterpoint
courses.description: The study of counterpoint of the Baroque, with emphasis on model composition and analysis of the keyboard works of J.S. Bach.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Model Composition
courses.description: In Model Composition, students will study and imitate styles from three contrasting genres from the 20th century whose influences extend into 21st-century compositions. Past topics have included the quarter-tonal piano, spectral music, 8-bit video game music for the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES), and K-Pop production. Throughout the semester, students will discuss readings, analyze works and compose creative projects imitating the stylistic vocabulary of these genres.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to identify and analyze genre characteristics of the genre. Students will be able to create original compositions that demonstrate understanding of stylistic vocabulary covered in the course. Students will be able to engage in critical readings and discussions. Students will be able to cultivate independent research and exploration.
courses.topical_outline: The Art of the Steal/Model Composition as Theoretical Study Unit 1: Introduction, Context, Notation, Practicality, Physicality Unit 1: Technology Demos Unit 1: Music Analyses Creative Project 1: Drafts, Workshops, and Presentation Unit 2: Introduction, Context, Notation, Practicality, Physicality Unit 2: Technology Demos Unit 2: Music Analyses Creative Project 2: Drafts, Workshops, and Presentation Proposals: What information one should contain, and how to write one Small-group Peer Editing of Proposals and Presentation Creative Project 3: Drafts, Workshops, and Presentation

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Analysis of Non-Tonal Music
courses.description: Introduces basic concepts for the analysis of non-tonal music from the twentieth- and twenty-first centuries, focusing on theories and analysis of pitch, rhythm, form, and other elements in works from this time period. Content for the course will vary depending on the instructor, and aural skills and listening strategies are part of the course’s evaluation.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Analysis of Texted Music
courses.description: Detailed analytical exploration of texted music. The course begins with a preliminary section that reviews harmony and small form and considers analytical methods for interpreting texts. After that preparatory unit, the course progresses into an in-depth study of how composers and musicians use a text to convey an array of meanings. To facilitate delivery, the course’s contents are organized according to genre and/or conceptual area.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Dissolution of Tonality
courses.description: Poses the questions “What do we mean by tonality?” and “How can we describe music when it challenges the norms of tonality?” Through diverse repertory (much of it from the 19th and early 20th centuries), techniques designed for tonal, chromatic, and post-tonal music are synthesized and expanded to explore answers to those questions.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Exploring Math and Music
courses.description: Provides opportunities for students to survey the rich intersections of mathematics and music. Classes will be organized around broad topics (such as proportions, modular arithmetic, networks, and geometry) and will involve equal parts discussion and exploration. Assessment will include small homework exercises and open-ended, student-proposed projects. (The class requires no specific mathematical knowledge, beyond what is typical for a music major.)

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Special Topics in Composition and Music Technology
courses.description: Changing series of topics in composition and music technology that are not covered in other courses.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Special Topics in Music Theory and Analysis
courses.description: Changing series of topics in music theory and analysis that are not covered in other courses.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Ancient, Medieval, and Renaissance Music
courses.description: Music from Greek and Roman society to the death of Josquin (c. 1520).

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Late Renaissance and Baroque Music
courses.description: Musical styles and genres from the 16th century through Bach andHandel.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music in the Classic Period
courses.description: Chamber, orchestral, keyboard, and operatic works from the middle and late eighteenth century.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music in the Romantic Period
courses.description: Emphasis on the development of song, symphony, chamber music, and opera.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Modern Music
courses.description: Modern trends in music from Schoenberg, Stravinsky, Hindemith, and Bartok to the present.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Women and Music
courses.description: Roles of women in music, including the history of women musicians in western art music, world cultures, and popular music; gender studies in music.
courses.prerequisiteText: MUSI 3020 or MUSI 3021 or MUSI 3030 or MUSI 3210 or MUSI 3220 or permission of department
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: History of Opera
courses.description: Examination of representative operas of each period inhistorical context. It analyses the roles played in the creationand production of operas by the patron/audience, librettist,composer, singers, conductor, director, machinist, and (whenappropriate) film director.
courses.prerequisiteText: MUSI 3030 or MUSI 3210 or MUSI 3220 or permission of department

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Topics in Musical Cultures of the World
courses.description: In-depth study of the music of a select culture, area, topic, or genre.  Investigates historical aspects, social functions, aesthetic preferences, the musician, musical instruments, structures and forms, performance contexts, and practices.
courses.prerequisiteText: MUSI 3020 or MUSI 3021 or MUSI 3030 or MUSI 3210 or MUSI 3220 or permission of department

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Instrumental/Vocal/Wind/Choral Literature
courses.description: Solo, sonata, and ensemble music composed for winds, brass, strings, piano and harpsichord, organ or voice, dating from the earliest appropriate period to the present.
courses.course_objectives: Upon completion of the course, the successful student will be able to place works in a historical context. Upon completion of the course, the successful student will be able to identify characteristic traits for style periods, national styles, and major composers. Upon completion of the course, the successful student will be able to perform works in a historically informed manner, especially with respect to ornamentation and expression.
courses.topical_outline: Evolution of the repertoire throughout major style periods Conventions of composition and performance for each era Major composers and representative masterworks for each era

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Selected Studies in Musicology
courses.description: Investigation of a special topic not otherwise covered in the curriculum. Topics and instructors vary from one semester to thenext.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Seminar in Musicology-Ethnomusicology
courses.description: Investigation of a special topic not otherwise covered in thecurriculum. Topics and instructors vary from semester to semester.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Guitar Techniques
courses.description: Basic principles and methods of guitar performance and pedagogy.
courses.course_objectives: Students will perform in individual and group guitar experiences, including leading and teaching monophonic melodies, chords, scales, and improvisation. Students will apply theory and aural skill concepts to guitar performance and pedagogy. Students will create and arrange simple melodies in assigned keys. Students will prepare chord sheets in proper rhythmic alignment and chordal structures. Students will perform a 3-chord folk song to lead in class. Students will participate in class discussion pertaining to common problems and misconceptions related to folk guitar performance and pedagogy.
courses.topical_outline: Introduction to the guitar Leading and teaching monophonic melodies Leading and teaching chords Leading and teaching scales Leading and teaching improvisation

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Guitar Skills for Music Therapists
courses.description: Functional guitar skills and repertoire appropriate for use in music therapy practice.
courses.course_objectives: Students will learn advanced functional guitar skills. Students will have the ability to use advanced right-hand strumming and finger picking techniques. Students will have the ability to accompany his/her voice and small instrumental ensembles using basic chord changes while adding bass note passages, and other ornamental musical elements. Students will learn advanced left-hand techniques. Students will have the ability to use alternate tunings. Students will have the ability to sightread chord charts and guitar tablature.
courses.topical_outline: Right-hand, flat-pick, and finger-style techniques Ear training for chord progressions and transposition Improvisation Chordal and melodic embellishments Rock, folk, country, jazz, pop, R&B, and Latin styles

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Percussion for Music Therapists
courses.description: Functional percussion skills, techniques, and repertoire appropriate for use in music therapy practice.
courses.course_objectives: The student will demonstrate through instrumental performance knowledge of world percussion instruments and their tuning, performance techniques, and sound production techniques. The student will demonstrate through instrumental performance knowledge of world percussion traditional repertoire. The student will demonstrate through instrumental performance knowledge of improvisation on a variety of percussion instruments.
courses.topical_outline: World percussion instruments World percussion performance and sound production techniques World percussion rhythms and traditional repertoire Notation system Drumset coordination and styles

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: String Instrumental Techniques
courses.description: Basic principles and methods of string performance and pedagogy.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Woodwind Instrumental Techniques
courses.description: Basic principles and methods of woodwind performance and pedagogy.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Brass Instrumental Techniques
courses.description: Basic principles and methods of brass instrument performance and pedagogy.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Percussion Techniques for Music Educators
courses.description: Basic principles and methods of percussion performance and pedagogy.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Foundations of Lesson Planning
courses.description: Course will focus on developing lesson planning skills and strategies, authentic assessments, Backwards Design, Universal Design for Learning, and culturally responsive pedagogy. Students will put theory into practice through attending a practicum.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to plan, implement, and create lesson plans that are developmentally appropriate and multimodal in music instruction for students of varying abilities and cultures through teaching preschool music lessons within the community. Students will apply knowledge gained from community service experience by contribution to class discussions and lesson planning. Students will develop reflective practices through observation, writing, and goal setting. Students will be able to evaluate student feedback in order to inform lesson planning and authentic assessment through preschool practicum placement within the community. Students will be able to critically discuss, create, implement, and reflect on a variety of assessment tools and age-appropriate lessons based on music standards. Students will become familiar with leading pedagogical practices used in music classrooms Students will be able to identify specific techniques that may be used with exceptional learners to help ensure success in the music classroom. Students will demonstrate specific techniques that show the integration of music from a variety of cultures within instruction. Students will apply new knowledge about lesson planning and teaching to their service experience as well as apply their service experience to their new knowledge.
courses.topical_outline: What is lesson planning? Planning strategies for the overall course Planning for individual classes Introduction to Preschool Music: Developing Appropriate Expectations for Young Musicians Learning Objectives Assessments: Formative & Summative Now that I have all this data, what do I do with it? Sequencing Feedback: Who does it come from and how can I use it in my planning? Evaluation Cycle Portfolio of Lesson Plans

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Pre-College Music Theory Pedagogy
courses.description: Designed primarily to prepare you to teach topics that are typically described as “music theory” to pre-college students. Such topics include several different areas of musicianship including fundamentals, harmony and voice leading, sight-singing, contextual listening, transcription/dictation, and analysis. Designed to be a practical course that places an emphasis on how to teach pre-college music theory topics through effective lesson planning and model teaching.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Melody Harmonization
courses.description: Course is intended for music therapy majors and explores theoretical and analytical approaches to harmonizing diatonic and chromatic melodies on guitar, piano, and other instruments. Course begins with a review of diatonic and chromatic harmony before moving into alternate forms of harmonic representation that include lead-sheet notation, Nashville numbers, tablature, and chord box reading. The goal of the course is fluency in harmonization, as demonstrated through skills-based assessments, performances, and projects.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Performance and Racialization
courses.description: Drawing from work in anthropology, sociology, performance studies, and legal theory, this course explores how modern discourses of racialization and performance in the U.S. context emerge from a long history of travel writing, colonial and postcolonial encounters, and other circulations of people and goods throughout the world.
courses.prerequisiteText: Permission of department | Graduate Prerequisite | Permission of department

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Bollywood and Its Others: Cinema in South Asia
courses.description: Examination of the ways in which various kinds of identities are constructed and negotiated through the film industries of South Asia. Exploration of narratives of place and their expression through performance underscore processes of social identification across the South Asian subcontinent. Through our study, we will explore mediums and topics such as: religion and myth; colonialism and postcolonialism; gender and sexuality; language and ethnic identity; caste and other forms of discrimination; and the politics of national and subnational identity.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Country Music, Race, and the Idea of America
courses.description: This interdisciplinary music history course is built around a few basic questions: What is Country Music? Is it a genre? Is it American? If so, why? In this class we’ll explore the complex construction of country music as a 20th-century modern American musical practice.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: History of American Music
courses.description: A survey of art and vernacular music traditions of the United States.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Acting for Singers
courses.description: Students will apply basic theatrical performance techniques to enhance their music performance training, including song interpretation, intentions, objectives, emotional connectivity, movement, active listening, and responding while utilizing their existing vocal technique to achieve a deeper sense of truth and the creation of a more realistic, natural, and nuanced performance.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Intellectual Property and the Arts
courses.description: Course is designed to familiarize students with the basic legal contours of American intellectual property law, with a focus on copyright, trademark, and how these legal topics apply to the creation, distribution, commercialization, and reuse of creative artistic endeavors. There will be a focus on the practical application of intellectual property law to common issues that arise in the creative economy. No prior legal training or experience is required.
courses.course_objectives: By the end of this course, students will be conversant with the legal foundations of intellectual property law in the United States, including familiarity with copyright and trademark law and key court decisions regarding intellectual property and the arts. By the end of this course, students will have a demonstrable knowledge of how to identify intellectual property issues in commercial and/or academic settings. By the end of this course, students will have developed strategies for protecting their own intellectual property as well as respecting the intellectual property rights of others.
courses.topical_outline:
The Basics of Intellectual Property – Copyright and Trademark Understanding the key tools used by courts to analyze questions of intellectual property ownership Exploring the application of intellectual property law concepts to practical situations in commercial and academic settings Intellectual property licensing, Creative Commons and the Public Domain Special topics: 
The First Amendment and Intellectual Property
Artificial Intelligence and Intellectual Property

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Performance Anxiety and Focus
courses.description: Students will learn about the issues regarding performance anxiety and discover solutions to work through these issues. The course will also cover strategies for improving focus, resilience, courage, and perspective. Includes readings from a variety of texts, videos, writing assignments, in-class discussions, and in-class exercises and performances. In-class performances by each student are a required part of the course. These can be in music, theatre, dance, and comedy.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Music Techniques and Experiences for Children
courses.description: Methods and field experience for music education majors. Course consists of a survey of effective teaching techniques, research in learning, and materials, including use of technology and multicultural materials.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Piano for Choral Music Educators
courses.description: Piano course for music majors who have completed Piano Class III. Emphasis is on functional piano skills for music education majors aiming to work in a classroom/choral setting. Emphasis is on further development of keyboard reading, technique, accompaniment, improvisation, transposition, and harmonization. Repertoire includes solo, collaborative, and choral repertoire in a variety of classical and contemporary styles.
courses.course_objectives: Students will develop greater comfort in keyboard reading and technique. Students will learn solo/collaborative repertoire of classical and contemporary styles. Students will learn accompaniment patterns for use in studio and classroom settings. Students will develop functional skills in score reading, improvisation, harmonization, and transposition.
courses.topical_outline: Keyboard technique; scale/arpeggio/chord inversions and fingerings Solo, collaborative, and choral ensemble repertoire Vocal warm-ups using various keyboard accompaniments SATB score reading Conducting and playing at the keyboard Improvisation (12-bar blues, other styles, and harmonic progressions) Harmonization and Transposition

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Piano for Music Therapists
courses.description: Piano course for music majors who have completed Piano Class III. Emphasis is on functional piano skills for music therapists, to include keyboard reading and technique, accompaniment styles, improvisation, transposition, and harmonization. Repertoire includes solo and collaborative repertoire of various styles (classical, folk, blues, sacred, and contemporary).
courses.course_objectives: Students will develop greater comfort in keyboard reading and ensemble playing skills. Students will learn repertoire that includes classical, sacred, blues, and contemporary styles. Students will learn a variety of accompaniment styles and patterns for use in solo and group settings. Students will develop additional functional piano skills in improvisation, harmonization, and transposition.
courses.topical_outline: Keyboard technique; scale/arpeggio/chord inversions and fingerings Solo, collaborative, and ensemble playing Piano accompaniments in various styles for solo/group music settings “Sing and play” repertoire (folk song, popular music) Improvisation (12-bar blues, other styles and harmonic progressions) Harmonization and transposition

courses.subject: MUSI

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: World Music Pedagogy
courses.description: Course introduces teaching music in a multiethnic American society. Students will interact with diverse music while developing understanding for music teaching and cultural awareness. This course is suitable for all music teachers.
courses.course_objectives: Students will explore of issues of multicultural education theories and practices in a variety of teaching contexts. Students will expand their musical perception, understanding, and analysis tools through active listening of non-Western musics. Students will develop an increased awareness of the interaction of music with its social and cultural contexts. Students will develop knowledge of teaching and learning world music by creating and implementing lesson (teaching) plans that incorporate a diverse selection of musics and objectives.
courses.topical_outline: Teaching & learning world music in context Attentive listening to develop cultural awareness “Participatory Musicking” with engaged and enactive listening Performing world music Creating world music Integrating world music Overcoming challenges and possible outcomes Final Project: Music Culture Curricular Unit
courses.prerequisiteText: Permission of department | Graduate Prerequisite | Permission of department

courses.subject: MUSI

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Suzuki Violin and Viola Pedagogy I
courses.description: Course includes the Suzuki Association of the Americas (SAA) Every Child Can!, Violin Book 1, and Viola Book 1, and Group Class Strategies courses. Provides students with skills and resources needed to teach beginning violin and viola to students using the Suzuki method.

courses.description: A continuation of Suzuki Violin and Viola Pedagogy I; provides students with further skills and resources for teaching violin and viola students using the Suzuki method at the Book 2 and 3 levels. Students will be required to provide recorded teaching segments and will include live teaching experiences and feedback.
courses.prerequisiteText: MUSI 4600/6600 or permission of department | Graduate Prerequisite | MUSI 4600/6600 or permission of department

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Suzuki Violin Pedagogy III
courses.description: A continuation of Suzuki Pedagogy I and II. Will provide students with further skills and resources needed to teach violin students using the Suzuki Association of the Americas Violin Books 4 and 5 levels.
courses.prerequisiteText: MUSI 4610/6610 or permission of department | Graduate Prerequisite | MUSI 4610/6610 or permission of department

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Suzuki Violin Pedagogy IV
courses.description: The Suzuki Association of the Americas (SAA) Violin Books 6, 7, and 8 courses. It is a continuation of Suzuki Pedagogy I, II, and III and will provide students with further skills and resources needed to teach violin students using the Suzuki Method at the Books 6 through 8 levels.
courses.prerequisiteText: MUSI 4620/6620 or permission of department | Graduate Prerequisite | MUSI 4620/6620 or permission of department

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Media Composition and Production I
courses.description: An in-depth look at the composition process for media. Both linear (film, tv) and non-linear (game) composing processes will be studied. How does underscore “help tell the story”? How, as composers, do we use themes, harmony, instrumentation, rhythm, and tempo to accomplish these goals? In film scoring, how do we address these ideas as the picture changes? In game scoring, how are these ideas accomplished?
courses.course_objectives: At the completion of this course, the student will have learned to compose pictures using an industry-standard digital-audio workstation (DAW). This includes being able to import pictures, set markers, set up a template for the project, and compose as the picture changes. The student will learn how to digitally orchestrate their pieces and learn techniques to make their mockups sound good. The student will learn to export their MIDI into industry-standard notation software and notate for live instrumental recording. In videogames composition, the student will learn to write loops, hits, and stingers, and learn about horizontal layering. The students will learn about other film and videogame composers through score study and listening/visual examples.
courses.topical_outline: Class concepts: harmony, melody, instrumentation, tempo, rhythm, working with a DAW Setting up a template for a project; proper track organization, music production concepts: EQ, compression, reverb Composing themes outside of the picture: compose to a narrative or script idea, composing themes from viewing pictures without music Importing pictures and setting up your markers, importing your themes and making them work with your new markers, music editing and extending ideas, tempo changes and time signature changes to make a hit Digital orchestration: making your MIDI sound as good a possible – techniques and tricks, phrasing automation, note velocities, instrument doubling, instrument balancing Recording real instruments: single instrument recording, mixing techniques Videogame composing: composing the perfect loop that has no beginning or end, strategies Videogame composing: composing hits and stingers Videogame composing: horizontal layering
courses.prerequisiteText: MUSI 1100 or MUSI 3550 | Undergraduate Pre or

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Media Composition and Production II
courses.description: A continuation of the concepts of Media Composition and Production I, moving forward into the process of recording live instruments with scores. Students will continue to compose pieces to picture, as well as the continued study of other film scores through score reading and analysis. Different instruments and instrument groups will be studied and recorded with their compositions to picture over the course of the semester.
courses.prerequisiteText: MUSI 4650/6650 and MUSI 5800/7800 | Graduate Prerequisite | MUSI 4650/6650 and MUSI 5800/7800

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Orchestration for Film
courses.description: A review of instrument ranges and techniques, traditional orchestration in practice, and an in-depth discussion and application of orchestration techniques used in film scores, including practical applications of MIDI and notation software packages.
courses.course_objectives: At the completion of this course, the student will have learned the instrument ranges, transpositions, and colors for the whole orchestra. At the completion of this course, the student will have learned traditional orchestrations and arranging for orchestra. At the completion of this course, the student will have learned common practice techniques for film scores. At the completion of this course, the student will have learned taking MIDI from a DAW and learning to orchestrate and arrange from the MIDI. At the completion of this course, the student will have learned common application techniques and problems.
courses.topical_outline: Class Concepts: Orchestral Instrument ranges, transpositions, timbres for Strings, Winds, Brass, Percussion, Piano, and Harp Traditional Arrangement and Orchestration technique In-Depth study of Orchestration for film scores, and extended techniques Practical applications of Orchestrations MIDI from a DAW

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Orchestration for Film
courses.description: A review of instrument ranges and techniques, traditional orchestration in practice, and an in-depth discussion and application of orchestration techniques used in film scores, including practical applications of MIDI and notation software packages.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Game Composition and Production
courses.description: Students learn to compose and produce tracks or a series of layered tracks to accommodate game scoring or non-linear scoring. Game composers will ask how their music “Helps Tell the Story” of the game, but also how to accommodate non-linear scoring and functions.
courses.prerequisiteText: MUSI 4650/6650 or permission of department | Graduate Prerequisite | MUSI 4650/6650 or permission of department

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: The UGA Glee Club
courses.description: Concentration on choral literature for lower voice singers (tenors and basses) from all periods of music history, including sacred, secular, folk, and popular music.
courses.course_objectives: The students will be able to demonstrate technical and musical skills required for successful performance in a choral ensemble. The students will be able to demonstrate knowledge of the selected repertoire in terms of performance practice, stylistic elements, and historical and cultural contexts.

courses.description: Orchestral ensemble open to music majors and non-majors. Audition required for all players. Ensemble will perform standard orchestral repertoire and accompany opera productions as appropriate.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: University Chorus
courses.description: Performance of choral literature for mixed voices from all periods of music history, including sacred, secular, folk, and popular music.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Guitar Ensemble
courses.description: This is a performance course open to all guitar majors. Designed to give guitar students experience performing in a large conducted ensemble. Repertoire includes music from a variety of stylistic periods. Open to non-majors; requires ability to read standard notation and a classical guitar. One public performance per semester.
courses.course_objectives: Students will perform concerts in an ensemble setting, working together towards a common goal. Section leaders and the conductor will aid in shared governance towards achieving a high-level performance following weekly rehearsals. Students will experience a variety of musical styles. Students will be able to demonstrate good control of appropriate articulation and make stylistically appropriate interpretive choices. Most importantly, students will be able to communicate musical gestures non-verbally and follow such cues. Students will gain increased familiarity with important guitar ensemble repertoire.
courses.topical_outline: Topics covered will lead to the performance of a public concert. Each week specific pieces will be rehearsed in full ensemble as well as in small sections. Musical topics will include intonation and timbre control rhythmic precision and  flexibility, dynamic shaping and phrasing, and communication. Pieces selected will reflect a variety of stylistic periods as  expected in a well-balanced concert program.
courses.prerequisiteText: Two hours of MUSI 4700 or MUSI 4710 or MUSI 4750/6750

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: UGA Hodgson Singers
courses.description: Performance of choral literature for mixed voices from all periods of music history, including sacred, secular, folk, and popular music.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Piano Ensemble
courses.description: Class piano elective for undergraduate music majors who have completed Piano Class III. Students develop ensemble and reading skills through the study and performance of literature written for piano-four hands, piano-six hands, two pianos, and multi-keyboard ensembles.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Studio Orchestra
courses.description: Provides an opportunity for students to perform in a unique ensemble setting that combines the instrumentations of a traditional jazz ensemble with a chamber orchestra. This type of ensemble has been historically used in movie soundtracks, Broadway show orchestras, recording, and concert settings.

courses.title: Jazz Ensemble I
courses.description: Advanced level big band. This ensemble is made up of traditionalinstrumentation of saxophones, trombones, trumpets, piano, bass, drums, and guitar. This ensemble performs a difficult level of music from a variety of jazz styles, including swing, be-bop, Latin jazz, and contemporary.

courses.title: Jazz History
courses.description: Aural identification of factual stylistic knowledge of the majorworks, stylistic trends, and performance practices intwentieth-century jazz.  Awareness of the major composers andgeographical areas of influence in jazz from the late nineteenthcentury to the present.  Development of a vocabulary fordiscussing jazz compositions, jazz performance, andimprovisation.  Demonstrable ability to process and write aboutmusic heard in concerts and in the class.
courses.prerequisiteText: Permission of department | Graduate Prerequisite | Permission of department

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Jazz Improvisation I
courses.description: The study of chords and corresponding scales and how they are used in jazz context. Students will practice the skill of creating melodies on all chord/scales qualities. Students will study a variety of song forms used in the jazz style, 12-bar major blues, 12-bar minor blues, 32-AABA song form.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.title: Jazz Ensemble II
courses.description: Introductory level jazz big band. Instrumentation is saxophones,trombones, trumpets, plus rhythm section, including piano, bass, drums, and guitar. This ensemble rehearses music from all eras of big band jazz from Duke Ellington through contemporary composers. Students are accepted by audition.

courses.title: Jazz Improvisation II
