Students will have a broad comprehension of what it means to have cancer on several levels: 1) the patient; 2) the
oncology team; 3) the family; and 4) societal. Students will understand basic tumor biology. Students will understand the multitude of treatment options that have become available and how financial hardships
factor into these decisions. Students will understand the overwhelming "fear factor" that follows a cancer diagnosis. Students will understand descriptions of the most common types of cancer. Students will be able to describe the War on Cancer in sufficient detail to understand the competing interests involved and the complexity of this battle. Students will understand why the question, "Why haven't we cured cancer yet?" is an unreasonable question that 
requires more detail about the type of disease and other specifics.
courses.topical_outline:
1) The human/patient aspect of cancer
a) What does it mean to receive a diagnosis of cancer?
b) What are some of the challenges faced by the patient and their families?
c) What happens after a diagnosis?
d) What is the role of the caregiver? 
e) How can families work to prepare for cancer treatment and manage the process? 2) The oncology clinic
a) What occurs in the clinical setting, and how are the diagnosis and treatment approached?
b) What are the goals and options for cancer treatment? How do these goals vary by tumor type?
c) How have approaches changed over the years?
d) What are the long-term goals once a patient is in remission?
e) What are some of the consequences of treatment? 3) Tumor Biology
a) What is our current understanding of tumor biology?
b) How does our knowledge reflect the targeted and non-specific approaches taken to achieve 'cure' or remission?
c) What are the major challenges after a patient has reached a period of remission when the cancer is no longer detected?
d) On a molecular level, what is the function of tumor suppressors and genomic surveillance proteins?
e) How does familial genetics play a role in cancer?
courses.prerequisiteText: [(BIOL 1107 or BIOL 1107E or BIOL 2107H) and (BIOL 1108 or BIOL 2108H)] or permission of department

courses.subject: PHRM(PMCY)
courses.title: Pharmaceutical and Health Care Marketing
courses.description: Exploration of current health care and pharmaceutical marketing environment to provide insights into industry operation and career building. Application of general marketing principles to all aspects of health care and pharmaceutical marketing.

courses.subject: PHRM(PMCY)
courses.title: Specialty Pharmacy
courses.description: An introduction to specialty pharmacy and the disease states serviced by specialty pharmacists.
courses.prerequisiteText: PMCY 2020 or PHRM 3040 or permission of department

courses.subject: PHRM(PMCY)
courses.title: Abused Drugs
courses.description: The history, abuse, misuse, effects, and detection of selected drugs.  Guest lecturers are invited to present their views on these subjects.
courses.prerequisiteText: For PHRM: Enrolled in Doctor of Pharmacy Program; For PMCY: None

courses.subject: PHRM(PMCY)
courses.title: International Comparisons of Pharmacy Services and Health Care Delivery
courses.description: A comparison of international systems of delivery of pharmacyservices and health care delivery mechanisms, including varyingmethods of pharmacy care and medical systems in an internationalcontext.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: PHRM(PMCY)
courses.title: Ethics in Health Care
courses.description: A focus on the ethical issues and dilemmas facing healthprofessionals in today's environment.  Beliefs, humanexperimentation, professional responsibility, confidentiality,and conflicts of interest will be addressed to develop thecritical thinking process important to the personal andprofessional resolution of ethical issues.
courses.prerequisiteText: For PHRM: Enrolled in Doctor of Pharmacy Program; For PMCY: None

courses.subject: PHRM(PMCY)
courses.title: Public Health and the Health Professions
courses.description: Relationship between the public's health and the healthprofessions, including the role of the health care professionalin local, state, and national public health systems, the HealthyPeople 2010 program, interdisciplinary public health professionalteams, and the health care professional's role in preventionprograms.
courses.prerequisiteText: Enrolled in Doctor of Pharmacy Program or permission of department

courses.subject: PHRM(POPH)
courses.title: Essentials of Animals in Biomedical Research
courses.description: Humane methods of animal maintenance and experimentation; the testing methods which minimize animal distress; use of anesthetics, analgesics, and tranquilizers for commonly used lab species; methods for reporting deficiencies in animal care; laws pertaining to the use of animals in biomedical research.

courses.subject: PHRM(VPHY)(EHSC)
courses.title: Introductory Toxicology
courses.description: Basic toxicology principles, including dose-response relationships, principles of toxicity and safety evaluation, pharmacokinetics and metabolism of chemicals, basic mechanisms of cellular injury, factors influencing toxicity, carcinogenesis/mutagenesis, governmental regulations, and exposure and risk assessment.

courses.subject: PHRM(VPHY)
courses.title: Organ Systems Toxicology
courses.description: Mechanisms of injury of biological systems produced by chemical exposure.  Adverse effects of chemicals on major bodily organs and organ systems, including the blood, respiratory system, nervous system, kidneys, cardiovascular system, liver, immune system, reproductive system, skin, and eyes.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Essentials of Pharmacy Practice I
courses.description: Introduction to essential clinical, professional, and practice-based skills needed to provide pharmacy care.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Essentials of Pharmacy Practice II
courses.description: Introduction to essential clinical, professional, and practice-based skills needed to provide pharmacy care.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Medicinal Chemistry I
courses.description: Drugs acting on the peripheral nervous system and cardiovascular system, including structure-activity relationships, mechanisms of action, storage, and chemical stability reactions.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Introduction to Public Health
courses.description: An overview of the United States Public Health System as itcurrently exists and operates, with an emphasis on the corefunctions of public health.  A survey of different approaches topublic health problems, including health promotion and diseaseprevention.
courses.prerequisiteText: Student enrolled in the UGA College of Pharmacy

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmaceutical Calculations
courses.description: Mathematical principles and quantitative methods utilized in the contemporary practice of pharmacy. Calculations required in the quantitative development and assessment of prescriptions, dosage forms, drug delivery systems, and drug therapy modalities applicable to pharmacy practice.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Principles of Pharmacology I
courses.description: Principles of pharmacology, including pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and drug metabolism. Actions of agents on the autonomic nervous system and significant nonprescription drugs.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Principles of Pharmacology II
courses.description: Neuropharmacology and major classes of drugs acting on the central nervous system, including the clinical indication(s), mechanism and site of action, side effects, and potential drug interactions.
courses.prerequisiteText: Doctor of Pharmacy degree program | Pre or

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Anatomy and Physiology I
courses.description: Anatomy and physiology of the human body with emphasis on the central nervous system, autonomic nervous system, cardiovascular and renal systems.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pathophysiology I
courses.description: Fundamental mechanisms of human disease process, including manifestation, diagnosis, and treatment.  Emphasis on central nervous system, musculoskeletal, oncological, neurological, dermatological, and gastrointestinal diseases.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Career Opportunities and Development
courses.description: Pharmacy career pathways, including the necessary career development (i.e., residency/fellowship, CE, board certification, etc.) for each path. Discussions of the role and importance of professional organizations, networking, and professional behaviors necessary to succeed in pharmacy practice.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Interpreting Clinical Laboratory Tests
courses.description: Commonly used laboratory tests for each major organ system and their application for detecting disease, diagnosing medical problems, guiding treatment, and/or monitoring safety and efficacy.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to identify the most commonly used laboratory tests. Students will be able to state the medical terminology when given a medical abbreviation. Students will be able to differentiate between normal and abnormal laboratory values. Students will be able to interpret laboratory results to detect or diagnose disease, guide treatment, and/or monitor safety and efficacy of therapy.
courses.topical_outline: 1. Introduction to Clinical Laboratory Tests 2. Electrolytes 3. Kidneys/Urinalysis 4. Pulmonary Function and Related Tests 5. Heart 6. Liver and Pancreas Tests 7. Diabetes and Thyroid 8. Lipid Disorders 9. Hematology: Red and White Blood Cell Tests 10. Hematology: Blood Coagulation Tests 11. Men and Women's Health 12. Drug Screens

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Nutrition and Lifestyle Intervention in Pharmacy Practice
courses.description: Evidence-based principles of nutrition and lifestyle intervention relevant to pharmacy practice.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Human Pathophysiology
courses.description: Common human diseases and their pathophysiology (at the cell, tissue, organ, and system levels). Emphasis on the etiology of the disease, the symptoms, diagnosis, and classification. Introduction to drugs used to treat these diseases.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Immunology and Biotechnology
courses.description: Structure and function of the immune system and therapeutic products of biotechnology that are appropriate in patient counseling and treatment plans.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacy and the United States Health Care System
courses.description: The social, economic, and political forces that shape the environment in which health care currently is being delivered in America and how this affects the United States health care system and the practice of pharmacy.
courses.prerequisiteText: Doctor of Pharmacy student or permission of major

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Self-Care, Nonprescription Drugs, and Herbal Products
courses.description: The goal of this course is to prepare students to evaluate the needs of patients who consult pharmacists for recommendations regarding nonprescription medications or products. This includes collecting patient history, providing counseling on appropriate use, and referring to another provider if necessary.
courses.course_objectives: For each nonprescription drug product, the student should be able to recognize the usual indications for use. For each nonprescription drug product, the student should be able to evaluate the safety of each ingredient. For each nonprescription drug product, the student should be able to evaluate the efficacy of each ingredient. For each nonprescription drug product, the student should be able to select the most rational ingredient or combination of ingredients for a given treatment plan. For each nonprescription drug product, the student should be able to identify and make recommendations for the management of potential drug interactions. For each nonprescription drug product, the student should be able to identify and make recommendations for the management of potential adverse drug reactions. For each nonprescription drug product, the student should be able to state the contraindications for the use of nonprescription drug products. For each nonprescription drug product, the student should be able to state the usual dosage. For each nonprescription drug product, the student should be able to state the most appropriate route of administration. For each nonprescription drug product, the student should be able to recognize the label warnings on products and the rationale for each. For each nonprescription drug product, the student should be able to identify the usual therapeutic endpoint. For each nonprescription drug product, the student should be able to identify medication information to be communicated to the patient or a family member. For each common health complaint, the student should be able to identify associated signs and symptoms. For each common health complaint, the student should be able to determine which signs and symptoms may be ameliorated by nonprescription drug therapy. For each common health complaint, the student should be able to determine which signs and symptoms need further evaluation by home diagnostic devices. For each common health complaint, the student should be able to determine which signs and symptoms should not be treated with nonprescription drug therapy. For each common health complaint, the student should be able to identify the most appropriate type of health care practitioner or agency for patient referral, when self-medication is not advised. For each common health complaint, the student should be able to identify non-drug measures that may be included in the patient's treatment plan. For each common health complaint, the student should be able to identify which devices may be used to assess the patient's adherence with therapy and the presence of disease complications. For each common health complaint, the student should be able to describe products that are recommended for use with specific devices. The student pharmacist, given selected nonprescription drug products, should be able to explain the appropriate use (relative to administration), method of administration, and general precautions. For each nonprescription drug therapy plan or patient referral to another health care practitioner, the student pharmacist should be able to demonstrate communication skills and decision-making for the achievement of professional counsel and advice. The student pharmacist should know the commercial names and individual major ingredient or ingredients of common nonprescription products. Given a patient's medical and drug history, the student pharmacist will be able to select the most appropriate nonprescription drug product for use. The student pharmacist should be able to state and explain the steps that need to be taken in solving a common therapeutic problem/adverse effect presented by a patient and appropriately counsel the patient according to these steps and regarding any nonprescription product recommended.
courses.topical_outline: Clinical presentation, over-the-counter treatment options, management of special populations (e.g., pediatrics and pregnancy), and appropriate referral criteria Cough, cold, and allergies Pain and fever Dermatology (e.g., acne, burns) GI complaints (e.g., nausea, diarrhea) Durable medical equipment and home diagnostics Tobacco cessation Reproductive health Vitamins and herbal products
courses.prerequisiteText: PHRM 3030 and PHRM 3310 and PHRM 3900 and PHRM 3940

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacy Intercommunications
courses.description: The skills to effectively communicate with, teach, and counsel patients about their medications and health are taught. Effective inter-professional communication strategies and skills are presented, focusing on teamwork, roles and responsibilities, and ethics. Students are challenged to incorporate these skills into their own counseling and communication styles with patients and other health care professionals. Innovative technology is employed to promote interactive patient counseling.
courses.prerequisiteText: Doctor of Pharmacy student or permission of major

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Survey of Drug Information
courses.description: Primary, secondary, and tertiary drug information resources, including standard reference texts, computer systems and journals.  Emphasis will be placed on retrieval of information and communication of a response.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Introductory Pharmacy Practice Experience I
courses.description: Development of pharmacy practice skills within the community pharmacy setting. Emphasis will be on pharmacy operations (including prescription processing, vaccine administration, and inventory management), communication skills, the pharmacy patient care process, and professional development.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to collect and analyze information necessary to identify patient’s medication-related problems and health related needs. Students will be able to identify options for managing medication-related problems. Students will be able to communicate a patient’s medication-related problems to other health care providers. Students will be able to identify, use, and interpret appropriate resources to accurately answer medication-related questions. Students will be able to effectively counsel patients on the appropriate use of prescription and over-the-counter medications. Students will be able to accurately prepare, label, dispense, and distribute new and refill medications. Students will be able to accurately prepare, administer, and document vaccines. Students will be able to identify policies and procedures to prevent and report adverse drug events and medication errors. Students will be able to assist with the maintenance of pharmacy inventory. Students will be able to demonstrate professional and ethical behaviors and self-awareness of personal and professional attributes.
courses.topical_outline: 1) Pharmacist patient care process in the community pharmacy 2) Interprofessional collaboration 3) Assessing for medication-related problems and preventive health care needs 4) Policies and procedures to minimize adverse-drug events and medication errors 5) Evidence-based resources to advance patient care 6) Pharmacy operations including prescription processing, vaccine administration, and inventory management 7) Personal and professional development

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Essentials of Pharmacy Practice III
courses.description: Introduction to essential clinical, professional, and practice-based skills needed to provide pharmacy care.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Essentials of Pharmacy Practice IV
courses.description: Introduction to essential clinical, professional, and practice-based skills needed to provide pharmacy care.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Medicinal Chemistry II
courses.description: Central nervous system drugs, including their physio-chemical properties, structure-activity relationships and toxicities, side effects, and drug interactions.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Infectious Disease and Antitumor Agents
courses.description: Chemistry, spectrum of activity, stability, incompatibilities, and toxicities of agents used in the treatment of infectious diseases and cancers and the general aspects of anti-infectious disease agent use.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Fundamentals of Pharmaceutics I - Physical Pharmacy and Dosage Form Design
courses.description: Fundamentals of physical pharmacy and pharmaceutical dosage formdesign.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmaceutics II: Biopharmaceutics and Pharmacokinetics
courses.description: Basic concepts associated with drug absorption, distribution,metabolism, excretion, and transport with an emphasis oncompartmental modeling related to dosing of drugs.  Specificdisease states that alter drug disposition.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Physical Assessment for Pharmacists
courses.description: Basic principles and techniques of physical assessment performed by pharmacists.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacology III
courses.description: Pharmacological principles of drugs which affect the cardiovascular system, the endocrine system, the skin, bones, the GI system, and neurodegenerative diseases. Principles of toxicology will also be discussed.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacotherapeutic Issues in Women's Health
courses.description: Case-based pharmacotherapeutic course related to women's health. Interactive classroom discussion of female-specific conditions across the lifespan requiring pharmacologic treatment, including reproductive health, obstetrics, and menopause. Pre-class readings will be required to facilitate classroom discussion.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Health System Introductory Pharmacy Practice Experience
courses.description: Development of pharmacy practice skills in a health system setting, focusing on exposure to health system medication use processes and pharmacy patient care services.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Statistical Approaches to Drug Literature Evaluation
courses.description: Basic statistical methods and analysis used to criticallyevaluate drug literature are discussed.  Topics includestatistical inference and hypothesis testing, selection ofappropriate statistical tests, correlation and regressionanalysis, and research design.  Students will apply these topicswhile evaluating published clinical trials, outcome studies, andmaterials from pharmaceutical manufacturers.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee Drug Evaluation
courses.description: Development of a variety of skills, including critical analysis of drug literature, clinical and pharmacoeconomic evaluation of drugs, and written and oral presentation of recommendations, with an emphasis on the techniques used to make effective formulary decisions in managed care settings.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Addiction Pharmacy: The Pharmacist’s Role in the Management of Addiction Treatment
courses.description: The pharmacist's role in addiction pharmacy, including psychiatric medications, addiction treatment management medications, and pain management medications.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Addiction Pharmacy: Assessment, Evaluation, and Intervention Strategies
courses.description: Advanced addiction pharmacy, including psychiatric medications, addiction treatment management medications, and pain management medications through a “hands-on” approach of interviewing recovering patients in the classroom setting.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacotherapy I
courses.description: Evidence-based information and expert insight covering a wide variety of disease states and their associated therapies.
courses.prerequisiteText: PHRM 3040 and PHRM 3320 and PHRM 3070 and PHRM 3550 and PHRM 3520

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacotherapy II
courses.description: Evidence-based guidelines and information on management of common disease states as well as expert insight covering a wide variety of medical conditions and their associated therapies.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research I
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research II
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Faculty-Mentored Undergraduate Research III
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data and to present results in writing and other relevant communication formats.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Undergraduate Research Thesis (or Final Project)
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent or collaborative inquiry into fundamental and applied problems within a discipline that requires students to gather, analyze, synthesize, and interpret data. Students will write or produce a thesis or other professional capstone product, such as a report or portfolio that describes their systematic and in-depth inquiry.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Personal Financial Management for Pharmacists
courses.description: Effective management of the pharmacy graduate's personal finances. A life-cycle approach with special emphasis on actions needed during critical stages of the pharmacist's professional and personal life.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Antiviral Chemotherapy
courses.description: An in-depth discussion of human viral disease and the managementof these diseases.
courses.prerequisiteText: PHRM 4180/6180 or permission of department | Graduate Prerequisite | PHRM 4180/6180 or permission of department

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Antiviral Chemotherapy
courses.description: The etiology, epidemiology, and characteristics of human viraldiseases and the management and prevention of these diseases.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Diabetes Disease Management
courses.description: Provision of diabetes education/management services to patients.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Nuclear Pharmacy
courses.description: Procedures and techniques involved in handling and use of radio isotopes in nuclear pharmacy practice.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Entrepreneurship Beyond Dispensing
courses.description: Innovative pharmacy services beyond traditional dispensing practices.  Emphasis will be placed on identifying and evaluating new services, new businesses, and a different way to do “business.”

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Applied Pharmacy Practice I
courses.description: Application of knowledge to simulated cases and discussions as well as to real patient encounters.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Applied Pharmacy Practice II
courses.description: Application of knowledge to simulated cases and discussions as well as to real patient encounters.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacist's Role in Addiction Management
courses.description: Topics in addiction pharmacy, including psychiatric medications, addiction treatment management medications, and pain management medications. In-depth discussions of pharmacotherapeutic approaches for the treatment of all psychiatric illnesses, acute and chronic pain syndromes, and behavioral/chemical dependencies.
courses.prerequisiteText: Doctor of Pharmacy students or permission of school

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Anticancer Therapeutics
courses.description: Anticancer therapeutics and patient management with a focus on the prescribing basics, adverse effects of anticancer therapeutics necessary for patient management, along with drug administration and some biology of malignant disease.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Special Topics in Pharmacy
courses.description: Specialized pharmaceutical systems, processes and techniques, including assignment of current literature and student presentations.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Health Research Methods
courses.description: Application of principles, practices, and strategies for conducting research in health care.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: ECG interpretation
courses.description: Principles of cardiac function and electrophysiology with a focus on systematic interpretation of cardiac rate and rhythm parameters for electro-cardiogram. The course will also review principles of advanced cardiac life support and provide an opportunity for ACLS provider certification.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Advanced Compounding
courses.description: Novel and traditional dosage forms and advanced principles ofpharmaceutics for dosage form preparation and administration.
courses.prerequisiteText: PHRM 4120 and PHRM 4130 and PHRM 4200/6200 and PHRM 4211/6211 | Graduate Prerequisite | Permission of department

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Entrepreneurship for Pharmacists
courses.description: Current management and strategic issues in operating anindependent pharmacy.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Introduction to Veterinary Pharmacy
courses.description: Integration of veterinary pharmacology information with critical evaluation of the variances between common human versus animal pharmaceutical dosing. Students will analyze prescriptions for appropriateness and legal issues as well as demonstrate appropriate counseling skills.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Cardiology
courses.description: Use of drug therapy to treat patients with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases.  Emphasis on the pharmacotherapy used in treating diseases, treatment plans, patient counseling, and monitoring patient outcomes.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Consultant Pharmacy and Long-Term Patient Care
courses.description: Clinical skills and practical knowledge needed to prepare for asuccessful consulting practice. Topics include ConsultantPharmacist and Long Term Care Patients, Regulatory MinimalStandards, Medication Management Program in Long Term Care Inappropriate Drug Use in the Elderly, Safe Medication Use inOlder Adults, and Drug Regimen Review.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Basic Emergency Preparedness
courses.description: Basic first aid and disaster relief training for future pharmacists, other health care professionals, and graduate students.  First responders training and mock simulations for weapons of destruction events, including case studies, tabletop exercises, and mass casualty medical response.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Geriatric Medication Therapy Management
courses.description: Preparation for a geriatric or senior care area clerkship, suchas the pharmacy or primary care clinic, personal care,assisted-living, or nursing facility in appropriate management ofdrug use in older adults.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Critical Care Pharmacy
courses.description: In-depth discussions of disease states most commonly encountered in critical care patients and the associated pharmacotherapeutic management of these conditions.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pediatric Pharmacotherapy
courses.description: An overview of the health care needs of the pediatric patient, including the knowledge and skills to provide pharmaceutical care to pediatric patients in both ambulatory and inpatient settings.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacogenomic Therapies
courses.description: Pharmacogenomics is rapidly evolving with numerous drugsapplicable only to a specific patient population. In addition,emerging trends exhibit a major shift towards precision medicine.In this regard, avoiding unnecessary adverse events and tailoringappropriate medications to patients is a critical part ofadministering medication. There are more than 150 drugs withpharmacogenomic drug labeling.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Clinical Pharmacy Topics
courses.description: Topics from Pharmacy Grand Rounds lecture series, including specific areas in clinical pharmacy to global issues in healthcare. Presenters include faculty, guest lecturers, and pharamacy residents. Students provide a written concise summary for each presentation.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacy Health Services Outcomes
courses.description: Medication use from a systems perspective and strategies to improve outcomes. Personal, social, and organizational factors that affect the quality of medication use and outcomes as well as processes for evaluating medication-use systems and identifying ineffective system operations.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Nutraceuticals
courses.description: Rationale for use of nutraceuticals in both prevention andtreatment of human disease.  Course emphasizes nutritionalgenomic targets for nutraceutical research and development. Students will study several functional medicine topics related tothe use of nutraceuticals.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Parenterals
courses.description: Preparation and therapeutic uses of parenteral medicinal agentsuse in institutional (hospital) practice and home health caresettings.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Forensic Pharmacy
courses.description: Application of pharmacy to legal issues, including drug testing,analyzing adverse drug reactions for causation, evaluation of druginteractions, medication errors and drug effects as mitigatingfactors in criminal activity.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Community-Based Pharmacy Outreach
courses.description: A service-learning framework for implementing community-based programs in practice settings for health risk reduction with an emphasis on disease states and various target groups.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacy Informatics
courses.description: Enhancement of health information technology (HIT) is critical to advancing the quality, safety, and efficiency of patient care. The purpose of this course is to support student development in pharmacy informatics. Through an online delivery format emphasizing a practice-based perspective, students will develop knowledge in key pharmacy informatics concepts.
courses.prerequisiteText: Enrolled in Doctor of Pharmacy Program or permission of school

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Cases in Neurology
courses.description: The use of drug therapy to treat patients with neurologic diseases, including the pharmacotherapy used in treating diseases, disorders or syndromes, and a review of the disorder, therapeutic goals, treatment plans, patient counseling and patient outcome monitoring.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Integrated Patient Cases
courses.description: Complex patient cases in which students complete a work-up of a patient; identify and prioritize medication-related problems; and design a regimen, including monitoring parameters, to resolve medication-related problems.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Leadership and Management in Pharmacy Practice
courses.description: Pharmacy leadership and management principles, attributes of effective leaders and managers, importance of passion, vision, integrity, trust, and risk-taking by leaders andmanagers. Concepts of change management, effective communicationskills, mentorship, negotiation, delegation, and conflictmanagement.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Academic Pharmacy
courses.description: Career opportunities in academic pharmacy, including issues pertaining to the structure and function of colleges of pharmacy.
courses.prerequisiteText: Admission to the Doctor of Pharmacy degree program

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Advanced Cardiovascular Life Support
courses.description: The Advanced Cardiovascular Life Support (ACLS) elective provides detailed training in ACLS skills. The course involves ten weeks of guided self-study, including videos, reading, discussion boards, and quizzes, followed by an in-person simulation-based skills session. The class culminates with the American Heart Association certification in ACLS.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Interprofessional Approach to Simulated Patient Care
courses.description: Designed to prepare third-year Pharmacy students (P3s) for Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experiences (APPEs) and for providing direct patient care in the clinical setting. Emphasis on the necessity of working within a team when caring for patients and providing opportunities for P3s to work side-by-side with second-year medical students (M2s) in managing simulated patients in an acute setting. There will be three interprofessional education (IPE)-driven simulation experiences in collaboration with M2 students utilizing the Simulation Center located on the Augusta University/UGA Partnership campus.
courses.prerequisiteText: PHRM 3520 or PHRM 3900 or PHRM 4030 or PHRM 4040 or PHRM 4300 or PHRM 5160 or PHRM 5880

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Recruitment and Admissions of Pharmacy Students
courses.description: Engages students in the recruitment and admissions process for the Pharm.D. program in the College of Pharmacy. Students will learn about, discuss, and critique current recruitment/admissions practices; conduct benchmarking research about recruitment/admissions at peer/aspirational institutions; participate in recruiting events; and propose a new recruiting initiative for the College of Pharmacy.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacy Care Management
courses.description: Presentation of management principles, organizational needs,accounting practices, entrepreneurial aspects, marketing needs,and associated topics for use in future pharmacy and health caresystem practice milieus. The analysis of management principles asthey relate to community and health-systems management.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacy Law and Ethics
courses.description: Laws and regulations that govern the practice of pharmacy, including those of patient care, professional conduct, business conduct, hospital practice, and the dispensing and provision of pharmaceuticals.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Drug Interactions and Adverse Drug Reactions
courses.description: Most common drug interactions and adverse drug reactions with an emphasis on detection, prevention, and management.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Introduction to Postgraduate Residency Training
courses.description: In-depth description of residency training to prepare students to seek and obtain a residency position upon graduation. Course format includes informal lecture, panel discussion, written assignments, and competencies.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacotherapy III
courses.description: Evidence-based information and expert insight on establishing medication therapy plans in which students design, assess, and modify for varied clinical conditions.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacotherapy IV
courses.description: Evidence-based information and expert insight on establishing medication therapy plans in which students design, assess, and modify for varied clinical conditions.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience I
courses.description: Clinical practice in outpatient and inpatient settings with emphasis on pharmaceutical care.
courses.prerequisiteText: PHRM 4650 and PHRM 4211/6211 and PHRM 5560 and PHRM 5890

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience II
courses.description: Clinical practice in outpatient and inpatient settings with emphasis on pharmaceutical care.
courses.prerequisiteText: PHRM 4650 and PHRM 4211/6211 and PHRM 5560 and PHRM 5890

courses.title: Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience III
courses.description: Clinical practice in outpatient and inpatient settings with emphasis on pharmaceutical care.
courses.prerequisiteText: PHRM 4650 and PHRM 4211/6211 and PHRM 5560 and PHRM 5890

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience IV
courses.description: Clinical practice in outpatient and inpatient setting with emphasis on pharmaceutical care.
courses.prerequisiteText: PHRM 4650 and PHRM 4211/6211 and PHRM 5560 and PHRM 5890

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience V
courses.description: Clinical practice in outpatient and inpatient settings with emphasis on pharmaceutical care.
courses.prerequisiteText: PHRM 4650 and PHRM 4211/6211 and PHRM 5560 and PHRM 5890

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience VI
courses.description: Clinical practice in outpatient and inpatient settings with emphasis on pharmaceutical care.
courses.prerequisiteText: PHRM 4650 and PHRM 4211/6211 and PHRM 5560 and PHRM 5890

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience VII
courses.description: Clinical practice in outpatient and inpatient settings with emphasis on pharmaceutical care.
courses.prerequisiteText: PHRM 4650 and PHRM 4211/6211 and PHRM 5560 and PHRM 5890

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience VIII
courses.description: Clinical practice in outpatient and inpatient settings with emphasis on pharmaceutical care.
courses.prerequisiteText: PHRM 4650 and PHRM 4211/6211 and PHRM 5560 and PHRM 5890

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience IX
courses.description: Clinical practice in outpatient and inpatient settings with emphasis on pharmaceutical care.
courses.prerequisiteText: PHRM 4650 and PHRM 4211/6211 and PHRM 5560 and PHRM 5890

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Clinical Seminar
courses.description: Elements of an effective clinical presentation, including the use of slides, overheads, handouts, and other visual aids;  methods of answering audience questions;  steps to evaluate the presentation.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacotherapy Care Plans and Professional Development
courses.description: Capstone course (during last three semesters) for the advanced pharmacy experiences, including integration and utilization of student's knowledge of drug therapy and professional practice for patients with common disease states.  Development of professional attitudes and behaviors through completion of professional development activities.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Advanced Drug Information and Drug Policy Management
courses.description: Advanced concepts of drug information provision, including newsletter publication, ADR monitoring systems, drug usage evaluation, formulary management, and drug information retrieval and analysis.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Undergraduate Research Problem
courses.description: An introduction to research methods.  A problem will be assigned and the student will perform library and laboratory work and write up results.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Human Physiology I
courses.description: Physiology of the human body with emphasis on the central nervous system, autonomic nervous system and digestive system.
courses.prerequisiteText: (BIOL 1104 and CHEM 2410 and CHEM 2410L) or permission of department

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacology I
courses.description: Mechanisms of action of drugs in the human body.  Specific drug classes that are covered include nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs, male and female reproductive agents, thyroid drugs, insulin and diabetes treatments, diuretics, ACTH, cholinergic, antihypertensives, hyperlipidemias, antianginals, cardiac glycosides, thrombolytics, and antiarrhythmics.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacology II
courses.description: Pharmacologic mechanisms of action, therapeutic application, andtoxicology of drugs, focusing on central nervous system.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Human Physiology and Pathophysiology I
courses.description: Physiology and pathophysiology of the human body with emphasis on cellular function, the immune system, the nervous system, including the special senses.  Diseases of each of these systems will be covered in detail.  Additional emphasis will be placed on reviewing current scientific literature emphasizing recent advances in both fields.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pathophysiology I
courses.description: Mechanisms of human disease processes, including manifestation, mechanisms, diagnosis, treatment, prognosis.  Emphasis is on cell injury, neurological, dermatological, oncological, gastrointestinal, visual, and auditory disorders.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pathophysiology II
courses.description: Mechanisms of human disease processes, including manifestation, mechanisms, diagnosis, treatment, prognosis.  Emphasis is on inflammation, blood, endocrine, cardiovascular, pulmonary, and renal disorders.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Human Physiology II
courses.description: Human physiology of the cardiovascular, renal, endocrine, respiratory, immune, and reproductive systems, including selected topics in integrated physiological regulation.  Directed literature studies in human physiology.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Nutrition and Lifestyle Intervention in Pharmacy Practice
courses.description: Evidence-based principles of nutrition and lifestyle intervention relevant to pharmacy practice.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Human Physiology and Pathophysiology II
courses.description: Human physiology and pathophysiology of the endocrine, muscle, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, renal, and respiratory systems.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis in Healthcare
courses.description: Unlock your potential to shape evidence-based practice with this cutting-edge course on systematic reviews and meta-analyses. Gain mastery in critically evaluating, integrating, and applying empirical evidence to make groundbreaking contributions in healthcare decision-making. Engage in interactive lectures, hands-on statistical workshops, and collaborative appraisals of published research.
courses.course_objectives: Students will have a mastery of systematic review methodology and meta-analytic approaches, with a dual focus on frequentist and Bayesian statistics. Students will have the ability to critically assess and integrate scientific evidence, formulating research questions and developing comprehensive review protocols. Students will have proficiency in conducting literature searches, data extraction, and quality assessment. Students will have competence in critiquing existing evidence and published systematic reviews.
courses.topical_outline: Introduction to Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Research Question Formulation and Protocol Development Comprehensive Literature Search Techniques Data Management and Extraction Methods Frequentist and Bayesian Meta-Analytical Techniques Critical Appraisal of Published Reviews Capstone Project for Practical Application

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacy and the United States Health Care System
courses.description: The social, economic, and political forces that shape the environment in which health care currently is being delivered in the United States and how this affects the practice of pharmacy.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Applied Project in the Pharmaceutical and Biomedical Sciences
courses.description: Applied study of a topic or problem in Pharmaceutical and Biomedical Sciences related to the student’s interests.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Applied Project Writing and Defense
courses.description: The final assessment of the applied project requirement for the non-thesis M.Sc. in Pharmaceutical and Biomedical Sciences.
courses.course_objectives: Students will complete an applied project on an approved topic fulfilling the requirements for a non-thesis M.Sc. degree in the Pharmaceutical and Biomedical Sciences. Students will gain in-depth knowledge of a specialized topic in the Pharmaceutical and Biomedical Sciences. Students will gain scientific communication skills by presenting their project to a group of faculty.
courses.topical_outline: Conduct research on an approved topic in the Pharmaceutical and Biomedical Sciences Prepare a written report summarizing the results of your research project Prepare a presentation of your project for a group of faculty Make updates to your written report based on feedback from faculty

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Master's Research
courses.description: Research while enrolled for a master's degree under the direction of faculty members.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmaceutical Sciences Internship
courses.description: Research experience in an appropriate industrial or government environment.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Special Topics in Pharmacy
courses.description: Specialized pharmaceutical systems, processes and techniques,  assignments of current literature and student presentations.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Special Topics in Pharmacy
courses.description: Specialized pharmaceutical systems, processes and techniques, assignments of current literature and student presentations.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Master's Thesis
courses.description: Thesis writing under the direction of the major professor.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Introduction to Clinical Therapeutics
courses.description: Management of patients in the Health Care System. Casediscussions and certification in clinical research.  Studentswill gain competency necessary for translational research.
courses.prerequisiteText: Admission to the Clinical and Experimental Therapeutics PhD program in Pharmacy

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Graduate Teaching Seminar
courses.description: Provides graduate teaching assistants with opportunities to develop their teaching skills and a forum to discuss discipline-related teaching strategies and challenges. Also provides training for teaching, introduces students to instructional resources and support services available at UGA, and provides the opportunity to practice effective teaching strategies.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: PBS Laboratory Rotations I
courses.description: Introduction to department research opportunities.  Students will attend short research talks from PBS faculty and choose onefaculty member to serve as a rotation adviser.  Students willperform research rotations in their adviser's laboratory.
courses.course_objectives: This course is a one-semester series to give new graduate students introductory research experiences in laboratories that are accepting new students. This course is a one-semester series to help graduate students identify a research major professor. In addition, students gain experience in scientific writing.
courses.topical_outline: In the first half of the semester, students will complete assigned reading and attend weekly short seminars by departmental faculty interested in recruiting new graduate students. The topics will vary according to the research interests of the faculty. In the second half of the semester, students will choose a faculty rotation adviser and perform an eight-week rotation. Students are expected to perform experiments related to a research project, attend group meetings, and discuss their results with the research adviser.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Patient Care
courses.description: Residency experiences in the provision of advanced clinical services, development and maintenance of innovative clinical programs, teaching and precepting pharmacy students.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Healthcare Professional Education
courses.description: Presentation and discussion of current topics related topharmaceutical care in the community and hospital settings.
courses.course_objectives: Critically evaluate clinical and scientific literature. Identify emerging clinical concepts and treatments and evaluate how these concepts can be applied in the clinical pharmacy setting. Develop effective presentation and communication skills in presenting scientific, clinical, and translational information to health care professionals. Deliver a minimum of one presentation.
courses.topical_outline: Topics will be focused on clinical pharmacy and will vary depending on the speaker.
courses.prerequisiteText: PharmD degree and permission of department

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Graduate Pharmacy Residency Research
courses.description: Developing expertise in the process of research methods, including proposal development, data collection, analysis, and scholarly reporting of results, which are vital skills for clinical pharmacists and faculty working in healthcare and academia.
courses.prerequisiteText: PharmD degree and permission of department

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Teaching in Pharmacy Practice
courses.description: Evidence-based teaching skills and techniques for health careeducators with structured, peer-reviewed opportunities to develop teaching skills in classroom and clinical environments.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Health Outcomes for Practitioners
courses.description: Evaluation of health outcomes (or quality of life) in practiceand/or research settings with emphasis on practice-basedapplication for health professions students.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacy Resident Enrichment
courses.description: Varied pharmacy profession topics, supporting the development of training clinical pharmacists through weekly discussions and presentations.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: PBS Laboratory Rotations II
courses.description: Two eight-week research rotations in the laboratories of PBSfaculty members who are recruiting new students. Course isdesigned for first-year graduate students only.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Advanced Patient Care
courses.description: Residents will engage in advanced clinical pharmacy practice in specialized, complex patient populations to enable advanced clinical and practice management skill development. Upon completion, it is expected that the learner will be able to demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and attitudes of an expert practitioner to the faculty directing the course.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Advanced Healthcare Professional Education
courses.description: Academic presentation and discussion of current topics related to specialized and advanced direct patient care and/or research.Learners are expected to present seminars and evaluate seminarsgiven by other graduate students in the course.
courses.course_objectives: To critically evaluate clinical and scientific literature related to a current practice topic To identify emerging clinical concepts, processes, and pharmacotherapy and evaluate their potential application in the advanced practice setting To demonstrate effective communication and presentation skills through delivery of two formal seminars
courses.topical_outline: Topics will be focused on advanced clinical pharmacy practice and associated research and will vary depending on specialty. This course requires independent study and research, which provides opportunity for student to keep current on emerging clinical issues and to continue developing the knowledge and skills initiated in previous courses.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Advanced Graduate Residency Research
courses.description: An advanced clinical practice-based or translational researchproject developed and conducted under the direction of facultymembers.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Advanced Teaching in Pharmacy Practice
courses.description: Development and demonstration of advanced evidence-based teaching skills and techniques in multiple teaching environments.  All experiences will be peer-reviewed and included in students' teaching portfolios.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Clinical Applications
courses.description: Focuses on updates in therapeutics and advanced clinical topic review for teaching and practice. The course is only open to students enrolled in the College of Pharmacy's Graduate Residency Certificate Program (non-degree).

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Scholarship Development
courses.description: This course is only open to students enrolled in the College of Pharmacy's Graduate Residency Certificate Program (non-degree). Students will review clinical and research topics related to project completion and publication. Students are expected to complete a research study as part of the year-long certification program.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmaceutical and Biomedical Sciences Research Survey
courses.description: Seminar survey of research activities of faculty in the Department of Pharmaceutical and Biomedical Sciences.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Structural Biology and Medicinal Chemistry
courses.description: Lead discovery, chemical synthesis, and validation methodologycentral to medicinal chemistry. Structural biology techniques,including NMR, X-ray crystallography, and elements of modeling.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Molecular Pharmacology of Disease and Therapeutics
courses.description: The molecular basis of drug action and major disease states. Related laboratory techniques and current literature will complement didactic lectures.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Advanced Pharmaceutics and Biopharmaceutics
courses.description: Foundational and advanced topics in pharmaceutical and biopharmaceutical sciences focusing on physiochemical propertiesof drugs, delivery systems, and factors influencing the ADME of drugs.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Methods in Pharmaceutical and Biomedical Sciences
courses.description: Methods employed in cellular and molecular biomedical sciences, including the basis from which students can develop specific,in-depth skills as required in their research. Course addresses both theoretical and practical aspects of the various techniques.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Methods in Pharmaceutical and Biomedical Sciences II
courses.description: Methods employed in chemical and pharmaceutical sciences,including a basis from which students can develop specific,in-depth skills as required in their research. Course addressesboth the theoretical and practical aspects of the various techniques.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Grantsmanship
courses.description: Organization and origination of research ideas and data into grants, manuscript, and other submissions.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmaceutical Analysis I
courses.description: Separation, identification, and analysis of drugs by thin-layer, gas, and high performance liquid chromatography, supercritical fluid chromatography, and capillary electrophoresis.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmaceutical Analysis II
courses.description: The separation, identification, and analysis of drugs and metabolites in biological samples.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmaceutical Analysis III
courses.description: Identification and analysis of drugs and other biomolecules by mass spectrometry.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Chemistry of Synthetic Drugs
courses.description: New and established methods for synthetic preparation of organic medicinal agents.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Advanced Topics In Macromolecular Crystallography
courses.description: This course will cover specific topics concerning the theory of macromolecular crystallographic methods as well as new developments in the field.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Carbohydrate and Nucleoside Chemistry
courses.description: Carbohydrate chemistry and its application to the synthesis of nucleosides and related classes of compounds.
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Cancer Biology and Therapy
courses.description: A comprehensive and in-depth understanding of the cellularprinciples of cancer in regard to the molecular biology ofmalignancy and how optimal drugs can target these biological factors.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmaceutical and Biomedical Sciences Seminar
courses.description: Provides graduate students with an opportunity to attend scientific seminars from a range of research topics. The goal is for students to be exposed to a wide variety of research topics to broaden their scientific scope. Additionally, students will further gain seminar presentation skills through critique and practice.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Advanced Topics in the Pharmaceutical and Biomedical Sciences
courses.description: Recent developments in the pharmaceutical and biomedical sciencesusing a variety of literature, discussion, and laboratory methods.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Physical Pharmacy
courses.description: Physical concepts and methods as they apply to pharmaceutical problems.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Drug Delivery Systems
courses.description: The concepts, principles, technology, and assessment of drug delivery to the blood and target sites by various routes.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Technology in Industrial Pharmacy
courses.description: Formation and production of powders, capsules, compressed tablets, coated tablets, liquids, and semisolids.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Presentation Skills
courses.description: Provides graduate students with presentation and seminar skills. The goal is to teach students, through practice, examples, and critique, how to give an effective scientific talk and what components of a seminar constitute an effective presentation.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacokinetics
courses.description: The kinetics of drug absorption, distribution, and elimination with emphasis on the development and evaluation of mathematical models.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Contemporary Concepts in Pharmacokinetics
courses.description: Techniques of pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic modeling and data treatment.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Dispersion Laboratory of Industrial Pharmacy
courses.description: Laboratory skills in industrial pharmacy for manufacturingpharmaceutical dispersion dosage forms.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Drug Targets in Signal Transduction Pathways
courses.description: Molecular mechanisms of signal transduction pathways, withspecific emphasis on sites for therapeutic intervention andmanipulation.  Lecture, discussion, and student presentationsfrom primary literature.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Cancer Biology
courses.description: The focus of this course is molecular driving force and events in cancer initiation, progression, and metastasis; the contribution of micro-environment to cancer; current pharmaceutical strategies for treatment of cancer; and fundamental technologies in studying cancer biology.
courses.course_objectives: Students will be able to tackle fundamental cancer-biology questions through hypothesis-driven experimental design. Students will be able to collect examples of addressing specific questions in cancer biology. Students will be familiar with a variety of approaches for mining cancer data. Students will understand the underlined molecular mechanisms including presence of oncogenes and loss of tumor suppress genes in cancer initiation, progression, and metastasis. Students will be able to list and describe the main factors controlling the evolution of cancer cell populations. Students will develop a solid understanding of the tumor immunology and the basis of current cancer immunotherapy technologies. Students will have an understanding fundamental knowledge of cancer treatments including those related to pharmacological cancer therapies. Students will have an understanding of fundamental technologies in cancer research.
courses.topical_outline:
Part I: Intrinsic nature of cancer and cancer data-mining
1.	Cancer genome
2.	Eternal life: cell immortalization and tumorigenesis
3.	How tumorigenesis takes multi-step via selection and evolution
4.	Cancer invasion and metastasis 
5.	Cancer data mining Part II: Key facilitators of cancer initiation and progression
1.	Cancer driven by viral infection
2.	Cancer driven by oncogenes
3.	Growth factors and receptors
4.	Cytoplasmic signaling: Transmission of oncogenic signaling from cytoplasmic membrane to nucleus
5.	Cancer driven by loss of tumor suppressor genes Part III: Micro-environment for cancer evolution
1.     Functional role of angiogenesis in cancer progression
2.     Tumor microenvironment: Interaction of tumor cells with stromal cells
3.	Interaction of tumor cells with microphage
4.	Interaction of tumor cells with endothelial cells
5.	Cancer co-exist with the host immune system Part IV: Cancer pharmaceutic therapeutics and fundamental technology
1.	Cancer treatment including surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy
2.	Pharmaceutical drug discovery and clinic trials
3.	Fundamental molecular technology in exploring cancer

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Cardiovascular Pharmacology
courses.description: Mechanisms of action of drugs used in the treatment of cardiovascular disease states at the system, organ, and molecular level.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Coronary Heart Disease
courses.description: Pathophysiology of and therapeutic strategies for treatment of coronary heart disease, including lipid profiles, stress, alcohol, smoking and obesity as interactive risks in coronary artery disease.  The vascular biology of arteries and the biochemistry and cell biology of atherogenesis are examined.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Engineering of Protein Therapeutics
courses.description: This course uses literature or biotech industry examples for each topic together with some literature reviews. There will be a small component that requires the student to know or to learn some basic programming skills. For graduate students of any level with a background in biomedical sciences, chemistry, biochemistry, or engineering. Undergraduate-level courses in either basic molecular biology or biochemistry are required.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Drug Targets in Signal Transduction Pathways
courses.description: Cellular mechanisms of signal transduction by multiple pathways,with specific emphasis on sites for therapeutic intervention andmanipulation.  Function, regulation, and structure of thecomponents of the pathway including current or potentialstrategies to pharmacologically manipulate components of the pathway.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Social Behavioral Theory in Health Care
courses.description: Social behavioral theory and research methods used by health services researchers, focusing on determinants of health and illness, the interplay between values, technology, economics, and patient care.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacy Care Administration Seminar
courses.description: Current topics of pharmacy and health care services research.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Research Methods in Pharmacy Care Administration
courses.description: Research methodology, including formulation of research questions and research hypotheses, selection of the research design, sampling, internal and external validity, data collection, data analysis, results presentation and discussion.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Advanced Research Methods in Pharmacy Care Administration
courses.description: Advanced research methods in pharmaceutical and health care sciences employing a large claims data base. Course work includes design and execution of research hypotheses relating to medical outcomes, drug utilization review, and policy analysis. Methods include use of the Statistical Analysis System and mainframe control language.
courses.offeredText: Offered summer semester every odd-numbered year.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Health Care Marketing
courses.description: Application of the marketing process to health care and exploration of how marketing theory and practice are applied in health care environments.  Development and marketing of health care technology and consumer behavior issues, health beliefs, health promotion, and the role of patient education on behavior are explored.

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Pharmacoepidemiology
courses.description: Nature, purpose, and methods in pharmacoepidemiology and their place in pharmacy and health policy.  The general concepts in epidemiology and pharmacoepidemiology such as study population, drug exposure, basic measurements, quality of measurements, designs, bias and confounding factors.
courses.course_objectives: Students will understand foundational concepts in pharmacoepidemiology Students will describe the scope, history, and applications of pharmacoepidemiology in evaluating the use, safety, and effectiveness of medications in human populations. Students will identify and compare common data sources Students will evaluate strengths and limitations of various data sources used in pharmacoepidemiologic research, including administrative claims data, electronic health records, and national surveillance systems. Students will apply appropriate study designs and analytic methods Students will differentiate among cohort, case-control, cross-sectional, and experimental designs, and select appropriate designs for specific research questions. Students will assess bias and confounding in observational studies Students will identify and address key sources of bias (e.g., selection bias, immortal time bias) and confounding in pharmacoepidemiologic analyses. Students will interpret pharmacoepidemiologic literature Students will critically evaluate peer-reviewed research articles and assess the validity and implications of study findings. Students will design and present an independent research project Students will formulate a pharmacoepidemiologic research question, analyze real-world or secondary data, and communicate results through a written abstract and oral presentation.
courses.topical_outline: Epidemiology, Pharmacoepidemiology: Definitions and concepts and applications Descriptive Measures: Proportions, rates, ratios, incidence prevalence, mortality rates, case fatality ratio Quality of Measurement: Sensitivity, specificity, predictive value, validity, reliability Measuring Drug Exposure: Importance of appropriate time-windows Study Designs: Cohort studies, case-control studies, cross-sectional studies, experimental designs Measurement Errors: Random errors, systematic errors, Type I and Type II errors Bias: Selection bias, information bias, confounding bias Control of Biases: By design, by analysis Causality Use of Databases in Pharmacoepidemiology Clinical Epidemiology Meta-Analysis Epidemiologic Basis of Strategic Planning Epidemiology of Cardiovascular Diseases Evaluation of Health Care Programs: An Epidemiology Perspective

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Health Outcomes
courses.description: Quality of life assessment: history, measurement, and their place in pharmacy and health policy. Application in addition to theory is addressed.
courses.course_objectives: Upon course completion, students will be able to discuss conceptual and methodological approaches to health outcomes research. Upon course completion, students will be able to name and resolve issues with health outcomes measurement. Upon course completion, students will be able to apply a variety of generic and condition-specific health outcomes measures. Upon course completion, students will be able to make informed decisions for adequate data analysis, reporting, and interpretation of health outcomes data.
courses.topical_outline: 1.	Health outcomes research study designs and threats to the validity of the study design 2.	Methods for collecting health outcomes data 3.	Measurement (scaling methods, sensibility, reliability, validity) 4.	Use of generic outcomes measures versus condition-specific measures 5.	Use of multiple vs. single-item measures 6.	Generic outcome measures: physical functioning, psychological well-being, social functioning, cognitive functioning, vitality, overall well-being 7.	Measurement of demographic, psychologic, and social factors 8.	Measurement of patient satisfaction with care 9.	Health-related quality of life measures 10.	Use of condition-specific measures 11.	Considerations for risk adjustment strategies 12.	Considerations for analysis, reporting, and interpreting health outcomes research data

courses.subject: PHRM
courses.title: Advanced Therapeutics I
courses.description: The basic science and clinical issues associated with the use of pharmacological agents with a special emphasis on the pathogenesis and pharmacological management of cardiovascular, respiratory, and renal disorders.

courses.subject: PHRM

courses.title: Methods in Experimental Therapeutics
courses.description: Basic understanding of commonly employed methods in experimentaltherapeutics referencing the following topics:  i) animal modelsof stroke, diabetic retinopathy, cancer, pulmonaryhypertension/fibrosis, atherosclerosis, diabetic vascularcomplications (I); and ii) cell culture models and molecularbiological techniques (II).
courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: PHRM

courses.offeredText: Not offered on a regular basis.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physical Science
courses.description: An introduction to the concepts and laws of physics, and how their applications can be used to understand the behavior of familiar phenomena and objects.  Concepts are emphasized more than formulas and numbers.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Introductory Physics-Mechanics, Waves, Thermodynamics
courses.description: The first semester of a two-semester introductory course in physics.  A knowledge of algebra and trigonometry is assumed.  Mechanics (forces, Newton's laws of motion), wave phenomena, and thermodynamics.
courses.course_objectives: Students should be able to analyze text, diagrams, and graphs representing basic problems in classical mechanics to identify the physics principles and concepts needed to solve the problem. Students should be able to derive relevant mathematical relationships from the physical principles and concepts. Students should be able to apply those mathematical relationships to solve quantitative problems and reason abstractly with regard to dimensional and scaling arguments. Students should be able to explain their reasoning and describe their problem-solving process when approaching classical mechanics problems. Students should be able to evaluate the reasonableness of any solution through such methods as dimensional analysis, limiting/special cases, and order of magnitude estimates. Students should be able to generate diagrams, graphs, and other visual representations of classical mechanics data and measurements.
courses.topical_outline: Vectors and coordinate systems Kinematics: describing motion Dynamics: interactions of objects and Newton’s Laws Force and momentum Energy and work Torque and angular momentum Oscillations and waves

courses.title: Introductory Physics-Electricity and Magnetism, Optics, Modern Physics
courses.description: The continuation of Introductory Physics-Mechanics, Waves, Thermodynamics.  Electricity and electric circuits, magnetism, geometric and wave optics, and elementary atomic and nuclear physics.
courses.course_objectives: Students should be able to analyze text, diagrams, and graphs representing basic problems in optics and electromagnetism to identify the physics principles and concepts needed to solve the problem. Students should be able to derive relevant mathematical relationships from the physical principles and concepts. Students should be able to apply those mathematical relationships to solve quantitative problems and reason abstractly with regard to dimensional and scaling arguments. Students should be able to explain their reasoning and describe their problem-solving process when approaching optics and electromagnetism problems. Students should be able to evaluate the reasonableness of any solution through such methods as dimensional analysis, limiting/special cases, and order of magnitude estimates. Students should be able to generate diagrams, graphs, and other visual representations of optics, electric, and/or magnetic data and measurements.
